answers.D: Use a SageMaker Processing job that calls AWS KMS GenerateDataKey to encrypt each email, storing ciphertext and encrypted data key columns.

explanation: GenerateDataKey provides a data key for encrypt/decrypt; processing job can encrypt email with the data key and store encrypted data key per row.

stem: A health insurance company needs to predict claim costs using tabular data with dozens of numeric and categorical features. The model must be explainable for compliance and deployed quickly without custom code. Which modeling approach should the ML engineer choose?

answers.A: Train a deep neural network in SageMaker with a custom PyTorch script.
answers.B: Use the SageMaker built-in XGBoost linear learner in linear-learner mode.
answers.C: Deploy an Amazon Bedrock foundation model for tabular regression.
answers.D: Use SageMaker JumpStart to fine-tune a random forest model.

explanation: The SageMaker linear learner in linear mode offers both speed of built-in algorithms and coefficient-based explainability, meeting compliance without custom code.

stem: A startup has millions of short text support tickets. They need to automatically categorize them into about ten categories. They require near real-time inference and minimal infrastructure management. Which approach is most appropriate?

answers.A: Use SageMaker built-in Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) to extract topics.
answers.B: Train a K-means clustering model on bag-of-words features.
answers.C: Use Amazon Comprehend custom classification endpoints.
answers.D: Fine-tune a SageMaker JumpStart GPT model for classification.

explanation: Amazon Comprehend custom classification provides a managed, low-latency service optimized for text classification without heavy infrastructure or custom training.

stem: A financial firm must model customer churn using a dataset of 100,000 rows and 200 features, many of which are sparse. They need both high accuracy and moderate interpretability. Which algorithm should they select?

answers.A: Regularized gradient-boosted trees with SHAP explainability in SageMaker.
answers.B: Deep neural network with attention layers in SageMaker Training.
answers.C: K-nearest neighbors classifier on the full feature set.
answers.D: SageMaker linear learner without feature interactions.

explanation: Gradient-boosted trees provide strong accuracy on structured data and SHAP integration yields moderate interpretability, balancing both requirements.

stem: A retailer wants to forecast hourly product demand across 500 stores. They need a model that handles seasonality and multiple time series simultaneously with minimal custom development. Which AWS capability should they use?

answers.A: Build a Seq2Seq model in PyTorch with SageMaker script mode.
answers.B: Use SageMaker built-in DeepAR forecasting.
answers.C: Fine-tune a Bedrock LLM for time series forecasting.
answers.D: Use Amazon Forecast with a custom recipe for seasonal demand.

explanation: Amazon Forecast is a managed service specialized in multi-dimensional time series forecasting with built-in seasonality handling and minimal development.

stem: An e-commerce company needs to detect anomalous orders in real time. The data has 50 continuous and categorical features. They want full control over algorithm selection and hyperparameters. Which modeling approach is best?

answers.A: Train an Isolation Forest using SageMaker built-in with batch inference enabled.
answers.B: Deploy Amazon Lookout for Metrics for anomaly detection.
answers.C: Use SageMaker KNN anomaly detection with default parameters.
answers.D: Fine-tune a JumpStart anomaly detection model on Amazon Bedrock.

explanation: SageMaker built-in Isolation Forest gives full control over hyperparameters and supports custom batch inference while being managed.

stem: A logistics company wants to segment customers into behavioral clusters using both shipment frequency and cost. They expect clear cluster centroids for interpretability. Which algorithm should they choose?

answers.A: DBSCAN clustering in SageMaker Processing.
answers.B: Hierarchical clustering in SageMaker Spark.
answers.C: Gaussian Mixture Model with EM in SageMaker.
answers.D: K-means clustering with the SageMaker built-in algorithm.

explanation: K-means provides clear centroids and is available as a built-in SageMaker algorithm, balancing interpretability and managed operation.

stem: A media company needs to recommend movies using collaborative filtering on user-item ratings. They require a scalable solution integrated with SageMaker. Which modeling approach fits?

answers.A: Train a matrix factorization model in Scikit-Learn on SageMaker Training.
answers.B: Use Amazon Personalize batch recommendations.
answers.C: Use SageMaker built-in factorization machines algorithm.
answers.D: Fine-tune a JumpStart recommender system foundation model.

explanation: SageMaker factorization machines are optimized for collaborative filtering, scalable, and integrated into SageMaker workflows.

stem: A biotech startup must classify protein sequences. Labeled data is scarce, and interpretability is not critical. They want to leverage pretrained models. Which approach is most appropriate?

answers.A: Train a CNN from scratch in SageMaker script mode.
answers.B: Fine-tune a JumpStart protein foundation model.
answers.C: Use SageMaker built-in XGBoost with k-mer features.
answers.D: Develop a random forest on physicochemical features.

explanation: JumpStart protein foundation models leverage pretrained knowledge, requiring limited data and engineering, ideal for scarce labels without interpretability needs.

stem: A compliance-driven enterprise must predict default risk on personal loans. They need to justify each decision to auditors. Which modeling approach balances accuracy and full explainability?

answers.A: Use SageMaker built-in linear learner and present feature coefficients.
answers.B: Train an XGBoost model and approximate SHAP explanations.
answers.C: Deploy an Amazon Bedrock LLM to explain historical decisions.
answers.D: Use DeepAR to forecast default probabilities.

explanation: Linear learner provides transparent coefficients for direct auditing, ensuring full explainability though with modest accuracy trade-off.

stem: A gaming company needs to classify images of player avatars into categories. They want to minimize GPU cost and only require coarse-grained accuracy. Which SageMaker option should they choose?

answers.A: Fine-tune a JumpStart ResNet model.
answers.B: Train a custom CNN in PyTorch on GPU.
answers.C: Use SageMaker built-in image classification algorithm on CPU.
answers.D: Deploy Amazon Rekognition with custom labels.

explanation: The built-in image classifier can run on CPU for coarse tasks with lower cost, avoiding GPU and heavy customization.

stem: An IoT company collects multivariate sensor time series and needs to detect anomalies streaming. They prefer managed services and minimal model maintenance. Which approach is best?

answers.A: Train an LSTM autoencoder in SageMaker script mode.
answers.B: Use the SageMaker built-in random cut forest algorithm in batch.
answers.C: Fine-tune an LLM for time series anomaly detection.
answers.D: Use Amazon Lookout for Equipment for streaming anomalies.

explanation: Amazon Lookout for Equipment is managed, supports streaming anomaly detection on sensor data with minimal maintenance.

stem: A marketing team wants to segment emails by topic automatically. They need a fully managed NLP solution that adapts over time. Which AWS service should they use?

answers.A: Train LDA in SageMaker Processing.
answers.B: Use Amazon Comprehend topic modeling APIs.
answers.C: Fine-tune a JumpStart GPT-3 model for topic extraction.
answers.D: Use Amazon SageMaker BlazingText for unsupervised topic clusters.

explanation: Amazon Comprehend provides managed topic modeling that adapts to new data without custom training.

stem: A telecom wants to predict customer churn with an imbalanced dataset and needs to prioritize recall over precision. They plan to tune thresholds. Which algorithm and metric combination should they choose?

answers.A: Train XGBoost in SageMaker and optimize for recall using hyperparameter tuning with custom F-beta metric.
answers.B: Use logistic regression and evaluate accuracy.
answers.C: Deploy random forest and adjust class weights only at inference.
answers.D: Use built-in factorization machines with default evaluation.

explanation: XGBoost with custom metric optimization allows tuning hyperparameters for recall, matching business priority on false negatives.

stem: A media analytics team needs to extract entities from video transcripts. They require deep customization of entity categories and managed model hosting. What should they choose?

answers.A: Train a custom spaCy NER model on SageMaker Processing.
answers.B: Fine-tune a JumpStart language model and deploy on SageMaker.
answers.C: Use Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognition endpoints.
answers.D: Use Amazon Textract to extract text and regex on transcripts.

explanation: Comprehend custom entity recognition offers managed training and hosting with customizable entities, minimizing infra effort.

stem: A fraud detection use case has a growing number of streaming events per second and requires sub-millisecond inference. They need high throughput and low latency with minimal operational overhead. Which approach fits?

answers.A: Deploy XGBoost model on SageMaker real-time endpoint on CPU.
answers.B: Use SageMaker serverless inference with ProvisionedConcurrency.
answers.C: Deploy model on ECS Fargate behind API Gateway.
answers.D: Use Lambda to host model via Docker image.

explanation: Serverless inference with provisioned concurrency handles variable volumes and low latency without managing servers.

stem: A retailer wants price elasticity estimates per product category, requiring interpretable coefficients. They have limited compute budget. Which modeling approach should they select?

answers.A: Train a tree-based ensemble and use SHAP.
answers.B: Fine-tune a Bedrock regression foundation model.
answers.C: Use SageMaker XGBoost regressor default.
answers.D: Use SageMaker linear learner with L1 regularization for sparse features.

explanation: Linear learner yields direct coefficients for price elasticity, with L1 handling sparsity and minimal compute overhead.

stem: An ML engineer must automatically classify customer reviews into positive or negative sentiment. They need near zero code and managed endpoints. Which AWS service should they choose?

answers.A: Build a logistic regression in SageMaker script mode.
answers.B: Use Amazon Comprehend sentiment analysis endpoints.
answers.C: Fine-tune a JumpStart BERT model.
answers.D: Train SageMaker built-in BlazingText skip-gram model.

explanation: Comprehend provides out-of-the-box sentiment analysis API with no code and managed hosting.

stem: A company has sparse high-dimensional clickstream data and wants a scalable algorithm for binary classification. They prioritize L1 regularization to perform feature selection. Which SageMaker built-in algorithm should they choose?

answers.A: SageMaker built-in linear learner with L1 mode.
answers.B: Built-in XGBoost with default settings.
answers.C: Built-in KNN.
answers.D: Built-in K-means.

explanation: Linear learner supports L1 regularization for feature selection and scales to high dimensions.

stem: A healthcare provider needs to detect disease from X-ray images with regulatory constraints on data privacy. They want to use a managed service and avoid moving data off-premises. Which solution is best?

answers.A: Use SageMaker built-in image classification in public endpoints.
answers.B: Deploy a JumpStart Vision transformer in SageMaker Studio.
answers.C: Configure SageMaker Inference on AWS Outposts with the built-in image classification algorithm.
answers.D: Use Amazon Rekognition for custom labels.

explanation: SageMaker on AWS Outposts runs locally, preserving data privacy without sending images off-premises.

stem: A startup needs to detect default probability from loan applications with limited GPU budget. They require class probability outputs and fast training. Which algorithm should they pick?

answers.A: Deep AR forecasting model.
answers.B: Built-in XGBoost classifier.
answers.C: Built-in K-means clustering.
answers.D: Built-in PCA.

explanation: XGBoost classifier offers fast training on CPU/GPU, outputs probabilities, and is cost-efficient.

stem: A legal firm wants to identify key contract clauses in documents. They need a managed NLP solution they can tailor without hosting infrastructure. Which should they use?

answers.A: Amazon Comprehend custom classification for clause categories.
answers.B: Fine-tune JumpStart GPT-3 and host on SageMaker.
answers.C: Use SageMaker built-in BlazingText.
answers.D: Train a custom BERT model in SageMaker script mode.

explanation: Comprehend custom classification lets them define clause categories and uses managed endpoints without infra overhead.

stem: A search engine needs to rank results by relevance using user click logs. They require pairwise ranking and integration with SageMaker. Which algorithm is suitable?

answers.A: Built-in random forest classifier.
answers.B: Built-in KNN algorithm.
answers.C: DeepAR forecasting.
answers.D: SageMaker Factorization Machines with ranking objective.

explanation: Factorization Machines support pairwise ranking objectives and integrate seamlessly in SageMaker pipelines.

stem: An agricultural startup wants to detect crop diseases from leaf images. They have limited labeled data and need transfer learning with minimal fine-tuning. Which approach should they choose?

answers.A: Train a CNN from scratch in PyTorch on SageMaker.
answers.B: Use SageMaker built-in XGBoost on flattened image features.
answers.C: Fine-tune a JumpStart transfer learning image classification model.
answers.D: Deploy Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels.

explanation: JumpStart transfer learning models require minimal labeled data and fine-tuning for image tasks, reducing effort.

stem: A robotics company collects multi-modal sensor data (images and lidar). They need a model that natively handles heterogeneous inputs. Which modeling approach is best?

answers.A: Ensemble separate built-in algorithms for each modality.
answers.B: Train a multimodal PyTorch model in SageMaker script mode.
answers.C: Use Amazon SageMaker built-in Linear Learner with concatenated features.
answers.D: Fine-tune a JumpStart text foundation model.

explanation: A custom PyTorch script enables combining different data types in a single model, which built-ins cannot natively handle.

stem: A voice assistant service must detect five spoken commands in streaming audio. They need low latency and a managed solution. Which AWS offering should they use?

answers.A: Train a CNN in SageMaker to classify spectrograms.
answers.B: Use SageMaker built-in KNN on MFCC vectors.
answers.C: Fine-tune a JumpStart Transformer.
answers.D: Use Amazon Transcribe to convert speech to text and Comprehend custom classification.

explanation: Transcribe plus Comprehend custom classification offers managed low-latency command detection without building audio models.

stem: A rideshare company needs to price surge multipliers based on real-time location and demand. They require sub-second inference at scale. Which modeling approach and deployment should they choose?

answers.A: Train a decision tree in SageMaker and deploy on CPU endpoint.
answers.B: Use SageMaker real-time multi-model endpoints with XGBoost model.
answers.C: Host a neural network on ECS Fargate.
answers.D: Use Amazon Forecast predictor endpoint.

explanation: XGBoost on multi-model endpoints provides low-latency at scale with minimal endpoint overhead for multiple regions.

stem: A financial services company observes that their fraud-detection model has high overall accuracy but low recall on high-value transactions. They suspect the model underfits rare, high-value cases. Which of the following evaluation strategies best identifies this issue?

answers.A: Plot a single ROC curve on the full dataset and inspect AUC
answers.B: Compute macro-averaged precision across all transaction values
answers.C: Segment the test set by transaction value and compute per-segment recall
answers.D: Evaluate overall F1 score without stratification

explanation: Segmenting by transaction value and computing recall highlights underperformance on high-value cases. Overall AUC or aggregated metrics mask segment-specific issues.

stem: An ML engineer deploys two XGBoost models: a control and a new variant. After 1M predictions, the variant shows a slightly higher latency but 2% higher recall. How should they evaluate if this trade-off is acceptable?

answers.A: Compare single-sample inference logs for outliers
answers.B: Plot precision-recall curves and latency distributions for both variants
answers.C: Compute overall accuracy for both and pick model with higher accuracy
answers.D: Use confusion matrix of the slower model only

explanation: Precision-recall curves reveal how recall gain trades off against precision, while latency distributions quantify performance cost. Overall accuracy and single-sample latency don’t capture distribution details.

stem: During hyperparameter tuning of a neural network, SageMaker Debugger reports gradient vanishing in early layers. Which metric or visualization should you use to pinpoint the affected layers?

answers.A: Plot TensorBoard histograms of weight and gradient distributions per layer
answers.B: Inspect model’s overall loss curve only
answers.C: Compute validation accuracy after each epoch
answers.D: View average prediction confidence on test data

explanation: Layer-wise weight and gradient histograms directly show vanishing or exploding gradients. Loss curves and accuracy trends are too coarse to locate the problem.

stem: A classification model shows 95% accuracy but customers complain of frequent false positives. Which metric will best capture the operational false-positive rate?

answers.A: ROC AUC
answers.B: Accuracy
answers.C: Macro F1 score
answers.D: False positive rate (FP/(FP+TN))

explanation: False positive rate directly measures proportion of non-events incorrectly flagged. Aggregate metrics and AUC do not quantify FP in production terms.

stem: An ML engineer wants to compare a shadow variant’s performance to production. They have stored logs with predictions and ground truth over a week. What’s the most reproducible approach?

answers.A: Re-run inference on production endpoint and compute metrics
answers.B: Compute metrics in real time on live data
answers.C: Use the stored logs to batch calculate identical evaluation metrics for both models
answers.D: Use shadow variant accuracy reported in CloudWatch metrics

explanation: Batch calculating evaluation metrics on the same logged data ensures reproducibility. CloudWatch reports may differ in metric definitions, and re-running inference can produce drift.

stem: After deploying a regression model, business users report that error increases when feature "loan_amount" exceeds $100k. Which diagnostic step is most appropriate?

answers.A: Check overall RMSE
answers.B: Plot residuals against loan_amount
answers.C: Compute R² on training data
answers.D: Re-train model without loan_amount

explanation: Residual-vs-feature plots reveal heteroscedasticity or feature-specific error patterns. Overall RMSE or training R² mask inequalities across feature ranges.

stem: SageMaker Clarify indicates a high feature importance contribution from "zipcode" in loan approval model. Finance team worries about proxy bias. What evaluation should be done next?

answers.A: Compute disparity metrics for protected groups defined by zipcode demographics
answers.B: Remove zipcode and retrain immediately
answers.C: Ignore since importance doesn’t imply bias
answers.D: Compute overall feature correlation matrix

explanation: High importance for zipcode may proxy demographic bias; computing disparity metrics for protected groups reveals actual bias. Simply removing the feature may degrade performance without confirming bias.

stem: A model’s AUC on validation is 0.85 but drops to 0.75 in production. Which step best isolates the cause?

answers.A: Increase regularization to reduce overfitting
answers.B: Retrain with more epochs
answers.C: Change the threshold to match validation TPR
answers.D: Compare feature distribution between validation and production using Clarify data drift reports

explanation: Distribution drift analysis identifies covariate changes causing performance drop. Regularization and threshold tuning don’t address data mismatch.

stem: During batch experiments, an engineer notices that increasing tree depth raises precision but lowers recall. Which plot best illustrates this trade-off?

answers.A: Precision-recall curve parametrized by depth
answers.B: ROC curve at each depth
answers.C: Confusion matrix for the deepest tree only
answers.D: Histogram of prediction confidences

explanation: Precision-recall curves for each depth show the precision/recall trade-off directly. ROC curves and single-depth confusion matrices do not illuminate that trade dynamically.

stem: After hyperparameter tuning, two models have identical validation loss but different generalization gaps. Which metric indicates stronger overfitting?

answers.A: Higher training loss
answers.B: Larger difference between training and validation accuracy
answers.C: Higher validation AUC
answers.D: Lower inference latency

explanation: A large gap between training and validation accuracy indicates overfitting. Validation AUC and latency don’t measure overfitting directly.

stem: An NLP classification model shows significantly higher F1 for short texts versus long texts. How do you quantify performance disparity?

answers.A: Overall F1 score
answers.B: Word count distribution histogram
answers.C: Group test samples by text length bins and compute per-bin F1
answers.D: Pearson correlation between length and predicted label

explanation: Bin by text length and compute F1 per bin to quantify disparity. Overall metrics and correlation don’t isolate the problem.

stem: You need to determine if a drop in model accuracy after a code change is due to random seed variance or genuine performance loss. Which practice ensures reproducibility?

answers.A: Fix random seed across training, log model parameters, and compare artifacts
answers.B: Re-run training with different seeds and average
answers.C: Use early stopping to stabilize performance
answers.D: Only compare inference results on live data

explanation: Fixing seeds and logging artifacts ensures reproducible runs. Averaging across seeds helps smooth noise but doesn’t isolate change impact.

stem: An engineer suspects label leakage because a high validation AUC is too good to be true. Which diagnostic will reveal leakage?

answers.A: Increase regularization
answers.B: Shuffle labels and retrain to observe AUC
answers.C: Add more layers
answers.D: Compute feature correlations only

explanation: Shuffling labels destroys true signal; if AUC remains high, leakage exists. Feature correlations alone may miss leakage patterns.

stem: A deployed model exhibits high memory consumption during inference. Which SageMaker Debugger profiler metric helps pinpoint bottlenecks?

answers.A: Overall endpoint invocation count
answers.B: CloudWatch memory usage graphs
answers.C: Inference latencies per request
answers.D: Model container’s PeakHostMemoryUsage metric

explanation: PeakHostMemoryUsage from Debugger profiling identifies model container memory peaks. Invocation counts and latency don’t measure memory usage.

stem: When comparing two regression models, you find one has lower MAE but higher RMSE. What does this indicate?

answers.A: The second model has larger outlier errors
answers.B: The second model performs better on average
answers.C: The first model is overfitting
answers.D: The first model has higher variance

explanation: Higher RMSE than MAE implies presence of larger outlier errors, since RMSE penalizes them more. Average performance may be similar.

stem: You deploy an image classifier and monitor per-class recall. Class A recall drops below SLA overnight. Logs show no data drift. What is your next diagnostic?

answers.A: Increase batch size
answers.B: Retrain with more epochs
answers.C: Analyze inference input distribution for class A by sampling inputs
answers.D: Reduce learning rate

explanation: Sampling inputs checks if unexpected inputs are arriving for Class A. No drift in overall features doesn’t guarantee class-specific input change.

stem: Your model’s production log shows many low-confidence predictions. Which threshold-based method helps maintain production SLA?

answers.A: Use maximum probability per sample as a calibration correction
answers.B: Implement a confidence threshold to send low-confidence cases to manual review
answers.C: Retrain until all predictions exceed a fixed threshold
answers.D: Always return top-2 classes to clients

explanation: A confidence threshold with fallback to manual review maintains SLA. Calibration alone won’t meet SLA guarantees.

stem: An ML pipeline reruns hyperparameter tuning daily. You want to compare results over time. Which practice aids trend analysis?

answers.A: Log only best tuning job’s metrics
answers.B: Store only final model artifacts
answers.C: Compare only today's and yesterday's tuning graphs
answers.D: Archive tuning job metrics and hyperparameter configurations in SageMaker Experiments

explanation: SageMaker Experiments archives metrics and configs over time, enabling trend and retrospective analysis. Comparing partial data isn’t sufficient.

stem: After retraining a model with more data, confusion matrix shows increased FN but decreased FP. Business impact of FNs is higher. How do you adjust the model?

answers.A: Shift decision threshold to favor recall over precision
answers.B: Increase regularization
answers.C: Reduce training data size
answers.D: Switch to a different algorithm

explanation: Threshold adjustment trades precision and recall bias to reduce FNs, aligning with higher cost of FNs. Algorithm shift or data size changes are heavier-handed.

stem: SageMaker Clarify reports a DPL (difference in proportions of labels) of 0.12 for a protected group. Which conclusion is correct?

answers.A: Model is fair, since DPL < 0.2
answers.B: There is moderate demographic bias requiring mitigation
answers.C: DPL only applies to continuous features
answers.D: Bias can be ignored if overall accuracy is high

explanation: DPL of 0.12 indicates non-trivial bias that should be addressed. Fairness thresholds vary, but non-zero DPL warrants mitigation. Accuracy doesn’t nullify bias.

stem: You need to diagnose why training loss plateaus early. Which combined SageMaker Debugger rule is most helpful?

answers.A: LossNotDecreasing and LargeGradient
answers.B: VanishingGradient and OverTraining
answers.C: LossNotDecreasing and VanishingGradient
answers.D: OverTraining and HighThroughput

explanation: LossNotDecreasing flags plateau, VanishingGradient identifies small gradients. Together they pinpoint stalled training due to gradient issues.

stem: After enabling endpoint data capture, you observe data skew for feature X. Which remediation reduces skew immediately?

answers.A: Retrain online with captured data
answers.B: Increase endpoint instance count
answers.C: Switch to a different instance type
answers.D: Implement input feature transformation to normalize X at inference

explanation: Applying transformation at inference normalizes skewed feature values immediately. Retraining is longer-term and won’t reduce skew on streaming data.

stem: Your binary classifier has high variance between folds in cross-validation. What change will most reduce variance?

answers.A: Use ensembles like random forests
answers.B: Increase learning rate
answers.C: Use fewer features
answers.D: Reduce training set size

explanation: Ensembling reduces model variance by averaging multiple learners. Lower LR or fewer features may increase bias. Reducing data increases variance.

stem: A class-imbalanced dataset yields high recall but poor precision. Which metric-guided tuning step helps restore balance?

answers.A: Increase tree depth
answers.B: Use mean squared error loss
answers.C: Optimize model using precision-recall AUC as objective
answers.D: Switch to accuracy objective

explanation: Using PR AUC aligns hyperparameter tuning to both precision and recall on imbalanced data. MSE or accuracy objectives aren’t appropriate for classification imbalance.

stem: An LSTM model overfits after 10 epochs. You add dropout but performance still degrades. Which debugging step helps find root cause?

answers.A: Increase L2 regularization
answers.B: Use Debugger’s tensor shape rule to confirm no unintended dimension mismatch causing overfitting
answers.C: Increase learning rate
answers.D: Reduce batch size

explanation: Tensor shape mismatches can cause incorrect weight updates that appear as overfitting. Debugger shape rules detect such bugs. Regularization alone may mask deeper issues.

stem: Your model produces inconsistent outputs when served on GPU versus CPU instances. How do you isolate source?

answers.A: Retrain separately on GPU and CPU
answers.B: Enable inference latency metrics
answers.C: Use SageMaker Clarify to detect drift
answers.D: Run inference deterministically on both environments with same input batch and compare element-wise outputs

explanation: Deterministic inference comparison on CPU vs GPU pinpoints numerical instability or library inconsistency. Drift detection and latency metrics don’t isolate environment differences.

stem: A regression model’s residuals exhibit non-constant variance. Which transformation corrects this?

answers.A: Standardize all features
answers.B: Apply log transform to the target variable
answers.C: Increase polynomial degree of predictors
answers.D: Use one-hot encoding for categorical features

explanation: Log-transforming the dependent variable often stabilizes variance (heteroscedasticity). Feature standardization doesn’t address residual variance issues.

stem: After changing preprocessing, model performance unexpectedly improved in test but dropped in validation. Which practice uncovers this data leakage?

answers.A: Inspect preprocessing pipelines for operations applied before train-test split
answers.B: Increase test set size
answers.C: Add more regularization
answers.D: Use k-fold CV on original split

explanation: Applying preprocessing (e.g., normalization) before splitting leaks test information. Reviewing pipeline order reveals leakage.

stem: Your model’s precision increases when you add a new feature but recall drops. You need to quantify the net business impact. What analysis should you perform?

answers.A: Compute new overall F1 score
answers.B: Plot ROC curve
answers.C: Estimate expected cost change using per-error cost matrix
answers.D: Compare AUC-PR before/after

explanation: Cost matrix analysis translates precision/recall changes into business impact. F1 and curves are abstract performance measures without cost context.

stem: A fintech startup has an image-based document verification model that requires sub-100ms inference latency at the edge. They must deploy the optimized model to ARM-based devices with intermittent connectivity. Which deployment infrastructure best meets these requirements?

answers.A: Host the model on a SageMaker real-time endpoint in a VPC and use IoT Greengrass to pull predictions.
answers.B: Compile the model with SageMaker Neo for ARM, deploy to IoT Greengrass devices for local real-time inference.
answers.C: Package the model in a custom Docker container, deploy to AWS Lambda on ARM architecture.
answers.D: Use a SageMaker serverless endpoint and cache responses on edge devices.

explanation: SageMaker Neo produces highly optimized ARM binaries for local (<100ms) inference. IoT Greengrass ensures offline capability.

stem: An e-commerce application has a recommendation model that sees large traffic spikes during flash sales. It runs in a private VPC, uses GPU instances, and needs multi-model hosting with auto-scaling. Which architecture is optimal?

answers.A: Deploy separate single-model SageMaker real-time endpoints per model with target-tracking scaling.
answers.B: Use a SageMaker serverless endpoint with model registry versioning.
answers.C: Containerize models and host on ECS Fargate behind an ALB with custom scaling scripts.
answers.D: Use a multi-model SageMaker real-time endpoint in the VPC with provisioned concurrency and auto-scaling policies.

explanation: Multi-model endpoint reduces overhead, shares GPU, and auto-scaling in VPC meets spikes.

stem: A research team needs to batch-process 10 TB of genomic data weekly. They want to minimize cost, use the same container as real-time inference, and avoid idle pods. Which infra is best?

answers.A: Create a SageMaker asynchronous endpoint with batch transform inside it.
answers.B: Deploy models on EKS pods with KNative autoscaling.
answers.C: Use SageMaker batch transform jobs with the real-time container and spot instances.
answers.D: Host on a long-running ECS Fargate service and schedule container tasks.

explanation: Batch transform jobs spin up only for jobs, reuse container, support spot to reduce cost.

stem: A global SaaS company requires GDPR compliance. Their NLP model must serve EU-only traffic in dedicated subnets and scale on demand. Which deployment solution is most appropriate?

answers.A: Deploy regional SageMaker real-time endpoints in EU-based subnets with endpoint auto scaling.
answers.B: Deploy a single SageMaker serverless endpoint and enforce subnet restrictions.
answers.C: Host on ECS Fargate in one EU cluster and route all traffic through it.
answers.D: Use Lambda functions behind API Gateway with VPC peering to subnets.

explanation: Regional real-time endpoints in EU subnets ensure data residency and scalable performance.

stem: A startup needs to test a new fraud-detection model in production without risking customer impact. They want to route 5% of traffic to the new model, track performance, and easily roll back. Which deployment strategy and infra should they use?

answers.A: Deploy two SageMaker asynchronous endpoints and split payloads manually.
answers.B: Use a SageMaker serverless endpoint for the new model and shift DNS entries.
answers.C: Deploy the new model to a SageMaker real-time endpoint variant in the same endpoint, configure a canary traffic shift.
answers.D: Host the new model in ECS Fargate and use Application Load Balancer weighted routing.

explanation: Real-time endpoint variants support canary deployments and easy rollback within the same endpoint.

stem: An advertising platform has multiple small models (<100MB) that share similar preprocessing code. They need to deploy 50 models, optimize resource utilization, and minimize cost. What is the best approach?

answers.A: Deploy 50 separate real-time SageMaker endpoints.
answers.B: Use ECS Fargate and spin up a container per model.
answers.C: Bundle all models into one Docker image and host on a single serverless endpoint.
answers.D: Use a SageMaker multi-model endpoint with shared container in a single VPC endpoint.

explanation: Multi-model endpoints share the container and infra, reducing cost and overhead for many small models.

stem: A biotech firm must run long-running inference jobs (up to 30 minutes each) that process large data packages. They want predictable scaling and pay-per-use cost. Which SageMaker deployment fits best?

answers.A: Configure a SageMaker asynchronous inference endpoint with appropriate max payload size.
answers.B: Use a SageMaker real-time endpoint and extend Lambda timeouts.
answers.C: Submit each job as a batch transform.
answers.D: Host it on ECS Fargate with long-running tasks.

explanation: Asynchronous endpoints handle long payloads, non-blocking, scale predictably and charge per call.

stem: A media company needs GPU acceleration for video-related inference but wants to minimize idle GPU costs during off-hours. They can tolerate 1–2 second cold start. Which infra is optimal?

answers.A: Keep a provisioned GPU SageMaker real-time endpoint running with auto-scaling.
answers.B: Use SageMaker serverless endpoints configured with GPU support.
answers.C: Deploy on ECS Fargate GPU instances with manual scaling schedules.
answers.D: Host on Lambda GPU functions behind an ALB.

explanation: Serverless endpoints with GPU avoid idle costs and manage cold starts within tolerance.

stem: An auto manufacturer needs to deploy multiple model versions concurrently for A/B tests, with equal traffic share and easy rollback. They must run in the same VPC. Which infra supports this?

answers.A: Deploy separate ECS services per version behind an ALB.
answers.B: Use Lambda versions and aliases in VPC.
answers.C: Deploy separate SageMaker serverless endpoints per version.
answers.D: Use a SageMaker real-time endpoint with two production variants and traffic weights.

explanation: Production variants in one real-time endpoint allow weighted traffic splitting and quick rollback.

stem: A retailer needs to deploy a recommendation model to handle unpredictable holiday season traffic. They need <50ms latency, GPU inference, and minimal ops overhead. Which solution is best?

answers.A: Use SageMaker serverless endpoints with GPU acceleration and auto-scaling.
answers.B: Deploy a spot-based ECS GPU cluster with custom autoscaler.
answers.C: Maintain a provisioned GPU real-time endpoint with scheduled scaling.
answers.D: Run inference in Lambda with EFS-mounted model files.

explanation: Serverless GPU endpoints auto-scale without manual capacity management and meet latency.

stem: A healthcare application requires batch scoring of PHI data with encryption at rest and in transit. They want to reuse existing VPC resources and avoid cross-account data movement. Best infra?

answers.A: SageMaker serverless endpoint in VPC with data capture.
answers.B: Real-time endpoint in VPC with KMS encryption.
answers.C: Batch transform jobs configured in the same VPC and encrypted S3.
answers.D: ECS Fargate with EFS encryption.

explanation: Batch transform in VPC uses S3 encrypted data, no constant endpoint and reuse VPC security.

stem: A gaming company needs to deploy a scoring model to hundreds of edge kiosks with no always-on internet and limited compute. They need occasional connectivity to sync metrics. Which infra fits?

answers.A: Use a SageMaker real-time endpoint through AWS IoT Core.
answers.B: Compile via SageMaker Neo, deploy to Lambda@Edge on Greengrass devices.
answers.C: Host containerized model on small EC2 instances at each kiosk.
answers.D: Deploy inference code as AWS Lambda functions invoked by MQTT.

explanation: Neo-compiled model on Greengrass devices runs locally, syncs periodically over IoT Core.

stem: A logistics company has a micro-batch inference requirement: group deliveries into sets of 100 and process every 5 minutes. They want minimal latency overhead and no idle endpoints. What infrastructure should they choose?

answers.A: Deploy a real-time endpoint and buffer requests into batches.
answers.B: Use serverless endpoint with batched invocation.
answers.C: Submit jobs to ECS Fargate tasks scheduled every 5 minutes.
answers.D: Configure a SageMaker asynchronous inference endpoint with batching config.

explanation: Asynchronous endpoint supports batching and scheduled triggers without idle infra.

stem: A startup wants to experiment with GPU- and CPU-based inference to compare cost-performance trade-offs. They need a common orchestration tool and seamless model promotion. Which approach is best?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Pipelines to deploy the same model to GPU and CPU real-time endpoints.
answers.B: Script deployments in Terraform to provision ECS GPU and CPU clusters.
answers.C: Use AWS Batch for GPU and Lambda for CPU inference.
answers.D: Manually launch EC2 GPU and CPU instances and copy containers.

explanation: SageMaker Pipelines automates deployment steps, tracks versions, and supports multiple compute targets.

stem: A financial modeling team needs to deploy Python-based models that require custom system libraries. They want minimal management and autoscaling. Which deployment target is most appropriate?

answers.A: Deploy as a SageMaker serverless endpoint with layers.
answers.B: Use Lambda with custom runtime layer.
answers.C: Build a custom Docker container and host on SageMaker real-time endpoint in VPC.
answers.D: Use ECS Fargate with code-build pipelines.

explanation: Custom container on SageMaker real-time endpoint supports all dependencies, auto-scales, VPC support.

stem: A data science team wants to automate their ML workflow so that any code commit on the ‘develop’ branch runs unit tests, data validation, and triggers a SageMaker training pipeline. After successful training, the model should be registered and automatically deployed to a staging endpoint for integration tests, before manual approval pushes to production. Which CI/CD design best meets these requirements?

answers.A: Use CodePipeline with a Source action on GitHub ‘develop’, CodeBuild to run unit tests and data validation scripts, a CodeBuild action to invoke a SageMaker Pipeline for training, a stage to register the model in the Model Registry, a CloudFormation action to deploy to staging, an integration-test CodeBuild action, followed by a manual approval and a Lambda action to swap the staging endpoint to production.
answers.B: Use SageMaker Pipelines with Git integration triggering on ‘develop’ for training and registration, then use a separate CodePipeline triggered by new Model Registry entries to deploy to staging and run integration tests, with manual approval for production.
answers.C: Use CodePipeline with a GitHub source on ‘develop’, a CodeBuild stage to run unit tests and data quality checks, a SageMaker Pipeline action to train and register the model, a CloudFormation stage to deploy to a staging endpoint, a CodeBuild integration-test stage, then a manual approval stage and a CloudFormation canary-deployment stage for production.
answers.D: Use CodeDeploy directly to push code changes to SageMaker endpoints, adding a CodeDeploy pre-deployment hook to run tests and trigger training before deployment.

explanation: Option C uses CodePipeline native actions for each stage, integrates SageMaker Pipelines, staging, tests, manual approval, and a canary production deployment with minimal glue code.

stem: A compliance policy requires monthly retraining of an ML model using new data uploaded to s3://company/data/monthly/ at 1 AM on the first of each month. The workflow must run data quality checks, trigger SageMaker model training, register the model, and send an email if any stage fails. How should you configure this with minimal overhead?

answers.A: Create an EventBridge scheduled rule that invokes a Lambda function which runs data quality checks, starts a SageMaker training job, registers the model, and publishes to SNS on failure.
answers.B: Create an EventBridge scheduled rule to start a CodePipeline at 1 AM monthly. In CodePipeline, add: a Source stage (S3 polling), a CodeBuild stage for data quality checks, a SageMaker Pipeline invoke stage for training and registration, and a CloudWatch Events action to notify via SNS on failure.
answers.C: Use SageMaker Pipelines with a Schedule trigger for monthly runs, include DataQualityCheck, Train, Register steps, and configure an SNS Alarm for failed steps.
answers.D: Use AWS Batch scheduled on EventBridge to run a container that executes the entire workflow and sends SNS notifications.

explanation: Option B leverages EventBridge→CodePipeline schedule, built-in actions (S3 source, CodeBuild, SageMaker Pipeline, SNS) with minimal custom code.

stem: An organization maintains separate dev and prod AWS accounts. They want a centralized CI/CD in dev that, upon merging to master in CodeCommit, triggers a deployment pipeline in prod account to update the SageMaker endpoint. How should they configure this cross-account pipeline?

answers.A: In dev account create a CodePipeline with a CloudFormation action targeting prod account using StackSets.
answers.B: Push artifacts from dev S3 bucket to prod S3 bucket, then have a prod pipeline polling that bucket to start deployment.
answers.C: Use AWS CodeDeploy cross-account deployments from dev to prod.
answers.D: In dev CodePipeline, add an IAM role action with a role ARN in prod account. Grant the dev pipeline role permission in prod to assume that role. In prod, that role’s trust policy allows the dev pipeline service role to assume it and run deployment actions.

explanation: Option D correctly uses IAM role assumption to allow a pipeline in one account to execute actions in another account without custom polling.

stem: A team follows Gitflow: feature/* branches, develop, release/*, and master. They want two pipelines: one for develop that runs tests and staging deployments on merges to develop, and one for production on merges to master. How should they filter source triggers in CodePipeline?

answers.A: Use two CodePipelines with GitHub source actions configured: one with branch filter pattern '^refs/heads/develop$' and webhooks enabled, the other with '^refs/heads/master$'.
answers.B: Use a single pipeline triggered on all branches; in the first stage inspect the branch name and abort if not develop or master.
answers.C: Use CloudWatch Events on push events with wildcard branch patterns to start pipelines via Lambda.
answers.D: Configure CodePipeline to poll S3 artifacts tagged with branch names to distinguish branches.

explanation: Option A uses CodePipeline’s built-in branch filters in source actions to isolate triggers per pipeline.

stem: A data engineering pipeline produces a delta file in S3 upon completion. You must ensure that your ML CI/CD pipeline ingests this file, validates schema against a baseline, and fails if mismatched, before triggering training. How do you integrate this into CodePipeline?

answers.A: Have CodePipeline poll the S3 prefix for the delta file and pass it to a Lambda that does schema validation and returns success/fail.
answers.B: Trigger CodePipeline with an S3 event notification directly to the pipeline’s StartPipelineExecution API.
answers.C: Use an EventBridge rule matching the S3 PutObject event to call StartPipelineExecution, then in CodePipeline add a CodeBuild stage that runs a schema-validation script against the new file and fails on mismatch.
answers.D: Use Lambda to copy the file to a Kinesis stream, use a CodePipeline source action on the stream, and a CodeBuild validation stage.

explanation: Option C uses EventBridge→CodePipeline to start on S3 writes and uses CodeBuild to validate schema, failing if mismatched.

stem: Your ML pipeline requires a secret API key available to training jobs at build time. You must not expose the secret in plain text or logs. Which CodePipeline stage configuration meets this requirement?

answers.A: Store the API key in S3 encrypted with KMS. In CodeBuild, download and decrypt it inside the build script.
answers.B: Store the API key in AWS Secrets Manager. In the CodeBuild project definition, set an environment variable that references the Secrets Manager ARN and enable 'Reveal secrets in build logs' to false.
answers.C: Hard-code the secret in an encrypted parameter in Systems Manager Parameter Store and pull it during the build.
answers.D: Pass the secret as a plaintext environment variable in the CodePipeline action configuration, relying on IAM to protect it.

explanation: Option B uses Secrets Manager with environment variables in CodeBuild, ensuring secrets aren’t logged.

stem: A reloadable data pipeline updates feature data daily. You want to trigger model retraining automatically whenever a new featureset lands in the SageMaker Feature Store. What’s the least‐maintenance way to integrate this into your CI/CD pipeline?

answers.A: Modify your daily ETL job to call the CodePipeline StartPipelineExecution API at its end.
answers.B: Use S3 event notifications on the Feature Store underlying S3 bucket to trigger a Lambda that starts the pipeline.
answers.C: Add a CloudWatch alarm on Feature Store PutRecord metrics and have it trigger pipeline via SNS.
answers.D: Create an EventBridge rule matching the SageMaker Feature Store PutRecord API via CloudTrail, target StartPipelineExecution for your training pipeline.

explanation: Option D leverages CloudTrail events in EventBridge to detect new records and start the pipeline with zero custom code in the ETL job.

stem: You need to implement a canary deployment for a real-time SageMaker endpoint in your pipeline. It must shift 5% traffic to the new model initially, then 50%, then 100%, with automatic rollback on errors. Which combination of actions do you use in CodePipeline?

answers.A: Use CloudFormation deploy action with TYPE=BLUE_GREEN and trafficRoutingConfig CanaryInterval (5%) and CanaryInterval (50%), and a CloudWatch alarm action to auto-rollback.
answers.B: Use CodeDeploy with application type 'AWS Lambda' against the SageMaker endpoint and set canaryDeploymentConfig.
answers.C: Invoke a Lambda function in each stage to call UpdateEndpointWeightsAndCapacities on the endpoint.
answers.D: Use a custom CodeBuild action to call the SageMaker API to shift traffic and monitor latency; if latency rises, call rollback API.

explanation: Option A uses CloudFormation blue/green with canary traffic routing and automatic rollback via alarms, requiring no custom code.

stem: A governance requirement mandates that any pipeline change must be peer-reviewed before execution. You want to enforce code reviews for the buildspec.yaml and pipeline definition in CDK. What CI/CD pattern accomplishes this?

answers.A: Allow developers to commit directly to main; have a pre-build hook that runs only if PR label 'reviewed' exists.
answers.B: Store CDK pipeline code and buildspec in a feature branch, require PR approval in CodeCommit/GitHub, merge only after two approvers, then trigger pipeline on merge to main.
answers.C: Use CodeBuild PreBuild commands to validate a 'reviewed-by' tag in Git metadata before proceeding.
answers.D: Configure a manual approval action at the start of every pipeline run to verify that PRs were reviewed externally.

explanation: Option B leverages standard Git-based code-review gating before code merges and pipeline triggers.

stem: Your pipeline runs SageMaker training jobs in parallel for hyperparameter tuning. Sometimes runs collide and exceed resource quotas, causing failures. How do you prevent concurrent training executions?

answers.A: Limit the maximum concurrent CodeBuild builds in the project settings to 1.
answers.B: Use a Lambda in your pipeline to list current SageMaker jobs and fail fast if any RUNNING jobs exist.
answers.C: Configure the CodePipeline stage for training to use an ActionConfiguration including a custom concurrency token in your state machine so that only one execution at a time proceeds.
answers.D: Set the SageMaker training action’s maximum concurrency to 1 in the pipeline definition.

explanation: Option C uses a concurrency token to serialize that action’s invocations; CodePipeline supports concurrencyToken to prevent parallel runs.

stem: You want to include a data-skew check using SageMaker Clarify in your CI/CD before training. Which pipeline stage sequence and actions accomplish this without custom containers?

answers.A: After unit tests, add a CodeBuild stage that invokes SageMaker Clarify ProcessingStep via AWS CLI, passing baseline and new dataset; fail build on detected skew.
answers.B: Add a custom Docker build to run a Python script that calls Clarify SDK inside CodeBuild.
answers.C: Trigger SageMaker Pipelines containing a ClarifyBaselineStep; ingest results via SNS into CodePipeline.
answers.D: Use Lambda action in CodePipeline to call Clarify’s API and post results to S3, then have pipeline poll for results.

explanation: Option A uses CodeBuild with the AWS CLI to call SageMaker Clarify ProcessingJob, avoiding custom Docker images.

stem: Your pipeline must run unit tests, then integration tests against a temporary SageMaker endpoint after deployment, and delete the endpoint automatically when tests complete or fail. What do you add?

answers.A: A CodeDeploy preTraffic hook to run tests and a postRollback hook to delete the endpoint.
answers.B: A Lambda in CodePipeline to run tests and then call DeleteEndpoint.
answers.C: A CodeBuild test stage that spins up the endpoint, tests, then calls DeleteEndpoint in the same build.
answers.D: Two CodeBuild actions: one for integration tests against the staging endpoint, then one that deletes the endpoint by calling AWS CLI delete-endpoint; add them sequentially and configure failureAction=Abort.

explanation: Option D cleanly separates testing and teardown in CodeBuild stages, ensuring teardown always runs after tests if preceding stages succeed.

stem: A developer accidentally pushed sensitive data to a feature branch. You need to prevent that branch from ever triggering your CI/CD pipeline. How do you modify your pipeline’s source action?

answers.A: Add a whitelist of allowed branch patterns in the buildspec to abort on unallowed patterns.
answers.B: Configure the GitHub source action to include an exclude filter 'refs/heads/feature/sensitive*'.
answers.C: Use a Lambda in the source stage to inspect commits and abort if the file pattern matches.
answers.D: Add a pre-build CodeBuild action that checks commit history for sensitive files.

explanation: Option B uses the source action’s exclude filter to prevent specific branch patterns from triggering the pipeline.

stem: Your ML pipeline needs to use Spot Instances for cost-saving on training. How do you enable this in your CodePipeline/SageMaker training integration?

answers.A: In the SageMaker Pipeline definition YAML, set ResourceConfig.AuxiliarySpotCapacity to the desired percentage and invoke via CodePipeline’s SageMakerPipelineAction.
answers.B: Add a CodeBuild stage that runs 'aws sagemaker create-training-job' CLI with --use-spot-instances flag.
answers.C: Wrap training in a Lambda function configured with capacityType=SPOT and call it from CodePipeline.
answers.D: Switch the CodePipeline action type to AWS Batch and configure Spot in the ComputeEnvironment.

explanation: Option A leverages SageMaker Pipelines spot training support via ResourceConfig and CodePipeline’s SageMakerPipelineAction without custom code.

stem: You need to trigger your CI/CD pipeline whenever a pull request is opened or updated, and only for PRs targeting develop. How is this configured?

answers.A: Configure CodePipeline Source with GitHub webhook on all PR events and in the build stage inspect the target branch.
answers.B: Use EventBridge rule for GitHub PullRequest events filtering on repository name.
answers.C: Enable GitHub Pull Request webhooks in the source action and set the targetReference filter to 'refs/heads/develop'.
answers.D: Use a Lambda subscriber to GitHub webhooks to call StartPipelineExecution when PR target is develop.

explanation: Option C uses the source action’s webhook pull request event support with targetReference filters to limit triggers to PRs against develop.

stem: Your staging endpoint runs expensive benchmarks as part of integration tests. To avoid excessive cost, you only want to run tests when changes affect inference code. How do you optimize your pipeline?

answers.A: Cache build artifacts between runs to speed up deployment.
answers.B: Use a manual approval before integration tests.
answers.C: Use a Lambda pre-check in CodePipeline to compare diff of inference directory and skip tests stage if no changes.
answers.D: Split your repository: place inference code in its own folder and configure two pipelines—one that triggers full workflow on inference folder changes (using source filters) and one for other changes.

explanation: Option D uses separate pipelines with source filtering to avoid running expensive tests when unrelated code changes.

stem: Your pipeline fails intermittently at the SageMaker Pipeline invocation stage due to transient throttling errors. How do you make the pipeline more resilient?

answers.A: Wrap the SageMakerPipelineAction in a CodeBuild action with a retry loop using exponential backoff on throttling errors.
answers.B: Increase the service quota for StartPipelineExecution calls.
answers.C: Add a manual retry approval stage after the failure.
answers.D: Use a Lambda-based custom action that catches throttles and auto-retries once.

explanation: Option A uses a CodeBuild wrapper to implement retries with backoff, improving resilience without manual intervention.

stem: You want your CI/CD pipeline to automatically rollback to the last known good model if performance metrics degrade after deployment. How can you implement this in CodePipeline?

answers.A: Include a manual approval stage that runs a performance test, and if it fails, manually invoke rollback.
answers.B: Use a Lambda in the post-deploy stage to run a test; if metrics below threshold, call UpdateEndpoint to the previous variant.
answers.C: Use a CloudWatch alarm on performance metrics to trigger a CodePipeline retrigger of the deploy stage with the previous model via CodeDeploy automatic rollback.
answers.D: Publish the previous model as an alias in Model Registry and switch alias in a Lambda action on failure.

explanation: Option C ties CloudWatch alarms to CodePipeline’s deploy stage with a configured rollback in CodeDeploy, automating fallback.

stem: Your team uses GitHub Flow, pushing directly to main and using feature branches only for experiments. They want every merge to main to trigger a full pipeline. But they also use semantic version tags (e.g., v1.2.0) to denote releases. How do you ensure only tag pushes trigger production deployments?

answers.A: Configure CodePipeline source to only trigger on main branch updates.
answers.B: Use two pipelines with GitHub source actions: one listening to refs/tags/v* (for production) and another to refs/heads/main (for tests), and in the production pipeline restrict to tag pattern '^refs/tags/v[0-9]+.*$'.
answers.C: Add logic in the build stage to parse GIT_REF and only continue if it’s a tag.
answers.D: Use EventBridge pattern matching on GitHub Tag events to start the pipeline.

explanation: Option B cleanly separates pipelines by source filters: one triggers on tag pushes for production deployments.

stem: A pipeline source stage uses AWS CodeCommit. Developers occasionally force-push and rewrite history, causing source metadata mismatches. How do you make the pipeline robust against force pushes?

answers.A: Enable polling instead of webhooks in the CodeCommit source action.
answers.B: Add a pre-build stage to Git fetch --prune and reset --hard origin/branch.
answers.C: Configure the CodePipeline source action to use 'FullClone' fetch method to always get the current tip regardless of history rewrite.
answers.D: Disable code commit history rewrite in the repository settings.

explanation: Option C uses the FullClone fetch mode so the pipeline always pulls the latest commit independent of history changes.

stem: You need to integrate model explainability tests into your pipeline: after training, fail the pipeline if any feature attribution for protected classes exceeds a threshold. Which stage should you add?

answers.A: Add a CodeBuild stage that runs a SageMaker Clarify ModelExplainabilityProcessingJob via AWS CLI with the trained model, parses the results JSON, and exits non-zero if attribution drift exceeds the threshold.
answers.B: Invoke a Lambda function in a pipeline action that calls Clarify SDK and uses CloudWatch metrics to decide pass/fail.
answers.C: Embed the Clarify step inside the SageMaker Pipeline and then have CodePipeline poll for model registry tags to decide.
answers.D: Use a CloudFormation custom resource to run the Clarify job and roll back the stack on failure.

explanation: Option A uses CodeBuild to orchestrate Clarify explainability checks, parse results, and enforce pipeline success/failure cleanly.

stem: A pipeline stage builds and pushes a Docker image to ECR, then a SageMaker training action uses that image. Occasionally, the training job starts before the image is available, causing errors. How do you prevent this race condition?

answers.A: Add a fixed sleep delay in the training action’s custom script.
answers.B: Use an EventBridge rule on ECR image-push to trigger the pipeline second stage.
answers.C: Configure CodeBuild to push to a different tag and have training wait on tag propagation.
answers.D: Split the build-and-push into one CodeBuild stage that outputs the image URI as an artifact, and configure the next SageMakerPipelineAction to consume that artifact, which enforces sequencing.

explanation: Option D uses CodePipeline artifact dependency to guarantee that the training stage does not start until the image has been successfully pushed and the URI passed along.

stem: Your pipeline’s CodeBuild unit-test stage frequently downloads the entire repository, slowing builds. How do you optimize clone behavior?

answers.A: Configure the GitHub source action to use 'ShallowClone' with a depth of 1, and enable CodeBuild’s source cache for the repo.
answers.B: Use Git LFS to store large binaries outside the repo.
answers.C: Split the repo into micro-repos each with its own pipeline.
answers.D: Switch the source action to S3 and upload only changed files manually.

explanation: Option A combines shallow cloning at the source action with CodeBuild caching to speed up fetch time without repo restructuring.

stem: A CI/CD pipeline should only deploy models when both unit tests and integration tests pass. However, you need integration tests to run against a live endpoint, which itself requires deployment. How do you model this in CodePipeline?

answers.A: Run both unit and integration tests in the same CodeBuild action after deployment.
answers.B: Chain two separate pipelines: one for tests, one for deployment, and only call the deploy pipeline if tests pass.
answers.C: In a single pipeline: Stage1 run unit tests via CodeBuild, Stage2 deploy to staging via CloudFormation, Stage3 run integration tests via CodeBuild, Stage4 manual approval and production deploy.
answers.D: Use a SageMaker Pipeline that supports validation steps natively and call it from CodePipeline.

explanation: Option C lays out a linear pipeline with distinct stages for unit tests, deployment, integration tests, and production approval.

stem: You want to notify your team in Slack whenever any pipeline stage fails, including the stage name and error message. How do you configure this?

answers.A: Attach an SNS topic to pipeline notifications and configure an AWS Chatbot integration for Slack.
answers.B: Create a CloudWatch EventBridge rule matching CodePipeline 'Stage Execution Failed' events, target a Lambda that formats the message and posts to Slack via webhook.
answers.C: In each CodePipeline stage’s onFailure hook, invoke a Lambda to post to Slack.
answers.D: Enable CloudTrail logs for CodePipeline and stream failures to Slack using Log Insights.

explanation: Option B uses a single EventBridge rule and a Lambda to capture failure events and send formatted Slack messages, minimizing per-stage configuration.

stem: An executive insists that production deployments require two separate approvers. How can you enforce this in CodePipeline?

answers.A: Add two successive ManualApproval actions in the production deployment stage, each assigned to a different user group.
answers.B: Configure the ManualApproval action with 'approvalThreshold' set to 2.
answers.C: Use IAM policies to require MFA for invoking the production stage.
answers.D: Chain two identical manual approval actions but restrict both to the same group.

explanation: Option A ensures two distinct approvals by having two manual approval actions in series, each can be assigned to different user sets.

stem: Your CodePipeline deploys a SageMaker model via CloudFormation. When the deployment fails, the pipeline remains stuck in a FAILED state and you must manually clean up. How do you configure automatic rollback of the CloudFormation stack?

answers.A: Add a CloudFormation DeleteStack action after the deploy action conditioned on failure.
answers.B: Use a Lambda in the onFailure hook to delete the stack.
answers.C: Set the CloudFormation action’s 'ActionMode' to CHANGE_SET_REPLACE and 'RollbackOnFailure' parameter to true.
answers.D: Wrap the CloudFormation deploy in an AWS Step Functions state machine with a Catch to delete the stack.

explanation: Option C leverages CloudFormation action parameters to rollback automatically, avoiding manual cleanup.

stem: You need to run parallel hyperparameter tuning and data quality steps in your pipeline to reduce total runtime. How do you implement parallel actions in CodePipeline?

answers.A: Create multiple pipelines and start them simultaneously from a Lambda.
answers.B: Use SageMaker Pipelines which natively parallelizes steps.
answers.C: Run one CodeBuild action that multiplexes both tasks in background processes.
answers.D: Define two actions within the same pipeline stage; CodePipeline will execute them in parallel, then proceed only when both succeed.

explanation: Option D uses CodePipeline’s support for parallel actions in a single stage to run tasks concurrently.

stem: An online retailer deploys a real-time inference endpoint for product recommendations. Shortly after launch, they notice that the distribution of a key categorical feature "user_region" has shifted, although model accuracy remains within SLA. Which automated monitoring solution should they implement to detect and alert on this feature distribution change with minimal custom coding?

answers.A: Configure a SageMaker Model Quality Monitor job to check for data drift on "user_region" using ground truth labels.
answers.B: Use SageMaker Model Monitor DataQuality baselining to establish constraints on "user_region" and schedule a drift detection job.
answers.C: Deploy SageMaker Clarify to compute SHAP values for "user_region" on each inference and alert when feature importance changes.
answers.D: Write an AWS Lambda that polls CloudWatch logs, computes a KS test on "user_region", and sends SNS alerts.

explanation: Model Monitor DataQuality jobs can baseline feature distributions and automatically detect drift with minimal custom code. ModelQualityMonitor requires labels; Clarify focuses on bias/importance rather than raw distribution; a Lambda solution requires more custom work.

stem: A financial institution uses a SageMaker real-time endpoint for credit scoring. They need to monitor inference latency degradation and data schema violations. Which combination of SageMaker features meets both requirements natively?

answers.A: Configure SageMaker Model Debugger to capture latency and data quality metrics.
answers.B: Use CloudWatch Contributor Insights for the endpoint to detect schema violations and latency issues.
answers.C: Enable Data Capture on the endpoint and run SageMaker Model Monitor with both DataQuality and ModelQuality checks.
answers.D: Deploy AWS X-Ray for latency tracing and AWS Glue Data Quality for schema validation.

explanation: Data Capture plus Model Monitor can track payload schema violations via DataQuality checks and latency via custom metrics. Model Debugger focuses on training/debug; Contributor Insights and Glue don’t natively integrate inference monitoring as well.

stem: A company wants to detect concept drift in predicted probabilities of a binary classifier in production in near real-time. They also want to minimize cost. Which monitoring configuration should they choose?

answers.A: Run a SageMaker Clarify ModelExplainabilityMonitor on each batch of incoming requests.
answers.B: Configure an asynchronous SageMaker endpoint with built-in data drift detection.
answers.C: Use SageMaker Model Quality Monitor with ground truth labels and a 5-minute schedule.
answers.D: Enable Data Capture on the endpoint and schedule a SageMaker Model Monitor DataQuality drift check on predicted score distribution.

explanation: Without ground truth, ModelQualityMonitor isn’t applicable. Clarify ExplainabilityMonitor focuses on SHAP. Asynchronous endpoints have no built-in drift. DataQuality drift checks on predictions detect concept drift cost effectively.

stem: An ML engineer deployed two production variants (A and B) for A/B testing. They need to monitor emerging data skew between the variants for a continuous categorical feature "device_type". Which approach best surfaces variant-specific data skew?

answers.A: Configure two separate Model Monitor DataQuality jobs, each capturing and analyzing "device_type" for its variant.
answers.B: Use a single Model Monitor DataQuality job that collects data from both variants and uses filters on "variant_name".
answers.C: Use SageMaker Clarify to detect bias between variants on "device_type".
answers.D: Aggregate CloudWatch logs across variants and run a post-processing job to compare distributions.

explanation: Separate DataQuality jobs allow per-variant baselines and alerts. A single job with filters isn't supported; Clarify is for bias interpretation, not raw skew; log aggregation is more custom work.

stem: During inference, a regression model returns NaN for target predictions intermittently. Which Model Monitor configuration will automatically detect this anomaly and notify the team?

answers.A: Enable SageMaker Model Debugger to capture NaNs during inference.
answers.B: Use Model Monitor DataQuality baseline constraints to flag NaN values in the prediction column.
answers.C: Set up Amazon CloudWatch anomaly detection on inference response logs to catch NaNs.
answers.D: Configure SageMaker Clarify to test for invalid prediction values.

explanation: DataQuality monitors can enforce no-NaN constraints on any column. Debugger focuses on training tensors; CloudWatch anomaly detection requires custom log parsing; Clarify is for bias/explainability.

stem: A language translation model hosted on SageMaker Edge Manager runs on devices with intermittent connectivity. The team needs to detect and report when local input data statistics drift significantly. Which architecture is most appropriate?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Model Monitor DataQuality jobs in the AWS cloud to poll edge logs hourly.
answers.B: Install SageMaker Debugger on devices to log input metrics to CloudWatch.
answers.C: Embed the SageMaker Edge Manager monitoring SDK on device to emit metrics to AWS IoT, then trigger a Model Monitor drift check in the cloud.
answers.D: Deploy AWS Greengrass Lambda functions to run Clarify drift checks locally.

explanation: Edge Manager SDK plus IoT ingestion allows capture of local stats; cloud Model Monitor then runs drift. Debugger isn’t for inference; Greengrass + Clarify unsupported; cloud polling logs is inefficient.

stem: An ML engineer must monitor prediction skew between two ensembles serving the same traffic for anomaly detection. They require automatic, per-minute alerts if the divergence of prediction distributions exceeds a threshold. How should they implement this?

answers.A: Enable Data Capture for both ensemble endpoints, schedule two Model Monitor drift checks on predictions with a 1-minute interval, and configure CloudWatch alarms on the job results.
answers.B: Run SageMaker Clarify on both ensembles every minute to compute PSI on prediction distributions.
answers.C: Write a custom Lambda that pulls logs from both endpoints, computes KS test, and pushes CloudWatch metrics.
answers.D: Use CloudWatch Contributor Insights to track prediction distribution per minute.

explanation: Two Data Capture + Model Monitor drift checks with CloudWatch alarms automates per-minute divergence alerts. Clarify isn’t for raw distribution drift; custom Lambda is higher overhead; Contributor Insights not suited.

stem: After deploying a multi-model SageMaker endpoint, a sudden spike in malformed JSON requests is observed. The engineer wants to monitor schema violations per model. Which solution provides the most granular alerts?

answers.A: Configure a single Model Monitor DataQuality job on the endpoint to catch all schema violations.
answers.B: Enable Data Capture and configure a separate DataQuality job per model container with JSON schema constraints.
answers.C: Use AWS WAF JSON body inspection rules to log violations to CloudWatch.
answers.D: Parse inference logs with CloudWatch Logs Insights and trigger SNS alerts.

explanation: Separate DataQuality jobs per model in the multi-model endpoint allow per-container schema checks. A single job cannot differentiate models; WAF and custom log parsing add external complexity.

stem: A streaming inference pipeline uses an asynchronous endpoint. They want to detect if more than 1% of requests take longer than 10 seconds. Which AWS-native feature combination best achieves this?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Model Monitor latency metrics with custom Python script to parse logs.
answers.B: Configure AWS X-Ray on the endpoint and set up CloudWatch alarms for trace duration.
answers.C: Enable Data Capture and schedule Model Quality Monitor to evaluate latency distribution.
answers.D: Enable Data Capture on the endpoint, configure CloudWatch metric filters for invocation duration, and set alarms for >1% above 10s.

explanation: Data Capture plus CloudWatch metric filters allow latency distribution monitoring and alarms without custom training jobs. Model Quality Monitor isn’t for latency; X-Ray traces require code hooks.

stem: A healthcare inference service must monitor PII leakage: requests and responses must contain no PHI tokens. The model returns free-form text. Which monitoring approach will detect policy violations?

answers.A: Use Model Monitor DataQuality to enforce a regex constraint rejecting PHI patterns in responses.
answers.B: Configure AWS WAF with a custom rule to block PHI regex in JSON payload.
answers.C: Enable Data Capture, run a scheduled SageMaker Clarify bias check with custom detectors for PHI tokens.
answers.D: Write a Lambda for each inference to scan for PHI and generate CloudWatch events.

explanation: Clarify allows custom text analyzers via pre-built detectors to detect sensitive tokens. DataQuality regex can catch patterns but is limited; WAF doesn’t inspect model responses; Lambda is higher overhead.

stem: A model predicts customer churn and uses 50 numeric features. They need to detect multivariate drift (covariate shift) across those features. Which monitoring setup is best?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Model Monitor DataQuality with a multilook at a multivariate drift check (using dataset_format=“JSON” with drift_check_categories).
answers.B: Configure SageMaker Clarify to compute pairwise SHAP drift metrics for all feature pairs.
answers.C: Schedule a batch transform job daily and compare covariance matrices via AWS Glue.
answers.D: Write custom Spark on EMR to compute Mahalanobis distance across features.

explanation: Model Monitor supports multivariate drift checks during DataQuality monitoring. Clarify focuses on feature importance; batch transform and custom Spark are inefficient and higher overhead.

stem: A retailer serves an image-classification model via SageMaker. They need to detect when the distribution of image size (in bytes) drifts and when inference latency spikes. Which out-of-the-box features should they enable?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Clarify DataBias monitors on image_size and SageMaker Model Debugger for latency.
answers.B: Enable Data Capture and schedule Model Monitor DataQuality jobs to track image_size distribution and custom CloudWatch latency metrics.
answers.C: Configure a Lambda pre-processor to log image_size and usage of SageMaker Profiler for latency.
answers.D: Deploy a Step Functions workflow around the endpoint to log metrics and analyze separately.

explanation: Data Capture plus Model Monitor DataQuality tracks input size drift; CloudWatch latency metrics catch spikes. Clarify and Debugger don’t cover both needs; lambda and Step Functions add complexity.

stem: An enterprise requires that no inference job runs outside their VPC and that monitoring data remains within their private subnet. How can they deploy Model Monitor under these constraints?

answers.A: Enable network isolation on Model Monitor jobs.
answers.B: Run Model Monitor on a public subnet with NAT gateway to pull data.
answers.C: Use VPC endpoints for S3 and CloudWatch and run jobs on public instances.
answers.D: Configure Model Monitor Processing Job with VPC configuration in private subnets and use VPC S3 endpoints.

explanation: Model Monitor jobs run as SageMaker Processing Jobs and support VPC config. Private subnets plus S3 VPC endpoints ensure data stays in VPC. Network isolation is for training/inference only.

stem: A financial model returns probability scores. The team needs to detect if the median score changes by more than 5% compared to baseline daily. Which feature and configuration accomplish this?

answers.A: Use Model Monitor DataQuality drift check on the prediction field with a median tolerance constraint of ±5%.
answers.B: Schedule a Clarify ModelBiasMonitor job to compute median changes.
answers.C: Extract daily predictions to Athena and run SQL analytics to compare medians.
answers.D: Enable CloudWatch percentile-based alarms on the endpoint’s inference metric.

explanation: DataQuality drift constraints support median checks on numeric fields. Clarify bias monitors aren’t for central tendency; Athena SQL is custom; CloudWatch latency alarms only handle infrastructure metrics.

stem: To comply with regulations, a bank must audit all inference inputs and outputs and ensure they cannot be modified post-hoc. Which combination of services and features meets this requirement?

answers.A: Enable Data Capture to write logs to an encrypted S3 bucket and use ACLs for write-once.
answers.B: Use Data Capture to store inputs/outputs in an S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode and encryption by KMS.
answers.C: Configure CloudTrail to log inference API calls and point logs to S3 with versioning.
answers.D: Use Athena for logging inputs/outputs and store results in a write-only DynamoDB table.

explanation: Data Capture plus S3 Object Lock (Compliance) and KMS encryption provides immutable audit trail. CloudTrail logs API calls but not payloads; ACLs alone don’t enforce write-once.

stem: A data scientist wants to spot-time batch inference data quality issues such as missing values and invalid formats before consuming results. Which approach should they apply?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Clarify to compute bias metrics on batch responses.
answers.B: Schedule a CloudWatch Logs Insights query on batch transform logs.
answers.C: Run a SageMaker Processing job with Model Monitor DataQuality checks on batch output.
answers.D: Validate outputs manually in Jupyter notebooks after batch jobs complete.
