explanation: Model Monitor Processing jobs can validate batch outputs via DataQuality checks. Clarify is for bias; Logs Insights doesn’t parse output payload; manual validation lacks automation.

stem: An autonomous driving model processes high-frequence sensor data. They need to detect when any input channel has degraded signal quality (e.g., constant zeros) in real time. Which solution best addresses this?

answers.A: Use Model Debugger to capture input tensor anomalies.
answers.B: Set up CloudWatch metric filters on inference logs to detect zero-value readings.
answers.C: Implement an AWS IoT rule to check sensor message contents for zeros.
answers.D: Enable Data Capture on the endpoint, schedule a Model Monitor DataQuality job with custom tolerances for each channel.

explanation: Data Capture and DataQuality allow custom numeric constraints per feature. Debugger isn’t for inference; CloudWatch requires custom parsing; IoT rules don’t integrate inference model context.

stem: A model returns a confidence score as a float between 0 and 1. The team must ensure no inference returns a score outside this range. Which monitoring configuration should they use?

answers.A: Write a custom CloudWatch metric filter on response logs to detect invalid scores.
answers.B: Use Model Monitor DataQuality constraints to flag scores <0 or >1.
answers.C: Apply SageMaker Clarify to validate output distributions within range.
answers.D: Include assertion logic in the inference container to throw errors on invalid values.

explanation: DataQuality constraints can enforce numeric ranges on columns. Clarify doesn’t enforce hard constraints; custom filter or container logic increases maintenance.

stem: A marketing model predicts click-through probability and requires monitoring of high skew in the "campaign_id" feature usage. Which Service Lens should they use in Model Monitor to inspect this categorical feature?

answers.A: Use the Categorical Lens in SageMaker Model Monitor DataQuality to monitor "campaign_id".
answers.B: Use the Label Lens in SageMaker Clarify to monitor campaign labeling.
answers.C: Use the Numeric Lens in Model Monitor to inspect category counts.
answers.D: Use the Bias Lens in Clarify to track category fairness.

explanation: The Categorical Lens in Model Monitor DataQuality jobs specializes in tracking categorical feature distribution. Numeric Lens monitors only numeric features; Clarify lenses focus on bias/explainability.

stem: An engineering team notices that model inference failures often coincide with sudden changes in request payload size. They want to correlate error rate with payload size anomalies. Which approach is simplest?

answers.A: Upload logs to CloudWatch Logs and manually correlate with payload sizes stored in S3.
answers.B: Instrument the container to push custom CloudWatch metrics for payload size and errors.
answers.C: Enable Data Capture with custom JSONPath for payload_size and error_code, then run Model Monitor DataQuality job with both fields.
answers.D: Use AWS X-Ray annotations to trace payload size and exceptions.

explanation: Data Capture with custom JSONPath can extract both payload_size and error_code; DataQuality jobs can detect anomalies and correlations. Container instrumentation or X-Ray require more custom code.

stem: A translation service uses a multi-model endpoint. They need to monitor latency at the container level for each model separately. What’s the most direct AWS-native way?

answers.A: Configure Model Monitor on the endpoint to track per-model latency.
answers.B: Enable per-model invocation logging with Data Capture and use CloudWatch metric filters to calculate latency.
answers.C: Deploy a CloudWatch Agent on the endpoint hosts to capture container metrics.
answers.D: Use SageMaker Debugger profiling on inference containers.

explanation: Data Capture logs invocation metadata per model; CloudWatch logs filters can compute latency per container. Model Monitor and Debugger don’t provide per-container latency; CloudWatch Agent isn’t supported on managed endpoints.

stem: A company must detect malicious adversarial inputs that cause anomalous model outputs. They define an acceptable range for each output. Which monitoring solution enforces this at scale?

answers.A: Model Monitor DataQuality constraints on the output columns with defined min/max thresholds.
answers.B: Deploy a WAF rule inspecting response bodies against known attack signatures.
answers.C: Use Clarify Explainability to detect adversarial perturbations.
answers.D: Stream inference logs to Lambda for custom anomaly detection.

explanation: DataQuality constraint checks on output enforce numeric ranges and can scale. WAF and Clarify aren’t designed for content-based validation; Lambda adds overhead.

stem: An endpoint serves an NLP model that occasionally returns excessively long generated text (>1000 tokens). They want real-time alerts when this happens. Which setup is most efficient?

answers.A: Use Model Monitor to check response length length via DataQuality.
answers.B: Run Clarify to measure token counts and alert.
answers.C: Enable CloudWatch RUM to capture response sizes.
answers.D: Configure Data Capture to extract response_text, set a DataQuality constraint for max token count, and schedule frequent jobs.

explanation: Data Capture plus DataQuality constraint handles response length checks. Clarify and RUM unsuited; CloudWatch RUM is for front-end metrics.

stem: A pharmaceutical company must catch silent inference failures where the model returns a default value of 0. They want automated detection. Which AWS feature configuration accomplishes this?

answers.A: Configure SageMaker Debugger to flag constant zero outputs.
answers.B: Use Model Monitor DataQuality constraints to detect when output equals 0 more than a threshold.
answers.C: Enable CloudWatch metric filters on logs for zero values and alert.
answers.D: Instrument the model container to throw errors on zeros.

explanation: DataQuality constraints detect when a column value matches an anomaly pattern. Debugger is for training; logs filtering is custom; container instrumentation has higher overhead.

stem: To monitor inference drift for streaming predictions without ground truth, which monitor type and category should they choose?

answers.A: ModelQualityMonitor with concept drift category.
answers.B: Clarify ModelBiasMonitor on predictions.
answers.C: Model Monitor DataQuality with drift_check_categories set to "data" on the prediction field.
answers.D: Clarify ModelExplainabilityMonitor for prediction distribution.

explanation: DataQuality monitors support drift_check_categories on arbitrary fields. ModelQualityMonitor requires labels. Clarify focuses on bias/explainability.

stem: A company needs to ensure that feature engineering code doesn’t introduce new features unseen during training. They want to monitor for any new column names in inference payloads. What’s the best strategy?

answers.A: Use Model Monitor DataQuality with input schema constraints listing allowed column names.
answers.B: Implement a Lambda authorizer on API Gateway to validate JSON keys.
answers.C: Enable SageMaker Clarify DatasetDriftMonitor on input keys.
answers.D: Use AWS Config rules on the SageMaker endpoint inference setting.

explanation: DataQuality constraints can enforce allowed input schema. Lambda authorizer works but is outside SageMaker; Clarify and Config aren’t for schema enforcement.

stem: An ML engineer observes that the distribution of a numerical feature is bimodal in training but has become unimodal in production. They must detect this change automatically. Which Model Monitor configuration handles multimodal distribution drift?

answers.A: Use Clarify ModelBiasMonitor to detect distribution shape changes.
answers.B: Schedule a batch transform and post-process histograms in Athena.
answers.C: Use CloudWatch anomaly detection on the feature metric.
answers.D: Configure Model Monitor DataQuality with DistributionLens on the feature and enable drift checks.

explanation: DistributionLens in DataQuality monitors supports multiple bins for drift detection. Clarify bias monitors don’t assess raw distribution shape; Athena/CloudWatch require custom coding.

stem: A subscription service uses asynchronous batch endpoints. They need to monitor end-to-end inference job failures and durations. How can they instrument this without modifying model code?

answers.A: Use Model Monitor DataQuality to track batch job status and duration.
answers.B: Configure Clarify to track job failures.
answers.C: Configure CloudWatch Events on SageMaker BatchTransform job state change and subscribe to SNS.
answers.D: Deploy GuardDuty to detect anomalies in batch failures.

explanation: CloudWatch Events for job state and duration require no code changes. Model Monitor doesn’t monitor batch job lifecycle; Clarify doesn’t cover jobs; GuardDuty is for security threats.

stem: An experiment uses shadow deployments: incoming traffic is mirrored to a new model. They want to compare output distributions in near real time and alert if divergence >2%. Which design is simplest?

answers.A: Deploy two DataQuality jobs separately and post-process alerts via Lambda.
answers.B: Enable Data Capture on both endpoints, schedule a single DriftsCheck Job that references both datasets as baseline and target.
answers.C: Use Clarify to compute PSI between baseline and candidate in near real time.
answers.D: Implement a Step Functions workflow to fetch logs and compare distributions.

explanation: A single DriftCheck job can accept two datasets as baseline and target. DataQuality jobs per endpoint or Step Functions add complexity; Clarify mismatched purpose.

stem: A biotech startup requires monitoring of model feature importance drift in production. They want to detect if SHAP importance of any feature changes by >10%. Which AWS feature combination achieves this?

answers.A: Use Model Monitor DataQuality drift_check on SHAP values.
answers.B: Schedule a Model Quality Monitor job with SHAP-based metrics.
answers.C: Configure Clarify ModelBiasMonitor with feature_importance thresholds.
answers.D: Enable SageMaker Clarify ModelExplainabilityMonitor on the endpoint with max_absolute_shap_change constraint.

explanation: Clarify’s ModelExplainabilityMonitor captures SHAP importance drift and supports constraints. DataQuality and ModelQualityMonitoring don’t handle SHAP; ModelBiasMonitor focuses on bias not drift.

stem: A team must implement an alert if any inference job experiences input payload with more than 50 unique categorical feature values. Which approach scales best?

answers.A: Use AWS Config custom rules to inspect payloads.
answers.B: Deploy WAF rate-limit rules on JSON body parser.
answers.C: Enable Data Capture and configure a Model Monitor DataQuality custom constraint on cardinality >50.
answers.D: Run Athena queries on S3 logs and send alerts via Lambda.

explanation: DataQuality custom cardinality constraints enforce unique value limits. AWS Config and WAF don’t inspect inference payloads; Athena+Lambda is higher latency.

stem: A model is deprecated but still receives stale requests. The team wants to detect any inference calls to the old endpoint and retire it promptly. Which CloudWatch configuration helps?

answers.A: Set up a CloudWatch metric filter on SageMakerAPI logs for InvokeEndpointOldModel API and alert.
answers.B: Use Model Monitor to detect zero-inference values.
answers.C: Configure a Custom Resource in CloudFormation to log invocations.
answers.D: Enable SageMaker Clarify to flag calls to old endpoint.

explanation: CloudWatch metric filters on API logs for specific endpoint names detect calls. Model Monitor and Clarify aren’t for endpoint invocation detection; custom resource is unnecessary.

stem: A gaming app uses an ML endpoint that must maintain 95th percentile latency under 200ms. They need to alert if the SLA is broken. Which AWS native setup is recommended?

answers.A: Run Model Monitor with a latency constraint on the endpoint logs.
answers.B: Use CloudWatch percentile-based alarms on the AWS/SageMaker metric InferenceLatency.
answers.C: Deploy SageMaker Debugger to capture latency tensors.
answers.D: Implement a Lambda to sample requests and measure SLA.

explanation: CloudWatch percentile-based alarms directly monitor InferenceLatency p95. Model Monitor isn’t designed for latency; Debugger and Lambda require extra work.

stem: An e-commerce company uses a SageMaker real-time endpoint for TensorFlow models with a strict p95 latency SLA. During peak traffic hours, end-to-end latency spikes intermittently even though CPU and memory utilization remain under thresholds. Which monitoring approach and remediation provides the deepest insight into latency sources and optimizes cost?

answers.A: Enable AWS X-Ray tracing on the SageMaker endpoint, analyze service map latencies, identify cold-start segments, then provision minimal concurrency and configure auto scaling.
answers.B: Increase the instance type to a larger CPU-optimized instance and create a CloudWatch Alarm on CPU utilization.
answers.C: Enable SageMaker endpoint invocation metrics in CloudWatch and auto scale based on p95 latency.
answers.D: Convert the endpoint to a multi-model endpoint to share a single container across models and reduce overhead.

explanation: X-Ray reveals where time is spent (initialization vs. inference). Provisioned concurrency mitigates cold starts. CPU scaling alone misses framework overhead.

stem: A financial services company runs a batch transform job on EC2 instances via SageMaker. Transform jobs run once per day, but 80% of capacity is idle for most of the job. The team wants to reduce cost without increasing job duration. Which solution meets this requirement?

answers.A: Switch to CPU-optimized On-Demand instances sized for peak utilization and scale cluster size dynamically.
answers.B: Use larger GPU instances to process in parallel and decrease overall run time.
answers.C: Run the batch transform job on Lambda functions to parallelize tasks.
answers.D: Configure the batch transform job to use Spot Instances with a fallback to On-Demand and set instance count for peak load.

explanation: Spot with fallback saves cost during idle periods and matches peak capacity, while On-Demand-only wastes money.

stem: Your team deployed multiple SageMaker endpoints in three regions. They must tag endpoints for cost allocation and alert if untagged resources appear. Which configuration achieves this with the least operational overhead?

answers.A: Write a Lambda polling script to list endpoints daily, check tags, and send notifications.
answers.B: Use CloudWatch Logs subscription to trigger a Lambda on CreateEndpoint API events to validate tags.
answers.C: Create an AWS Config rule (required-tags) scoped to SageMaker::Endpoint resources and set SNS notifications.
answers.D: Implement CloudTrail log analysis in CloudWatch Logs Insights to detect untagged CreateEndpoint events and alert.

explanation: AWS Config rule automatically checks tags on creation with built-in functionality and SNS notifications, minimal custom code.

stem: A gaming company uses SageMaker Processing to prepare game telemetry data. They notice sporadic high I/O wait times on EBS volumes attached to processing jobs. Which combination of monitoring metrics and actions will identify and mitigate the issue?

answers.A: Monitor ProcessingJobIOBytes metric in Amazon CloudWatch and increase instance count.
answers.B: Enable CloudWatch EBS Volume metrics (VolumeQueueLength, VolumeThroughputPercentage), use higher IOPS gp3 volumes and adjust volume throughput settings.
answers.C: Monitor SageMaker Processing CPUUtilization and switch to GPU instance.
answers.D: Enable CloudTrail logging on processing containers and analyze volume errors.

explanation: VolumeQueueLength and throughput % diagnose EBS bottleneck; gp3 allows tuning of IOPS separately and resolves I/O wait.

stem: A retail ML pipeline uses SageMaker endpoints and ECS-based preprocessing. The finance team needs a single dashboard showing endpoint cost, CPU utilization, ECS Fargate memory utilization, and Lambda durations. Which solution meets this requirement with minimal latency?

answers.A: Build separate CloudWatch dashboards per service and share links.
answers.B: Export all metrics to an external monitoring tool via Fluentd.
answers.C: Configure CloudTrail Lake queries to join logs and visualize in QuickSight.
answers.D: Use CloudWatch unified metric namespace with metric math and create a combined CloudWatch dashboard with all resources.

explanation: CloudWatch dashboards support service metrics and metric math in one place without external tools or manual stitching.

stem: A biotech startup has a GPU-based SageMaker endpoint used intermittently. The CFO demands a cost-optimized solution that does not sacrifice startup latency. Which approach balances both?

answers.A: Use provisioned concurrency with a small number of GPU instances, enable endpoint auto scaling to scale down to zero using asynchronous endpoints.
answers.B: Switch to smaller CPU instances and batch requests to save cost.
answers.C: Use Spot Instances for the real-time endpoint to lower cost.
answers.D: Migrate to multi-model CPU endpoint and load one model at a time.

explanation: Provisioned concurrency preserves low latency, auto scaling to zero reduces idle cost; spot not supported for real-time.

stem: A team observes their inference pipeline fails under burst traffic due to hitting service quotas. They want proactive alerts when approaching SageMaker endpoint invocation quota. How should they implement this?

answers.A: Configure a CloudWatch alarm on SageMaker API ThrottledRequests metric.
answers.B: Create a CloudWatch alarm on the ThrottledRequests metric in the AWS/SageMaker namespace with threshold at 80% of quota.
answers.C: Use EventBridge to detect service quota event and call SNS.
answers.D: Poll DescribeEndpoint API hourly via Lambda and compare against known quotas.

explanation: ThrottledRequests metric directly signals when quota is approached; threshold at 80% gives early warning.

stem: Your model training jobs on GPU EC2 instances often underutilize GPU memory, leaving 40% unused for most jobs. You want better rightsizing. Which tool or service gives an automated recommendation?

answers.A: AWS Trusted Advisor’s cost optimization checks.
answers.B: CloudWatch anomaly detection on GPU utilization.
answers.C: AWS Compute Optimizer for EC2 instances.
answers.D: SageMaker Model Monitor for resource utilization analytics.

explanation: Compute Optimizer analyzes EC2/GPU instance metrics and recommends right-sized instance types and sizes.

stem: A media company streams video analysis via SageMaker batch transform jobs. They want to optimize data transfer costs between S3 and training instances. What combination of configurations reduces cost?

answers.A: Use cross-region replication to move data closer to training instances.
answers.B: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration to speed transfer and reduce egress cost.
answers.C: Configure batch transform to download from a public S3 bucket.
answers.D: Place instances and S3 in same AZ and use VPC endpoints for S3 traffic.

explanation: Same AZ VPC endpoints keeps traffic on AWS network, avoids cross-AZ data transfer charges.

stem: A regulated healthcare application must log all changes to SageMaker model endpoints for audit. They also want to trigger cost alerts when monthly spend exceeds budget. Which combined setup achieves both?

answers.A: Enable AWS CloudTrail data events for SageMaker API and create an AWS Budget with SNS notifications.
answers.B: Use CloudWatch Logs to collect API calls and set a Lambda to parse logs and send alerts.
answers.C: Configure CloudWatch Events for CreateEndpoint and UpdateEndpoint events and notify SNS.
answers.D: Integrate AWS Config for resource changes and rely on CloudWatch billing alarms.

explanation: CloudTrail data events capture every API call for audit; AWS Budgets integrates natively with SNS for cost alerts.

stem: Your SageMaker endpoint sees memory out-of-memory (OOM) errors for large images. You need to diagnose the frame where OOM occurs across many hosts. Which logs and queries should you use?

answers.A: Download Docker container logs from CloudWatch Logs and grep for "OOM".
answers.B: Use CloudWatch Logs Insights on /aws/sagemaker/Endpoints/* to query ERROR messages with "OutOfMemoryError" and filter by hostID.
answers.C: Enable SageMaker Debugger hook for memory profiling.
answers.D: Switch to X-Ray and trace memory allocations.

explanation: CloudWatch Logs Insights can aggregate and filter OOM errors across endpoint hosts quickly; Debugger is for training.

stem: A data pipeline uses EMR for preprocessing and then writes to S3 for SageMaker. During heavy loads, EMR tasks throttle due to hitting S3 request quotas. How do you monitor and remediate this?

answers.A: Enable EMRFS consistent view and increase retries.
answers.B: Use CloudTrail to monitor S3 503 errors and back off EMR jobs.
answers.C: Enable CloudWatch anomaly detection on EMRTaskDuration metric.
answers.D: Monitor S3 4XX/5XX request metrics in CloudWatch and add S3 request rate limiting or use S3 prefix sharding.

explanation: S3 request metrics reveal throttling; prefix sharding or client-side rate limiting reduces 503 errors.

stem: Your team deployed a multi-model endpoint behind an Application Load Balancer. They need to track per-model invocation counts for billing and auto scaling. Which approach is most effective?

answers.A: Enable ALB access logs and parse them in Athena.
answers.B: Add custom CloudWatch metrics inside the inference container to emit per-model Invoke counts.
answers.C: Use CloudTrail logs for InvokeEndpoint calls with model name filters.
answers.D: Tag each model and use SageMaker built-in metrics.

explanation: Containers can push custom metrics (model=inference) to CloudWatch for precise counts; ALB logs parsing is more complex.

stem: A startup runs GPU-based SageMaker training nightly. They want to reduce EC2 instance costs by 30% without increasing job time. Which purchasing option should they choose?

answers.A: Reserved Instances for a one-year term.
answers.B: EC2 Savings Plans covering all compute usage.
answers.C: Spot Instances with checkpointing in S3 and automatic retry.
answers.D: Dedicated Hosts to benefit from volume discounts.

explanation: Spot Instances offer largest discounts (up to 90%) and with checkpointing maintain job duration; RIs and SPs only 50%.

stem: A large dataset processing job on SageMaker Processing has unpredictable CPU loads. They want to automatically adjust compute within a run. Which strategy works?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Processing with auto scaling instance type list.
answers.B: Orchestrate multiple processing jobs in Step Functions with dynamic instance count based on CloudWatch metrics.
answers.C: Embed CPU usage watchers in the processing script and call the AWS API to change instance count.
answers.D: Switch to EMR on EKS with dynamic allocation.

explanation: Step Functions can branch logic mid-workflow and launch new Processing jobs sized by metrics; Processing itself doesn’t auto scale.

stem: Your SageMaker endpoint is deployed in a VPC. Data scientists observe increased inference latency. Which VPC configuration issue should you monitor and how?

answers.A: Monitor NAT Gateway CloudWatch NetworkPacketsOut to detect throttling and add NAT Gateways for scale.
answers.B: Monitor VPC Flow Logs for high packet loss and increase MTU.
answers.C: Monitor Security Group rejected packet metrics and open more ports.
answers.D: Monitor Elastic IP usage and allocate more addresses.

explanation: VPC endpoints without dedicated NAT may bottleneck at NAT Gateway; NetworkPacketsOut metric shows if throughput is hitting limits.

stem: A global SaaS product needs to track inference costs per customer across multiple SageMaker endpoints. What tagging and billing configuration should you apply?

answers.A: Add customer ID as an environment variable in the container and parse logs.
answers.B: Use separate AWS accounts per customer and consolidate billing.
answers.C: Instrument the SDK client to send customer metadata in X-ray trace.
answers.D: Tag each endpoint with a customer cost center tag, activate cost allocation tags in Billing console, and use Cost Explorer grouped by tag.

explanation: Cost allocation tags are the AWS best practice for per-resource cost tracking in Cost Explorer.

stem: A team uses Lambda functions for preprocessing before SageMaker. They receive occasional OutOfMemory errors in Lambda, causing increased retries and cost. How should they monitor and prevent this?

answers.A: Increase Lambda memory and rely on CloudWatch alarms on Duration.
answers.B: Enable CloudWatch Logs Insights on Lambda error logs to filter OOM, set a CloudWatch alarm on Errors metric, and adjust memory allocation.
answers.C: Switch to a Step Functions workflow to control memory.
answers.D: Use X-Ray to trace memory usage of the function.

explanation: Errors metric combined with Logs Insights identifies OOM events; alarms notify and right-size memory to eliminate retries.

stem: Your preprocessing uses an ECS service on Fargate that sporadically fails CPU credit balance. Which CloudWatch metrics and configuration should you monitor and adjust?

answers.A: Monitor Fargate MemoryReservation metric and increase CPU share.
answers.B: Enable Container Insights and watch host CPUUtilization, then switch to EC2 launch type.
answers.C: Monitor Fargate CPUCreditBalance and CPUUtilization in CloudWatch; adjust the CPU configuration (e.g., move from 0.25 vCPU to 0.5 vCPU) to maintain credits.
answers.D: Use CloudTrail to log throttled tasks and set a budget alert.

explanation: Fargate tasks use CPU credits; monitoring CPUCreditBalance prevents throttling, and adjusting vCPU allocation maintains balance.

stem: An ML endpoint in production has highly variable traffic. The team configured auto scaling on CPU utilization. They see scale-in immediately after scale-out, causing thrashing and increased cost. How should they fix it?

answers.A: Add scale-in and scale-out cooldown periods and use target tracking on average invocation per instance.
answers.B: Switch to step scaling based on p90 latency.
answers.C: Increase the CPU utilization threshold for scale-in.
answers.D: Use a multi-model endpoint instead to reduce container startup time.

explanation: Cooldown prevents rapid scale-in/out oscillations; target tracking on per-instance invocations stabilizes scaling.

stem: Your SageMaker Model Monitor baseline job generates drift violation alerts, but you also want to correlate them with infrastructure metrics to determine if CPU saturation causes data delays. How do you integrate these?

answers.A: Ingest Model Monitor CloudWatch logs into ElasticSearch and join with CPU metrics.
answers.B: Use CloudWatch metric math to overlay ModelMonitorDataQualityViolationCount and SageMakerEndpoint CPUUtilization in a unified dashboard.
answers.C: Export Model Monitor S3 reports to Athena and join with CPU metrics exported by CloudWatch.
answers.D: Implement a Lambda to capture both metrics on violation events and store in DynamoDB.

explanation: Metric math in CloudWatch provides immediate combining of application and infra metrics in one graph without custom code.

stem: A company is charged cross-account for S3 data egress when SageMaker in Account A reads from Account B buckets. They want to avoid egress charges. Which networking option solves this?

answers.A: Enable inter-account VPC peering and route traffic through private IP.
answers.B: Use S3 Transfer Acceleration.
answers.C: Create VPC Interface Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) for S3 in Account A’s VPC.
answers.D: Copy data periodically to Account A’s S3 bucket.

explanation: VPC Interface endpoints for S3 keep traffic within AWS network and avoid cross-account egress fees; bucket copy still incurs egress.

stem: Your nightly SageMaker hyperparameter tuning jobs sporadically hit EBS throughput limits, causing tunings to fail. Which combination of monitoring and remediation addresses this?

answers.A: Enable CloudTrail on CreateTrainingJob and throttle job submission.
answers.B: Monitor EC2 Instance CPUUtilization and switch to instance with higher compute.
answers.C: Use CloudWatch anomaly detection on TrainingJobRuntime metric.
answers.D: Monitor EBS VolumeThroughputPercentage metrics and migrate to gp3 volumes with provisioned throughput.

explanation: VolumeThroughputPercentage shows EBS bottleneck; gp3 lets you tune throughput independently of volume size.

stem: A data science team regularly creates and deletes dozens of notebooks in SageMaker Studio. The finance team wants to detect orphaned EBS volumes to stop incurring storage costs. What is the simplest solution?

answers.A: Enable AWS Config managed rule for unattached EBS volumes and set automatic remediation to delete.
answers.B: Write a Lambda to query DescribeVolumes for unattached volumes and delete.
answers.C: Set CloudWatch Events on DeleteNotebookInstance to trigger volume clean up.
answers.D: Use AWS Trusted Advisor’s underutilized EBS check.

explanation: AWS Config rule for unattached volumes and auto-remediation offers built-in, no-code solution; Trusted Advisor only alerts.

stem: A model training team wants to track costs per experiment across multiple SageMaker jobs, notebooks, and endpoints. Which tagging strategy and AWS service combination provides accurate reporting?

answers.A: Tag resources at creation with ExperimentID and use CloudTrail logs to calculate costs.
answers.B: Use SageMaker Experiments API to tag runs and rely on EMR cost reports.
answers.C: Enable cost allocation tags for ExperimentID, tag all SageMaker resources, and view groupings in AWS Cost Explorer.
answers.D: Import cost data into Quicksight and join on ExperimentID from logs.

explanation: Cost allocation tags in Cost Explorer directly associate resource costs with tags; Experiments API doesn’t feed billing data automatically.

stem: Your preprocessing job uses AWS Glue and feeds data into SageMaker. You need to monitor Glue job CPU, Glue Data Catalog calls, and track Glue errors alongside SageMaker job failures in a single pane. Which tool do you choose?

answers.A: CloudWatch dashboards per service linked manually.
answers.B: CloudWatch Unified Dashboards with metrics from AWS/Glue and AWS/SageMaker plus logs insights widgets.
answers.C: Athena querying Glue and SageMaker logs in S3.
answers.D: QuickSight pulling billing data.

explanation: CloudWatch dashboards can incorporate multiple metrics and logs insights widgets for near real-time observability without custom ETL.

stem: A SageMaker endpoint in a private subnet loses internet connectivity after a VPC route table change and fails to download model artifacts. How do you monitor and alert on such failures?

answers.A: Enable CloudWatch Logs for the endpoint container and search for network exceptions.
answers.B: Monitor CloudTrail events for GetObject failures on S3.
answers.C: Set a CloudWatch alarm on EndpointInvocationErrors metric.
answers.D: Create a CloudWatch anomaly detection alarm on SageMakerEndpointInvocation5XXErrors to catch connectivity failures.

explanation: 5XX errors include network and container issues. Anomaly detection spots sudden error spikes without log parsing.

stem: Your inference pipeline uses Lambda behind API Gateway calling SageMaker endpoints. You notice high tail latencies occasionally. Which combined metrics should you monitor and how to differentiate between GP and HTTP latencies?

answers.A: Monitor API Gateway Latency and IntegrationLatency in CloudWatch to separate client-facing vs. backend invocation delays.
answers.B: Monitor SageMaker Endpoint ModelLatency and InvocationsPerInstance metrics only.
answers.C: Enable X-Ray for Lambda and use cold start latency metrics.
answers.D: Use CloudWatch Synthetics to measure end-to-end latency.

explanation: API Gateway Latency measures total, IntegrationLatency isolates backend; ModelLatency doesn’t include network overhead.

stem: Your team’s SageMaker batch transform jobs intermittently fail due to insufficient vCPU quotas in a new AWS Region. What is the recommended monitoring step and long-term mitigation?

answers.A: Use CloudWatch to monitor ThrottledRequests and request a service quota increase manually when alarms fire.
answers.B: Implement retries in the job script.
answers.C: Create a CloudWatch alarm on ServiceQuotaExceeded metric via Service Quotas namespace and automate quota requests via AWS Service Quotas APIs.
answers.D: Switch to GPU instances which have separate quotas.

explanation: ServiceQuotaExceeded metric alerts on hitting quotas. Automating via Service Quotas APIs ensures timely increases.

stem: A global inference workload runs on SageMaker endpoints in multiple regions. They need to compare cost per inference across regions. What’s the best way to collect and visualize this data?

answers.A: Aggregate SageMaker billing metrics into CloudWatch using PutMetricData and graph them.
answers.B: Enable cost allocation tags for Region on endpoints and use Cost Explorer filtering by tag.
answers.C: Export Cost & Usage report to S3 and query with Athena manually.
answers.D: Use QuickSight to connect to Billing API.

explanation: Cost Explorer with allocation tags gives near real-time region-based cost per resource without manual report queries.

stem: An ML endpoint behind a Network Load Balancer exhibits higher packet drop during bursts. Which VPC metric should you monitor, and what corrective action should you take?

answers.A: Monitor NetworkBytesIn and move to larger instance.
answers.B: Monitor HostNetworkRxErrors and increase MTU.
answers.C: Monitor Flow Logs for REJECT entries and open more ports.
answers.D: Monitor Elastic Network Interface (ENI) ReceivePacketDrops and use enhanced networking (ENA) instances or increase ENI count.

explanation: ReceivePacketDrops signals NIC saturation; ENA or more ENIs improves network performance for burst traffic.

stem: A team using SageMaker Debugger for training also wants to monitor GPU utilization and EC2 metrics in one place. Which monitoring solution should they implement?

answers.A: Use CloudWatch Container Insights for the training job’s underlying EC2 instances alongside Debugger tensor metrics.
answers.B: Send EC2 metrics to CloudTrail for correlation.
answers.C: Parse Debugger logs with CloudWatch Logs Insights and join with EC2 metrics in Athena.
answers.D: Load all metrics into QuickSight and build a dashboard.

explanation: Container Insights collects EC2 host metrics and container-level metrics in CloudWatch seamlessly, enabling side-by-side visualization with Debugger metrics.

stem: A team must restrict a SageMaker notebook instance so that it can read and write data only in a specific S3 bucket prefix. The notebook uses its execution role to access S3. Which configuration enforces least privilege?

answers.A: Attach an IAM policy to the notebook execution role allowing s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject only on arn:aws:s3:::marketing-data/train/*
answers.B: Add an S3 bucket policy granting the notebook role full access to the bucket and deny other principals
answers.C: Create a VPC gateway endpoint for S3 with a policy restricting access to that prefix
answers.D: Modify the KMS key policy to allow decryption only for that bucket prefix

explanation: Least privilege is enforced by restricting the notebook’s execution role with an inline IAM policy on the specific prefix. S3 endpoint policies or bucket policies can work but are more complex and less direct; KMS policy controls only encryption.

stem: A security requirement mandates that SageMaker training jobs must not have internet access, yet must pull training images from Amazon ECR. How should you configure the training job?

answers.A: Launch the training job in public subnets with a restrictive security group
answers.B: Provide a customer-managed NAT gateway in the VPC used by the job
answers.C: Specify VpcConfig with private subnets that have an ECR VPC endpoint and no NAT
answers.D: Use a service-linked role that disables internet access by default

explanation: By placing the training job in private subnets with an ECR VPC endpoint and no NAT gateway, you prevent internet access but allow ECR pulls. Public subnets or NAT would allow internet egress.

stem: A SageMaker endpoint must be private within a VPC and only allow traffic from instances in another VPC over AWS PrivateLink. Which steps meet these requirements?

answers.A: Launch endpoint without VPCConfig and restrict with security groups referencing peer VPC
answers.B: Create interface VPC endpoint for SageMaker runtime in the consumer VPC, deploy the endpoint in a private subnet, and apply SG allowing traffic only from peer VPC CIDR
answers.C: Use NAT gateway and public endpoint but restrict source IPs in SG
answers.D: Enable endpoint public access and add route53 private hosted zone entries

explanation: Deploying the endpoint in a VPC with no public access plus creating an interface endpoint in the consumer VPC over PrivateLink and restricting with SG enforces private-only access.

stem: A DevOps engineer needs to grant AWS CodePipeline permission to deploy SageMaker models and endpoints but must follow least privilege. Which IAM policy attachment is correct?

answers.A: Attach AmazonSageMakerFullAccess to the CodePipeline role
answers.B: Allow sagemaker:* on resource '*' for the pipeline role
answers.C: Create an SCP denying all actions except sagemaker:CreateEndpoint
answers.D: Attach a scoped IAM policy allowing only sagemaker:CreateModel, sagemaker:CreateEndpointConfig, sagemaker:CreateEndpoint on identified resource ARNs

explanation: Granting only the specific deploy actions on the exact model and endpoint ARNs enforces least privilege. FullAccess or wildcard would be overly permissive; SCP is for accounts.

stem: An organization requires CloudTrail logs of all SageMaker API calls to be encrypted using a KMS key managed by SecurityOperations. Which configuration satisfies this?

answers.A: Enable CloudTrail for SageMaker and leave default encryption
answers.B: Configure CloudTrail with the SecurityOperations KMS key ARN for SSE-KMS encryption of logs
answers.C: Apply an S3 bucket policy to encrypt objects using SSE-S3
answers.D: Modify Trail event selectors to include SSE-KMS

explanation: Specifying the KMS key ARN in the CloudTrail configuration ensures that logs are encrypted with that key. SSE-S3 or bucket policy alone cannot enforce use of a customer-managed key.

stem: A notebook lifecycle configuration retrieves secrets from AWS Secrets Manager. You must ensure the lifecycle lambda can decrypt the secret but no other SageMaker service can. How do you tighten permissions?

answers.A: Attach AWSSecretsManagerReadWrite to the notebook role
answers.B: Add a resource policy on the secret allowing the notebook role
answers.C: Add a KMS key policy granting decrypt only to the notebook lifecycle role principal
answers.D: Enable automatic rotation on the secret

explanation: Tightening access at the KMS key policy level restricts decryption to only the specified lifecycle role. Resource policies on the secret do not control the KMS decryption step.

stem: A SOC team requires that any SageMaker endpoint creation must be approved by a central admin. How can you enforce this in CodePipeline?

answers.A: Add a Manual Approval action before the CreateEndpoint stage
answers.B: Use a CloudWatch rule to detect CreateEndpoint and block it
answers.C: Implement an SCP to deny sagemaker:CreateEndpoint
answers.D: Require MFA in the pipeline role

explanation: A Manual Approval action in CodePipeline forces human approval. SCP would prevent creation globally; CloudWatch can only alert after the fact.

stem: A model registry in SageMaker stores sensitive models. You need to prevent direct API deletes of models, but allow deletion through a daily cleanup Lambda. Which IAM policy accomplishes this?

answers.A: Deny sagemaker:DeleteModel to everyone
answers.B: Remove sagemaker:DeleteModel from all roles except Lambda by attaching a policy to the Lambda role only
answers.C: Create an SCP denying DeleteModel for all principals
answers.D: Attach a deny statement in a permission boundary that applies to principals unless aws:PrincipalArn equals the Lambda function execution role

explanation: A permission boundary with a conditional deny unless the principal is the cleanup Lambda enforces that only that role may delete models, without affecting Service roles.

stem: A compliance rule requires that only approved subnets are used in SageMaker jobs. How can you enforce this?

answers.A: Use an SCP to deny SageMaker calls in unapproved subnets
answers.B: Write an IAM permissions policy with Deny on sagemaker:CreateTrainingJob when sagemaker:VpcConfig.Subnets ≠ approved IDs
answers.C: Enforce via CloudWatch alarms and manual remediation
answers.D: Use AWS Config managed rules without enforcement

explanation: Embedding a Deny in the IAM policy conditioned on the VpcConfig.Subnets attribute blocks jobs launched in unapproved subnets. SCP cannot inspect parameters.

stem: A training job needs to write to a DynamoDB table, but only to specific items. How do you restrict the SageMaker execution role accordingly?

answers.A: Grant dynamodb:* on the table ARN
answers.B: Attach AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess
answers.C: Grant dynamodb:PutItem only on arn:aws:dynamodb:…:table/MyTable with a Condition on dynamodb:LeadingKeys for the key prefix
answers.D: Use an SCP to restrict all DynamoDB writes

explanation: Using a resource-level IAM policy with a condition on LeadingKeys ensures writes only to items matching the key prefix. Full table or wildcard actions are too broad.

stem: A DevSecOps requirement: all SageMaker model artifacts in S3 must be encrypted with a specific KMS key. Which is the simplest enforcement?

answers.A: Add SSE-KMS in the CreateModel call parameters
answers.B: Use a bucket policy requiring x-amz-server-side-encryption header
answers.C: Implement a CloudWatch rule that checks artifact uploads
answers.D: Add an S3 bucket policy Deny PutObject unless x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id matches the key

explanation: An S3 bucket policy that denies PutObject requests unless the correct KMS key ID header is present enforces encryption at write time.

stem: A SageMaker pipeline stores intermediate data in S3. The security team wants to prevent access to these artifacts except by the pipeline service. How do you enforce this?

answers.A: Grant pipeline roles wide access to the bucket
answers.B: Use an S3 bucket policy allowing only the SageMaker Pipelines service principal and the pipeline execution role ARN
answers.C: Encrypt with a KMS key and rely on default key policy
answers.D: Use a resource-based IAM policy on the pipeline role

explanation: An S3 bucket policy that permits only the SageMaker Pipelines service principal and the specific execution role to access the bucket restricts all other access.

stem: A model deployed in SageMaker must only be invoked by authenticated users in an Amazon Cognito identity pool. How can you secure the endpoint?

answers.A: Use an endpoint policy with Allow for principal '*' and check Token in code
answers.B: Attach a resource policy to Cognito to allow SageMakerInvoke
answers.C: Create an endpoint policy requiring aws:PrincipalOrgID and aws:RequestContext.authorizer.claims.sub from Cognito identity
answers.D: Use a VPC endpoint and IP-based SG only

explanation: An endpoint policy can restrict invocation to principals from the specific Cognito identity pool by checking the principal’s token claims in aws:RequestContext.

stem: A notebook lifecycle script clones code from CodeCommit. The IAM role has ListRepos and GitPull permissions but the clone fails. On inspecting the trust policy, you find no conditions. What’s the missing configuration?

answers.A: Add an SCP allowing codecommit:GitPull
answers.B: Add a Condition in the IAM trust policy restricting the service principal to sagemaker.amazonaws.com
answers.C: Attach AWSCodeCommitPowerUser to the role
answers.D: Enable cross-account access in CodeCommit

explanation: Notebook lifecycle functions are invoked by the SageMaker service, so the role’s trust policy must allow sagemaker.amazonaws.com as a principal to assume the role. Without it, the role cannot be assumed and clone fails.

stem: A security audit reveals CloudWatch Logs for SageMaker were publicly accessible. How do you block public access while preserving individual user access?

answers.A: Delete the log group ACLs
answers.B: Enable KMS encryption on the log group
answers.C: Apply an SCP to prevent DescribeLogGroups
answers.D: Attach a resource policy to the log group denying Principal '*' for log:Describe and log:Get

explanation: A CloudWatch Logs resource policy can explicitly deny calls from anonymous principals (*) while allowing authenticated IAM principals to continue accessing the logs.

stem: A data scientist left a SageMaker endpoint open to the internet. You need to remediate: lock down to a VPC in us-east-1 and allow only IPs from 10.0.0.0/16. What is the fastest remediation?

answers.A: Delete the endpoint and recreate within a VPC
answers.B: Update the endpoint configuration with VpcConfig and apply a security group that allows only 10.0.0.0/16
answers.C: Attach an endpoint policy restricting CIDR
answers.D: Apply a bucket policy on model artifacts

explanation: Updating the existing endpoint’s VpcConfig and security group is fastest. Deletion and recreation is slower; endpoint policies do not control network access.

stem: Your CodeBuild project for ML uses Docker containers on shared hardware. You must ensure build logs are encrypted with a custom KMS key. Which change meets this?

answers.A: Enable CloudWatch Logs for the project
answers.B: Attach AWSKeyManagementServicePowerUser to CodeBuild role
answers.C: Specify project’s logsConfig.cloudWatchLogs.encryptionDisabled=false and kmsKey in CloudFormation
answers.D: Use SSE-S3 for the CodeBuild logs bucket

explanation: In the CodeBuild logsConfig, setting encryptionDisabled to false and specifying the KMS key ensures logs are encrypted with the customer-managed key.

stem: A compliance mandate: all secrets accessed by SageMaker (e.g., DB credentials) must require KMS grant usage via key grants rather than policy. How to implement?

answers.A: Use KMS grants to give the SageMaker execution role temporary decrypt privileges for the secret’s CMK
answers.B: Modify the key policy to allow the SageMaker role Decrypt
answers.C: Add the SageMaker role to a KMS key alias
answers.D: Enable automatic rotation on the secret

explanation: KMS grants provide temporary, auditable decrypt permissions. Modifying key policies is static and not per-request as required.

stem: A model registry must only allow promotion of approved models. You need to restrict who can call CreateModelPackageVersion. What’s the best practice?

answers.A: Use an SCP denying sagemaker:CreateModelPackageVersion
answers.B: Enable AWS Config rule for non-approved models
answers.C: Create a SageMaker model registry tag rule
answers.D: Attach an IAM policy requiring a specific request tag (e.g., ApprovedBy) for CreateModelPackageVersion

explanation: Requiring a request tag via IAM policy ensures that only requests including the ApprovedBy tag can create new versions, enforcing the approval workflow.

stem: A Dev team’s pipeline stores its CloudFormation templates in S3. You must ensure only specific pipeline roles can read and write these templates. Which is correct?

answers.A: Grant public read and limit write via signed URLs
answers.B: Apply S3 bucket policy allowing List, Get, Put only to the IAM roles of the pipeline stages
answers.C: Use KMS encryption only
answers.D: Restrict via VPC endpoint policy

explanation: An S3 bucket policy scoped to only the pipeline’s IAM role ARNs for List, Get, and Put enforces that no other principals can read or write.

stem: A post-deployment check must validate that SageMaker Notebook Instances are encrypted at rest. Which automated check fulfills this?

answers.A: CloudWatch alarm on unencrypted volumes
answers.B: Enable AWS Config managed rule EC2_ENCRYPTED_VOLUMES
answers.C: Enable AWS Config managed rule SAGEMAKER_NOTEBOOK_INSTANCE_ENCRYPTED_VOLUME_CHECK
answers.D: Use GuardDuty on notebooks

explanation: AWS Config’s SageMaker-specific managed rule checks encryption of notebook volumes directly. EC2 rules do not cover SageMaker notebook volumes.

stem: A SageMaker Processing job uses a role that also has S3ListAllMyBuckets permission. Security wants to remove ListAll permission but still allow list on two buckets. How to implement?

answers.A: Replace wildcard list permission with explicit s3:ListBucket on the two bucket ARNs
answers.B: Add an SCP denying s3:ListAllMyBuckets
answers.C: Use bucket policies on S3 buckets
answers.D: Rotate IAM role credentials daily

explanation: Restricting the role’s IAM policy to only s3:ListBucket on the two specified buckets removes global list permission while allowing needed buckets.

stem: A pipeline deploys a SageMaker model using AWS CDK. The synth step fails due to lack of KMS decrypt for the secret used in a CDK context. How can you fix this?

answers.A: Grant the CDK role kms:GenerateDataKey*
answers.B: Attach SecretsManagerReadWrite to CDK role
answers.C: Use plaintext secret in code
answers.D: Grant the CDK execution role kms:Decrypt on the secret’s CMK in the key policy

explanation: The CDK synth needs kms:Decrypt rights on the CMK to read the secret. Adding that to the key policy resolves the failure.

stem: A regulatory requirement: all IAM role assumptions by SageMaker must be logged and alerts sent on unusual assume-role calls. How do you implement?

answers.A: Enable CloudWatch Logs on SageMaker
answers.B: Create CloudTrail trail capturing IAM:AssumeRole, create CloudWatch metric filter for the SageMaker service principal, and alarm
answers.C: Use AWS Config rule to check unusual assume-role calls
answers.D: Rotate the SageMaker service role daily

explanation: A CloudTrail trail logs all AssumeRole calls; a metric filter on the CloudWatch Logs for the SageMaker principal can trigger alarms for any assumption events.

stem: A data scientist requests temporary credentials for S3 to use inside a notebook, without exposing long-lived keys. What is the most secure pattern?

answers.A: Use AWS STS GetSessionToken in the notebook to generate time-limited credentials
answers.B: Embed an IAM user access key in the notebook
answers.C: Use an S3 pre-signed URL for each object access
answers.D: Use root account credentials stored in Secrets Manager

explanation: Using STS GetSessionToken provides temporary credentials with limited lifetime. Pre-signed URLs are object-specific and not convenient; root or static keys are insecure.

stem: A SageMaker Endpoint in VPC must only communicate with ECR and CloudWatch Logs, not the public internet. How do you enforce this?

answers.A: Attach a bucket policy on ECR
answers.B: Use NAT Gateway with restrictive route tables
answers.C: Deploy endpoint in private subnets with interface endpoints for ECR and CloudWatch Logs and no NAT
answers.D: Use Security Group to block 0.0.0.0/0

explanation: Interface VPC endpoints allow access to AWS services without internet. Deploying in private subnets without NAT ensures no egress to public internet.

stem: A build in CodeBuild requires access to a VPC-only RDS instance. The CodeBuild service role has all necessary DB permissions, but builds fail to connect. What must you configure?

answers.A: Open the DB’s security group to 0.0.0.0/0
answers.B: Configure the CodeBuild project’s VpcConfig with the DB’s subnets and security group
answers.C: Use a NAT gateway in the project’s VPC
answers.D: Attach AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole to the CodeBuild role

explanation: CodeBuild must be configured with VpcConfig to attach ENIs in the same subnets/security groups as the RDS. Without this, it runs in default network and cannot reach the DB.

stem: An audit finds that some SageMaker endpoint access logs contain PII. You must restrict retrieval of those logs to a security analysis role. How?

answers.A: Attach a resource policy on the CloudWatch Logs group allowing only the security role principal to get logs
answers.B: Encrypt logs with SSE-S3
answers.C: Use an SCP to deny DescribeLogStreams
answers.D: Disable logging on the endpoint

explanation: A CloudWatch Logs resource policy scoped to the security analysis role ensures only that role can retrieve the logs; others will be denied.

stem: A new security control: SageMaker projects must only use predefined IAM permission boundaries. How to ensure new roles created by SageMaker pipelines comply?

answers.A: Use an SCP to deny iam:CreateRole
answers.B: Tag all new roles and enforce with AWS Config
answers.C: Use CodePipeline approval stage
answers.D: Attach the managed permission boundary policy in the SageMaker pipeline role so that any new role inherits the boundary

explanation: Permission boundaries attached to the role that creates new roles propagate the boundary to child roles, ensuring they cannot be more permissive.

stem: A SageMaker Model Monitor job must write drift reports to S3 but only to a single bucket. The monitor role has wild-card S3 permissions. How do you tighten permissions without affecting other workflows?

answers.A: Use a bucket policy to deny PutObject from that role
answers.B: Replace the role’s S3 wildcard with a policy granting PutObject only on the monitor reports bucket
answers.C: Implement an SCP
answers.D: Encrypt the bucket with default encryption

explanation: Updating the monitor role’s IAM policy to allow only the specific bucket reduces blast radius without impacting other S3 workflows.

stem: A security guideline: all SageMaker processing jobs must use a VPC endpoint to S3. One job failed to access data. Which misconfiguration is most likely?

answers.A: The role lacks s3:GetObject
answers.B: The bucket policy denies all traffic
answers.C: VpcConfig lacked the S3 gateway endpoint in the subnet route tables
answers.D: The job ran in a public subnet

explanation: If the S3 gateway endpoint is not added to the subnet route tables in VpcConfig, the job cannot reach S3. A public subnet or role error would yield different symptoms.

stem: A data science team needs to deploy a SageMaker real-time inference endpoint in a private VPC. They want to script the entire environment using AWS CloudFormation. Which resources and configuration should they include to ensure proper VPC connectivity and auto scaling of the endpoint?

answers.A: Define an AWS::SageMaker::Endpoint with VpcConfig, and rely on SageMaker’s built-in auto scaling by setting EnableAutoScaling: true.
answers.B: Create AWS::SageMaker::EndpointConfig with VpcConfig.SecurityGroupIds and Subnets, an AWS::SageMaker::Endpoint that references that config, an AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalableTarget for sagemaker:variant:DesiredInstanceCount, and an AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalingPolicy.
answers.C: Use AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint for SageMaker API, then AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup to scale instances behind the endpoint.
answers.D: Use AWS::Lambda-backed custom resource to modify the SageMaker endpoint configuration after deploy for VPC and scaling settings.

explanation: CloudFormation requires separate AppAutoScaling resources; SageMaker endpoint resource does not directly support scaling.

stem: An ML engineer wants to provision a multi-container SageMaker endpoint via AWS CDK in Python. They need one container for model A, one for model B, each with different IAM roles and different environment variables. Which CDK constructs and pattern should they use?

answers.A: Use sagemaker.CfnModel for each container with respective environment and roles, then sagemaker.CfnEndpointConfig listing both models, and sagemaker.CfnEndpoint.
answers.B: Use sagemaker.Model for each container, then sagemaker.MultiModelEndpoint to combine them automatically.
answers.C: Define two sagemaker.CfnModel constructs with separate ExecutionRoleArn and Environment properties, create a single sagemaker.CfnEndpointConfig with both ModelName entries under ProductionVariants, then a sagemaker.CfnEndpoint.
answers.D: Use sagemaker.EndpointBatchTransform with multiple TransformJobDefinitions for each container.

explanation: Multi-container real-time endpoints require separate CfnModel and listing in a single EndpointConfig.

stem: A team uses AWS CDK to deploy their SageMaker endpoint, but CloudFormation reports drift in the EndpointConfig when they manually update the environment variables via console. How can they prevent drift and enforce configuration as code?

answers.A: Remove manual updates; enforce changes only through CDK by maintaining environment variables in code and deploying via CDK pipelines.
answers.B: Set EnableDriftCorrection: true on the CfnEndpointConfig resource.
answers.C: Use AWS Config to ignore drift on SageMaker endpoint resources.
answers.D: Use a CloudFormation macro to override the console changes at deployment time.

explanation: Prevent drift by managing all changes in code; CloudFormation cannot auto-correct SageMaker endpoints.

stem: An organization requires that all SageMaker endpoint logs be sent to CloudWatch Logs in a separate AWS account. They want to script this via AWS CloudFormation. Which approach satisfies least-privilege and cross-account delivery?

answers.A: Grant the SageMaker execution role cross-account CloudWatchPutLogEvents permission.
answers.B: Attach AWS::Logs::SubscriptionFilter on the endpoint’s log group to the destination account.
answers.C: Use AWS::CloudWatch::Destination in the SageMaker stack to forward logs directly.
answers.D: Deploy a CloudWatch Log Group export task via AWS::Logs::Destination in the central account and use resource policy on the SageMaker log group to allow PutSubscriptionFilter to the destination.

explanation: Cross-account subscription requires a CloudWatch Logs destination with resource policy granting permissions.

stem: A dev team needs to automate creation of multiple SageMaker endpoints with different instance types and scaling policies using AWS CDK. They want to avoid duplication of code. Which CDK pattern is most appropriate?

answers.A: Write separate stacks for each endpoint and instantiate them individually.
answers.B: Define a high-level construct class that takes instance type and scaling parameters as properties, and reuse it for each endpoint.
answers.C: Use a single CfnInclude to import an existing CloudFormation template with parameters.
answers.D: Leverage AWS::CloudFormation::Stack resource within the same template for each endpoint.

explanation: A custom CDK construct promotes reuse and parameterization across multiple endpoints.

stem: A security audit requires that SageMaker endpoints be deployed only within private subnets and routed through NAT for internet access. How should this be scripted in AWS CDK to satisfy both requirements?

answers.A: Specify subnetSelection with subnetType.PUBLIC in VpcConfig so endpoints use NAT automatically.
answers.B: Set EndpointConfig.KmsKeyId to use private subnets.
answers.C: Pass private subnet IDs and security group IDs in VpcConfig when defining CfnEndpointConfig in CDK, ensuring they are Private isolated subnets with NAT configured on the VPC.
answers.D: Use VpcLink to attach the endpoint to a private Network Load Balancer.

explanation: VpcConfig must reference private subnets and SGs; NAT is configured at VPC level, not endpoint.

stem: An ML team wants to integrate spot instances into their inference fleet behind an Application Load Balancer with automatic scaling. They decide to use ECS on Fargate Spot. Which CloudFormation resource definitions must they include to ensure the desired capacity and scaling behavior?

answers.A: AWS::ECS::CapacityProvider with AutoScalingGroupProvider using Spot Instances, AWS::ECS::Cluster defaultCapacityProviderStrategy including that capacity provider, and AWS::ECS::Service with desiredCount parameter.
answers.B: AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup with MixedInstancesPolicy using ON_DEMAND_ONLY, and AWS::ECS::Service.
answers.C: AWS::ECS::Service with LaunchType FARGATE only, and AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalableTarget for ECS service.
answers.D: AWS::Batch::ComputeEnvironment configured for Spot, and AWS::Batch::JobDefinition for inference jobs.

explanation: ECS Fargate Spot requires a capacity provider defined, then attach to the service for scaling on Spot.

stem: Your organization mandates that all ML model container images be stored in Amazon ECR with image scanning enabled at push time. You must script this using AWS CDK. Which steps are required?

answers.A: Define an ECR repository in CDK with imageScanningConfiguration enabled, grant SageMaker execution role pull permissions, then use that repository URI in CfnModel.
answers.B: Use ecr.Repository with imageScanOnPush: true in CDK, add repository.grantPull(sagemakerRole), then pass repository.repositoryUri to SageMaker Model property in CfnModel or CfnModelPackage.
answers.C: Create AWS::ECR::LifecyclePolicy in CloudFormation and set scanOnPush: ENABLED.
answers.D: Use AWS CLI in a custom resource to enable image scan on existing repo.

explanation: CDK’s ecr.Repository supports imageScanOnPush; then grant pull to the role used by SageMaker.

stem: A SageMaker endpoint fails health checks intermittently due to VPC ENI provisioning delays, causing AWS CloudFormation deployment to rollback. How can you modify your CloudFormation template to handle this?

answers.A: Set EndpointConfig.DeleteAfterUse: false.
answers.B: Add CreationPolicy with ResourceSignal on AWS::SageMaker::Endpoint.
answers.C: Wrap the CfnEndpoint resource in a Custom::SageMakerEndpoint that retries.
answers.D: Use DependsOn with a custom wait condition Lambda that polls DescribeEndpointStatus until InService before signaling success.

explanation: CloudFormation offers no native retry for SageMaker endpoints; implement a wait condition via Lambda or custom resource.

stem: Your infra-as-code pipeline uses AWS CDK to deploy a SageMaker inference endpoint. During a deployment, you need to update the endpoint's variant weight to shift 20% traffic to a new model variant. How do you script this with least downtime?

answers.A: Update the existing EndpointConfig in-place via CfnUpdatePolicy in CloudFormation.
answers.B: Delete and recreate the endpoint with the new variant weight settings.
answers.C: Create a new AWS::SageMaker::EndpointConfig with both variants and desired weights, then update the AWS::SageMaker::Endpoint to point to the new config.
answers.D: Use AWS CLI in a CDK CustomResource to call UpdateEndpointWeight directly.

explanation: Endpoint updates must reference a new EndpointConfig; creating a new config and pointing the endpoint to it avoids downtime.

stem: A DevOps engineer must ensure that SageMaker endpoint deployments are idempotent and environment-specific. They decide to use CloudFormation parameter overrides. Which of these strategies will achieve both requirements?

answers.A: Store instance type and count in template metadata and reference via Fn::GetAtt.
answers.B: Define Parameters for InstanceType, InitialInstanceCount, VPC Subnet IDs, and SecurityGroup IDs; reference them in CfnEndpointConfig, ensuring different values per environment.
answers.C: Use Mappings section keyed by environment name to look up all values.
answers.D: Use a separate template per environment to hardcode values.

explanation: Parameters allow idempotent, repeatable deployments with all settings externalized per environment.

stem: You need to deploy a SageMaker multi-model endpoint for cost-effective hosting of hundreds of small models. You want to automate provisioning with CloudFormation and enforce container image immutability. What is the correct approach?

answers.A: Create one AWS::SageMaker::ModelPackage for each container with ModelApprovalStatus set to Approved and InferenceSpecification referencing ECR image digests, then one AWS::SageMaker::EndpointConfig with MultiModelConfig.
answers.B: Use AWS::SageMaker::Model with LocalCode option and set ImageConfig.AutoUpdate: false.
answers.C: Deploy a custom multi-model server on an EC2 Auto Scaling group instead.
answers.D: Use a single AWS::SageMaker::Endpoint with MultiModelEndpoint property.

explanation: ModelPackage with approved inference spec and image digest ensures immutability; EndpointConfig multi-model supports dynamic loading.

stem: A regulated environment requires all SageMaker endpoints to be deployed via AWS CloudFormation and reviewed via change sets. When a change to endpoint instance type is approved, CloudFormation update fails because of immutable properties. How should you script your template to allow instance-type changes without replacing resources?

answers.A: Set UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain on the Endpoint resource.
answers.B: Use AWS::SageMaker::EndpointConfig with EndpointConfigName generated by a GUID to force replacement.
answers.C: Use a nested stack for the endpoint and update only nested stacks.
answers.D: Decouple endpoint from endpoint config: script EndpointConfig as separate resource and update the EndpointConfigName in the Endpoint resource, so only the config is replaced, not the endpoint.

explanation: EndpointConfig can be replaced independently; endpoint resource simply points to new config name.

stem: Your team wants to use AWS CDK in TypeScript to deploy SageMaker endpoints and test them automatically post-deployment. They need to add an automated post-deploy test hook in the same pipeline. Which CDK pattern should they adopt?

answers.A: Use CDK aspect to inject Lambda-backed custom resources.
answers.B: Utilize CDK Pipelines’ testing framework: add CodeBuild Step after deployment stage invoking a smoke-test Lambda or script.
answers.C: Add AWS::CodeDeploy::DeploymentGroup in the CDK template.
answers.D: Write a CDK Custom Resource that runs tests as part of deployment.

explanation: CDK Pipelines support post-deploy tests via CodeBuild steps integrated into the pipeline.

stem: An engineer must ensure that SageMaker endpoint container images are built, pushed to ECR, and deployed in one IaC deployment. Using AWS CDK, which sequence of constructs accomplishes this atomically?

answers.A: Define a CodeBuild Project in CDK that builds the image, then a separate CDK app that references the ECR repository.
answers.B: Use a custom resource to call AWS CLI to build and push, then define the CfnModel.
answers.C: Use CodePipeline CDK constructs: define a pipeline with Source stage, Build stage (CodeBuild building and pushing to ECR), then a Deploy stage with CDK deploy of the SageMaker endpoint stack referencing image URI as pipeline output.
answers.D: Use CDK Bundling API on the sagemaker.Model construct.

explanation: CDK Pipelines can orchestrate build and deploy stages, ensuring atomic transition from image build to endpoint deployment.

stem: Your infra team must grant least-privilege permissions for SageMaker to pull container images from a private ECR in another AWS account. Which IAM policy should you script in CloudFormation on the SageMaker execution role?

answers.A: Allow ecr:BatchGetImage, ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer on the repository Arn directly in the role policy.
answers.B: Policy allowing sts:AssumeRole on a role in the ECR account that has ecr:GetAuthorizationToken, BatchGetImage, GetDownloadUrlForLayer, and in the ECR account’s repository policy grant the SageMaker role’s AWS principal those actions.
answers.C: Grant AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryFullAccess to the SageMaker execution role.
answers.D: Add AWS-managed policy AmazonSageMakerFullAccess which includes ECR pull permissions.

explanation: Cross-account ECR pull requires AssumeRole into the ECR account and corresponding repository policy; broad managed policies violate least privilege.

stem: A team uses AWS::CloudFormation::Stack resource to encapsulate SageMaker endpoint provisioning in a nested stack. They now need to expose the endpoint name to the parent stack for AutoScaling configuration. Which method achieves this?

answers.A: In the nested stack template, declare an Output for EndpointName; in the parent stack, reference it via Fn::GetAtt on the AWS::CloudFormation::Stack resource.
answers.B: Use ImportValue to pull it from the nested stack without declaring Output.
answers.C: Write a Lambda-backed custom resource in the parent to call DescribeStacks.
answers.D: Use AWS::SSM::Parameter to store the endpoint name and read it in the parent.

explanation: Outputs and Fn::GetAtt on nested stacks pass values to parent stacks.

stem: Your company requires that all SageMaker endpoint configurations be version controlled and reviewed. Which AWS CDK and CloudFormation features should you use to allow change visibility and prevent unreviewed drift?

answers.A: Enable termination protection on CfnEndpoint resources.
answers.B: Use sagemaker.Endpoint.fromEndpointName to reference existing endpoint without managing it.
answers.C: Use CDK to synthesize CloudFormation change sets and require manual approval before execution in pipelines.
answers.D: Enable rolling updates in CloudFormation on the SageMaker stack.

explanation: Change sets provide visibility into what will change before applying; CDK pipelines can enforce manual approvals.

stem: An ML engineer needs to script blue/green deployments of a SageMaker endpoint using AWS CloudFormation and minimize invocation errors during traffic shift. Which pattern should they implement?

answers.A: Use AWS::SageMaker::EndpointVariants property to specify both blue and green variants and weights.
answers.B: Define two separate Endpoint resources and swap DNS records in Route53.
answers.C: Use CodeDeploy with blue/green strategy for SageMaker service.
answers.D: Use AWS::SageMaker::EndpointConfig to define two production variants with weights, attach AppAutoScaling policy to adjust weights gradually as part of CloudFormation update.

explanation: Defining both variants and adjusting weights via scaling policies enables gradual traffic shift without downtime.

stem: A DevOps pipeline must deploy a SageMaker batch transform job definition and a serving endpoint in one CloudFormation template. They encounter circular dependency between the IAM role and the endpoint config. How can they resolve this?

answers.A: Duplicate an IAM role resource for each service to break the cycle.
answers.B: Use separate CloudFormation nested stacks: one for IAM role definition, one for endpoint and transform referencing an exported role ARN.
answers.C: Use DependsOn between the role and endpoint config to force order.
answers.D: Use AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy to attach permissions instead of inline policies.

explanation: Splitting into nested stacks allows exporting the role ARN to avoid circular resource references.

stem: Your infrastructure uses AWS CDK to deploy SageMaker endpoints. A CloudFormation rollback occurs because the endpoint creation takes longer than the default timeout. How can you adjust the timeout in CDK?

answers.A: Set cfnOptions.creationPolicy with a Timeout value on the CfnEndpoint CDK construct.
answers.B: Set the AWS SDK client timeout in CDK context.
answers.C: Use AWS::CloudFormation::WaitCondition within the same stack.
answers.D: Wrap the deployment in a longer-running AWS Step Functions state machine.

explanation: CDK’s cfnOptions.creationPolicy allows specifying timeout for resource creation; other methods don’t apply to SageMaker endpoints.

stem: An ML platform team must deploy hundreds of endpoints with varying instance counts. They choose AWS CDK to loop constructs. How should they write their code to maintain performance and minimize synth time?

answers.A: Use a for loop in CDK to create each endpoint construct directly in the stack.
answers.B: Use AWS::CloudFormation::Stack for each endpoint to parallelize.
answers.C: Generate endpoint configurations via a CDK Construct that iterates over a configuration array at synthesis time, rather than at runtime, and emits only necessary CloudFormation resources.
answers.D: Use AWS Step Functions to call CDK synth for each endpoint separately.

explanation: Constructs iterate at synth time to produce a single CF template; runtime loops in Lambda or Step Functions are inappropriate.

stem: A compliance requirement mandates that all SageMaker endpoints be deployed in dedicated subnets per environment. You already have a CDK VPC with multiple isolated subnet groups. How do you guarantee subnet selection per environment?

answers.A: Hardcode subnet IDs in the CDK code per environment.
answers.B: Define CDK Stack context values for subnetGroupNames per environment and use vpc.selectSubnets({subnetGroupName: ...}).
answers.C: Use AWS::TaggedResource tagging on the VPC and filter subnets via CloudFormation Intrinsics.
answers.D: Use defaultSubnets selection and rely on AWS to pick isolated ones.

explanation: CDK context allows environment-specific parameters; vpc.selectSubnets filters by groupName tag.

stem: Your team wants to use AWS CDK to produce YAML CloudFormation templates for all resources. They need to validate their template for SageMaker endpoint VPC settings before deployment. Which CDK command and plugin should they use?

answers.A: cdk synth --no-staging and the cfn-lint plugin to lint the synthesized template.
answers.B: cdk diff and AWS::SageMaker::ValidateEndpoint API.
answers.C: cdk deploy --dry-run.
answers.D: cdk docs to generate CloudFormation schema and manually inspect.

explanation: cdk synth outputs the template for cfn-lint validation; diff shows changes but not schema errors.

stem: A healthcare provider has a highly imbalanced dataset (1% positive cases) stored in Amazon S3. They need to generate synthetic minority samples to train a disease detection model, ensure PHI compliance (no real patient data leakage), and prevent inversion attacks on synthetic data. Which approach best meets these requirements?

answers.A: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to oversample the minority class and enable record-level masking to anonymize PHI.
answers.B: Implement a CTGAN model in a SageMaker notebook with differential privacy (DP-SGD), generate synthetic samples within a VPC-backed FSx for Lustre, and use a KMS key for encryption.
answers.C: Use SageMaker Clarify’s synthetic data feature to generate samples and store results in an S3 bucket with default encryption.
answers.D: Subscribe to a third-party synthetic health dataset via Amazon Data Exchange and merge it with your S3 data.

explanation: CTGAN with DP-SGD ensures differential privacy (protects against inversion), runs in SageMaker within the VPC, uses FSx for high-performance storage, and KMS encryption prevents PHI leakage, satisfying all requirements.

stem: A bank wants to detect selection bias in its loan application dataset (applicants by ZIP code). They must quantify the difference in proportions of approval rates between urban and rural ZIP codes before training. Which SageMaker Clarify pre-training bias configuration is most appropriate?

answers.A: Use bias_config with 'label'='approval', 'facet_name'='ZIP_code_type', and 'metrics'=['dipl','ci'].
answers.B: Use ModelMonitor with DataQualityMonitor to compute missing values in the ZIP_code_type feature.
answers.C: Use bias_config with 'facet_name'='approval', 'label_values_or_threshold'=['urban','rural'], and 'metrics'=['feature_attribution'].
answers.D: Use Clarify post-training explainability job to get SHAP values for ZIP_code_type.

explanation: Pre-training bias_config must specify label and facet_name (ZIP_code_type) to compute DPL (difference in proportions of labels) and CI (class imbalance) before training. Other options misuse metrics or post-training tools.

stem: An online retailer stores customer data in DynamoDB with encrypted PII (customer_id, email). They export it to S3 for cleaning. They need to mask PII during data cleansing using AWS Glue DataBrew. Which recipe action and configuration should they use?

answers.A: Use 'maskValue' on columns [customer_id,email] with a static masked value.
answers.B: Use 'hash' on columns [customer_id] and 'tokenize' on [email] with default salts.
answers.C: Use 'encrypt' on columns [customer_id,email] using the DynamoDB table key.
answers.D: Use 'maskValue' with 'Mask Type'='Random Character', 'Character Set'='Alphanumeric', on [customer_id,email].

explanation: DataBrew’s maskValue recipe action with Random Character on specified PII columns properly masks values without exposing patterns. Hash and encryption aren’t available as DataBrew recipe actions, and static mask would reveal structure.

stem: A credit-scoring dataset has 10% missing values in the 'employment_length' feature. You need to impute missing values to reduce measurement bias and avoid skew in training. The distribution is right-skewed. What is the best imputation strategy using AWS Glue Data Quality rules?

answers.A: Impute missing 'employment_length' with the mean value computed over all records.
answers.B: Use median imputation per gender group via a DataBrew 'Fill with median' action partitioned by 'gender'.
answers.C: Use a Data Quality job to compute the median per 'employment_type' and then apply DataBrew 'Fill with value from column aggregation' partitioned by 'employment_type'.
answers.D: Apply mode imputation globally for 'employment_length' using the most frequent category.

explanation: Median per employment_type addresses right skew within similar segments and reduces bias. A Data Quality job can compute segment medians and DataBrew can apply partitioned imputation accordingly.

stem: You must ensure all S3 data at rest and in transit is encrypted for an ML training job. Data is loaded from S3 into a SageMaker Training job and stored on an FSx for Lustre file system. Which configuration satisfies both requirements?

answers.A: Enable SSE-KMS on the S3 bucket, attach an IAM role with KMS decrypt, launch FSx with transit encryption enabled and a customer-managed KMS key.
answers.B: Use SSE-S3 on the S3 bucket and launch FSx with default AWS-managed KMS key.
answers.C: Configure SageMaker training input to use SSL and store data in unencrypted FSx.
answers.D: Enable client-side encryption for S3 uploads and use FSx encryption at rest without transit encryption.

explanation: SSE-KMS on S3 and FSx with transit encryption via customer-managed KMS ensure encryption at rest and in transit. SSE-S3 lacks customer KMS control, and client-side or missing transit encryption fails one requirement.

stem: A telco data pipeline streams CDR logs into S3, with PII fields (phone_number) encrypted via KMS. A data scientist needs to preprocess and anonymize phone numbers before modeling using SageMaker Processing. Which approach ensures the data scientist cannot decrypt original values?

answers.A: Provide the processing job with KMS decrypt permissions and apply one-way hash.
answers.B: Use a KMS grant to decrypt phone_number, then pseudonymize with reversible mapping.
