answers.A: Modify the training CodeBuild to throw an exception when accuracy <85% and let the pipeline fail.
answers.B: Use CloudWatch Alarms on CodeBuild logs to alert and pause the pipeline.
answers.C: Write a Lambda in the evaluation stage to call CodePipeline StopPipelineExecution if accuracy <85%.
answers.D: In evaluation CodeBuild, use buildspec checks to fail the build when accuracy <85%, causing the pipeline to stop and send failure notifications.

explanation: Failing the evaluation CodeBuild via buildspec when accuracy <threshold automatically stops the pipeline and triggers failure notifications.

stem: A pipeline must deploy a new ML model version to a real-time endpoint with zero downtime and allow easy rollback. Which deployment strategy and pipeline configuration should be used?

answers.A: Use Lambda to deploy new model to same endpoint container, overwriting existing one.
answers.B: Configure a SageMaker multi-model endpoint in CodePipeline with blue/green deployment via CodeDeploy.
answers.C: Use SageMaker real-time endpoint with WarmPool and update endpoint configuration via CodeBuild.
answers.D: Launch a new endpoint, test it, then delete the old one via a final CodePipeline stage.

explanation: SageMaker multi-model endpoints with CodeDeploy blue/green strategy enable zero-downtime updates and easy rollback.

stem: The team needs to version control SageMaker Pipeline definitions, enforce PR reviews, and automatically trigger pipeline execution when changes are merged. How should they architect this?

answers.A: Store pipeline definitions in a Git repo. Use CodePipeline with Source from CodeCommit, add CodeBuild for linting, and deploy to SageMaker Pipelines using CloudFormation in a later stage.
answers.B: Use SageMaker Studio notebooks directly and rely on manual execution upon merge.
answers.C: Embed pipeline definitions in CodeBuild scripts, trigger on GitHub webhook, and start executions via SDK.
answers.D: Use AWS CDK in local environment, require manual CDK deploy after merge.

explanation: Using CodePipeline Source from CodeCommit with automated linting and CloudFormation deploy ensures version control, PR reviews, and auto-deploy on merge.

stem: A CodePipeline pipeline must orchestrate cross-account deployment of model inference containers. Account A builds and tests the image; Account B deploys to SageMaker. How should roles and permissions be set?

answers.A: In Account A, create an IAM role that trusts Account B’s CodePipeline service principal to push to ECR.
answers.B: In Account B, create a pipeline that assumes the CodeBuild role from Account A to pull images.
answers.C: In Account A’s ECR repository policy, allow pull by a deployment role in Account B. In Account B, create a pipeline with a service role that has pull permissions and assume role rights.
answers.D: Replicate ECR images to Account B automatically via cross-account replication.

explanation: Granting Account B’s pipeline role pull permissions in Account A’s ECR via repository policy allows secure cross-account access for deployment.

stem: A pipeline using AWS CodePipeline must package ML code and dependencies into a container, push to ECR, then deploy to ECS for batch inference. They also need to run unit tests on the packaged image. Which steps should the pipeline include?

answers.A: Source -> Build (Docker build & push) -> Deploy -> Test
answers.B: Source -> Build (Docker build) -> Test -> Deploy
answers.C: Source -> Test -> Build (Docker build & push) -> Deploy
answers.D: Source -> Build (Docker build) -> Test (CodeBuild uses image via local registry) -> Build (Docker push) -> Deploy

explanation: Building the image, running tests locally in CodeBuild, then pushing and deploying ensures integrity before pushing.

stem: An ML team wants to integrate Terraform-managed infrastructure into a CI/CD pipeline for SageMaker endpoint updates. They need a single pipeline. Which service combination achieves this?

answers.A: Use AWS CloudFormation with macros in CodePipeline.
answers.B: Use CodePipeline with Terraform CodeBuild actions: one to plan, manual approval, one to apply changes, then a SageMaker deployment stage.
answers.C: Use AWS CDK in CodeBuild to translate Terraform into CDK and deploy.
answers.D: Trigger Terraform from a Lambda invoked by EventBridge in between CodePipeline stages.

explanation: Running Terraform plan/apply in CodeBuild with approval inside CodePipeline integrates IaC and SageMaker deployments in one pipeline.

stem: Which pattern ensures that data scientists can trigger hyperparameter tuning experiments via pull request merge, with automated notifications on completion?

answers.A: Use CodePipeline triggered by CodeCommit pull request merge. In a CodeBuild stage, invoke SageMaker HPO via AWS CLI. Use CloudWatch Events to notify on job completion.
answers.B: Use SageMaker Experiments SDK manually invoked in notebooks.
answers.C: Configure EventBridge to start tuning on S3 object creation, send SNS on complete.
answers.D: Use Step Functions triggered by CodePipeline Webhook to start tuning.

explanation: CodePipeline on merge, CodeBuild to start tuning, and CloudWatch Events to notify provides CI/CD for experiments.

stem: When integrating a testing framework into CI/CD for ML, the team needs to run data schema validation, unit tests for transformations, and integration tests for training artifacts. How should they structure the CodePipeline?

answers.A: Single build stage running all tests sequentially.
answers.B: Separate pipelines for data tests, code tests, and training.
answers.C: Pipeline with Source -> Data Validation Test (CodeBuild) -> Unit Test (CodeBuild) -> Integration Test (CodeBuild) -> Deploy.
answers.D: Use Step Functions to orchestrate tests outside CodePipeline.

explanation: Separate CodeBuild stages in one pipeline for test types provide clear isolation and failure points.

stem: A compliance requirement mandates that any model deployment must pass through an audit stage capturing approvals in an immutable log. Which service and pipeline step combination satisfies this?

answers.A: Use CloudTrail to log manual approvals in SNS.
answers.B: Use CodeDeploy with manual approval.
answers.C: Use Step Functions Wait state with DynamoDB logging.
answers.D: Use CodePipeline Manual Approval action with execution details logged in CloudTrail.

explanation: CodePipeline Manual Approval action events are logged in CloudTrail, satisfying audit and immutability requirements.

stem: A data scientist merges new featurization code into GitHub. This should automatically update the SageMaker processing step in the CI/CD pipeline. How can this be achieved?

answers.A: Manually update pipeline JSON in S3.
answers.B: Use CodePipeline with a GitHub source action on the repo. Add a CodeBuild stage to synthesize updated pipeline definitions and deploy via CloudFormation update.
answers.C: Write a Lambda to watch GitHub and update SageMaker resources via SDK.
answers.D: Use AWS AppRunner to auto-deploy changes.

explanation: CodePipeline GitHub source plus CodeBuild to update pipeline definitions and CloudFormation deploy automates the update.

stem: Your pipeline uses AWS CodePipeline and CodeBuild to build, test, and deploy containers to SageMaker. You need to ensure that only approved container images are deployed. Which mechanism should you implement?

answers.A: Use ECR image scanning on push, and add a Lambda that checks scan results before CodeDeploy stage.
answers.B: Restrict CodePipeline IAM role to only allow unscanned images.
answers.C: Use a lifecycle policy in ECR to retain only scanned images.
answers.D: Configure CodeBuild to fail if image size exceeds threshold.

explanation: Integrating ECR image scan results via Lambda in the pipeline ensures only approved images proceed to deployment.

stem: The team must enforce that any pipeline change triggers a security compliance scan of both infrastructure and code. Which pattern achieves this end to end?

answers.A: Use Amazon Inspector on EC2 build agents.
answers.B: Use CloudWatch Events to trigger manual security review.
answers.C: In CodePipeline after Source stage, add a CodeBuild stage that runs static code analysis (e.g., cfn-nag) and container vulnerability scans, failing the build on issues.
answers.D: Use AWS Config rules to audit pipeline resources.

explanation: Placing a security scan CodeBuild stage in the pipeline ensures any change undergoes compliance checks before deployment.

stem: You need to orchestrate an ML pipeline that span multiple AWS Regions. How can you centralize pipeline definition and execution?

answers.A: Replicate the pipeline in each region manually.
answers.B: Use Route 53 to direct triggers to regional pipelines.
answers.C: Use EventBridge cross-region events to start different pipelines.
answers.D: Store pipeline code in a central CodeCommit repo and use CodePipeline cross-region actions with CloudFormation to deploy and execute regional pipelines.

explanation: CodePipeline cross-region actions and central repo allow centralized definition while executing region-specific pipelines.

stem: A team wants to provision ephemeral CI/CD infrastructure for each pull request to isolate changes during ML pipeline definition tests. Which approach is most automated and least overhead?

answers.A: Manually launch Cloud9 environments per PR.
answers.B: Use CodePipeline with a CodeBuild job that uses CDK to spin up a nested CloudFormation stack for the PR, runs tests, then tears it down.
answers.C: Use Step Functions to create stacks, run tests, delete stacks.
answers.D: Use AWS Batch to run tests in containers.

explanation: Using CDK in CodeBuild to deploy and teardown nested stacks per PR provides isolation with automation and minimal custom code.

stem: They need to integrate model explainability checks into CI/CD such that if SHAP feature importance shifts beyond threshold in new model, pipeline fails. How to implement?

answers.A: Add a CodeBuild stage using SageMaker Clarify SDK to compute SHAP values, compare them, and exit with failure if threshold exceeded.
answers.B: Use CloudWatch Metrics to monitor SHAP values after deployment.
answers.C: Embed checks in training script to abort training.
answers.D: Deploy model then run real-time inference to compute drift.

explanation: A dedicated CodeBuild stage for Clarify explainability tests before deployment stops the pipeline on SHAP drift.

stem: A centralized security team must approve any pipeline that grants broad IAM permissions. How can the CI/CD pipeline enforce this approval?

answers.A: Use AWS Config to detect wide permissions.
answers.B: Use Lambda to revoke permissions after deployment.
answers.C: Include a Manual Approval action after IAM change stage, before deployment, logged in CodePipeline.
answers.D: Use CloudTrail Insights alerts.

explanation: Manual Approval actions in CodePipeline halt progress until security team approval, fulfilling enforcement and logging.

stem: Your ML pipeline CodeBuild stage needs environment variables stored securely. Which practice provides secure injection and auditability in CI/CD?

answers.A: Store env vars in CodeBuild project settings.
answers.B: Use AWS Secrets Manager, grant CodeBuild role GetSecretValue, inject at runtime.
answers.C: Hard-code secrets in buildspec.
answers.D: Store secrets in S3 with public-read access.

explanation: Secrets Manager integration with CodeBuild provides secure retrieval and auditing; avoids hard-coding or insecure storage.

stem: A pipeline deploys SageMaker endpoints across multiple accounts. The build stage packages a SageMaker Model package. How can you share the model package across accounts securely in the pipeline?

answers.A: Manually copy model artifacts via S3 CLI.
answers.B: Use public S3 bucket for artifacts.
answers.C: Use AWS DMS to migrate artifacts.
answers.D: Use SageMaker Model Package Groups with cross-account grant via resource policy, and use CodePipeline roles to deploy.

explanation: SageMaker Model Package Groups support resource policies for cross-account sharing; CodePipeline roles can assume deploy permissions.

stem: How can you ensure pipeline stages for SageMaker training run on Spot instances to reduce cost, while controlling max runtime for retries?

answers.A: Set TrainingComputeType to ml.p3.2xlarge in pipeline.
answers.B: Use a separate Spot training pipeline.
answers.C: In SageMaker Pipeline TrainStep, specify TrainingInputMode with UseSpotInstances=true and MaxWaitTime/MaxRunTime.
answers.D: Modify IAM policy to allow Spot.

explanation: SageMaker Pipelines TrainStep supports UseSpotInstances and max wait/run time to leverage Spot with retry constraints.

stem: Your pipeline uses CodePipeline with CloudFormation deploy action to create SageMaker Pipeline stacks. The team wants to detect drift between the deployed pipeline definition and source. Which tool helps?

answers.A: Enable CloudFormation Drift Detection on the pipeline stack and integrate a CodeBuild stage to run detect-stack-drift and fail if drifted.
answers.B: Use AWS Config to detect code changes in CodeCommit.
answers.C: Add a Lambda to compare JSON definitions.
answers.D: Use Inspector to scan pipeline definitions.

explanation: CloudFormation Drift Detection identifies config drift; performing it in CodeBuild fails pipeline if drift exists.

stem: A pipeline must orchestrate a nightly batch inference job on new data via SageMaker Processing, then archive results to S3 Glacier. How can this be built in CodePipeline?

answers.A: Use Lambda for processing and then Glacier archive.
answers.B: Define pipeline with Source (EventBridge scheduled start), Processing stage using CodeBuild to call SageMaker Processing, then a Deploy stage to trigger a Lambda copying results to Glacier.
answers.C: Use Step Functions with Lambda tasks.
answers.D: Use Data Pipeline service.

explanation: CodePipeline with an EventBridge-triggered Source and CodeBuild action calling SageMaker Processing, followed by a Lambda archive Deploy stage, meets requirements.

stem: A pipeline deploys model code and container. You need to validate model container performance under load before routing production traffic. Which deployment strategy implements this in CI/CD?

answers.A: Use a single Lambda test after deployment.
answers.B: Deploy to Sagemaker endpoint and test within same stage.
answers.C: Use CodeDeploy with linear deployment configuration, sending small percentage of traffic to new container, run performance tests, then proceed.
answers.D: Use Canary deployments via ECS Blue/Green.

explanation: CodeDeploy linear deployment with traffic shifting and automated tests allows performance validation before full cutover.

stem: They need to incorporate code coverage metrics into their CI/CD pipeline for ML data transformation scripts. How can this be done of minimal complexity?

answers.A: Use CodeBuild to run pytest without coverage and interpret logs.
answers.B: Add a CodeBuild stage that runs pytest with coverage, then use CodeBuild reports feature to publish coverage artifacts.
answers.C: Use Coveralls external service triggered by EventBridge.
answers.D: Manually inspect coverage after each build.

explanation: CodeBuild reports support publishing coverage metrics natively, integrating smoothly in pipelines without external dependencies.

stem: A pipeline failure occurs when deploying to a private VPC endpoint because of missing permissions. Which policy change in CodePipeline role solves this?

answers.A: Add IAM permission for ec2:CreateNetworkInterface, ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces, ec2:DeleteNetworkInterface.
answers.B: Allow s3:GetObject VPC endpoints only.
answers.C: Grant AWSKeyManagementServiceDecrypt in Secrets Manager.
answers.D: Permit TagResource on CloudWatch Logs.

explanation: Deploying to private VPC endpoints requires network interface permissions for CodePipeline-managed actions; adding those resolves the failure.

stem: Your pipeline uses AWS CodeBuild to package and deploy a PyTorch model to SageMaker. The buildspec installs large ML libraries causing slow builds. How to speed up builds without sacrificing reproducibility?

answers.A: Use smaller instance size for CodeBuild.
answers.B: Cache from public PyPI mirror.
answers.C: Use requirement pre-install via pip wheel.
answers.D: Enable CodeBuild local caching for pip and container layers to reuse previous build artifacts.

explanation: CodeBuild local caching for pip and Docker layers significantly speeds up build times while ensuring same dependencies are installed.

stem: They need to rollback to the last successful SageMaker pipeline execution automatically if a new execution fails validation. How can this be configured?

answers.A: Use EventBridge to watch FailedExecution and trigger manual rollback.
answers.B: In SageMaker Pipelines, configure a CallbackStep that on failure starts an execution of the previous pipeline execution using StartPipelineExecution with previous execution id.
answers.C: Use CloudFormation change sets to revert pipeline definition.
answers.D: Use Step Functions with TRY/CATCH to revert.

explanation: SageMaker Pipelines CallbackStep can programmatically invoke a rollback to the last model by triggering an execution of the previous successful pipeline.

stem: A pipeline must enforce that secret rotation and updated credentials are picked up without pipeline definition changes. Which pattern supports this?

answers.A: Hardcode secrets in parameter store with long TTL.
answers.B: Re-deploy pipeline on rotation.
answers.C: Use SSM Parameter Store dynamic references in pipeline actions to retrieve credentials at runtime.
answers.D: Trigger pipeline manually after rotation.

explanation: Using dynamic references to Parameter Store ensures pipeline fetches updated secrets at runtime without redefining the pipeline.

stem: Multiple data teams share a central CI/CD pipeline for SageMaker training. They need isolation so one team’s pipeline failure doesn’t block others. How to configure?

answers.A: Create separate CodePipeline pipelines per team pointing to same buildspec and repos, with individual pipeline resource and IAM roles.
answers.B: Use single pipeline with parallel branches per team.
answers.C: Use Step Functions instead of CodePipeline.
answers.D: Use multi-branch CodeBuild project.

explanation: Separate pipelines per team isolate execution and failures, while sharing code and buildspec for consistency.

stem: A security change requires that any pipeline artifact stored in S3 be encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key. How to enforce this in CodePipeline?

answers.A: Use SSE-S3 default in artifact buckets.
answers.B: Specify encryption in CodeBuild project settings.
answers.C: Use CloudTrail to audit encryption.
answers.D: Configure CodePipeline artifact store with KMS key ARN in the pipeline definition.

explanation: Defining the artifactStore with a specific KMS key ARN in the pipeline ensures all pipeline artifacts are encrypted accordingly.

stem: A fraud-detection model is trained on a dataset where fraudulent cases are only 1% of the data. The model achieves 99% accuracy on a test set, but the business indicates that many frauds are missed. Which evaluation metric would most appropriately reflect the model’s ability to detect fraud?

answers.A: Overall accuracy on the test set
answers.B: ROC AUC
answers.C: Precision-Recall AUC
answers.D: Log-loss

explanation: With extreme class imbalance, overall accuracy and ROC AUC can be misleading. Precision-Recall AUC focuses on the positive (fraud) class and better reflects detection capability.

stem: A classifier on a highly imbalanced dataset yields ROC AUC = 0.95 but PR AUC = 0.4. What does this indicate, and what should you do next?

answers.A: The model discriminates well overall but has low precision on positives; tune the decision threshold to improve precision.
answers.B: The model is reliable; deploy it as is.
answers.C: The dataset is too balanced; rebalance it further.
answers.D: Collect more negative samples to improve ROC AUC.

explanation: High ROC AUC with low PR AUC shows many false positives. Adjusting the classification threshold based on PR curve can improve precision for the rare positive class.

stem: Your legacy model’s F1 score on the production validation set is 0.85. A new candidate model scores 0.87. To determine if this improvement is statistically significant, you should:

answers.A: Automatically deploy the new model because 0.87>0.85
answers.B: Perform a simple paired t-test on the F1 scores
answers.C: Use bootstrap sampling on hold-out data to compute confidence intervals of F1 difference
answers.D: Compare scores on a single test set without intervals

explanation: Bootstrap sampling yields confidence intervals on the difference in F1, allowing you to assess statistical significance rather than relying on point estimates.

stem: During training, your deep network’s training loss plateaus very early and validation loss remains high. Which SageMaker Debugger rule should you enable to diagnose this convergence issue?

answers.A: VanishingGradient
answers.B: LossNotDecreasing
answers.C: WeightUpdate
answers.D: OverfitDetection

explanation: The LossNotDecreasing rule alerts when training loss fails to decrease. VanishingGradient detects near-zero gradients, but first you must confirm loss stagnation with LossNotDecreasing.

stem: Your model achieves 100% training accuracy but only 60% validation accuracy. Which approach best detects and visualizes this overfitting?

answers.A: Plot training and validation loss curves using SageMaker Debugger
answers.B: Compute final confusion matrix on test set
answers.C: Inspect global SHAP values
answers.D: Monitor data quality with ModelMonitor

explanation: Plotting training vs validation loss curves identifies divergence indicative of overfitting; SageMaker Debugger automates rule-based collection of these tensors.

stem: You wish to conduct an A/B test between your production and shadow model variants using SageMaker endpoints. Which configuration allows a traffic split between variants?

answers.A: Deploy two separate endpoints and manually route traffic
answers.B: Use a multi-model endpoint with two models loaded
answers.C: Create an endpoint configuration with two production variants and specify traffic weights
answers.D: Use AWS CodePipeline to shift traffic between endpoints

explanation: Endpoint configurations in SageMaker allow multiple production variants with specified traffic weights for A/B testing without separate endpoints.

stem: Model A has F1 = 0.92 and requires 12 hours training; Model B has F1 = 0.91 and requires 1 hour. Retraining occurs weekly. Which model should you deploy, and why?

answers.A: Model A, because maximizing F1 is paramount
answers.B: Model B, because the small F1 loss is outweighed by 12× faster retraining
answers.C: Deploy both and ensemble
answers.D: Alternate weekly between A and B

explanation: In a weekly retraining pipeline, a 1% F1 reduction is acceptable given the 12× speedup, reducing compute cost and risk of stale models.

stem: You need to monitor inference data streams for feature distribution changes in production. Which SageMaker capability and baseline type will you use?

answers.A: ModelQualityMonitor with a model quality baseline
answers.B: ModelBiasMonitor with a bias baseline
answers.C: ModelExplainabilityMonitor with SHAP baseline
answers.D: ModelMonitor DataQualityMonitor with a data quality baseline

explanation: ModelMonitor’s DataQualityMonitor uses a data quality baseline to detect feature distribution drifts in incoming inference data.

stem: A particular prediction’s SHAP value for feature X is +2.5. What does this imply for that instance?

answers.A: Feature X increased the model’s output log-odds by 2.5 for this instance
answers.B: Feature X is the most important globally
answers.C: The model is biased toward feature X
answers.D: SHAP values above 0 indicate uncertainty

explanation: A positive SHAP value indicates that feature X contributed positively to the prediction (in log-odds space for classification) for that specific instance.

stem: You want to track hyperparameters, metrics, and artifacts across multiple training runs in SageMaker. Which feature provides built-in experiment management?

answers.A: SageMaker Experiments with trials and trial components
answers.B: SageMaker Clarify
answers.C: Resource tagging
answers.D: CloudWatch Logs

explanation: SageMaker Experiments lets you organize runs into experiments and trials, capturing hyperparameters, metrics, and artifacts for reproducibility.

stem: Your regression model will be used in a financial application where large errors are severely penalized. Which evaluation metric should you prefer?

answers.A: Root Mean Square Error (RMSE)
answers.B: Mean Absolute Error (MAE)
answers.C: R² (coefficient of determination)
answers.D: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE)

explanation: RMSE penalizes larger errors quadratically, aligning with applications that severely penalize large deviations.

stem: To optimize for recall over precision in a binary classifier, you decide to adjust the decision threshold. How should you determine the new threshold?

answers.A: Set threshold to 0.5 regardless of metrics
answers.B: Maximize accuracy on validation data
answers.C: Use the threshold that maximizes ROC AUC
answers.D: Analyze the precision-recall curve to find the point achieving the desired recall

explanation: Precision-recall curves show trade-offs for different thresholds; selecting the threshold that meets your recall requirement is appropriate.

stem: You have a multi-class classification problem with imbalanced class frequencies. You want each class to contribute equally to overall performance. Which averaging strategy do you use for F1 score?

answers.A: Micro average
answers.B: Macro average
answers.C: Weighted average
answers.D: Sample average

explanation: Macro-averaged F1 computes F1 per class then averages equally, ensuring each class contributes equally despite imbalance.

stem: Your model is deployed in a streaming inference pipeline. You need to detect sudden drops in model accuracy over recent data without storing all predictions. Which approach is best?

answers.A: Query historical S3 logs daily
answers.B: Compute a one-off accuracy on a large batch
answers.C: Use SageMaker Model Monitor with a sliding window and accuracy rule
answers.D: Use CloudWatch Metrics alone

explanation: Model Monitor can continuously compute metrics over sliding windows on production data without storing all raw predictions.

stem: Business requirements specify that predicted loan amounts must not decrease as applicant income increases. Which technique helps you verify this monotonic relationship in your deployed model?

answers.A: Generate a partial dependence plot (PDP) for income
answers.B: Examine the confusion matrix
answers.C: Use a data drift baseline
answers.D: Calculate overall RMSE

explanation: A PDP shows the average model prediction as a function of a feature, allowing you to verify monotonicity constraints.

stem: You suspect your neural network is overfitting early in training. Which SageMaker Debugger built-in rule can alert you when validation loss starts increasing while training loss decreases?

answers.A: LossNotDecreasing
answers.B: VanishingGradient
answers.C: Overflow
answers.D: Overfit

explanation: The Overfit rule in SageMaker Debugger flags when validation loss increases while training loss continues to decrease, a sign of overfitting.

stem: Given confusion matrix counts TP=80, FP=20, FN=10, TN=890, what is the false positive rate (FPR)?
You want to evaluate if two classifiers produce significantly different error rates on the same test set. Which statistical test is most appropriate?

answers.A: Paired t-test on accuracy scores
answers.B: McNemar’s test
answers.C: Chi-square test for independence
answers.D: Wilcoxon signed-rank test

explanation: McNemar’s test compares paired categorical outcomes (correct vs incorrect) from two classifiers on the same instances.

stem: After deployment, your model’s input distribution remains stable but prediction error gradually increases. What type of drift does this indicate?

answers.A: Covariate shift
answers.B: Label shift
answers.C: Data drift
answers.D: Concept drift

explanation: Concept drift occurs when the relationship between inputs and targets changes, causing error to rise despite stable input distribution.

stem: You observe gradients in the first layers of your network are vanishing, slowing learning. Which SageMaker Debugger rule detects this issue directly?

answers.A: VanishingGradient
answers.B: LossNotDecreasing
answers.C: Detection of hung jobs
answers.D: WeightDecay

explanation: The VanishingGradient rule monitors gradient norms and flags when they are near zero, indicating vanishing gradients.

stem: Your pruned model achieves 40% size reduction with only a 0.5% drop in accuracy. To decide whether to deploy it, you should analyze:

answers.A: Only the accuracy difference
answers.B: The trade-off between resource savings (memory, latency) and accuracy loss
answers.C: Global SHAP importance values
answers.D: Training time differences

explanation: Deployment decisions should weigh resource savings (e.g., reduced latency, memory) against any drop in accuracy to determine overall benefit.

stem: You want to assess whether your classifier’s probability outputs are well calibrated. Which metric or tool should you use?

answers.A: ROC AUC
answers.B: Precision-Recall AUC
answers.C: Log-loss (cross-entropy)
answers.D: F1 score

explanation: Log-loss penalizes incorrect probability estimates and is sensitive to calibration, making it suitable for assessing probability calibration.

stem: You need to compare model performance across multiple user segments (e.g., age groups) and give equal importance to each segment. Which aggregation of segment-level AUC metrics should you use?

answers.A: Arithmetic mean of AUC for each segment
answers.B: Overall AUC on combined data
answers.C: Weighted average by segment size
answers.D: Maximum AUC across segments

explanation: The unweighted (arithmetic) mean of segment-level AUCs treats each segment equally regardless of its size.

stem: Your cost matrix penalizes false negatives at 10× the cost of false positives. Which evaluation metric best aligns with this cost sensitivity?

answers.A: Expected cost computed from confusion matrix and cost weights
answers.B: ROC AUC
answers.C: Log-loss
answers.D: Overall accuracy

explanation: Computing the expected cost directly using confusion matrix counts and cost weights aligns evaluation with your business cost matrix.

stem: A model shows high overall accuracy but a high false negative rate on a protected group. To monitor fairness over time, which metric should you track with SageMaker Clarify?

answers.A: Overall RMSE
answers.B: ROC AUC
answers.C: Data drift percentage
answers.D: Difference in true positive rates (equal opportunity difference)

explanation: Equal opportunity difference measures TPR gap between groups, highlighting unfair false negatives for protected attributes.

stem: To detect label distribution changes in production (label drift), which SageMaker Model Monitor job and baseline do you configure?

answers.A: ModelQualityMonitor with a label distribution baseline
answers.B: DataQualityMonitor with feature baseline
answers.C: ModelBiasMonitor with bias baseline
answers.D: ModelExplainabilityMonitor with SHAP baseline

explanation: ModelQualityMonitor can track label statistics in inference data against a baseline to detect label drift.

stem: You need to choose a threshold for a binary classifier that minimizes a custom cost function of TPR and FPR. Which process accomplishes this?

answers.A: Select threshold = 0.5
answers.B: Maximize ROC AUC
answers.C: Minimize log-loss
answers.D: Compute cost for each threshold on validation probabilities and choose the minimum

explanation: Evaluating the custom cost at each threshold on validation data lets you select the threshold minimizing your cost function.

stem: Your regression model predicts three related targets simultaneously. To evaluate performance treating each target equally, you should:

answers.A: Compute RMSE per target and report their average
answers.B: Compute overall RMSE across all predictions
answers.C: Weight each target by its variance in a single loss
answers.D: Report only the highest RMSE target

explanation: Averaging per-target RMSE ensures each output is given equal importance in performance evaluation.

stem: Your classifier’s test set performance fluctuates significantly between runs. Which validation technique reduces variance and yields a more stable performance estimate?

answers.A: K-fold cross-validation
answers.B: Using a single larger test set
answers.C: Bootstrapping only
answers.D: Early stopping

explanation: K-fold cross-validation averages performance over multiple splits, reducing variance due to data sampling.

stem: You want to visualize model performance degradation over time in production. Which solution best automates this?

answers.A: Export logs daily and plot manually
answers.B: Use SageMaker Model Monitor to publish quality metrics to CloudWatch dashboards
answers.C: Run ad-hoc batch accuracy reports
answers.D: Embed metrics in application code

explanation: Model Monitor can stream quality metrics to CloudWatch, allowing automated dashboards tracking performance over time.

stem: You see a sudden increase in false positives without any change in input distribution. What type of drift is this, and what action should you take?

answers.A: Covariate drift; retrain on new features
answers.B: Concept drift; investigate changes in the real world and retrain
answers.C: Data drift; increase data validation
answers.D: Label shift; adjust class weights

explanation: A rise in error despite stable inputs indicates concept drift; investigate underlying changes and retrain the model accordingly.

stem: Observation of rapidly growing gradient norms across layers suggests exploding gradients. Which SageMaker Debugger rule will catch this?

answers.A: VanishingGradient
answers.B: LossNotDecreasing
answers.C: ExplodingGradient
answers.D: WeightDecay

explanation: The ExplodingGradient rule monitors for abnormally large gradient norms, flagging exploding gradient issues.

stem: You use SageMaker Clarify to monitor feature attribution drift. Which monitor type and baseline should you configure?

answers.A: ModelExplainabilityMonitor with a SHAP value baseline
answers.B: DataQualityMonitor with a distribution baseline
answers.C: ModelBiasMonitor with bias all baseline
answers.D: ModelQualityMonitor with accuracy baseline

explanation: ModelExplainabilityMonitor compares new SHAP attributions against a baseline to detect feature attribution drift.

stem: A data engineer needs to join a 1 TB Parquet dataset in Amazon S3 with a DynamoDB table of product metadata and register features in SageMaker Feature Store daily with minimal operational overhead and within a 2-hour window. Which approach should the engineer choose?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to import both datasets, perform the join, then execute a BatchPutRecord job to ingest features into Feature Store.
answers.B: Schedule an AWS Glue ETL job to read the Parquet data, use the DynamoDB Spark connector to join the tables, write results back to S3, and trigger a SageMaker processing job to ingest into Feature Store.
answers.C: Set up AWS Glue Streaming ETL to capture DynamoDB Streams updates and continuously merge against S3 data, writing directly into the online store.
answers.D: Deploy an AWS Lambda function triggered by each S3 PUT to read and join records on the fly, then call PutRecord for each feature into Feature Store.

explanation: Scheduling a bulk AWS Glue ETL job best handles 1 TB batch processing within a time window and decouples transformation from per-record Lambda overhead.

stem: A feature team must encode a categorical feature with 10 million distinct values for use in a neural network. They need to minimize memory and avoid introducing ordinal bias. Which encoding technique and pipeline step should they implement?

answers.A: Use one-hot encoding in SageMaker Data Wrangler to generate 10 million binary columns, then apply feature selection.
answers.B: Apply label encoding in DataBrew, converting each category to an integer index, and feed directly to the network.
answers.C: Use feature hashing in a SageMaker processing job to map categories into a fixed-size hash vector, then normalize hashed features.
answers.D: Group rare categories into an "Other" bucket before one-hot encoding in AWS Glue ETL.

explanation: Feature hashing maps high-cardinality categories into a fixed-size vector without ordinal bias and controls memory footprint.

stem: A time-series dataset has irregular timestamps and missing readings. A data scientist needs to impute missing values and generate lag features in SageMaker Data Wrangler for model training. Which sequence of transformations should they apply?

answers.A: Resample to a fixed interval with forward-fill imputation, compute lag features using the shifted timestamp, then scale features.
answers.B: Compute lag features first (with gaps), drop NA, then apply KNN imputation to fill missing values.
answers.C: Apply drop-rows where any null exists, generate lag features on remaining data, and finally apply standard scaling.
answers.D: Use quantile imputation on raw data, then apply rolling window aggregations for lag features, and normalize.

explanation: Resampling with forward fill ensures consistent intervals before computing lags; then scaling preserves temporal relationships.

stem: A large training dataset in S3 must be deduplicated by a composite key before feature scaling. The data volume exceeds what a single SageMaker Data Wrangler instance can process. What architecture meets the requirements?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler with distributed compute enabled for dedupe and scaling.
answers.B: Use an AWS Lambda function to split and dedupe small partitions, then reassemble.
answers.C: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to dedupe by key and apply scaling transformations inline.
answers.D: Use an AWS Glue Spark job on EMR to dedupe by composite key, write results to Parquet in S3, then use Data Wrangler for scaling on the reduced dataset.

explanation: A Spark job on EMR can handle large-scale deduplication; downstream Data Wrangler can operate efficiently on the smaller deduped data.

stem: A team must apply quantile binning on a continuous feature to reduce noise, then one-hot encode the bins. They need to evaluate bin edges on training only and apply identical bins to validation/test sets. How should they implement this in SageMaker Data Wrangler?

answers.A: Create a recipe step to compute quantile bin edges on the training partition, save edges as a parameter, then apply same edges in subsequent steps to all partitions before one-hot.
answers.B: Compute quantile bin edges over full dataset in Data Wrangler, then split into train/validation/test and one-hot encode separately.
answers.C: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to compute bins on training, export bin definitions, then import back into Data Wrangler for splits.
answers.D: Perform quantile binning and one-hot encoding in a SageMaker processing job where edges are recomputed per batch.

explanation: Computing bins on training only and saving edges ensures no leakage; applying stored edges uniformly maintains consistency.

stem: A streaming application ingests clickstream JSON records into Kinesis and needs to parse, clean, and feature-engineer fields in near real-time. Which architecture minimizes latency and offloads transformation operations?

answers.A: Use AWS Lambda to poll Kinesis, transform records inline, then push to SageMaker Feature Store.
answers.B: Write a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream with inline record transformation using AWS Glue.
answers.C: Deploy a Kinesis Data Analytics (Apache Flink) application to parse JSON, apply scalar and one-hot encodings, then write transformed records to an output stream.
answers.D: Use SageMaker Processing on a schedule to pull batches from Kinesis and process them.

explanation: Kinesis Data Analytics with Apache Flink provides low-latency, continuous transformations at scale, offloading work from Lambda.

stem: A pipeline must mask PII columns before any transformations to comply with compliance. They have CSV data with 5 sensitive columns. Using AWS Glue DataBrew, which recipe steps ordering ensures compliance and minimal reprocessing?

answers.A: Apply all feature scaling, encoding, and missing-value imputation, then mask PII at the end.
answers.B: Mask PII using column-level encryption, then apply transformations in the same recipe.
answers.C: Branch the job: first do transformation, output safe data; second, mask PII on original and join results.
answers.D: Create two DataBrew steps: first mask (using built-in Mask Column), then reference masked columns in subsequent transformation steps.

explanation: Masking PII first in the recipe prevents any downstream steps from accessing raw PII and avoids reprocessing masked data.

stem: A dataset contains a categorical feature with moderate cardinality and missing values. A data scientist wants to impute missing values as "Unknown" before one-hot encoding in SageMaker Data Wrangler. Which setting order in the recipe is correct?

answers.A: One-hot encode first, then treat missing values in generated dummy columns.
answers.B: Apply a Fill Missing Values step on the raw column to "Unknown", then apply a One-Hot Encoding step on the filled column.
answers.C: Drop rows with missing values, then one-hot encode remaining categories.
answers.D: Run one-hot encoding with the "Include Nulls" option, then rename the "null" column to "Unknown".

explanation: Imputing missing values before encoding ensures the "Unknown" category is represented correctly in the dummy variables.

stem: A text feature requires tokenization and vectorization using a pretrained BERT tokenizer. They need to integrate this into a SageMaker feature engineering pipeline. Which approach is best?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler built-in text tokenizer step with custom vocabulary.
answers.B: Invoke AWS Comprehend batch API to tokenize, then import tokens to Data Wrangler.
answers.C: Build a SageMaker Processing script container that loads the pretrained BERT tokenizer, tokenizes text, and writes token IDs to S3 for the next pipeline step.
answers.D: Use AWS Glue Spark job to apply the BERT tokenizer via a Glue Python shell job.

explanation: A custom processing container in SageMaker Processing provides full control over the pretrained tokenizer and integrates cleanly into ML pipelines.

stem: A data scientist wants to scale numeric features using Z-score normalization but only using statistics from the training set. They plan to scale validation/test sets identically. How can they configure SageMaker Data Wrangler?

answers.A: Apply Z-score normalization in a DataBrew recipe after splitting, selecting all partitions together.
answers.B: Use a SageMaker Processing job to compute mean/std on full dataset, then scale each partition separately in Data Wrangler.
answers.C: In Data Wrangler, split the dataset into train/validation/test, add a Normalize step in the recipe that refers to the training split only, and ensure the recipe applies the same parameters to other splits.
answers.D: Compute mean/std manually outside of Data Wrangler and hard-code values in a recipe.

explanation: Data Wrangler can compute normalization parameters on the training split and apply them uniformly to other splits within one recipe.

stem: During a SageMaker Data Wrangler flow, a shuffle step is added before splitting data into train/validation/test. The resulting model shows data leakage. What was the mistake?

answers.A: Shuffling after splitting caused overlap across sets.
answers.B: Shuffle did not include seed, producing non-reproducible splits.
answers.C: Shuffle was applied only to the training split, leaving test data ordered.
answers.D: Shuffle was applied before splitting, mixing records across temporal boundaries and causing leakage.

explanation: Shuffling before splitting time-series or grouped data can mix related records across splits, introducing leakage.

stem: A data engineer needs to generate rolling window statistics (mean, std) per user over the last 7 days from clickstream JSON data in S3. Data volume is 500 GB/month. Which cost-effective approach should they use?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to load all data and compute rolling stats with Python transforms.
answers.B: Use an AWS Glue Spark job with window functions to compute rolling statistics, write Parquet outputs back to S3.
answers.C: Load raw data into DynamoDB and use DynamoDB Streams with Lambda to update rolling metrics.
answers.D: Use SageMaker Feature Store with on-the-fly aggregation in training jobs.

explanation: A Glue Spark job with window functions scales to 500 GB and performs aggregations efficiently before model input.

stem: A team must remove outliers defined as values beyond 3 standard deviations for a numeric feature. They want to log how many records were removed. In SageMaker Data Wrangler, how should they configure this?

answers.A: Add a Filter recipe step to remove outliers, then use the Data Wrangler UI to view counts after run.
answers.B: Use a Custom Transform step with a Pandas script to drop outliers and log metrics to CloudWatch.
answers.C: Add an Aggregate Recipe step to calculate mean/std, then a Filter step referencing those values, and enable the record count output option to capture removed record counts.
answers.D: Export data to a processing job, implement outlier removal in code, and write counts to S3.

explanation: Data Wrangler’s recipe can calculate statistics and filter in separate steps, and the built-in count option provides removal metrics.

stem: A feature store offline dataset must be kept in sync with latest transformations from SageMaker Data Wrangler. Which mechanism ensures atomic replacement without downtime?

answers.A: Write transformed data to a staging S3 prefix, then use CFN to update the offline store import job to point to new prefix.
answers.B: Overwrite the existing S3 prefix directly with new Parquet files in place.
answers.C: Append new transformed data to the existing prefix, and use a Glue crawler to update partitions.
answers.D: Delete the offline store table and recreate it with new data after transformation.

explanation: Using a staging prefix and atomic pointer switch avoids partial reads and downtime.

stem: Continuous feature updates from AWS IoT devices stream into Kinesis Data Streams. A data scientist needs to window, normalize, and encode features before writing to Feature Store online. What real-time pipeline minimizes component count?

answers.A: Use Kinesis Data Firehose with AWS Lambda transform to process and send to Feature Store.
answers.B: Use a SageMaker endpoint to receive raw records, transform, and BatchPutRecord.
answers.C: Use AWS Glue Streaming ETL job to read, transform, and write to Feature Store offline.
answers.D: Deploy Kinesis Data Analytics (Apache Flink) application to window, normalize, encode, and call PutRecord API to Feature Store online.

explanation: Kinesis Data Analytics provides a single low-latency stream processing engine capable of calling AWS APIs directly.

stem: An image classification pipeline needs to apply resizing, normalization, and five types of augmentation (rotation, flip, crop, noise, color jitter) in SageMaker processing. To maximize GPU utilization and reproducibility, what should the team do?

answers.A: Chain multiple processing jobs sequentially, each handling one augmentation type.
answers.B: Use a single SageMaker Processing job with a PyTorch container that applies resizing, normalization, and augmentations in one GPU-accelerated DataLoader pipeline.
answers.C: Implement augmentations in AWS Lambda functions triggered by S3 events for each image.
answers.D: Use Data Wrangler custom transform steps for each preprocessing function and export as a combined dataset.

explanation: A single GPU-accelerated processing job with PyTorch DataLoader ensures reproducibility and efficient parallel augmentation.

stem: A dataset contains repeated nested JSON fields that must be flattened for feature extraction. In AWS Glue DataBrew, which recipe step correctly handles arbitrary nesting levels?

answers.A: Use a Pivot recipe step on the nested column.
answers.B: Use a Select recipe step and specify JSONPath for each nested field.
answers.C: Use a Join recipe step with the same column.
answers.D: Use the Unnest recipe step to iteratively flatten nested JSON arrays and objects into top-level columns.

explanation: The Unnest step is designed to flatten arbitrarily nested JSON structures into columns automatically.

stem: A feature with highly skewed distribution needs log transformation before scaling. A data scientist wants to ensure negative values are handled. In Data Wrangler, what transformation sequence should be used?

answers.A: Scale feature with MinMax, then apply log transform.
answers.B: Add a constant offset to make values positive, apply log transform, then standardize.
answers.C: Apply Box-Cox transformation directly (Box-Cox cannot handle negatives).
answers.D: Filter out negative values, then apply log transform on positives.

explanation: Adding a constant offset ensures all values are positive before log transform; standardizing afterwards preserves distribution.

stem: A team must detect and drop duplicate records defined by a composite key, but preserve the earliest timestamp record. They want to log count of dropped duplicates. What is the correct approach in Data Wrangler?

answers.A: Use the Remove Duplicates recipe step on the composite key then sort ascending by timestamp.
answers.B: Sort by timestamp and use the Remove Duplicates step without additional configuration.
answers.C: Sort descending by timestamp, then use the Remove Duplicates step on the composite key with "keep first occurrence" and enable Logging to capture drop counts.
answers.D: Use a Custom Transform step with a Pandas script to drop duplicates and write counts to CloudWatch.

explanation: Sorting descending ensures the earliest timestamp is last, then keeping the first occurrence drops later duplicates and logs counts.

stem: A text corpus requires feature hashing of TF-IDF vectors into 512 dimensions before training. Which SageMaker toolchain should be used and why?

answers.A: Use a SageMaker Processing job with a scikit-learn container to compute TF-IDF and apply FeatureHasher transformer in one job.
answers.B: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to compute TF-IDF and hashing in recipe steps.
answers.C: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler built-in TF-IDF and hashing steps.
answers.D: Use AWS Lambda to compute and hash vectors on each record.

explanation: A processing job with scikit-learn provides efficient batch computation of TF-IDF and hashing integrated into the ML pipeline.

stem: A feature store batch export job must produce engineered features that include one-hot encoded categories and normalized numerics. The export time window is 24 hours. Which orchestration ensures reproducibility and minimal drift?

answers.A: Manually run a Data Wrangler flow to export features daily.
answers.B: Schedule a Lambda that calls PutRecord for each export.
answers.C: Use AWS Glue job to read offline store and apply transformations at export time.
answers.D: Define a SageMaker Feature Store Batch Transform pipeline with saved Data Wrangler recipe steps to export and transform atomically.

explanation: Embedding Data Wrangler recipe in a Feature Store batch pipeline ensures consistent transformations and reproducibility.

stem: A data scientist wants to detect measurement bias in labeled data prior to model training. Which AWS tool and workflow should they use?

answers.A: Use AWS Glue Data Quality to compute missing value rates per label.
answers.B: Use SageMaker Clarify’s Data Bias job to generate pre-training bias metrics (e.g., CI, DPL) and produce a report for review.
answers.C: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to compute feature distributions per class.
answers.D: Use Amazon Athena to run SQL queries comparing label distributions across partitions.

explanation: SageMaker Clarify is specifically designed to compute pre-training bias metrics and provide actionable reports.

stem: An offline Spark feature pipeline writes to Parquet partitioned by date. A validation job must only process the latest two days and ignore older partitions. How can they configure an AWS Glue job?

answers.A: Use a dynamic frame with push_down_predicate on the date partition to filter to last two days before transformation.
answers.B: Read all partitions and filter in code.
answers.C: Use a Glue crawler to catalog only two latest partitions.
answers.D: Use AWS Glue DataBrew with a filter recipe to drop older partitions.

explanation: Using push_down_predicate filters partitions at read time, reducing data scanned and improving performance.

stem: A feature requires ranking users by activity per region, generating a rank feature. Which tool and technique should they use to compute this in a SageMaker pipeline?

answers.A: Use AWS Glue DataBrew with window aggregate recipe step.
answers.B: Use a SageMaker Processing job with pure Python for ranking.
answers.C: Use SageMaker Processing with a Spark container to apply window ranking functions by region, writing results to S3.
answers.D: Use Lambda and Step Functions to orchestrate row-by-row ranking.

explanation: A Spark container in a processing job can efficiently compute window functions and scale to large user sets.

stem: During a Data Wrangler flow, a customer ID column is misclassified as numeric, preventing correct encoding. How can this be fixed?

answers.A: Drop the column and reload.
answers.B: Override the inferred data type to String in the Data Wrangler schema settings, then apply categorical encoding.
answers.C: Cast the column inside a custom transform only.
answers.D: Use AWS Glue job to recast and save back to S3 before Data Wrangler.

explanation: Overriding the schema inference directly in Data Wrangler allows correct downstream categorical encoding without external ETL.

stem: A data scientist must anonymize email addresses by hashing them before any aggregation. The hashing function must be consistent across training and inference. How should they implement this in a SageMaker processing pipeline?

answers.A: Use a Data Wrangler custom step with Python hashing, then export hashed emails.
answers.B: Use AWS Glue DataBrew Mask Column with SHA256.
answers.C: Use a Lambda function triggered by S3 events to hash emails.
answers.D: Include a SageMaker Processing step with a custom container that applies SHA256 to the email column and writes to Parquet for downstream use.

explanation: A custom processing step ensures identical hashing logic in both training and inference pipelines.

stem: A dataset of IoT sensor readings requires deduplication, imputation of missing values using KNN, and feature scaling. Which order in a DataBrew recipe ensures correct results and performance?

answers.A: Scale, dedupe, then KNN impute.
answers.B: Deduplicate first, KNN impute missing values, then apply scaling.
answers.C: Impute missing values first, then dedupe, then scale.
answers.D: Perform all three in parallel using branching steps.

explanation: Deduplication should occur before imputation to avoid artificial neighbors; scaling is last to ensure normalized neighbor distances.

stem: A team needs to apply custom Python feature transformations (e.g., trigonometric functions) on numeric columns and integrate into SageMaker Pipelines. Which component should they use?

answers.A: A SageMaker Processing step with a custom Python script container.
answers.B: A Data Wrangler custom recipe step.
answers.C: A Lambda function in CodePipeline.
answers.D: AWS Glue DataBrew Python transforms.

explanation: A SageMaker Processing step in the pipeline allows custom scripts and integrates directly with SageMaker Pipelines.

stem: A dataset transformation in Data Wrangler fails due to schema drift: new columns appear. How can the recipe handle unknown columns without failing?

answers.A: Manually update the recipe to include new columns each time.
answers.B: Restrict the flow to specified columns only and drop unknown ones.
answers.C: Enable the "Ignore new columns" option in the Data Wrangler recipe settings to skip unknown fields.
answers.D: Use a SageMaker Processing job instead for dynamic schema.

explanation: Data Wrangler’s ignore new columns setting prevents failures when unexpected fields appear.

stem: A table join in SageMaker Data Wrangler is running out of memory because one table is 200 GB. Which alternative solution scales to this size?

answers.A: Increase the Data Wrangler instance type to more memory.
answers.B: Perform the join using an AWS Glue Spark ETL job and write result to S3, then import into Data Wrangler.
answers.C: Use a SageMaker Processing job with Pandas on a GPU instance.
answers.D: Split the larger table into chunks and join sequentially in Data Wrangler.

explanation: An AWS Glue Spark ETL job is designed to handle large-scale joins and can write partitioned outputs for downstream use.

stem: A feature extraction requires computing pairwise differences between two timestamp columns per record. Which recipe step in Data Wrangler should they choose and why?

answers.A: Use the Compute Feature step with a custom expression (timestamp2 - timestamp1) to derive duration.
answers.B: Use the Aggregate step grouping on record ID.
answers.C: Use the Pivot step on timestamp fields.
answers.D: Use a Custom Transform with a Pandas script to compute differences.

explanation: The Compute Feature step allows arithmetic expressions on columns and is more efficient than full Python transforms.

stem: A team must ensure that text tokenization and stop-word removal occur before computing count vector features in a Data Wrangler flow. How should they configure the recipe?

answers.A: Add Count Vectorization step, then Tokenization, then Stop-word removal.
answers.B: Add Stop-word removal, then Count Vectorization, then Tokenization.
answers.C: Add Tokenization, then Count Vectorization, then Stop-word removal.
answers.D: Add Tokenization, then Stop-word removal step, then Count Vectorization in sequence.

explanation: Tokenization must split text first, followed by stop-word removal on tokens, then count vectorization.

stem: A dataset stored as CSV in S3 must be converted to Parquet with snappy compression before feature engineering to improve I/O. Which tool and configuration should be used?

answers.A: Use a SageMaker Processing job with a Pandas script to read CSV and write Parquet.
answers.B: Use an AWS Glue ETL job with a PySpark script to read CSV, write Parquet with snappy compression, and partition by date.
answers.C: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler export with Parquet output and compression.
answers.D: Use AWS Lambda triggered per file to invoke Athena CTAS to create Parquet tables.

explanation: An AWS Glue Spark ETL job is well-suited for large-scale CSV to Parquet conversion with compression and partitioning.

stem: A company must ingest 10 TB of historical telemetry data from an on-premises Hadoop cluster into Amazon S3 within 5 days for model training. The WAN link is limited to 200 Mbps and encryption at rest is required. Which ingestion method meets the transfer window while minimizing operational overhead?

answers.A: Use AWS Snowball Edge to physically import the data into S3 with built-in encryption.
answers.B: Use S3 Transfer Acceleration over the internet with SSE-S3 encryption.
answers.C: Use AWS DataSync over the existing link with server-side encryption.
answers.D: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway in Volume mode and snapshot to S3.

explanation: Snowball Edge provides accelerated, encrypted bulk transfer when network bandwidth is constrained, minimizing operational overhead.

stem: An ML pipeline queries 500 GB of transaction logs in S3 via Athena, then ingests the results into SageMaker Data Wrangler. Which storage format and partitioning maximize query performance and minimize costs?

answers.A: Store logs as CSV files partitioned by year/month.
answers.B: Store logs as JSON files partitioned by customer ID.
answers.C: Store logs as Apache Parquet files partitioned by date.
answers.D: Store logs as unpartitioned text files in a single prefix.

explanation: Parquet’s columnar format plus date partitioning reduces scanned data and cost for Athena queries and speeds ingestion.

stem: A real-time anomaly detection model requires streaming sensor data into S3 for batch retraining. Which combination of services ingests JSON records at low latency with ordering guarantees?

answers.A: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivering directly to S3.
answers.B: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams then a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to S3.
answers.C: AWS Glue streaming ETL reading from S3 Event Notifications.
answers.D: Amazon Managed Kafka writing directly to S3.

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams preserves ordering and low latency; Firehose can then buffer and batch to S3 automatically.

stem: Your model needs high-throughput access to feature data during training. You must choose between Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, and Amazon S3. The data is >1 TB, highly structured, and training uses Spark on EMR. Which storage is best?

answers.A: Amazon EFS with provisioned throughput.
answers.B: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP.
answers.C: Amazon S3 with EMRFS Consistent View.
answers.D: Store data on EMR HDFS volumes.

explanation: S3 with EMRFS scales to TBs, offloads management, and is cost-effective for large structured datasets; HDFS adds management overhead.

stem: A team uses SageMaker Data Wrangler to profile 2 TB of CSV data stored in S3. They notice excessive request latencies. Which action will most reduce latency when reading from S3?

answers.A: Enable SSE-KMS on the S3 bucket.
answers.B: Convert CSV data to Apache Parquet with Snappy compression.
answers.C: Enable S3 Object Lock on the bucket.
answers.D: Enable S3 Versioning on the bucket.

explanation: Converting to Parquet reduces the number of S3 GET requests and data scanned, greatly lowering latency in Data Wrangler.

stem: An ML workflow must merge customer profile data in DynamoDB with clickstream logs in S3, then store results for training. Which approach minimizes custom code and operational complexity?

answers.A: Use AWS Glue ETL jobs with a DynamoDB connector to join and write to S3 in Parquet.
answers.B: Export DynamoDB to S3 via Data Pipeline, then use Lambda to merge with clickstream.
answers.C: Use SageMaker Processing to read both and write merged CSV to S3.
answers.D: Stream clickstream into DynamoDB and query joins at training time.

explanation: AWS Glue ETL handles connectors and joins natively and writes Parquet to S3, reducing custom orchestration.

stem: You must ingest 5 TB of Amazon RDS data into SageMaker Feature Store online store for low-latency feature retrieval. Which combination meets throughput and cost requirements?

answers.A: Export RDS snapshot to S3, use Glue to write to Feature Store.
answers.B: Use RDS native replication into DynamoDB, then batch ingest into Feature Store.
answers.C: Run a SageMaker Processing job to read from RDS and write to offline store.
answers.D: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to connect to RDS and directly ingest records into Feature Store online store.

explanation: Data Wrangler can connect to RDS and ingest into Feature Store online, meeting throughput needs with minimal glue code.

stem: A model requires streaming user events from mobile apps to S3 for nightly batch training. You need exactly-once delivery and minimal data loss. Which architecture is most appropriate?

answers.A: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose directly to S3.
answers.B: Use AWS Lambda triggered by API Gateway to write to S3.
answers.C: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with a consumer that writes to S3 via Firehose.
answers.D: Use Amazon SQS and a fleet of EC2 batch workers to write to S3.

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams ensures ordering and exactly-once semantics; Firehose delivers to S3 reliably with retries.

stem: During a cost audit, you discover that S3 GET and PUT costs for small files (<1 KB) used in training are high. How can you reduce costs while keeping data in S3?

answers.A: Switch to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access.
answers.B: Combine small files into larger Apache Avro container files.
answers.C: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration.
answers.D: Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

explanation: Combining small files into larger containers reduces request count and lowers GET/PUT request costs.

stem: A global company must ingest CSV sales data from multiple regional offices into a central S3 bucket. Some offices have poor upload bandwidth. How to ensure data arrives in the correct order and is fully available for batch processing in SageMaker?

answers.A: Use S3 Transfer Acceleration with directory replication.
answers.B: Use AWS DataSync scheduled tasks from each office.
answers.C: Use AWS Storage Gateway file gateway.
answers.D: Configure regional AWS Kinesis Data Firehose streams to deliver to a central S3 bucket with buffering and ordering enabled.

explanation: Regional Firehose streams buffer data, preserve ordering per shard, and reliably deliver to central S3 for downstream batch.

stem: Your training data resides in a high-CPU EBS volume attached to an EC2 instance. To ingest data into SageMaker Data Wrangler at scale, which approach minimizes network bottlenecks?

answers.A: Snapshot the EBS volume to S3 and let Data Wrangler read from S3.
answers.B: Attach the EBS volume to the SageMaker Data Wrangler notebook instance.
answers.C: Enable EBS multi-attach and mount on Data Wrangler instance.
answers.D: Run a DataSync task from the EC2 instance to the Data Wrangler volume.

explanation: Snapshot to S3 offloads network traffic and lets Data Wrangler ingest efficiently from S3 rather than over direct EBS mounts.

stem: A data scientist needs to join high-velocity Kafka events with a static dataset in S3 before training. They require minimal lag and schema evolution support. What ingestion pattern is best?

answers.A: Use Kinesis Data Firehose with Lambda to enrich events with S3 data.
answers.B: Deploy Amazon Managed Streaming for Kafka with AWS Glue streaming ETL to join and write to S3.
answers.C: Use SageMaker Processing to pull from Kafka and S3 periodically.
answers.D: Use AWS Lambda triggered by Kafka Connect and query S3 DynamoDB export.

explanation: Glue streaming ETL supports schema evolution and continuous joins with Kafka and S3, delivering results to S3 in near real time.

stem: A compliance requirement mandates encrypting sensor data and storing in S3 Glacier after ingestion. The data is 8 TB per month. What solution meets compliance with the lowest storage cost while remaining queryable for ML?

answers.A: Ingest to S3 Standard with SSE-KMS, transition to S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately.
answers.B: Ingest to S3 Glacier with client-side encryption.
answers.C: Ingest to S3 Standard-IA with SSE-KMS, configure lifecycle to move to Glacier after 30 days.
answers.D: Ingest to S3 One Zone-IA with SSE-KMS then transition to Glacier Flexible Retrieval.

explanation: Standard-IA with SSE-KMS and a 30-day lifecycle balances low cost while keeping data in S3 for Athena before Glacier transition.

stem: You must ingest and merge product catalog data from Amazon RDS and Alexa usage logs in S3 into SageMaker Feature Store offline store. How do you ingest with minimal code?

answers.A: Use AWS Glue jobs to extract from RDS and S3, transform, and write to Feature Store.
answers.B: Use SageMaker Processing to read both sources and write offline store.
answers.C: Export RDS to S3, then use Data Wrangler to merge and ingest.
answers.D: Use AWS AppFlow to replicate RDS and merge with S3 logs.

explanation: Glue ETL natively connects to RDS and S3 and can write to Feature Store with minimal custom code.

stem: An ML workflow streaming video metadata at 10 MB/sec must store data in S3 for batch training. Latencies <5 seconds acceptable. Which ingestion service provides auto-scaling and buffering without managing infrastructure?

answers.A: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with manual shard scaling.
answers.B: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver to S3.
answers.C: Run AWS Lambda to poll a custom endpoint and write to S3.
answers.D: Use AWS Managed Kafka with MirrorMaker to S3.

explanation: Firehose auto-scales and buffers transient bursts, delivering to S3 with minimal management.

stem: A dataset of images is stored in S3 and must be preprocessed via SageMaker Processing weekly. The team wants to minimize request overhead and latency when reading many small files. How should they reorganize the data?

answers.A: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration when reading each image.
answers.B: Copy images to an EFS mount for processing.
answers.C: Bundle images into TFRecord or RecordIO files and store in S3.
answers.D: Store images as base64-encoded JSON in single S3 objects.

explanation: Bundling into TFRecord/RecordIO reduces object count and request overhead, speeding SageMaker Processing.

stem: A financial services company deployed a SageMaker real-time endpoint for credit risk scoring. They need to detect, within one hour, any drift in the distribution of the applicant_age and debt_to_income_ratio features compared to production baselines and send alerts. Which solution meets these requirements with minimal custom development?

answers.A: Enable DataCaptureConfig on the endpoint, generate baseline statistics with ModelMonitor’s built-in methods, create a monitoring schedule for input feature drift, and configure CloudWatch alarms on the monitoring job metrics.
answers.B: Configure a Lambda function to read logs from CloudWatch Logs every hour, compute feature histograms, compare to baselines stored in S3, and send SNS alerts.
answers.C: Use Kinesis Data Analytics to ingest endpoint invocation payloads, run SQL queries to detect distribution changes, and trigger alarms through CloudWatch.
answers.D: Write a custom Spark job on EMR to read captured inference data, compute drift metrics, and schedule hourly cron jobs to publish alerts via Lambda.

explanation: A is correct because SageMaker Model Monitor can capture endpoint inputs, compute feature drift against baselines, and integrate with CloudWatch alarms with minimal coding. B and D require building custom data pipelines and drift logic. C uses Kinesis Data Analytics which is not optimized for SageMaker endpoint data capture and adds unnecessary complexity.

stem: An e-commerce company uses a SageMaker endpoint for fraud detection. They must monitor model performance by tracking the false positive rate (FPR) in production and automatically retrain if FPR exceeds 5%. Which architecture satisfies this requirement?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Model Monitor’s default data quality monitor to detect inference anomalies and trigger a Lambda to retrain the model when anomalies occur.
answers.B: Capture only input payloads, write a CloudWatch metric filter on the logs for false positives, and use a CloudWatch alarm to start a SageMaker batch transform retraining job.
answers.C: Enable DataCaptureConfig for both input and output, create ModelQualityMonitor with a custom metrics file specifying FPR, schedule hourly monitoring, and configure CloudWatch alarm to invoke a retraining pipeline.
answers.D: Log predictions to S3, use Athena with scheduled queries to compute FPR hourly, and use Step Functions to orchestrate retraining when threshold is exceeded.

explanation: C is correct because ModelQualityMonitor supports custom metrics (including FPR) computed from captured input/output and can trigger alarms. A lacks FPR tracking. B captures only inputs and relies on log parsing. D is possible but involves Athena and Step Functions, which is more complex and not leveraging built-in model quality monitoring.

stem: A healthcare provider has a batch inference pipeline that writes predictions and actual outcomes to S3 daily. They need to monitor model performance degradation (e.g., increasing RMSE) and alert DevOps when RMSE increases by more than 10% from baseline. Which move is best?

answers.A: Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query S3 logs via log aggregation and trigger alarms when RMSE query results exceed thresholds.
answers.B: Create a ModelQualityMonitor job using baseline metrics from training, supply the ground truth and prediction files from S3, schedule daily runs, and configure CloudWatch alarms.
answers.C: Configure SageMaker Clarify to detect bias drift which will also report RMSE change and use CloudWatch alarms for notifications.
answers.D: Invoke a Lambda function via EventBridge daily to compute RMSE from S3 data and send an SNS alert when RMSE >1.1× baseline.

explanation: B is correct because ModelQualityMonitor directly supports batch inference data from S3 with ground truth to compute metrics like RMSE and integrate with alarms. A and D require custom code. C is incorrect because Clarify focuses on bias and feature drift, not performance metrics like RMSE.

stem: A consumer app uses an endpoint for sentiment analysis. They observe occasional spikes in inference latency that degrade user experience. They need to detect latency anomalies in real time and trigger scaling actions. Which solution is most appropriate?

answers.A: Use ModelMonitor’s data quality monitor to detect latency outliers and send events to CloudWatch.
answers.B: Instrument the endpoint container to emit custom latency metrics to CloudWatch and set alarms on p95 latency.
answers.C: Schedule a daily ModelMonitor job to analyze captured requests and identify latency anomalies.
answers.D: Enable SageMaker endpoint invocation metrics (p90 and p95) in CloudWatch, create CloudWatch alarms for sudden increases, and attach Application Auto Scaling policies to the endpoint.

explanation: D is correct because SageMaker endpoints automatically emit latency metrics to CloudWatch, which can be used for real-time alarms and auto scaling. A and C misuse ModelMonitor, which is offline. B requires container modification when built-in metrics suffice.

stem: An IoT solution uses a SageMaker endpoint for anomaly detection on sensor streams. They require near real-time alerts when feature distributions drift beyond control limits, but they cannot incur high Lambda execution fees. Which design balances cost and responsiveness?

answers.A: Stream captured inference data to Kinesis Data Firehose, run a Lambda per record to compute drift and send alerts.
answers.B: Write all captured data to S3 and run a ModelMonitor daily job with low-cost spot instances.
answers.C: Use ModelMonitor endpoint preprocessor with custom monitoring script to detect drift thresholds on a 15-minute schedule and publish alerts via CloudWatch Events without Lambda.
answers.D: Use Kinesis Data Analytics SQL application to continuously compute drift metrics and send alerts through SNS.

explanation: C is correct because ModelMonitor supports custom scripts for drift detection on schedules, avoiding per-record Lambda costs. A and D incur compute in Kinesis/Lambda continuously. B reduces responsiveness to daily.

stem: A streaming inference endpoint uses DataCaptureConfig to write payloads and responses to S3. The team needs to detect when data quality (missing fields, invalid ranges) degrades in production and be paged immediately. Which process achieves this?

answers.A: Deploy ModelMonitor’s DefaultModelMonitor with a custom data quality constraints file, schedule it every 5 minutes, and configure CloudWatch alarms for violations.
answers.B: Configure SageMaker Clarify to analyze captured data for anomalies and configure alerts for missing features.
answers.C: Use Athena with scheduled queries every 5 minutes on the captured S3 files, detect invalid records, and notify via SNS.
answers.D: Stream S3 events to Lambda to validate each record in real time and alert on invalid data.

explanation: A is correct because DefaultModelMonitor supports data quality constraints with custom rules, scheduled frequently, with CloudWatch integration. B focuses on bias/feature importance. C and D require custom orchestration and are less integrated.

stem: A media company wants to monitor drift in top-5 features importance for its recommender model in production. They need automated alerts if the feature importance distribution shifts significantly. Which solution fits?

answers.A: Use ModelQualityMonitor to track feature importance values via ground truth comparisons.
answers.B: Use ModelExplainabilityMonitor to baseline SHAP feature importances during training, schedule production monitoring, and alarm on significant distribution shifts.
answers.C: Invoke Clarify’s bias detection in production to monitor feature importances.
answers.D: Export feature importance logs in JSON and use CloudWatch Logs Insights to compare distributions daily.

explanation: B is correct because ModelExplainabilityMonitor (part of Clarify) handles SHAP-based production monitoring of feature importances and can raise alarms. A is wrong because ModelQualityMonitor focuses on prediction quality, not explainability. C misuses bias detector. D is custom and manual.

stem: A logistics firm uses a SageMaker endpoint behind an ALB. They need to monitor end-to-end inference latency and alert if 95th percentile latency exceeds 300 ms for more than 5 minutes. How do they implement this with least maintenance?

answers.A: Embed custom timing code in inference container to publish custom CloudWatch metrics.
answers.B: Use ModelMonitor to capture input/output times and schedule drift checks on latency.
answers.C: Stream ALB access logs to CloudWatch Logs, parse latency percentile every minute via Logs Insights, and alarm.
answers.D: Use CloudWatch metric for SageMaker Endpoint p95 latency with a 5-minute period alarm, and connect to SNS for notifications.

explanation: D is correct: SageMaker endpoints expose p95 latency in CloudWatch, which supports threshold-based alarms. A requires custom code. B misuses ModelMonitor. C is indirect and involves complex log parsing.

stem: A biotech company runs batch inference nightly and stores predictions plus sample metadata in S3. They want to detect when the distribution of a key lab_measurement feature drifts compared to training data, and integrate alerts into PagerDuty. Which approach is best?

answers.A: Use Athena scheduled queries on S3 data to compute KLD between current and training histograms, and send alerts via SNS to PagerDuty.
answers.B: Set up a ModelMonitor batch monitoring job with a baseline from training data, schedule it nightly, and configure CloudWatch alarms to SNS for PagerDuty.
answers.C: Deploy Clarify drift detector to analyze batch outputs for distribution changes and integrate with EventBridge for notifications.
answers.D: Write custom PySpark EMR job to compute population stability index nightly and notify via Lambda.
