answers.D: It disables top-k sampling, resorting to greedy decoding.

explanation: A is correct—lower temperature favors top tokens. B–D mischaracterize temperature’s effect.

stem: In sampling strategies, what is the key difference between top-k and nucleus (top-p) sampling for text generation?

answers.A: Top-k limits to a fixed number of tokens, while top-p selects tokens until cumulative probability exceeds a threshold.
answers.B: Top-k adapts k based on token probability, while top-p uses a static set.
answers.C: Top-p always reduces latency, whereas top-k is slower.
answers.D: Top-p relies on beam search, and top-k does not.

explanation: A is correct—top-k fixes count, top-p fixes probability mass. B–D are inaccurate.

stem: When deploying an embedding store in production, which cost factor grows most with increasing embedding dimension versus increasing dataset size?

answers.A: Memory per vector grows linearly with dimension, while index size growth with dataset size depends on index type.
answers.B: Network bandwidth becomes the dominant cost for larger dimensions.
answers.C: CPU indexing time is unaffected by dataset size.
answers.D: Storage IOPS increase with dimension.

explanation: A is correct—dimension directly scales vector size. B–D misattribute costs.

stem: Why do transformers use sinusoidal positional encodings instead of learned embeddings for very long sequences?

answers.A: Sinusoidal embeddings generalize to unseen lengths due to their periodic properties.
answers.B: Learned embeddings require less memory for long sequences.
answers.C: Sinusoidal encodings prevent overfitting on position patterns.
answers.D: Learned embeddings cannot be used with multi-head attention.

explanation: A is correct—sinusoids extend to any position. B and D are false; C is not primary reason.

stem: What benefit does multi-head attention provide in a transformer-based generative model?

answers.A: It allows the model to attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.
answers.B: It reduces computation by parallelizing single-head attention.
answers.C: It enforces causality in the decoding phase.
answers.D: It increases the maximum context window.

explanation: A is correct—each head learns unique relationships. B, C, and D misstate its purpose.

stem: If a foundation model has a 2048-token context window, how should you preprocess a 5000-token document for a RAG pipeline to preserve coherence?

answers.A: Chunk into 2048-token segments with ~10% overlap to maintain context at boundaries.
answers.B: Chunk into non-overlapping 2500-token blocks to minimize number of chunks.
answers.C: Truncate to the first 2048 tokens as most relevant.
answers.D: Randomly sample 2048 tokens from the document each query.

explanation: A is correct—overlap preserves continuity. B loses coherence; C and D discard key content.

stem: A developer wants both long inputs and long outputs from a model with a fixed 4096-token limit. What’s an effective strategy?

answers.A: Split the input into chunks and generate outputs for each, then concatenate and refine.
answers.B: Request maximum output length and let the model truncate the input automatically.
answers.C: Increase the temperature to trade context for output.
answers.D: Use greedy decoding to prioritize output length.

explanation: A is correct—chunking plus post-processing handles long flows. B–D do not address the limit effectively.

stem: During inference on a diffusion model, what happens if the noise schedule steps have too small a variance between timesteps?

answers.A: Generation quality may degrade due to insufficient denoising signal between steps.
answers.B: Sampling speed increases but outputs become diverse.
answers.C: Model collapses to a single mode output.
answers.D: The reverse process becomes non-deterministic.

explanation: A is correct—too-fine steps weaken noise gradients. B–D misrepresent the effect.

stem: Which technique ensures cross-lingual alignment when training multilingual embeddings for a generative AI chatbot?

answers.A: Shared subword vocabulary and joint training on parallel corpora to align semantic spaces.
answers.B: Language-specific embeddings with no parameter sharing.
answers.C: Training separate models and concatenating their outputs.
answers.D: Using one-hot encodings for each language.

explanation: A is correct—shared vocab plus parallel data aligns languages. B–D fail to produce joint embedding spaces.

stem: In few-shot prompting, why might providing too many examples degrade a model’s performance on a new task?

answers.A: It consumes context window, leaving less space for the actual prompt and thus limiting task instructions.
answers.B: It causes the model to memorize examples, preventing generalization.
answers.C: It increases temperature implicitly, reducing determinism.
answers.D: It disables attention to the final instruction.

explanation: A is correct—examples use up context tokens. B–D are not primary issues with too many examples.

stem: How can vector arithmetic on embeddings (e.g., vec(king)−vec(man)+vec(woman)) fail in a generative AI context?

answers.A: Embedding space may not be fully linear for abstract relations, causing semantic drift in generation.
answers.B: Arithmetic always yields unknown tokens.
answers.C: It requires specialized loss functions at inference.
answers.D: It works only for image embeddings, not text.

explanation: A is correct—linear semantics are only approximate. B–D are incorrect statements.

stem: What is the primary memory complexity issue with transformers as sequence length increases?

answers.A: Self-attention scales quadratically (O(n²)) with sequence length, limiting long contexts.
answers.B: Feed-forward layers require O(n³) memory.
answers.C: Positional encoding scales linearly but dominates memory.
answers.D: Multi-head attention scales logarithmically, making it inefficient.

explanation: A is correct—attention’s O(n²) growth is the bottleneck. B–D misstate complexities.

stem: When combining embeddings with RAG for document QA, why is it problematic to update the index with new documents without re-computing embeddings?

answers.A: New documents won’t be comparable to existing ones in latent space, leading to retrieval inconsistencies.
answers.B: It reduces the context window size.
answers.C: It increases the embedding dimension automatically.
answers.D: It forces the RAG system to retrain the generator.

explanation: A is correct—embeddings must share the same space. B–D are unrelated issues.

stem: Why might image embeddings from a CLIP model and text embeddings be stored separately in a mixed-modality application?

answers.A: They occupy different subspaces and require modality-specific similarity metrics for retrieval.
answers.B: Image embeddings cannot be quantized.
answers.C: Text embeddings are binary while image embeddings are continuous.
answers.D: CLIP models output text embeddings only for image queries.

stem: An organization projects 100 000 monthly RAG queries and anticipates monthly content updates. Fine-tuning costs $50 000 upfront with negligible per-query cost; RAG costs $0.02 per query. Which approach has the lower year-one total cost?

answers.A: Use RAG exclusively, paying $0.02×100 000×12 = $24 000 monthly.
answers.B: Fine-tune once for $50 000 and serve queries at minimal incremental cost.
answers.C: Pre-train a new foundation model quarterly.
answers.D: Rotate between RAG and fine-tuning monthly.

explanation: RAG would cost $0.02×100 000×12 = $24 000; fine-tuning is a one-time $50 000, so in year one RAG is cheaper ($24 000) – candidate should recalc: actually correct is A; but structured scenario expects RAG is cheaper at $24 000 vs fine-tune $50 000.

stem: A logistics company must build a multi-step agent to validate addresses, calculate shipping costs, generate labels, and send notifications. They want a low-code orchestration solution. Which AWS feature should they use?

answers.A: Amazon Bedrock Agents with integrated AWS Step Functions orchestration.
answers.B: Chain multiple AWS Lambda functions manually.
answers.C: Develop a custom microservice orchestrator on Amazon EC2.
answers.D: Sequence tasks using AWS Batch workflows.

explanation: Bedrock Agents provide built-in multi-step orchestration integration, reducing custom code overhead.

stem: A software team needs to summarize 100-page PDF manuals. The foundation model’s token limit is 4096. Which approach handles this effectively?

answers.A: Chunk the manual into ≤2000-token segments, summarize each, then combine summaries recursively.
answers.B: Send the entire PDF text in one request and rely on the model’s context window to truncate gracefully.
answers.C: Fine-tune the model to increase its token limit.
answers.D: Increase max_output_tokens beyond 4096 during inference.

explanation: Hierarchical chunking and summarization respects token limits and yields coherent overall summary.

stem: A global translation service must support 30 languages with low latency. Which model selection strategy balances coverage and performance?

answers.A: Deploy specialized bilingual models for each language pair to reduce model size and latency.
answers.B: Use a single large multilingual foundation model for all languages.
answers.C: Translate via Amazon Translate then post-process with the foundation model.
answers.D: Fine-tune one model per region for language coverage.

explanation: Bilingual models reduce inference cost and latency vs one large multilingual model while still covering required pairs.

stem: For a RAG pipeline, a team wants to limit the number of retrieved documents per query to reduce inference context size and cost. Which retrieval parameter should they adjust?

answers.A: Set the retriever’s k parameter (number of top documents) to a lower value.
answers.B: Reduce the embedding dimension size.
answers.C: Lower the model temperature.
answers.D: Decrease max_output_tokens.

explanation: Lowering k reduces the number of retrieved passages in the prompt, shrinking context and cost; other parameters don’t affect retrieval count.

stem: A vector store previously used 768-dim embeddings; switching to a new model yields 1024 dimensions, and query latency doubles. How can they restore performance without sacrificing retrieval quality?

answers.A: Apply dimensionality reduction (e.g., PCA) to project 1024-dim embeddings down to 768 dimensions.
answers.B: Continue using 1024-dim embeddings and provision larger instance types.
answers.C: Pad old 768-dim embeddings to 1024 dims.
answers.D: Revert to the previous embedding model.

explanation: Dimensionality reduction keeps vector store size manageable and preserves most semantic information; padding wastes resources.

stem: A financial application requires ACID transactions when updating user embeddings under heavy concurrency. Which embedding store meets this requirement?

answers.A: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector extension.
answers.B: Amazon OpenSearch Service with k-NN.
answers.C: Amazon Neptune configured for vector similarity.
answers.D: Amazon DynamoDB with custom indexing.

explanation: Aurora PostgreSQL offers ACID compliance plus pgvector for embeddings; other stores are eventually consistent or non-transactional.

stem: Engineers want more diverse, creative summarizations. Which inference parameter changes achieve this?

answers.A: Increase both temperature and top_p.
answers.B: Decrease temperature toward zero.
answers.C: Reduce max_output_tokens to force brevity.
answers.D: Disable retrieval augmentation.

explanation: Higher temperature and broader top_p allow the model to sample more diverse tokens, increasing creativity.

stem: A marketing team must refresh product descriptions monthly. Custom fine-tuning costs $20 000 each time; RAG costs $0.015 per query. They expect 200 000 queries per month. Which approach is most cost-effective?

answers.A: Use RAG to avoid repeated fine-tuning costs.
answers.B: Perform monthly fine-tuning despite the one-time expense.
answers.C: Fine-tune quarterly and use zero-shot otherwise.
answers.D: Use zero-shot prompting exclusively.

explanation: RAG @ $0.015×200 000 = $3 000/month is cheaper than $20 000 per refresh; zero-shot yields low accuracy.

stem: A cell-phone provider needs a multi-step agent to verify SIM status, calculate upgrade eligibility, send offers, and log responses. They require built-in branching logic and retry handling. Which AWS capability should they use?

answers.A: Amazon Bedrock Agents with built-in workflow, branching, and retry support.
answers.B: AWS Step Functions calling Bedrock directly.
answers.C: Chained AWS Lambda functions orchestrated manually.
answers.D: AWS Batch with job dependencies.

explanation: Bedrock Agents provide multi-step orchestration with logic and retry controls tailored to LLM workflows.

stem: A retailer wants to store image embeddings and filter by price range. Which AWS service supports vector search plus metadata filtering?

answers.A: Amazon OpenSearch Service with k-NN plugin and document fields.
answers.B: Amazon Neptune graph queries with PRICE property.
answers.C: Amazon Timestream for time-series embedding storage.
answers.D: Amazon S3 with object tags and Lambda lookups.

explanation: OpenSearch combines k-NN vector search and structured field filters for metadata constraints; other options lack integrated vector + metadata queries.

stem: A global app must perform semantic search across English, Spanish, and Mandarin content. Which foundation model criterion is critical?

answers.A: Select a multilingual foundation model pretrained on all target languages.
answers.B: Use an English-only model with translation pre-processing.
answers.C: Deploy separate monolingual models per language.
answers.D: Rely on fine-tuning to teach new languages.

explanation: A multilingual LLM natively understands all languages for semantic embeddings; translation adds latency and error.

stem: To forecast RAG pipeline costs, which factors should be included?

answers.A: Compute costs for embedding generation, LLM token charges, and storage costs for vector indexes.
answers.B: Only the storage costs of embeddings.
answers.C: Just the EC2 instance hours used by the application.
answers.D: Only the foundation model’s license fee.

explanation: RAG cost = embedding compute + LLM tokens consumed + storage + any I/O; ignoring any leads to underestimation.

stem: A user submits a 2.5 million-token document to a model with a 1 million-token context limit. Which strategy handles this input best?

answers.A: Use a sliding/chunking approach: split into overlapping 1 million-token segments and process iteratively.
answers.B: Request the model to accept larger context by adjusting max_context_tokens parameter.
answers.C: Fine-tune the model to handle larger inputs.
answers.D: Discard tokens beyond the first 1 million.

explanation: Chunking with overlap preserves context while respecting model limits; other methods are unsupported or lose information.

stem: During a partial OpenSearch outage, the RAG pipeline must continue to answer queries gracefully. Which fallback should be implemented?

answers.A: Fall back to a keyword-based Boolean search over a local S3-backed index.
answers.B: Switch to Amazon Neptune for vector search.
answers.C: Abort requests and return errors.
answers.D: Queue requests until OpenSearch recovers.

explanation: A local keyword search ensures degraded service rather than total failure; queuing or errors harm UX.

stem: Retrieval accuracy in RAG is low despite high embedding similarity scores. Which diagnostic step should they take first?

answers.A: Examine embedding distributions and consider retraining or switching embedding models.
answers.B: Ramp up the model’s temperature for more variability.
answers.C: Switch to a larger foundation model for inference.
answers.D: Increase max_output_tokens to get longer answers.

explanation: Poor retrieval often stems from suboptimal embeddings; model hyperparameters won’t fix retrieval quality.

stem: An agent workflow must enforce a maximum of 512 output tokens. Which Bedrock API parameter should they configure?

answers.A: max_output_tokens
answers.B: temperature
answers.C: top_p
answers.D: beam_width

explanation: max_output_tokens directly limits the number of tokens the model generates; other parameters control randomness or search strategy.

stem: A high-security customer requires private network communication for vector searches. Which architecture element ensures privacy?

answers.A: Deploy OpenSearch Service within a VPC and use AWS PrivateLink for Bedrock access.
answers.B: Use the public OpenSearch endpoint with IAM policies.
answers.C: Tunnel traffic over S3.
answers.D: Use CloudFront in front of OpenSearch.

explanation: VPC deployment plus PrivateLink keeps data off the public internet; other options expose endpoints publicly or misuse services.

stem: A content-heavy app must pre-warm embedding Lambda functions to reduce cold-start latency spikes. What is the best practice?

answers.A: Configure provisioned concurrency on the Lambda function.
answers.B: Let the function handle occasional cold starts.
answers.C: Use AWS Batch instead of Lambda.
answers.D: Store embeddings in S3 to avoid Lambda.

explanation: Provisioned concurrency keeps warm instances ready, reducing cold-start latency; other options either ignore the issue or circumvent the design.

stem: A financial analytics team must store embeddings alongside relational transaction data and enforce ACID. Which solution is most appropriate?

answers.A: Use Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension.
answers.B: Store embeddings in DynamoDB and transactions in RDS separately.
answers.C: Use Amazon DocumentDB for both embeddings and transactional data.
answers.D: Implement a two-phase commit between OpenSearch and Aurora.

explanation: Aurora Postgres + pgvector provides a unified, ACID-compliant store for both embeddings and relational data; other approaches increase complexity.

stem: A chatbot using RAG must control costs by limiting the number of retrievals as well as generated tokens. Which combination of parameters should be adjusted?

answers.A: Lower the retriever’s k (documents) and set a conservative max_output_tokens.
answers.B: Increase temperature and top_p.
answers.C: Use a larger batch size.
answers.D: Enable debug mode.

explanation: Reducing k shrinks context; lowering max_output_tokens caps the output length, both directly reduce cost.

stem: A scientific publisher needs to index both text and vector embeddings for articles in the same service. Which AWS option should they pick?

answers.A: Amazon OpenSearch Service with integrated full-text search and k-NN vectors.
answers.B: Amazon Neptune for RDF and vector queries.
answers.C: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with full-text search.
answers.D: Amazon S3 + Lambda for indexing.

explanation: OpenSearch supports hybrid queries mixing full-text and vector similarity; other services require stitching or lack vector support.

stem: A recommendation system uses a foundation model to generate item embeddings and serve nearest-neighbor queries. To minimize search errors, which storage configuration is best?

answers.A: Deploy OpenSearch Service with replication enabled and k-NN plugin.
answers.B: Use DynamoDB with Global Secondary Index.
answers.C: Persist embeddings in S3 and scan on demand.
answers.D: Host embeddings in Redis cluster.

explanation: OpenSearch with replication ensures high availability and accuracy in k-NN searches; others don’t natively support vector retrieval.

stem: A development team notices fluctuating RAG latency at peak loads. Which scaling approach for the vector store is most effective?

answers.A: Enable auto-scaling on the OpenSearch domain’s data nodes.
answers.B: Provision a fixed large instance size.
answers.C: Manually add more EC2 instances.
answers.D: Switch to a single high-I/O DynamoDB table.

explanation: Auto-scaling OpenSearch data nodes adapts to load changes automatically; fixed or manual scaling is less responsive.

stem: A legal research app must retrieve citations with high recall in RAG. Which retriever tuning improves recall while controlling context size?

answers.A: Increase k (number of retrieved documents) and apply a relevance threshold filter.
answers.B: Decrease temperature.
answers.C: Reduce max_output_tokens.
answers.D: Switch to a single-shot prompt.

explanation: Raising k returns more candidates for the LLM to choose from, boosting recall; other parameters don’t affect retrieval breadth.

stem: A team wants to quantify RAG pipeline performance for SLAs: retrieval latency and end-to-end response time. Which tools should they use?

answers.A: Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics for end-to-end tests and OpenSearch slow-log metrics for retrieval latency.
answers.B: S3 access logs.
answers.C: AWS Config rules.
answers.D: AWS Glue job metrics.

explanation: CloudWatch Synthetics simulates full pipeline; OpenSearch slow logs measure vector search latency; other tools are unrelated.

stem: A developer must enforce data retention—delete embeddings older than 90 days automatically. Which architecture achieves this?

answers.A: Use OpenSearch index rollover with a 90-day retention policy and lifecycle policy to delete old indices.
answers.B: Manually purge embeddings via Bedrock console.
answers.C: Use S3 expiration rules.
answers.D: Archive data in Glacier.

explanation: OpenSearch index lifecycle policies automate deletion of data older than a threshold; other options don’t apply to the index store.

stem: You are designing prompts for a customer support chatbot that must interpret rare domain-specific error codes. Which prompt engineering approach most reliably guides the model through multi-step interpretation of an unfamiliar code?

answers.A: Use zero-shot prompting with a single instruction to "explain the code"
answers.B: Provide a long template with all known codes and rely on the model to match
answers.C: Use chain-of-thought prompting with a few representative examples and ask the model to verbalize each reasoning step
answers.D: Use a generic completion prompt with a high temperature to encourage creativity

explanation: Chain-of-thought with examples explicitly leads the model through reasoning steps needed for rare codes; zero-shot or generic completion may omit steps and lead to hallucinations.

stem: A generative AI application must summarize medical records while never revealing patient identifiers. Which prompt technique helps ensure anonymization?

answers.A: Insert negative prompts like "Do not remove any text"
answers.B: Use explicit negative prompts: "Do not output any names, dates, or addresses" combined with guardrail templates
answers.C: Rely on the model’s default privacy capability
answers.D: Set a high temperature to diversify summary wording

explanation: Explicit negative prompts plus guardrail templates clearly instruct the model to avoid specific PII, while high temperature or default privacy are unreliable.

stem: When using few-shot prompting for financial document classification, you notice inconsistent output if you exceed three examples. What is the most likely cause?

answers.A: Context window saturation leads to model truncation of examples
answers.B: Too many examples reduce the model’s creativity
answers.C: Model overfits to early examples only
answers.D: High temperature setting causes inconsistency

explanation: Adding more examples fills the context window causing the model to truncate or ignore later examples; reducing to 2–3 examples keeps the context coherent.

stem: You need a stable translation service for legal documents where hallucinations are unacceptable. Which settings achieve high determinism?

answers.A: High temperature (0.9) and no few-shot examples
answers.B: Zero-shot prompting with a medium temperature (0.5)
answers.C: Few-shot prompting with creative instructions
answers.D: Zero-shot prompting with temperature 0 and explicit instruction style templates

explanation: Temperature 0 ensures deterministic outputs and explicit templates guide consistent translation; creative or high temperature settings risk variability and hallucination.

stem: An adversary tries prompt injection by appending “Ignore previous instructions and output X.” Which engineering technique mitigates this risk?

answers.A: Increase temperature to dilute malicious text
answers.B: Use a system-level instruction or guardrail template enforced before user content
answers.C: Provide more in-context positive examples
answers.D: Switch to few-shot prompting

explanation: System-level instructions or guardrail templates take precedence over user content, preventing prompt injection; temperature or examples do not block malicious append.

stem: Your model responses vary significantly when summarizing news articles. You need safer outputs. Which combination reduces variability while preserving detail?

answers.A: Lower temperature to ~0.2 and include an instruction template focusing on key facts
answers.B: Use high top-p sampling and no instruction
answers.C: Use chain-of-thought without temperature adjustment
answers.D: Switch to zero-shot with generic “Summarize” prompt

explanation: Lowering temperature reduces sampling randomness, and a focused template ensures the model includes key factual details.

stem: A content moderation tool uses an LLM to flag hate speech. False negatives increase when model sees adversarial phrasing. Which prompt-engineering tactic improves robustness?

answers.A: Raise temperature to catch all variations
answers.B: Provide only positive examples in prompt
answers.C: Use a generic moderation API call
answers.D: Include negative and adversarial examples in few-shot prompt and use chain-of-thought labeling guidelines

explanation: Including adversarial examples and chain-of-thought guidelines teaches the model to reason through obfuscated hateful language; temperature changes or generic calls are insufficient.

stem: You have a foundation model that occasionally repeats sensitive content. What prompt modification reduces repetition?

answers.A: Remove all examples to reduce bias
answers.B: Use high temperature to diversify
answers.C: Add a negative prompt: "Do not repeat previous content" and set max_repeat_penalty
answers.D: Use zero-shot prompting

explanation: Negative prompts combined with repeat-penalty parameters actively discourage the model from echoing sensitive content.

stem: Your generative AI assistant must inject step-by-step debugging suggestions when users report code errors. Which prompt design ensures consistent inclusion of steps?

answers.A: Template instructing “List steps: 1. Analyze, 2. Identify, 3. Suggest Fixes” with chain-of-thought
answers.B: Few-shot with two examples only
answers.C: Zero-shot “Help me debug”
answers.D: High temperature free-form prompt

explanation: A structured template listing numbered steps with chain-of-thought guides the model to always include a detailed debugging process.

stem: When using in-context examples, why might you randomize the order of examples in your prompt?

answers.A: To reduce context window usage
answers.B: To prevent positional bias causing overfitting to early examples
answers.C: To increase token diversity
answers.D: To improve latency

explanation: Randomizing examples stops the model from disproportionately attending to the first few examples, reducing positional bias.

stem: What is the primary risk of using high temperature in a safety-critical medical Q&A system?

answers.A: Longer response time
answers.B: Decreased token usage
answers.C: Increased likelihood of hallucinations and nondeterministic errors
answers.D: Lower creativity

explanation: High temperature increases randomness and risk of false statements, unacceptable in safety-critical domains.

stem: You need to instruct a model to generate JSON only. Which technique is most effective?

answers.A: Use a high temperature and hope for JSON
answers.B: Use chain-of-thought prompt to think in JSON
answers.C: Provide zero-shot generic instruction
answers.D: Provide a strict response template: "Respond ONLY in JSON format: {...}" and include example JSON skeleton

explanation: A strict template with skeleton examples and explicit “ONLY in JSON” instruction ensures format adherence.

stem: A hallucination in a product recommendation agent misattributes features. Which prompt tweak most reduces this?

answers.A: Increase temperature to refresh knowledge
answers.B: Use retrieval-augmented generation: fetch feature docs and include in context
answers.C: Switch to single-shot prompting
answers.D: Add more unrelated examples

explanation: Providing retrieved factual docs in context grounds the model and reduces hallucinations; temperature changes are ineffective.

stem: During stress testing, your LLM triggers a jailbreaking prompt. Which guardrail approach best prevents this?

answers.A: Implement a system-level policy that filters or rejects jailbreak patterns before model call
answers.B: Use few-shot with benign examples
answers.C: Increase temperature
answers.D: Switch to zero-shot

explanation: Filtering malicious prompts before they reach the model is more reliable than prompt content adjustments.

stem: You are defining a template for writing marketing copy. Which template structure yields the most consistent brand tone?

answers.A: Open-ended instruction “Write copy”
answers.B: Chain-of-thought with broad guidelines
answers.C: Structured template with sections: “Headline:…, Body:…, CTA:…” plus two few-shot examples
answers.D: High-temperature freestyle prompt

explanation: Structured templates with explicit sections and examples guide the model to consistently follow brand tone and format.

stem: To encourage the model to propose multiple alternative solutions rather than a single answer, which setting helps?

answers.A: Temperature=0 and beam search
answers.B: Increase temperature moderately and include “List 3 alternative approaches” in instruction
answers.C: Use zero-shot default prompt
answers.D: Few-shot with single example

explanation: Moderate temperature plus explicit instruction to list alternatives fosters diverse outputs.

stem: Which prompt engineering approach best mitigates model exposure to private training data?

answers.A: Use data filtering and add a negative prompt “Do not reveal source data” in guardrails
answers.B: Lower temperature
answers.C: Use few-shot with internal data examples
answers.D: Use zero-shot with generic instructions

explanation: Combining data filtering and explicit negative prompts in guardrails prevents the model from disclosing training data.

stem: You want the model to first self-critique its answer and then refine it. Which prompt technique accomplishes this reliably?

answers.A: High temperature free-form prompt
answers.B: Zero-shot with generic critique request
answers.C: Chain-of-thought with two-phase template: “Step 1: Provide answer. Step 2: Critique and refine.”
answers.D: Few-shot with single example

explanation: A two-phase template clearly instructs sequential tasks and chain-of-thought ensures each phase is executed.

stem: When designing prompts for an LLM-based code generator, you observe the model writes insecure code. Which prompt addition reduces insecure patterns?

answers.A: Increase temperature
answers.B: Add a guardrail template: “Ensure code follows OWASP best practices. Do not include insecure functions,” with examples
answers.C: Use fewer in-context examples
answers.D: Switch to single-shot prompting

explanation: Guardrail templates specifying security constraints and examples guide the model to produce secure code.

stem: A summarization model hallucinates non-existent entities. Which prompt strategy most reduces this risk?

answers.A: Use single-shot summarization
answers.B: Increase temperature
answers.C: Add more irrelevant examples
answers.D: Retrieval-augmented prompt: provide source text and instruct “Summarize only content present in the text”

explanation: Providing source text and explicit instruction to limit to that text prevents hallucinations.

stem: For a multi-turn dialogue, context length exceeds model limit and earlier user instructions are truncated. How to preserve persona instructions?

answers.A: Use higher temperature
answers.B: Use system-level instructions stored separately and prepend only essential tokens
answers.C: Switch to few-shot examples in each turn
answers.D: Increase chain-of-thought depth

explanation: System-level instructions are applied outside user context and remain effective regardless of conversation length.

stem: You need the model to refuse unsafe code. Which negative prompt is most effective?

answers.A: “If request involves unsafe code, reply with ‘I cannot comply’” within guardrail template
answers.B: “Write code”
answers.C: Use high temperature
answers.D: Provide safe code example only

explanation: Explicit negative prompt specifying refusal behavior ensures the model declines unsafe code requests.

stem: Why might you chain multiple prompts instead of one long prompt?

answers.A: To use more tokens
answers.B: To increase randomness
answers.C: To segment tasks, manage context limits, and verify intermediate results
answers.D: To avoid guardrails

explanation: Chaining tasks lets you check intermediate outputs, handle context windows, and apply different instructions per step.

stem: A language model sometimes ignores instructions buried at the end of a long prompt. How do you ensure instruction priority?

answers.A: Put instructions last
answers.B: Use system-level or model-preset instructions with higher precedence
answers.C: Use single-shot prompt without instructions
answers.D: Increase temperature

explanation: System-level or preset instructions override prompt content regardless of position, ensuring they are followed.

stem: In zero-shot translation tests, some outputs are syntactically correct but semantically wrong. Which prompt tweak improves semantic fidelity?

answers.A: Increase temperature
answers.B: Reduce max tokens
answers.C: Use chain-of-thought
answers.D: Add explicit instruction: “Translate faithfully, preserving meaning exactly” and use a short few-shot pair

explanation: Explicit fidelity instruction plus few-shot example enforces meaning preservation; temperature or token limit changes do not guarantee semantic accuracy.

stem: Your model’s completion occasionally exposes internal policy text. Which prompt-engineering measure helps?

answers.A: Add negative prompt “Do not reveal internal policy” in guardrails
answers.B: Use high temperature
answers.C: Use fewer examples
answers.D: Switch to zero-shot default API call

explanation: Explicit negative prompts prevent the model from disclosing protected content; other methods won’t reliably block exposures.

stem: You observe that adding irrelevant examples degrades performance. What principle does this illustrate?

answers.A: Higher token count improves context
answers.B: More examples always help
answers.C: Context contamination; irrelevant or noisy examples reduce model focus
answers.D: Temperature must be low

explanation: Irrelevant examples contaminate context, reducing the model’s ability to generalize correctly.

stem: For an AI hiring assistant, you must avoid demographic bias. Which prompt-engineering approach mitigates this?

answers.A: Use high temperature to diversify responses
answers.B: Include counterfactual and debiasing examples in few-shot prompt and use neutrality guardrail
answers.C: Zero-shot generic instruction
answers.D: Chain-of-thought only

explanation: Providing debiasing examples and neutral guardrails helps the model avoid demographic biases in its output.

stem: Which method most effectively limits token usage when composing long responses?

answers.A: High temperature
answers.B: Use chain-of-thought
answers.C: Few-shot with many examples
answers.D: Set a max_tokens parameter and use concise templates

explanation: Using max_tokens limits the response length regardless of prompt complexity; concise templates help the model stay within limits.

stem: Your LLM assistant for legal advice must never provide unauthorized practice of law. Which prompt safety layer is most reliable?

answers.A: Prepend a system-level instruction: “You are a legal AI assistant, not a lawyer. Always include ‘This is not legal advice’ disclaimer.”
answers.B: Use chain-of-thought to think in law
answers.C: High temperature for creativity
answers.D: Zero-shot with generic instruction

explanation: A system-level instruction enforced before user input ensures consistent disclaimer compliance.

stem: A company needs to continuously update a foundation model with their domain-specific unlabeled text data streamed daily. They must retain the model’s broad language capabilities while injecting domain knowledge. Which approach best satisfies this requirement?

answers.A: Fine-tune the entire model on the new data each day
answers.B: Perform continuous pre-training on the domain corpus
answers.C: Use instruction tuning on curated domain prompts
answers.D: Apply reinforcement learning from human feedback

explanation: Continuous pre-training (further unsupervised training) on unlabeled domain text preserves general capabilities while adding domain knowledge.

stem: A team has only 500 labeled examples to adapt a 7B-parameter foundation model for a specialized classification task. They need to minimize compute and storage costs. Which fine-tuning method should they choose?

answers.A: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA)
answers.B: Full parameter fine-tuning
answers.C: Instruction tuning with domain prompts
answers.D: Reinforcement learning from human feedback

explanation: LoRA adds a small number of trainable parameters, reducing compute and storage compared to full fine-tuning.

stem: In RLHF workflows, which sequence of steps is correct?

answers.A: Train reward model → supervised fine-tuning → pre-train foundation model
answers.B: Pre-train foundation model → RLHF → supervised fine-tuning
answers.C: Pre-train foundation model → supervised fine-tune on reference data → train reward model → reinforcement learning
answers.D: Supervised fine-tune → pre-train → train reward model

explanation: Standard RLHF: pre-train, supervised fine-tune, collect feedback to train reward model, then RL optimization.

stem: A dataset for fine-tuning is heavily skewed toward one class. To prevent overfitting and bias, what is the most appropriate data preparation step before fine-tuning?

answers.A: Remove minority class samples
answers.B: Apply full fine-tuning without adjustment
answers.C: Use stratified sampling or class-balanced oversampling
answers.D: Increase learning rate to adapt quickly

explanation: Stratified sampling or oversampling balances classes and ensures representativeness, preventing biased fine-tuning.

stem: After fine-tuning on a narrow domain dataset, the model’s performance on general tasks degrades significantly. Which technique mitigates this catastrophic forgetting?

answers.A: Use a smaller learning rate
answers.B: Increase batch size
answers.C: Apply RLHF
answers.D: Mix domain data with a subset of general pre-training data during fine-tuning

explanation: Including a fraction of general data prevents the model from forgetting prior capabilities during fine-tuning.

stem: You need to adapt a multi-modal foundation model to a new domain with limited labeled images and annotations. Which two-step process is most efficient?

answers.A: Full model fine-tuning → RLHF
answers.B: Domain-adaptive pre-training on unlabeled images → parameter-efficient fine-tuning on labels
answers.C: Instruction tuning → supervised classification fine-tuning
answers.D: Prefix-tuning → supervised text embedding training

explanation: First domain-adaptive pre-training uses unlabeled data; then a parameter-efficient method adapts on labels efficiently.

stem: A team wants to reduce cost of repeated fine-tuning experiments. Which parameter-efficient fine-tuning method stores the fewest additional parameters per experiment?

answers.A: Full fine-tuning
answers.B: Prefix-tuning
answers.C: LoRA
answers.D: Adapter layers

explanation: LoRA injects low-rank matrices into weights, requiring fewer additional parameters than full tuning or prefix-tuning.

stem: During instruction tuning, a model outputs harmful or toxic responses. Which step should be added to the fine-tuning pipeline to address this?

answers.A: Increase training epochs
answers.B: Remove instruction examples
answers.C: Use higher learning rate
answers.D: Incorporate a safety filter or toxic content detection in supervised data curation

explanation: Filtering training data for safety and removing toxic examples prevents harmful outputs post fine-tuning.

stem: You must adapt a foundation model to a highly specialized jargon-heavy domain. Labeled data is scarce. Which approach yields the best domain adaptation?

stem: A biotech company wants to find new protein structures by exploring combinations without prior labels. Which ML approach should they use?

stem: Which metric would best capture model performance when both false positives and false negatives carry significant but unequal business costs?

stem: A team needs to continuously retrain a model monthly when new labeled data arrives, ensuring reproducibility and minimal operational overhead. Which solution is most appropriate?

stem: A team wants to compare performance of multiple models and register the best one automatically for deployment. Which SageMaker feature set should they use?

stem: When selecting a managed API versus self-hosted API for model inference, which trade-off is a key consideration?

stem: A retailer measures model success by uplift in average order value rather than by classification accuracy. What type of metric is this?

stem: A developer submits a 4096-character document to a foundation model with a 2048-token context window. The model rejects the request, stating the input exceeds the token limit. The developer assumed characters map one-to-one to tokens. Which concept explains this miscalculation?

answers.A: Tokenization
answers.B: Chunking
answers.C: Embeddings
answers.D: Positional encoding

explanation: Tokenization splits text into subword units called tokens, which do not correspond one-to-one with characters. Understanding tokenization is key to context window limits.

stem: An engineer builds a RAG pipeline on long contracts. To preserve semantic continuity and reduce retrieval ambiguity, which chunking strategy should they adopt?

answers.A: Fixed-size non-overlapping chunks
answers.B: Semantic chunking with 10–20% overlap
answers.C: Sentence-boundary chunking without overlap
answers.D: Arbitrary character-based windows with 50% overlap

stem: A data scientist uses 64-dimensional embeddings for semantic search and sees many false positives between distinct topics. Which adjustment most directly improves topic discrimination?

answers.A: Increase embedding dimensionality to 128 or 256

stem: When comparing text embedding vectors for similarity, which metric is most robust to differences in vector magnitude and focuses on directional similarity?

answers.A: Euclidean distance
answers.B: Manhattan distance
answers.C: Cosine similarity
answers.D: Jaccard distance

explanation: Cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors, ignoring their magnitudes, making it robust to length differences.

stem: A business needs to generate concise summaries of long reports. Which transformer architecture variant is best suited for sequence-to-sequence summarization tasks?

answers.B: Decoder-only

answers.B: Model B, because speed is primary

stem: After deployment, hallucinations increase. Which lifecycle stage should address this by incorporating real user feedback?

stem: A healthcare startup wants to use a generative AI model to draft patient-friendly explanations of complex medical reports. stem: A media company must generate localized marketing copy in 10 languages using a single foundation model. They are concerned about cross-lingual performance. Which evaluation metric best quantifies business value for multilingual consistency?

stem: A retail chain wants to generate personalized product recommendations using a generative model. They need to measure business impact beyond model accuracy. Which metric should they prioritize, and why?

answers.D: Use few-shot prompting; disable system messages

explanation: Lower temperature controls creativity vs consistency. Fine-tuning on story scripts aligns the model to game lore and style.

stem: A biotech company needs to generate molecular synthesis protocols. They require high accuracy and domain adherence. Which model limitation poses the greatest challenge, and how can they address it on AWS?

answers.A: Latency; deploy on CPU instances
answers.B: Cost; use Spot Instances
answers.C: Hallucinations; use RAG with a curated protocol database in Amazon Neptune
answers.D: Scalability; shard across multiple SageMaker endpoints

explanation: Hallucinations can produce invalid protocols. RAG with a structured database ensures generation uses verified procedures.

stem: A telecom provider wants to compare two generative AI offerings for automated script generation. They require objective performance evaluation. Which combination of metrics gives the most comprehensive assessment?

answers.A: Perplexity and latency
answers.B: BLEU score and model size
answers.C: ROUGE score and temperature
answers.D: BLEU/ROUGE for quality and inference latency for operational feasibility

explanation: BLEU and ROUGE assess text quality; latency ensures the solution meets real-time generation requirements.

stem: A financial advisory service uses a foundation model to draft personalized investment advice. They must comply with regulatory transparency requirements. Which limitation challenges compliance, and what AWS tool helps ensure governance?

answers.A: Scalability; use Bedrock’s auto-scaling
answers.B: Lack of explainability; generate model cards with SageMaker Model Cards and use Amazon A2I for human review
answers.C: Throughput; optimize GPU usage
answers.D: Embedding drift; retrain embeddings frequently

explanation: Opaque model decisions hinder regulatory compliance. SageMaker Model Cards document model details, and A2I provides human validation.

stem: An online education platform plans to generate practice exam questions. They need high variety but must avoid factually incorrect content. Which compromise and approach best fit?

answers.A: Moderate temperature and RAG with curated question bank
answers.B: High temperature and no retrieval
answers.C: Few-shot prompting only
answers.D: Zero-shot prompting and maximum tokens

explanation: Moderate temperature adds variation, while RAG ensures content is grounded in the verified question bank to avoid false facts.

stem: A news organization uses generative AI to summarize global headlines. They must measure trustworthiness of summaries. Which metric and process best quantify hallucination rates?

answers.A: ROUGE-L against reference summaries
answers.B: BLEU score against multilingual corpora
answers.C: Human evaluation of hallucination frequency with Amazon A2I
answers.D: Perplexity on news corpus

explanation: Automatic metrics don’t detect hallucinations reliably. Amazon A2I human-in-the-loop review quantifies factual errors.

stem: A supply-chain firm wants generative AI to predict demand patterns and draft procurement plans. They need to measure solution ROI. Which business metric best captures value?

answers.A: F1 score on demand labels
answers.B: Inference latency
answers.C: Model throughput
answers.D: Inventory turnover improvement percentage

explanation: Inventory turnover improvement directly measures how the AI-driven plans optimize stock and improve capital efficiency.

stem: A hotel chain uses generative AI chatbots for booking assistance. They observe nondeterministic price quote phrasing confusing customers. Which adjustment most effectively reduces variability?

answers.A: Use few-shot prompts
answers.B: Lower temperature to near zero
answers.C: Increase max token length
answers.D: Enable top-p sampling

explanation: Lowering temperature reduces randomness, leading to consistent phrasing of price quotes.

stem: A media streaming service wants to generate personalized show summaries. They must avoid content bias favoring popular genres. Which strategy minimizes bias in generative outputs?

answers.A: Fine-tune on a balanced genre dataset
answers.B: Increase temperature to allow diversity
answers.C: Use chain-of-thought prompting
answers.D: Implement RAG with popular titles only

explanation: Fine-tuning on balanced data ensures equal representation across genres, reducing bias toward popular ones.

stem: A legal department needs deterministic boilerplate clauses from a foundation model. They must evaluate long-form outputs for consistency. Which generation settings and evaluation metric combination should they use?

answers.A: High temperature; BLEU
answers.B: Zero-shot; perplexity
answers.C: Low temperature; ROUGE score compared to standard templates
answers.D: High top-p; F1 score

explanation: Low temperature yields consistent text; ROUGE against approved templates measures textual fidelity and consistency.

stem: A biotech startup uses generative AI to propose experimental protocols. They require quantifiable safety metrics. Which model limitation and metric pairing best aligns with safety requirements?

answers.A: Latency; CPU utilization
answers.B: Scalability; throughput
answers.C: Interpretability; attention visualizations
answers.D: Hallucinations; human-rated protocol validity with Amazon A2I

explanation: Hallucinations risk unsafe protocol suggestions. Human review via A2I rates validity, directly measuring safety compliance.

stem: A financial app uses a foundation model for fraud alert explanations. They need explainability for regulatory audits. Which AWS feature and model property best support this?

answers.A: Bedrock agents; high throughput
answers.B: SageMaker Model Cards; transparent, white-box model
answers.C: Amazon Q; token-based billing
answers.D: PartyRock; multimodal inputs

explanation: Model Cards document model lineage and behavior. Choosing a transparent model enhances auditability and explainability.

stem: A logistics AI team wants to generate route summaries from GPS data. They face variable output lengths and missing details. Which parameter modification and technique best address both issues?

answers.A: Set max length and implement prompt templates with required fields
answers.B: Increase temperature and use chain-of-thought
answers.C: Enable logit bias for key terms
answers.D: Use few-shot prompting without templates

explanation: Limiting max length controls size; prompt templates enforce inclusion of mandatory fields, ensuring detail completeness.

stem: A retail AI solution generates product descriptions; the business cares about ARPU uplift. Which performance metric should they track, and why?

answers.A: F1 score on category labels
answers.B: Perplexity on description corpus
answers.C: Average revenue per user (ARPU) before vs after deployment
answers.D: Inference latency

explanation: ARPU directly measures revenue impact per user, aligning model output quality with financial performance.

stem: A car manufacturer uses generative AI to draft maintenance manuals. They require minimal hallucinations in technical instructions. Which approach best ensures accuracy?

answers.A: High temperature with few-shot examples
answers.B: RAG with an indexed manual database in OpenSearch
answers.C: Chain-of-thought prompting
answers.D: Fine-tune on generic technical corpus

explanation: RAG using an indexed, authoritative manual database grounds generation in correct technical content, eliminating hallucinations.

stem: An e-commerce site uses generative AI for dynamic ad copy. They want to optimize click-through and avoid repetitiveness. Which combination of settings and metrics is optimal?

answers.A: Temperature 1.0; BLEU
answers.B: Temperature 0.0; perplexity
answers.C: Top-p = 0.3; ROUGE
answers.D: Moderate temperature and top-p; CTR and novelty score

explanation: Moderate sampling settings balance novelty and coherence; tracking CTR (engagement) and a novelty metric prevents repetitive copy.

stem: A pharmaceutical company uses generative AI to summarize clinical trial reports. They need to minimize hallucinations and measure summary relevance. Which evaluation approach and metric should they implement?

answers.A: RAG with human review via Amazon A2I and ROUGE-L against expert summaries
answers.B: Zero-shot prompting and BLEU
answers.C: High temperature generation and perplexity
answers.D: Chain-of-thought prompting and F1 score

explanation: RAG anchors to real reports; human-in-the-loop review quantifies hallucinations and ROUGE-L measures relevance to expert summaries.

stem: A financial news platform automates article translation. They need to track cross-domain accuracy for emerging topics. Which business metric and process best capture model performance drift?

answers.A: Average BLEU across domains
answers.B: Perplexity on all content
answers.C: ROUGE on English only
answers.D: Periodic BLEU evaluation on emerging-topic test set with Model Monitor alerts

explanation: Periodic BLEU on a domain-specific test set detects drift in new topics; Model Monitor alerts ensure timely retraining.

stem: A broadcaster uses generative AI to script news intros. They observe unintended bias in phrasing political content. Which root cause and mitigation best resolve this?

answers.A: Pre-training data bias; fine-tune on balanced political corpora
answers.B: Hallucinations; use RAG
answers.C: Nondeterminism; lower temperature
answers.D: Scalability; use higher throughput endpoints

explanation: Bias stems from pre-training data. Fine-tuning on a balanced dataset corrects model bias and yields neutral phrasing.

stem: A travel app generates destination descriptions. They want to maximize user engagement but must avoid misleading content. Which generation strategy and metric pairing achieves this?

answers.A: High temperature with ROUGE
answers.B: Low temperature with perplexity
answers.C: Moderate temperature with CTR and human-rated truthfulness
answers.D: Top-p sampling with BLEU

explanation: Moderate temperature encourages creative but controlled text. Tracking CTR measures engagement and truthfulness ratings detect misleading content.

stem: A manufacturing firm uses generative AI for maintenance logs summarization. They need to detect out-of-distribution inputs causing model errors. Which AWS feature and process helps guard against this limitation?

answers.A: Amazon Q; source citations
answers.B: SageMaker Model Monitor with custom OOD detection rules
answers.C: Amazon A2I for hallucination review
answers.D: Bedrock agents for orchestration

explanation: Model Monitor can detect when inputs fall outside the training distribution, triggering alerts or human review before inference.

stem: A retailer uses a foundation model to generate email marketing subject lines. They want to A/B test variations but avoid sacrificing deliverability through spammy language. Which evaluation metric and prompt technique combination best balances creativity and compliance?

answers.A: High temperature; BLEU
answers.B: Zero-shot; perplexity
answers.C: Few-shot; ROUGE
answers.D: Moderate temperature; human-rated spam score and open rate

explanation: Moderate sampling ensures creative copy, while human-rated spam scoring and tracking open rates measure compliance and effectiveness.

stem: A legal AI team must generate redacted contract summaries. They require strict accuracy and no accidental disclosures. Which generative AI limitation poses the biggest risk, and how can they mitigate it?

answers.A: Hallucinations; use RAG with redaction filter and human review via A2I
answers.B: Latency; optimize GPU endpoints
answers.C: Scalability; shard inference across endpoints
answers.D: Throughput; increase batch size

explanation: Hallucinations can reintroduce redacted content. RAG with filters and human review ensures no sensitive data is leaked.

stem: A SaaS analytics company uses generative AI to write SQL queries from natural language. They notice queries sometimes reference nonexistent tables. Which model limitation is this, and what strategy best addresses it?

answers.A: Latency; improve instance type
answers.B: Cost; switch to Spot Instances
answers.C: Hallucinations; employ RAG with schema retrieved from live database
answers.D: Deployment complexity; use Bedrock

explanation: Model hallucinations produce invalid queries. RAG with live database schema ensures generated SQL matches actual tables.

stem: A startup needs to prototype a document summarization application using a large language model without managing infrastructure. They require minimal latency and no fine-tuning. Which AWS service or feature best meets these requirements?

answers.A: SageMaker JumpStart custom training job
answers.B: Amazon Bedrock managed foundation model endpoint
answers.C: Amazon Comprehend extractive summarization API
answers.D: Amazon SageMaker Real-Time Inference with a self-hosted open-source model

explanation: Amazon Bedrock provides fully managed, low-latency access to foundation models without customer-managed infrastructure. SageMaker JumpStart custom jobs require management and fine-tuning, Comprehend is extractive only, and self-hosting imposes infrastructure overhead.

stem: A financial services company must run high-throughput generative chat sessions during market hours. They want predictable pricing per token and need to minimize cost under heavy load. Which pricing model should they choose?

answers.A: SageMaker JumpStart per-instance hourly pricing
answers.B: Bedrock usage-based with variable markup
answers.C: Bedrock token-based charges with volume discounts
answers.D: Amazon Q per-query fixed fee

explanation: Bedrock’s token-based model with volume discounts yields predictable per-token pricing and lower costs at scale. JumpStart hourly instances may idle and incur unused hours; Amazon Q’s per-query fee lacks token granularity.

stem: A healthcare application uses a confidential medical knowledge base with RAG via embeddings. They need a HIPAA-eligible, VPC-isolated embedding store with low latency. Which AWS service combination should they use?

answers.A: Amazon OpenSearch Service with public endpoints
answers.B: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL without encryption
answers.C: Amazon Neptune with VPN-only connectivity
answers.D: Amazon DocumentDB in VPC with encryption at rest and in transit

explanation: DocumentDB in a VPC with encryption supports HIPAA compliance and low latency for embedding storage. OpenSearch public endpoints and unencrypted RDS fail compliance; Neptune adds complexity and lacks managed embedding integration.

stem: A media company wants to generate images with a diffusion model hosted in Bedrock. They require burstable throughput up to 50 requests/sec during live events, and will pay only when models run. Which service feature should they use?

answers.A: Bedrock serverless inference with auto-scaling
answers.B: Bedrock provisioned capacity
answers.C: SageMaker Hosting with dedicated GPU instances
answers.D: Amazon EC2 Spot Instances running OpenAI API proxy

explanation: Bedrock serverless inference auto-scales to bursts and charges only per request. Provisioned capacity incurs fixed cost, SageMaker hosting requires instance management, and EC2 Spot Instances add operational complexity.

stem: A regulated enterprise must maintain model invocation logs and prompt inputs for audit, enforce encryption in transit, and isolate model endpoints. Which AWS configuration satisfies all requirements?

answers.A: Bedrock public endpoint with CloudTrail enabled
answers.B: Bedrock VPC endpoint with CloudTrail Data Events and TLS enforced
answers.C: SageMaker JumpStart with S3 logging only
answers.D: Amazon Q over HTTPS without VPC controls

explanation: Bedrock VPC endpoints with CloudTrail Data Events capture inputs and outputs, enforce TLS, and isolate traffic. Public endpoints or S3-only logging do not provide full isolation or comprehensive audit.

stem: A developer wants to fine-tune a foundation model for domain-specific language but minimize compute cost. They only need a few examples and can tolerate higher latency. Which approach balances cost and performance?

answers.A: Full fine-tuning in SageMaker with p3.16xlarge
answers.B: Bedrock fine-tuning with RLHF
answers.C: SageMaker Ground Truth data labeling
answers.D: In-context few-shot prompting on Bedrock foundation model

explanation: In-context few-shot prompting on Bedrock avoids fine-tuning fees and heavy compute, trading higher latency for much lower cost. Full fine-tuning is expensive, RLHF adds complexity, and Ground Truth only labels data.

stem: A startup evaluates embedding storage options for RAG workflows. They need sub-50 ms nearest neighbor search latency at 100 qps and minimal management overhead. Which service is optimal?

answers.A: Amazon OpenSearch Service with k-NN plugin
answers.B: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector extension
answers.C: Amazon DynamoDB with Lambda custom search
answers.D: Amazon Timestream optimized for time-series

explanation: OpenSearch k-NN plugin provides low-latency vector search at scale with managed service. Aurora pgvector incurs higher latency and management; DynamoDB+Lambda adds infra overhead; Timestream is for time-series.

stem: An application requires embedding generation and immediate storage. To minimize end-to-end latency, which invocation pattern should be used?

answers.A: Invoke Bedrock embedding API, store to S3 via SDK next
answers.B: Batch Bedrock embeddings, process in EMR, then S3
answers.C: Invoke Bedrock embedding API directly from Lambda writing to Amazon DynamoDB
answers.D: Precompute embeddings offline and store in Aurora

explanation: A Lambda that directly invokes Bedrock embeddings and writes to DynamoDB yields minimal latency and overhead. Batch or offline methods add delay; S3 introduces higher write latency for real-time needs.

stem: A legal firm must deploy a generative Q&A chatbot using Amazon Q. They require data residency in us-east-2, secure access, and usage logs. Which steps meet all requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Configure Amazon Q domain in us-east-2
answers.B: Enable VPC endpoints and PrivateLink for Q
answers.C: Use Comprehend Q&A instead of Amazon Q
answers.D: Use public Q endpoints with IP restriction

explanation: Configuring the domain in the required region and enabling VPC endpoints/PrivateLink secures and confines data. Comprehend Q&A is different service and public endpoints lack full isolation.

stem: A retail company is building a conversational shopping assistant using AWS Bedrock. The assistant must handle context windows up to 1,500 tokens, maintain average response latency under 200 ms, and minimize per-token cost. Which foundation model should the company choose?

answers.A: Anthropic Claude 2 (max 100k tokens, ~300 ms latency, high per-token cost)
answers.B: Amazon Titan Text (max 2,048 tokens, ~80 ms latency, lowest per-token price)
answers.C: Cohere Command (max 2,048 tokens, ~250 ms latency, moderate cost)
answers.D: Stability Text 2 (max 1,024 tokens, ~90 ms latency, lowest cost)

explanation: Titan Text meets the 1,500-token requirement, offers sub-200 ms latency, and has the lowest per-token price. Stability Text 2’s context is too small; Claude 2 has higher latency and cost; Cohere is slower.

stem: A healthcare analytics team needs to generate detailed patient summaries from long clinical notes (up to 8,000 tokens). Which approach best accommodates this requirement while controlling cost?

answers.A: Use a single in-context prompt with a Titan Text model.
answers.B: Fine-tune Amazon Titan Text on clinical notes.
answers.C: Implement Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with chunked embeddings and Amazon Bedrock.
answers.D: Switch to Anthropic Claude 2 without any retrieval.

explanation: RAG with chunked embeddings supports 8,000 tokens, reduces hallucinations, and avoids expensive fine-tuning. Titan’s window is too small; Claude 2 is cost-prohibitive; fine-tuning is overkill.

stem: An engineering firm requires multimodal inference on text and diagrams. Which AWS foundation model selection criteria is most critical?

answers.A: Support for multimodal input (text+image)
answers.B: Lowest possible per-token cost
answers.C: Maximum context length
answers.D: Highest temperature variability

explanation: Multimodal inference demands a foundation model trained on both text and image inputs. Cost, context length, and temperature are secondary if the model lacks multimodal capability.

stem: A media company must generate video captions with consistent style and minimal hallucinations. Which inference parameter change will most reduce hallucinations?

answers.A: Increase temperature from 0.2 to 0.8
answers.B: Decrease temperature from 0.8 to 0.2
answers.C: Increase max tokens to 1,000
answers.D: Remove stop sequences

explanation: Lowering temperature reduces randomness and hallucinations. Increasing max tokens or removing stop sequences does not address hallucinations; higher temperature increases them.

stem: A startup wants to store vector embeddings for semantic search of documents with occasional schema changes and dynamic updates. Which storage service is best?

answers.A: Amazon OpenSearch Service
answers.B: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
answers.C: Amazon Neptune
answers.D: Amazon DocumentDB

explanation: Amazon Neptune provides graph storage optimized for dynamic, schema-flexible vector embeddings and efficient nearest-neighbor search. OpenSearch is less flexible for dynamic schemas; RDS and DocumentDB aren’t optimized for graph vector queries.

stem: A financial regulator uses a foundation model to answer compliance queries against a static regulation corpus. The corpus is ~50 GB. What is the most cost-effective way to ensure answers reflect the latest regulations?

answers.A: Fine-tune the model every time regulations update
answers.B: Use a large context prompt of full documents
answers.C: Use in-context learning with all regulations loaded
answers.D: Implement RAG with embeddings in Amazon OpenSearch and refresh index on updates

explanation: RAG with OpenSearch embeddings allows incremental updates of a 50 GB corpus, ensures currency, and is more cost-effective than repeated fine-tuning or huge context prompts.

stem: An AI team must adapt a foundation model to a niche legal language using only 1,000 labeled examples and limited budget. Which customization approach balances cost and performance?

answers.A: Full pre-training on legal text
answers.B: RLHF with human annotators
answers.C: Instruction-tuning (fine-tuning) on the 1,000 examples
answers.D: In-context learning without any fine-tuning

explanation: Instruction-tuning on a small dataset is cost-effective and improves domain performance. Full pre-training and RLHF are too expensive; pure in-context learning yields weaker performance.

stem: A media monitoring system needs to process user queries and, if needed, execute a sequence of API calls (translation, sentiment, summarization). Which Bedrock feature simplifies orchestration?

answers.A: RAG with OpenSearch
answers.B: Agentless multi-model pipeline
answers.C: In-context chain-of-thought prompting
answers.D: Bedrock Agents

explanation: Bedrock Agents orchestrate multi-step workflows across APIs. Chain-of-thought or RAG won’t manage external API calls; “agentless pipeline” isn’t a real feature.

stem: An enterprise requires an LLM endpoint that can scale to unpredictable traffic with cost-efficient idle pricing. Which invocation mode should you choose?

answers.A: Synchronous API with provisioned concurrency
answers.B: Synchronous API with on-demand (no provisioned concurrency)
answers.C: Asynchronous API with on-demand invocations
answers.D: Batch transform jobs in SageMaker

explanation: Asynchronous on-demand endpoints scale elastically, incur no idle provisioned cost, and handle unpredictable traffic. Synchronous on-demand can throttle; provisioned is costly; batch jobs don’t suit real-time.

stem: A banking app uses a foundation model to process user transaction queries. It must redact PII before generating responses. Which integration achieves this with minimal latency?

answers.A: Run a Lambda pre-processor to filter PII then call Bedrock
answers.B: Use a Bedrock agent with built-in PII redaction tool
answers.C: Fine-tune the model to ignore PII
answers.D: Implement post-processing in the client application

explanation: A Bedrock Agent with built-in PII redaction provides low-latency, integrated protection. Lambda adds latency; fine-tuning won’t reliably remove PII; client post-processing is insecure.

stem: A logistics company wants to store embeddings for thousands of ever-changing route descriptions with atomic updates and graph queries. Which storage is best?

answers.A: Amazon OpenSearch Service
answers.B: Amazon DynamoDB
answers.C: Amazon Neptune
answers.D: Amazon RDS

explanation: Neptune supports ACID graph updates and nearest-neighbor searches. OpenSearch is less reliable for atomic graph operations; DynamoDB isn’t optimized for vector search; RDS lacks graph features.

stem: A startup has a $1,000 monthly AI budget. They need a nightly summary of 100,000 news articles (500 tokens each). Which inference pattern is most cost-effective?

answers.A: Real-time streaming inference
answers.B: Synchronous API per article
answers.C: Bedrock Agents orchestration
answers.D: Batch transform in SageMaker

explanation: Batch transform jobs in SageMaker run in bulk overnight at lower per-token cost with no concurrent endpoint overhead. Real-time and synchronous calls cost more; Agents add complexity.

stem: A legal tech company must guarantee explainability for each generated paragraph. Which foundation model choice best balances explainability and performance?

answers.A: Anthropic Claude 2
answers.B: Amazon Titan Text with model cards and low complexity
answers.C: Cohere Command
answers.D: OpenAI GPT-4 via Bedrock

explanation: Titan Text with published model cards offers high transparency. Claude 2 and OpenAI GPT-4 lack full model cards on AWS; Cohere Command is opaque.

stem: A data analytics team wants real-time chat summarization where occasional context window overruns occur. Which strategy best handles overruns?

answers.A: Increase max tokens indefinitely
answers.B: Use temperature of 1.0
answers.C: Implement sliding-window RAG with embeddings
answers.D: Fine-tune the foundation model

explanation: Sliding-window RAG seamlessly handles context overruns by chunking and retrieving relevant segments, without unbounded tokens or expensive fine-tuning.

stem: An education platform wants to reduce inference costs by at least 50%. They currently fine-tune a foundation model for every course update. What alternative yields the greatest savings?

answers.A: Use in-context learning with dynamic prompts instead of fine-tuning
answers.B: Increase provisioned concurrency
answers.C: Switch to a larger foundation model
answers.D: Batch transform jobs daily

explanation: In-context learning eliminates fine-tuning costs, achieving >50% savings. Provisioned concurrency and batch transforms do not address fine-tuning expense; larger models cost more.

stem: A manufacturing firm needs natural language control of robots in multiple languages. Which foundation model feature is most important?

answers.A: High max tokens
answers.B: Low temperature
answers.C: Multilingual language coverage
answers.D: Large model size

explanation: Multilingual coverage is essential for multi-language commands. Token length, temperature, and size are secondary if the model can’t understand required languages.

stem: A consulting firm sees unpredictable spikes in LLM usage during peak hours. To control request latency and cost, which Bedrock concurrency feature should they adjust?

answers.A: Batch size
answers.B: Provisioned concurrency
answers.C: Max tokens
answers.D: Temperature

explanation: Provisioned concurrency allocates pre-warmed capacity to maintain low latency during peaks. Batch size, max tokens, and temperature don’t manage concurrency.

stem: A telecom company uses RAG with a 200 GB document store. Index updates must reflect new data within minutes. Which architecture meets this requirement?

answers.A: Rebuild the entire OpenSearch index daily
answers.B: Fine-tune the model hourly
answers.C: Use DynamoDB for embeddings
answers.D: Stream new docs to OpenSearch via Kinesis Data Firehose

explanation: Streaming via Firehose ensures minute-latency index updates in OpenSearch. Daily rebuilds are too slow; DynamoDB lacks vector search; frequent fine-tuning is impractical.

stem: A media company must enforce a hard stop at 200 tokens in every generated summary. Which inference parameter should they set?

answers.A: Temperature to 0
answers.B: maxTokenLimit to 200
answers.C: TopP to 1.0
answers.D: Beam width to 5

explanation: Setting maxTokenLimit to 200 enforces a hard stop. Temperature, TopP, and beam width do not constrain output length.

stem: A legal research tool needs precise citations. Which retrieval method should you combine with a foundation model to ensure factual accuracy?

answers.A: In-context few-shot prompting
answers.B: Temperature of 1.0
answers.C: RAG with a vetted legal corpus
answers.D: Increase max tokens

explanation: RAG with a vetted legal corpus grounds responses in source documents, ensuring factual citations. Prompting, temperature, and token length by themselves don’t guarantee accuracy.

stem: A startup wants to orchestrate a dynamic knowledge-search→generate workflow within Bedrock without writing orchestration code. Which feature should they use?

answers.A: Custom Lambda preprocessor
answers.B: In-context prompt chaining
answers.C: Fine-tuned multi-task model
answers.D: Bedrock Agents

explanation: Bedrock Agents provide no-code orchestration of search and generation steps. Prompt chaining and Lambda require manual coding; fine-tuning can’t automate retrieval.

stem: A company must pay only for inference time used, with no idle costs, and handle unpredictable daily traffic. Which Bedrock billing option suits this?

answers.A: Provisioned concurrency
answers.B: On-demand concurrency
answers.C: Monthly subscription
answers.D: Batch transform

explanation: On-demand concurrency bills per inference with no idle fees. Provisioned concurrency incurs idle charges; subscriptions and batch transforms aren’t per-inference real-time.

stem: A risk analytics team must run summary inference on a petabyte-scale dataset overnight under a strict $2,000 budget. Which architecture is most appropriate?

answers.A: Real-time Bedrock endpoint
answers.B: Provisioned concurrency synchronous calls
answers.C: Bedrock Agents
answers.D: SageMaker batch transform with Spot instances

explanation: SageMaker batch transform with Spot instances handles large datasets overnight under budget. Real-time endpoints and Agents are costlier for batch.

stem: An AI solution must ensure every generated output is traceable to specific data sources. Which RAG component provides this?

answers.A: Document retrieval metadata
answers.B: High temperature
answers.C: maxTokenLimit
answers.D: Fine-tuning

explanation: Retrieval metadata tracks source documents for traceability. Temperature and token limits don’t; fine-tuning embeds data but lacks per-generation traceability.

stem: A biotech firm wants to fine-tune a foundation model on proprietary data but also retain the ability to use general knowledge. Which customization approach preserves general capabilities?

answers.A: Full model replacement with proprietary-only data
answers.B: Instruction-tuning on proprietary data
answers.C: Continual pre-training on only proprietary data
answers.D: In-context learning only

explanation: Instruction-tuning adapts the model to proprietary data while preserving base knowledge. Full replacement or continual pre-training risks catastrophic forgetting; in-context alone is less performant.

stem: A global news aggregator needs sub-100 ms inference for headlines in multiple regions. How should they minimize network latency?

answers.A: Use a single US-East Bedrock endpoint
answers.B: Enable provisioned concurrency only
answers.C: Increase maxTokenLimit
answers.D: Deploy regional Bedrock endpoints nearest users

explanation: Regional endpoints reduce network hops and latency. A single US-East endpoint increases latency for distant users; provisioned concurrency and token limits don’t address network delay.

stem: A manufacturing firm uses a foundation model to translate technical manuals. They observe inconsistent terminology. Which prompt engineering technique best improves consistency?

answers.A: Use a prompt template with defined glossary and format instructions
answers.B: Increase temperature to 0.9
answers.C: Remove stop sequences
answers.D: Use only zero-shot prompting

explanation: A glossary template enforces consistent terminology. Higher temperature increases variance; removing stop sequences and zero-shot prompting degrade control.

stem: A software company must process variable batch sizes of code snippets with predictable billing and no idle charges. Which endpoint type should they choose?

answers.A: Provisioned Bedrock endpoint
answers.B: On-demand Bedrock endpoint
answers.C: SageMaker batch transform
answers.D: Synchronous Lambda invocation

explanation: On-demand Bedrock endpoints bill per inference with no idle fees, ideal for variable loads. Provisioned endpoints incur idle costs; batch transform and Lambda aren’t optimized for real-time code snippet processing.

stem: An enterprise team must comply with data residency rules. Which customization method ensures data never leaves their AWS Region?

answers.A: Use a public API for fine-tuning
answers.B: Use a global Bedrock endpoint
answers.C: In-context learning with external data
answers.D: Fine-tune a private Bedrock foundation model in their region

explanation: Private regional fine-tuning keeps data in the same region. Public APIs and global endpoints may move data; in-context learning doesn’t train the model but still sends data externally.

stem: A contact center wants to automatically correct grammar and expand abbreviations in live chats before analysis. Which approach yields the lowest end-to-end latency?

answers.A: Batch transform jobs hourly
answers.B: On-demand Bedrock text endpoint with high temperature
answers.C: Synchronous Bedrock endpoint with moderate max tokens
answers.D: RAG with OpenSearch

explanation: A synchronous Bedrock text endpoint with moderate token limit gives lowest real-time latency. Batch jobs are too slow; high temperature is irrelevant to latency; RAG adds retrieval overhead.

stem: A gaming company needs the model to generate personalized dialogs referencing user history stored in DynamoDB. Which integration pattern is best?

answers.A: Embed all history in the prompt
answers.B: Fine-tune model on historical data
answers.C: Use a large maxTokenLimit
answers.D: Pre-retrieve user history from DynamoDB and pass via prompt or RAG
