explanation: Masking or hashing sensitive data in logs protects privacy while preserving auditability.

stem: Your prompt uses multi-shot examples but the order influences correctness. How do you mitigate ordering bias?

answers.A: Randomize the order of few-shot examples during prompt construction.
answers.B: Increase temperature.
answers.C: Use negative prompts blocking first examples.
answers.D: Switch to chain-of-thought.

explanation: Randomizing example order avoids accidental bias toward earlier examples.

stem: You need to test a prompt’s vulnerability to jailbreaking. Which step is most effective?

answers.A: Increase temperature to encourage rule breaking.
answers.B: Use few-shot allowed content examples.
answers.C: Add negative prompts blocking “jailbreak”.
answers.D: Design adversarial inputs that attempt to override instructions and test responses.

explanation: Adversarial testing reveals if malicious inputs can override system instructions, identifying jailbreak risks.

stem: A financial services firm needs a foundation model to understand domain‐specific jargon from its proprietary 10 GB corpus. They have limited human‐labelled data but extensive raw text. Which customization method should they apply to best adapt the foundation model to their domain?

answers.A: Instruction tuning using supervised examples
answers.B: Reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF)
answers.C: Domain adaptation via continuous pre‐training on raw text
answers.D: Transfer learning with a small labelled dataset only

explanation: Domain adaptation (continued pre‐training) uses raw domain text without heavy labels to adapt model.

stem: A startup wants to fine‐tune a public LLM for summarization of legal contracts but cannot afford extensive compute. Which low‐resource fine‐tuning approach balances cost and performance?

answers.A: Full parameter fine‐tuning on all layers
answers.B: Instruction tuning with a prompt example dataset
answers.C: Reinforcement learning with human feedback
answers.D: Domain adaptation with large unlabelled data

explanation: Instruction tuning with curated prompts uses less compute than full fine‐tuning and improves summarization.

stem: A retail company notices its fine‐tuned foundation model performance degrading monthly due to changing product catalogs. Which process addresses this issue?

answers.A: One‐time fine‐tuning on initial data
answers.B: Periodic instruction tuning only when issues appear
answers.C: Revert to the base foundation model
answers.D: Continuous pre‐training with recent catalog data

explanation: Continuous pre‐training on fresh data combats concept drift.

stem: When preparing data for fine‐tuning a foundation model with RLHF, which step is MOST critical to ensure high‐quality reward signals?

answers.A: Curating diverse human preference comparisons
answers.B: Balancing classes in the raw unlabeled corpus
answers.C: Normalizing text token lengths
answers.D: Applying data augmentation to unlabelled data

explanation: RLHF needs human‐annotated preference data for reward model training.

stem: A life‐sciences company wants to restrict a foundation model’s clinical advice to approved guidelines. Which fine‐tuning method best encodes these constraints?

answers.A: Instruction tuning with guideline‐based prompts
answers.B: Domain adaptation on general clinical text
answers.C: Supervised transfer learning on labeled Q&A pairs
answers.D: Reinforcement learning with patient feedback

explanation: Instruction tuning can encode guideline style and constraints directly.

stem: You have a foundation model fine‐tuned on 50k labeled examples. You want further improvement on a subcategory representing only 500 examples. Which approach is optimal?

answers.A: Retrain entire model on combined 50.5k dataset
answers.B: Perform targeted fine‐tuning (transfer learning) on 500 examples
answers.C: Use RLHF with broad general feedback
answers.D: Continuous pre‐training on unlabeled data

explanation: Targeted transfer learning on few examples adapts specialized subcategory.

stem: A conversational agent generates unsafe suggestions occasionally. You have developer time but limited data. Which customization pipeline addresses safety concerns?

answers.A: Domain adaptation on more unlabeled conversation logs
answers.B: Instruction tuning with longer prompts
answers.C: Transfer learning on generic safe corpora
answers.D: RLHF incorporating human safety feedback

explanation: RLHF with human‐defined safe/unsafe labels tunes reward for safety.

stem: During fine‐tuning a foundation model on image captioning, performance stalls. You suspect data issues. What should you evaluate FIRST?

answers.A: Model hyperparameters like learning rate
answers.B: Compute instance type
answers.C: Representativeness and labeling consistency of captioned images
answers.D: Batch size and tokenization schema

explanation: Data quality and representativeness are first to inspect when fine‐tuning stalls.

stem: An LLM trained for medical advice must comply with data‐privacy laws. Which data preparation practice is MOST important before fine‐tuning?

answers.A: Converting text to lower‐case tokens
answers.B: Anonymizing and removing personal identifiers
answers.C: Segmenting documents by sentence length
answers.D: Balancing positive/negative sentiment

explanation: Removing personally identifiable information is key for compliance.

stem: A customer support chatbot was instruction tuned but underperforms on technical queries. Which next step will most effectively improve domain accuracy?

answers.A: Increase prompt length
answers.B: Switch to RLHF
answers.C: Domain adaptation with technical support transcripts
answers.D: Fine‐tune on general instruction datasets

explanation: Continued pre‐training on domain transcripts boosts technical knowledge.

stem: Which characteristic distinguishes instruction tuning from domain adaptation?

answers.A: Instruction tuning uses paired input‐output examples
answers.B: Domain adaptation requires human feedback loops
answers.C: Instruction tuning uses raw unlabeled text
answers.D: Domain adaptation modifies reward functions

explanation: Instruction tuning relies on (instruction, response) supervised pairs.

stem: A retailer fine‐tuned a model on product descriptions but wants to reduce hallucinations. Which addition to the fine‐tuning pipeline helps?

answers.A: Increase batch size
answers.B: Swap tokenizer for larger vocabulary
answers.C: Add more unlabeled data
answers.D: Incorporate RLHF with human‐rated truthfulness

explanation: RLHF can penalize hallucinations via human feedback.

stem: You must measure the impact of fine‐tuning on model size and latency. Which evaluation metric combination is most relevant?

answers.A: Perplexity and BLEU score
answers.B: Model parameter count and inference time
answers.C: ROUGE and BERTScore
answers.D: Training loss and validation accuracy

explanation: Parameter count and latency directly measure size and inference performance.

stem: A LLM fine‐tuning job on AWS Bedrock fails due to OOM errors. Which action best mitigates the issue?

answers.A: Increase learning rate
answers.B: Use larger batch size
answers.C: Enable parameter-efficient fine‐tuning (PEFT)
answers.D: Switch to full model fine‐tuning

explanation: PEFT reduces memory use by tuning fewer parameters.

stem: For training a specialized legal model you need detailed citations. Which fine‐tuning method supports injecting citations into outputs?

answers.A: Instruction tuning with citation‐annotated examples
answers.B: Domain adaptation on legal text only
answers.C: Transfer learning on generic corpora
answers.D: RLHF without examples

explanation: Instruction tuning with explicit examples teaches citation patterns.

stem: A media company wants to adapt an LLM to generate poetry in a niche style. They have 1k curated poems. Which approach?

answers.A: Domain adaptation on large unlabeled text
answers.B: Instruction tuning (few‐shot) with provided poems
answers.C: RLHF with reader preferences
answers.D: Continuous pre‐training on general poetry

explanation: Instruction tuning on curated examples captures niche style effectively.

stem: Which risk is MOST associated with a foundation model undergoing continuous pre‐training on uncurated data?

answers.A: Longer inference latency
answers.B: Insufficient parameter updates
answers.C: Introduction of bias and drift
answers.D: Loss of base‐model capabilities

explanation: Uncurated data can introduce unwanted biases and concept drift.

stem: After instruction tuning, a model still fails a key business requirement 30% of the time. What is the MOST direct way to further optimize output quality?

answers.A: Increase dataset size by adding raw text
answers.B: Switch foundation model to a larger variant
answers.C: Decrease training epochs
answers.D: Apply RLHF with quality‐weighted feedback

explanation: RLHF optimizes according to human‐rated quality metrics.

stem: A foundation model fine‐tuning on SageMaker took days. You need faster iterations. Which practice speeds up experiments?

answers.A: Use full‐precision (FP32) training
answers.B: Employ parameter‐efficient fine‐tuning methods
answers.C: Remove early stopping
answers.D: Increase dataset size

explanation: Parameter‐efficient methods reduce compute and speed up tuning.

stem: Which dataset split is MOST appropriate for preventing data leakage in fine‐tuning evaluation?

answers.A: 80% train, 20% train
answers.B: 90% train, 10% test (no validation)
answers.C: Train, validation, test with disjoint IDs
answers.D: Train on combined train/validation and test on same

explanation: Disjoint splits avoid leakage and ensure true evaluation.

stem: A sensitive language model requires high transparency. Which customization step provides the best audit trail?

answers.A: Record data lineage and fine‐tuning parameters
answers.B: Use only instruction tuning
answers.C: Skip continuous pre‐training
answers.D: Rely solely on prompt engineering

explanation: Versioning data and parameters ensures auditability.

stem: A model fine‐tuned via RLHF exhibits mode collapse. Which corrective action is most effective?

answers.A: Increase batch size
answers.B: Add more uncurated data
answers.C: Diversify human feedback and reward coverage
answers.D: Reduce feedback frequency

explanation: Broadening feedback signals prevents collapse to narrow outputs.

stem: Your team wants to reuse a fine‐tuning pipeline for multiple domains. Which architectural choice ensures modularity?

answers.A: Embed all data in a single preprocessing script
answers.B: Parameterize data pipelines per domain
answers.C: Hard‐code model names
answers.D: Use one monolithic training job

explanation: Parameterization allows easy swapping of domain data.

stem: Which fine‐tuning strategy best minimizes catastrophic forgetting of base knowledge?

answers.A: Combined training on base and new data
answers.B: Full fine‐tuning only on new data
answers.C: Domain adaptation on new data alone
answers.D: Instruction tuning after base training

explanation: Mixing base and domain data retains original capabilities.

stem: You have limited human feedback for RLHF. Which technique improves the reward model training?

answers.A: Remove low‐variance feedback
answers.B: Train on raw unlabelled data
answers.C: Increase model size
answers.D: Apply data augmentation on feedback pairs

explanation: Augmenting few feedback pairs increases diversity for reward training.

stem: A compliance audit demands record of each fine‐tuning run. Which AWS feature ensures full traceability?

answers.A: SageMaker Hyperparameter Tuning jobs
answers.B: SageMaker Experiments and model registry
answers.C: AWS CloudTrail only
answers.D: SNS notifications

explanation: SageMaker Experiments tracks run metadata and model versions.

stem: A large multimodal foundation model is adapted to classify medical images. Which fine‐tuning method uses both image and text pairs?

answers.A: Instruction tuning on text only
answers.B: RLHF with clinician feedback
answers.C: Multimodal transfer learning with paired datasets
answers.D: Continuous pre‐training on image tags

explanation: Multimodal transfer learning adapts model on both modalities.

stem: Your fine‐tuning budget is fixed. You need to decide dataset size vs label quality trade‐off. Which guideline is MOST appropriate?

answers.A: Prefer smaller high‐quality labelled data over larger noisy data
answers.B: Always maximize dataset size
answers.C: Label all data regardless of noise
answers.D: Use only unlabelled data

explanation: High‐quality labels have more impact than noisy large data.

stem: During continuous pre‐training, model overfits to recent data. Which addition to pipeline mitigates this?

answers.A: Increase training epochs
answers.B: Include regularization with replay of older data
answers.C: Remove older data entirely
answers.D: Decrease batch size

explanation: Regular replay of old data prevents overfitting to new data.

stem: A retail company fine-tunes a foundation model to summarize customer reviews. They notice that ROUGE scores are high, but human evaluators rate summaries as irrelevant. Which action MOST effectively diagnoses the issue?

answers.A: Increase the beam width during inference to improve relevance.
answers.B: Switch from ROUGE to BLEU to better capture summary quality.
answers.C: Apply a larger prompt context window before generation.
answers.D: Perform a human evaluation focused on summary faithfulness and compare against ROUGE components.

explanation: Comparing human faithfulness ratings with ROUGE sub-scores (e.g., ROUGE-L for longest common subsequence) reveals where automatic metrics diverge from human judgment, diagnosing the misalignment.

stem: An enterprise uses a foundation model for code generation. They benchmark on a public dataset and report BLEU-4 of 45. After deploying to production, user satisfaction drops. Which evaluation step could have predicted this drop?

answers.A: Measuring perplexity on the public dataset.
answers.B: Tracking model loss during fine-tuning.
answers.C: Conducting scenario-based human evaluation with real developer prompts.
answers.D: Comparing BLEU scores across different code languages.

explanation: Real-world developer prompts differ from benchmark data; scenario-based human evaluation reveals usability issues before deployment.

stem: A team uses BERTScore to evaluate translation quality, but it favors verbose outputs. What complementary metric should they include to penalize verbosity?

answers.A: SARI
answers.B: Length-penalized BLEU (BLEU with brevity penalty)
answers.C: ROUGE recall
answers.D: METEOR without synonym matching

explanation: BLEU’s brevity penalty discourages overly long translations, complementing BERTScore which does not penalize verbosity.

stem: A chatbot powered by a foundation model shows high automated metric scores but low conversion rates. Which evaluation metric addresses this gap?

answers.A: Online A/B testing measuring end-to-end conversion
answers.B: Token-level accuracy on a held-out dataset
answers.C: Self-BLEU to measure diversity
answers.D: Embedding cosine similarity against training data

explanation: Online A/B testing with conversion as the key metric ties model performance directly to business objectives, unlike offline metrics.

stem: During evaluation of a summarization foundation model, diversity of outputs is a priority. Which metric combination BEST captures both quality and diversity?

answers.A: ROUGE-L and BLEU-4
answers.B: BLEU-4 and perplexity
answers.C: BERTScore and sequence length variance
answers.D: ROUGE for quality and Self-BLEU for diversity

explanation: ROUGE assesses quality against references, while Self-BLEU measures diversity by evaluating overlap among generated summaries.

stem: A finance company fine-tunes a model to generate risk analysis reports. They must ensure factual accuracy. Which evaluation approach is MOST appropriate?

answers.A: Compute ROUGE-F1 against sample reports.
answers.B: Use a domain expert human evaluation with a fact-checking rubric.
answers.C: Measure perplexity on a financial corpus.
answers.D: Evaluate BLEU against generic report templates.

explanation: Only domain experts can reliably assess factual accuracy in risk reports; automated metrics cannot detect subtle errors.

stem: A team compares two foundation models for dialogue generation using BLEU score. The model with higher BLEU yields more generic responses. What evaluation change addresses this?

answers.A: Increase training data size.
answers.B: Switch to ROUGE-L metric.
answers.C: Include human evaluation of response informativeness.
answers.D: Add length penalty to BLEU.

explanation: Human evaluation of informativeness identifies generic but high-BLEU outputs, guiding selection of the model that better satisfies user needs.

stem: A model yields high BERTScore but low user engagement. Which additional metric or process should be introduced?

answers.A: Task completion rate in an interactive user study
answers.B: Perplexity measured on training data
answers.C: ROUGE recall
answers.D: BLEU-1 to check unigram overlap

explanation: Task completion rate in actual interactions ties performance to user engagement, uncovering issues automated scores miss.

stem: An LLM-based summarization service is evaluated using ROUGE. Reports show high recall but low precision. What does this imply and how can it be improved?

answers.A: Summaries are too short; increase summary length.
answers.B: Summaries include too much irrelevant content; implement extractive filtering.
answers.C: Models are underfitting; increase training epochs.
answers.D: ROUGE is unreliable; switch to BLEU.

explanation: High recall/low precision indicates summaries cover all reference content but add noise; extractive filtering removes irrelevant parts, improving precision.

stem: A model’s BLEU score is stable but user satisfaction drops after fine-tuning. Which evaluation should have been run pre-deployment?

answers.A: Compute higher n-gram BLEU (BLEU-5)
answers.B: Measure BLEU on a larger validation set
answers.C: Conduct blind human evaluations comparing pre- and post-fine-tuning outputs
answers.D: Check perplexity on fine-tuning data

explanation: Blind human evaluations directly compare outputs to detect declines in quality that BLEU alone may not reveal.

stem: When evaluating a generation model across multiple languages, which metric combination balances adequacy and fluency?

answers.A: BLEU for adequacy and perplexity for fluency
answers.B: ROUGE for fluency and BERTScore for adequacy
answers.C: Self-BLEU for consistency and BLEU for adequacy
answers.D: METEOR for adequacy and language-specific perplexity for fluency

explanation: METEOR accounts for synonyms and alignments indicating adequacy, while perplexity per language measures fluency in that language.

stem: A company uses a benchmark dataset to evaluate a foundation model but suspects data leakage. Which approach BEST uncovers leakage?

answers.A: Compute overlap of n-grams between training and test sets.
answers.B: Re-run evaluation with a different metric.
answers.C: Increase the test set size.
answers.D: Shuffle the test data.

explanation: N-gram overlap analysis reveals if test examples are too similar to training data, indicating potential leakage.

stem: During evaluation, a summary model’s ROUGE scores vary significantly across topics. What evaluation strategy addresses this variability?

answers.A: Use BLEU instead of ROUGE.
answers.B: Segment evaluation by topic and report per-topic metrics.
answers.C: Aggregate scores across all topics only.
answers.D: Increase model size to reduce variability.

explanation: Per-topic metrics identify domains where performance lags, guiding targeted improvements.

stem: A model generates financial recommendations. Business requires explanations. Which evaluation method assures explanation quality?

answers.A: Compute BERTScore on explanation tokens.
answers.B: Use perplexity to assess explanation fluency.
answers.C: Conduct human evaluation with a rubric for explanation completeness and correctness.
answers.D: Measure explanation length.

explanation: Only human evaluators using a rubric can reliably assess the substance and correctness of model-generated explanations.

stem: A foundation model returns biased generation for certain demographics. Which evaluation process best uncovers this bias?

answers.A: Check perplexity across demographics.
answers.B: Compute aggregate BLEU scores across the dataset.
answers.C: Use Self-BLEU for diversity.
answers.D: Perform targeted human evaluation on demographic-specific prompts.

explanation: Targeted human evaluation reveals bias in outputs across demographic groups, which automated metrics may not detect.

stem: You need to evaluate grounding in RAG-enhanced generation. Which approach measures ground-truth consistency?

answers.A: Compute ROUGE against retrieval documents only.
answers.B: Use factuality metrics or human fact-checking against source documents.
answers.C: Measure Self-BLEU against previous answers.
answers.D: Evaluate token perplexity conditional on retrieved context.

explanation: Factuality metrics or human fact-checking directly assess whether generated content is consistent with retrieved source documents.

stem: A document QA system for legal files reports high EM (Exact Match) but low user trust. What evaluation should be added?

answers.A: Human evaluation of answer justification coherence.
answers.B: Compute BLEU against answer keys.
answers.C: Increase EM to higher n-grams.
answers.D: Measure Self-BLEU for consistency.

explanation: Human assessment of justification coherence evaluates trustworthiness beyond exact matching of answers.

stem: An AI agent orchestrating multiple foundation models must be evaluated holistically. Which method captures end-to-end task success?

answers.A: Compute average BLEU per subtask.
answers.B: Use combined ROUGE-BLEU macro score.
answers.C: Define and measure a multi-step task completion metric in simulation.
answers.D: Measure cumulative perplexity.

explanation: A task completion metric that tracks successful execution of all steps in simulation evaluates orchestration performance end to end.

stem: During offline evaluation of a model for news article generation, automated metrics correlate poorly with editorial ratings. What is the root cause?

answers.A: Test set too small.
answers.B: Metrics (ROUGE/BLEU) emphasize n-gram overlap rather than style and coherence.
answers.C: Training data imbalance.
answers.D: Inference temperature too high.

explanation: ROUGE/BLEU focus on overlap, failing to capture narrative style and coherence valued by editors.

stem: A cross-domain foundation model shows varied performance on different benchmarks. How can you fairly compare its overall performance?

answers.A: Average raw scores across benchmarks.
answers.B: Use the highest score from any benchmark.
answers.C: Evaluate on only one benchmark domain.
answers.D: Normalize scores within each benchmark and compute a weighted aggregate.

explanation: Normalization accounts for differing score ranges across benchmarks, allowing fair aggregated comparison.

stem: You want to automate ongoing evaluation of a deployed LLM summary service. Which pipeline component is essential?

answers.A: Scheduled sampling of production summaries with periodic human or crowdsource review.
answers.B: Real-time BLEU computation on user-provided inputs.
answers.C: Automatic ROUGE computation against live user feedback.
answers.D: Self-BLEU to measure production diversity.

explanation: Scheduled human review of sampled production outputs is necessary for reliable ongoing evaluation, as automated metrics alone are insufficient.

stem: A team assesses hallucinations by measuring overlap between output and source documents. Which automated metric can help?

answers.A: ROUGE-L recall
answers.B: QAEval (question-answering based factuality)
answers.C: Self-BLEU
answers.D: Perplexity

explanation: QAEval uses QA over source documents to check factual consistency, detecting hallucinations automatically.

stem: An LLM generates marketing copy. Which evaluation metric aligns best with expected business KPIs?

answers.A: Click-through rate measured via A/B testing.
answers.B: BLEU against a reference ad copy.
answers.C: ROUGE-F1 against training examples.
answers.D: Perplexity on marketing dataset.

explanation: Click-through rate directly measures the business goal of marketing copy performance, aligning evaluation with KPIs.

stem: When evaluating multilingual summarization, the team must ensure language fairness. Which evaluation strategy ensures no language is underrepresented?

answers.A: Compute aggregate ROUGE across all languages.
answers.B: Use English reference translations only.
answers.C: Maintain per-language test sets with equal sample sizes and report metrics separately.
answers.D: Use a single English-centric metric for all languages.

explanation: Equal per-language test sets and separate reporting detect performance disparities, promoting fairness.

stem: A foundation model exhibits high metric scores on public benchmarks but fails on proprietary data. What evaluation practice could have prevented this?

answers.A: Include proprietary hold-out data in the evaluation benchmark.
answers.B: Increase public benchmark size.
answers.C: Compute Self-BLEU on public benchmarks.
answers.D: Measure perplexity on public data.

explanation: Including proprietary data in evaluation ensures the model is tested on domain-specific content, preventing overreliance on public benchmarks.

stem: Your team measures BLEU-4 for a poetry generator but suspects it penalizes creativity. Which metric or strategy addresses this?

answers.A: Use BLEU-2 instead.
answers.B: Increase reference set size to many poems.
answers.C: Measure perplexity instead of BLEU.
answers.D: Adopt human evaluation of creativity and stylistic quality.

explanation: Human evaluation is required for subjective qualities like creativity, which BLEU cannot capture adequately.

stem: You must evaluate a model’s responsiveness to user instructions in few-shot prompts. Which evaluation method verifies instruction compliance?

answers.A: Measure n-gram recall against instruction text.
answers.B: Human evaluation scoring compliance and correctness of responses.
answers.C: Compute ROUGE-LF against instruction examples.
answers.D: Use perplexity conditioned on instruction tokens.

explanation: Human evaluation directly assesses whether model outputs follow instructions and are correct, which automated metrics cannot reliably do.

stem: A generative model’s performance is evaluated with a single reference per input. What is a key risk and how to mitigate it?

answers.A: Overfitting to reference; reduce training epochs.
answers.B: Underestimating recall; increase beam size.
answers.C: Lower metric reliability due to limited references; use multiple diverse references or human evaluation.
answers.D: Inflated BLEU scores; apply brevity penalty.

explanation: Single references limit metric reliability; adding multiple references or human evaluation improves reliability and fairness.

stem: An LLM-based search assistant’s relevance is evaluated by Precision@5 but gives poor recall. Which complementary metric provides a fuller view?

answers.A: Recall@5
answers.B: ROUGE-L
answers.C: BLEU-1
answers.D: Perplexity

explanation: Recall@5 measures the proportion of relevant documents retrieved, complementing Precision@5 for balanced evaluation.

stem: A team logs user interactions to evaluate a deployed chatbot. Which observed metric best indicates dialogue coherence?

answers.A: Average response length
answers.B: Turn-taking frequency
answers.C: Conversation success rate (user achieves goal without mid-dialog corrections)
answers.D: BLEU score against template responses

explanation: Conversation success rate reflects coherence and goal achievement in dialogue, which automated metrics do not capture.

stem: A financial institution uses an ML model to screen loan applications and discovers that applicants from a specific demographic group are disproportionately rejected. Which responsible AI principle is most directly violated?

answers.A: Fairness – the model is treating demographic groups unequally.
answers.B: Transparency – the model’s decision logic is hidden.
answers.C: Robustness – the model cannot handle noisy data.
answers.D: Safety – the model is causing harm to users.

explanation: Disparate treatment of a demographic group indicates a fairness violation, as responsible AI demands equal outcomes across groups.

stem: An HR recruiter deploys a resume‐screening model that filters out all non‐English resumes, thereby excluding qualified multilingual candidates. Which responsible AI feature is lacking?

answers.A: Inclusivity – the model fails to consider diverse candidate backgrounds.
answers.B: Veracity – the model is providing inaccurate screening.
answers.C: Robustness – the model cannot process different document formats.
answers.D: Safety – the model is exposing sensitive information.

explanation: Excluding non‐English resumes indicates a lack of inclusivity, as a responsible AI system should serve diverse users.

stem: A self‐driving car’s perception model performs well in clear weather but fails in foggy conditions. Which responsible AI characteristic should be improved?

answers.A: Fairness – ensure equal performance across users.
answers.B: Transparency – explain the model’s failure mode.
answers.C: Robustness – maintain performance under varied conditions.
answers.D: Veracity – avoid generating false sensor readings.

explanation: Robustness refers to consistent performance under different real‐world conditions; failure in fog indicates a robustness issue.

stem: A chatbot powered by a foundation model confidently fabricates statistics in its responses. Which responsible AI principle is compromised?

answers.A: Safety – the model must avoid harmful outputs.
answers.B: Fairness – the model must treat user queries equally.
answers.C: Robustness – the model must handle adversarial prompts.
answers.D: Veracity – the model’s outputs must be truthful and accurate.

explanation: Veracity is about truthfulness and accuracy; hallucinated statistics violate veracity.

stem: A medical advice AI system suggests a treatment that poses health risks to users. Which responsible AI attribute has been neglected?

answers.A: Fairness – equal recommendation quality.
answers.B: Safety – avoiding harm to end users.
answers.C: Inclusivity – serving diverse patient groups.
answers.D: Veracity – providing only factual information.

explanation: Safety focuses on preventing harm; recommending risky treatments shows a safety lapse.

stem: Your team needs to enforce content policies (e.g., block hate speech) and prevent hallucinations in responses from a foundation model. Which AWS feature should you use?

answers.A: AWS WAF – protects web applications only.
answers.B: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor – monitors metrics post‐deployment.
answers.C: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails – enforces input/output policies in real time.
answers.D: Amazon Macie – discovers and protects sensitive data in S3.

explanation: Bedrock Guardrails allows you to define input/output policies to block disallowed content and reduce hallucinations in generative AI.

stem: To trigger an alert whenever a Bedrock Guardrails policy is violated, which AWS service should you integrate?

answers.A: Amazon CloudWatch Events – can detect and alert on Guardrails events.
answers.B: AWS Config – tracks configuration changes, not real‐time guardrail events.
answers.C: AWS CodePipeline – orchestrates CI/CD, not monitoring.
answers.D: Amazon GuardDuty – detects threats, not policy violations in LLM responses.

explanation: CloudWatch Events can be configured to catch Bedrock Guardrails violations and send alerts or trigger workflows.

stem: You want to validate user input against allowed schemas before sending it to a foundation model and reject malformed requests. Which component of Bedrock Guardrails addresses this?

answers.A: Output guard – sanitizes model responses.
answers.B: Input guard – enforces schema/patterns before invocation.
answers.C: Model selector – chooses which model to use.
answers.D: Fallback mechanism – handles service outages.

explanation: Input guards are designed to validate and reject unauthorized or malformed inputs before invoking the model.

stem: You need to automatically mask profanity in generative responses without modifying your application code. Which Bedrock Guardrails feature do you configure?

answers.A: Input guard – stops profanity at input stage.
answers.B: IAM policy – controls access, not content.
answers.C: Model selector – picks a sanitized model.
answers.D: Output guard – transforms or filters responses to remove profanity.

explanation: Output guards can apply transformations or filters to model-generated text, such as masking profanity.

stem: To audit all calls made to your Bedrock foundation models and any guardrail violations for compliance, which AWS service provides an immutable record?

answers.A: Amazon CloudWatch Logs – useful but not immutable.
answers.B: AWS Config – captures resource configs, not API calls.
answers.C: AWS CloudTrail – records API calls and guardrail events immutably.
answers.D: Amazon X-Ray – traces requests but not policy violations.

explanation: CloudTrail records all API calls, including Bedrock invocations and guardrail events, for auditing.

stem: A company must choose between a large foundation model and a parameter‐efficient adapter layer approach to minimize carbon emissions. Which choice best meets sustainability goals?

answers.A: Use the largest available model for higher accuracy.
answers.B: Implement parameter-efficient fine-tuning with a smaller base model.
answers.C: Train the model longer to improve performance.
answers.D: Host models in on-premises data centers to control cooling.

explanation: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of a smaller base model substantially reduces compute and hence carbon footprint compared to large full-model training.

stem: To reduce the energy consumption of inference in production, which technique should you apply?

answers.A: Quantize the model to lower-precision (e.g., INT8) operations.
answers.B: Execute inference in real time only.
answers.C: Increase batch size to 1 for latency improvement.
answers.D: Fine-tune the model with more data.

explanation: Quantization reduces compute and memory requirements, lowering energy consumption during inference.

stem: A team is deciding between AWS Graviton-based instances and GPU instances for large-scale model training. Which choice improves energy efficiency?

answers.A: Use Graviton-based instances for CPU-optimized, energy-efficient training.
answers.B: Choose the highest-end GPU for maximum throughput.
answers.C: Run training on on-premises hardware to reduce cloud usage.
answers.D: Use burstable instances to save cost only.

explanation: Arm-based Graviton processors deliver better performance per watt for many ML workloads, reducing energy usage.

stem: Scheduling batch inference jobs during off-peak hours to take advantage of a lower PUE (power usage effectiveness) is an example of which sustainability practice?

answers.A: Model quantization – reduces model size.
answers.B: Workload scheduling – aligns compute with grid efficiency.
answers.C: Using renewable energy certificates – purchases carbon offsets.
answers.D: Data pruning – reduces dataset size.

explanation: Scheduling workloads when the data center’s PUE is lower minimizes overall energy overhead, a key sustainability tactic.

stem: A business wants to minimize its AI carbon footprint by selecting an AWS region. Which factor should guide their choice?

answers.A: Lowest network latency for user traffic only.
answers.B: Region with all available instance types.
answers.C: Region with deepest discount pricing.
answers.D: Region with higher renewable energy usage on the local grid.

explanation: Regions powered by cleaner energy sources reduce the carbon footprint of compute workloads.

stem: An ML team fine‐tunes a foundation model using unlicensed internet text, ignoring copyright constraints. Which legal risk are they exposed to?

answers.A: Intellectual property infringement – unauthorized use of copyrighted content.
answers.B: Model drift – performance degradation over time.
answers.C: Data poisoning – malicious training inputs.
answers.D: Overfitting – too specific to training data.

explanation: Using copyrighted text without permission risks IP infringement and potential legal action.

stem: A chatbot trained on scraped forum posts inadvertently reveals personal user data. Which legal/compliance risk does this represent?

answers.A: Hallucinations – fabricating facts.
answers.B: IP infringement – misusing copyrighted content.
answers.C: Privacy violation – exposing personal identifiable information.
answers.D: Overfitting – echoing training examples.

explanation: Revealing PII from training data breaches privacy regulations and violates data protection laws.

stem: A lender’s credit-scoring model shows statistically significant bias against a protected group, undermining consumer trust and inviting regulatory scrutiny. Which risk category best describes this issue?

answers.A: Safety risk – potential physical harm.
answers.B: Customer trust loss – reputational and compliance risk.
answers.C: Sustainability risk – environmental impact.
answers.D: Latency risk – slow response times.

explanation: Biased outcomes erode customer trust and invite legal/regulatory consequences, a customer trust risk.

stem: An insurance chatbot confidently gives incorrect policy advice that leads to financial harm. Which specific risk from responsible AI does this example illustrate?

answers.A: Data poisoning – corrupted training data.
answers.B: Class imbalance – skewed training labels.
answers.C: Drift – changing data distributions.
answers.D: Hallucinations – inaccurate outputs presented as fact.

explanation: Confidently incorrect advice from a generative model is a hallucination, risking legal liabilities.

stem: A healthcare application’s language model suggests off-label drug uses without evidence, exposing the company to legal liability. Which risk type is this?

answers.A: Bias risk – unfair treatment across populations.
answers.B: Sustainability risk – high energy usage.
answers.C: End‐user risk – harm from incorrect guidance.
answers.D: Veracity risk – lack of model explainability.

explanation: Incorrect medical guidance poses direct harm to end users, an end‐user risk under responsible AI.

stem: A computer vision dataset for facial recognition lacks images of darker skin tones, resulting in higher error rates for certain groups. Which dataset characteristic is missing?

answers.A: Curation – removing low-quality images.
answers.B: Diversity – including varied skin tones.
answers.C: Balanced classes – equal count for each class.
answers.D: Inclusivity – serving all age groups.

explanation: Lack of varied skin tones indicates poor diversity, leading to biased performance.

stem: Your image classification dataset contains duplicates, mislabeled entries, and missing annotations. Which dataset characteristic issue does this describe?

answers.A: Inclusivity – unsuitable for demographic fairness.
answers.B: Diversity – missing variation of classes.
answers.C: Curation – poor data quality and organization.
answers.D: Balance – unequal class representation.

explanation: Duplication and mislabels reflect poor data curation practices, harming model quality.

stem: A binary classification dataset has 95% of examples in one class and 5% in the other. What dataset property should you address?

answers.A: Inclusivity – demographic representation.
answers.B: Curation – data cleanliness.
answers.C: Diversity – feature variation.
answers.D: Class imbalance – skewed target distribution.

explanation: A 95/5 split indicates severe class imbalance, which can bias model predictions toward the majority class.

stem: A global voice assistant is trained exclusively on North American English accents. Which dataset characteristic is lacking?

answers.A: Inclusivity – support for diverse accents and dialects.
answers.B: Balance – equal number of male/female voices.
answers.C: Curation – removal of background noise.
answers.D: Veracity – truthful responses.

explanation: Excluding non–North American accents shows lack of inclusivity, leading to poor user experience globally.

stem: Before training, you resample your dataset so each class reflects real‐world population proportions. Which property does this ensure?

answers.A: Diversity – varied feature space coverage.
answers.B: Inclusivity – demographic fairness.
answers.C: Balance – representative class distribution.
answers.D: Sustainability – efficient data usage.

explanation: Resampling to real‐world proportions addresses class balance, ensuring representative distribution.

stem: Your model achieves 99% accuracy on training data but only 60% on validation data. Which bias/variance issue does this indicate?

answers.A: High bias – underfitting the data.
answers.B: High variance – overfitting to the training set.
answers.C: Data drift – changing data distribution over time.
answers.D: Concept drift – evolving relationship between features and labels.

explanation: A large gap between train and validation accuracy indicates high variance (overfitting).

stem: To detect demographic bias in model predictions post‐deployment, which AWS service should you use?

answers.A: Amazon SageMaker Clarify – analyzes bias and feature attributions.
answers.B: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor – monitors data drift only.
answers.C: Amazon A2I – human-review workflow for low-confidence cases.
answers.D: AWS Config – monitors resource configurations.

explanation: SageMaker Clarify provides bias detection and feature importance analysis across defined groups.

stem: You want to continuously track fairness metrics (e.g., false-positive rates across groups) in production. Which AWS tool is best?

answers.A: SageMaker Clarify – batch analysis only.
answers.B: SageMaker Model Monitor – continuous real‐time monitoring of metrics.
answers.C: Amazon A2I – human review only.
answers.D: AWS CloudTrail – API audit logs, not metrics.

explanation: Model Monitor can track custom metrics, including fairness, in real time.

stem: To route low-confidence or high-risk predictions for human review, which AWS service should you integrate?

answers.A: SageMaker Clarify – bias detection but no routing.
answers.B: SageMaker Model Monitor – metrics tracking only.
answers.C: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) – orchestrates human reviews.
answers.D: Amazon Rekognition – only for image analysis.

explanation: Amazon A2I allows you to define human-review workflows for model outputs based on confidence or policy criteria.

stem: After running SageMaker Clarify, you observe that a feature’s importance differs significantly across demographic groups. Which concept does this reveal?

answers.A: Data drift – change in feature distributions over time.
answers.B: Overfitting – model too complex.
answers.C: Variance – model instability across datasets.
answers.D: Disparate impact – unequal model behavior across groups.

explanation: Differing feature importance across groups indicates disparate impact, a form of bias requiring mitigation.

stem: A healthcare startup must deploy a model to predict patient readmission risk. Regulators require clear rationale for each prediction. Which model choice best balances accuracy and explainability?

answers.A: A deep ensemble of neural networks with gradient-based saliency maps
answers.B: A random forest with thousands of trees and SHAP explanations
answers.C: A shallow decision tree pruned for clarity with feature importance annotations
answers.D: A support vector machine with RBF kernel and LIME explanations

explanation: A pruned decision tree yields inherently transparent rules, satisfying regulators with minimal complexity, whereas complex ensembles or SVMs remain opaque despite post hoc methods.

stem: An e-commerce company uses SageMaker Model Cards for several models. A risk audit requires assessment of data lineage and bias evaluation. Which section of the Model Card provides this information?

answers.A: Quantitative analysis section detailing performance metrics
answers.B: Training data section documenting sources, preprocessing, and bias checks
answers.C: Usage recommendations section explaining inference patterns
answers.D: Hyperparameter section listing tuning configurations

explanation: The training data section of a Model Card records data provenance and any bias analyses, which is needed for risk and lineage audits.

stem: A finance firm must choose a pre-trained NLP model under an open-source license that allows modification and internal transparency. Which license attribute ensures the firm can inspect and modify the model code?

answers.A: Proprietary commercial license with source code escrow
answers.B: Non-commercial Creative Commons license
answers.C: End-user license agreement without vendor source access
answers.D: OSI-approved permissive license (e.g., Apache 2.0)

explanation: An OSI-approved permissive license like Apache 2.0 grants rights to view, modify, and redistribute source code, meeting transparency needs.

stem: A user interface team requires explanations in layman’s terms for model predictions. Which human-centered design principle should guide the explanation content?

answers.A: Contextualizing model output in domain-specific language familiar to end users
answers.B: Providing raw feature importance scores without interpretation
answers.C: Including advanced mathematical derivations for transparency
answers.D: Displaying performance metrics like precision and recall

explanation: Contextualizing predictions using common domain terminology aligns explanations with users’ mental models, improving comprehension.

stem: A model’s Model Card indicates high accuracy but warns of demographic bias in certain groups. Which step is most appropriate before deployment?

answers.A: Ignore the warning because accuracy is sufficient
answers.B: Retrain or tune preprocessing to balance representation before deploying
answers.C: Deploy and monitor only high-confidence predictions
answers.D: Apply ensemble averaging to mask bias

explanation: Addressing bias through data balancing or preprocessing is required to mitigate demographic disparities rather than ignoring or masking them.

stem: A bank must explain credit decisions to customers. Which model explanation technique provides individual-level counterfactual examples?

answers.A: Partial dependence plots
answers.B: Global SHAP summary plots
answers.C: LIME local feature attribution
answers.D: Counterfactual explanation generation

explanation: Counterfactual explanations show how input changes alter decisions at the individual level, supporting regulatory right-to-explanation.

stem: An operations team debates using a black-box model with high throughput vs. an interpretable white-box model with lower throughput. What trade-off should they document?

answers.A: Interpretability vs. performance in latency-critical applications
answers.B: Accuracy vs. model complexity when performance metrics are equal
answers.C: Cost vs. regulatory compliance if throughput varies
answers.D: Scalability vs. maintenance overhead

explanation: They need to weigh interpretability against latency/performance, especially if auditability is required in real time.

stem: Which AWS tool can be used to generate global and local feature attributions to improve model transparency?

answers.A: SageMaker Model Monitor
answers.B: SageMaker Clarify
answers.C: SageMaker Autopilot
answers.D: Amazon A2I

explanation: SageMaker Clarify provides built-in methods for global and local feature attribution, aiding transparency analyses.

stem: A text‐classification model gives reasons like “word occurrence frequency” to end users. Which explanation method does this represent?

answers.A: Intrinsic explanations using model-internal weights
answers.B: Post hoc example‐based explanations
answers.C: Surrogate decision tree explanations
answers.D: Counterfactual explanation

explanation: Describing predictions based on internal token weight frequencies is an intrinsic explanation, reflecting model internals.

stem: A team uses SHAP values but end users find the output confusing. How can they improve human-centered explainability?

answers.A: Switch to raw weight visualizations
answers.B: Provide detailed mathematical formulas alongside plots
answers.C: Translate SHAP values into natural language summaries
answers.D: Expose full data distributions for each feature

explanation: Summarizing SHAP insights in natural language makes explanations accessible, aligning with human-centered design.

stem: A self-driving car project needs transparent vision models. Which architecture offers the best explainability without drastic performance loss?

answers.A: Deep convolutional network without modifications
answers.B: Shallow convolutional network combined with attention maps
answers.C: Ensemble of deep generative adversarial networks
answers.D: Transformer-based vision model with no interpretability features

explanation: Adding attention maps to a shallow CNN yields insight into areas driving predictions while maintaining acceptable performance.

stem: A PwC auditor requests a summary of model limitations before deployment. Which part of the Model Card should be updated?

answers.A: Quantitative results
answers.B: Training details
answers.C: Usage recommendations
answers.D: Limitations and caveats section

explanation: The limitations and caveats section explicitly documents known weaknesses for audit transparency.

stem: Your company plans to fine-tune a foundation model but needs to maintain explainability. What approach minimizes opacity?

answers.A: Fine-tune all layers with large datasets
answers.B: Use prompt tuning rather than full model fine-tuning
answers.C: Increase model depth post fine-tuning
answers.D: Apply knowledge distillation without retaining student model

explanation: Prompt tuning customizes model behavior without altering internal weights, preserving transparency of the base model.

stem: A credit model must log all decisions and rationales. Which AWS service can automate capturing predictions and explanation metadata?

answers.A: SageMaker Model Monitor with Clarify integration
answers.B: SageMaker Ground Truth
answers.C: Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights
answers.D: AWS Config

explanation: Model Monitor with Clarify captures prediction inputs, outputs, and feature attributions for logging and review.

stem: To comply with GDPR’s right-to-explanation, which design practice is essential?

answers.A: Encrypt all decision logs
answers.B: Use only cloud-managed proprietary models
answers.C: Provide counterfactual or feature‐based explanations
answers.D: Store model artifacts indefinitely

explanation: GDPR requires providing explanations of automated decisions, which is met by counterfactual or feature‐based explanations.

stem: A chat assistant uses a black-box large language model. Users report inconsistent reasoning. Which strategy improves transparency?

answers.A: Increase model temperature
answers.B: Add more user feedback loops
answers.C: Limit response length
answers.D: Use a retrieval augmented generation pipeline with provenance citations

explanation: RAG with provenance citations shows source documents, making model outputs more transparent and verifiable.

stem: Which explanation method is model-agnostic and builds a local surrogate to explain individual predictions?

answers.A: SHAP TreeExplainer
answers.B: LIME
answers.C: Integrated Gradients
answers.D: Attention heatmaps

explanation: LIME fits a simple interpretable model locally around each prediction, regardless of the underlying model type.

stem: Your product team insists on maximal model performance and opposes transparency features that slow inference. How do you address this?

answers.A: Propose a hybrid system: high‐performance model behind the scenes with an interpretable surrogate for user explanations
answers.B: Disable logging to speed up inference
answers.C: Switch entirely to an interpretable model and accept accuracy loss
answers.D: Use asynchronous explanation requests after inference

explanation: A surrogate for explanations preserves throughput while offering users transparent reasoning separate from core inference.

stem: Which is a risk of choosing a highly transparent model in a security-sensitive application?

answers.A: Regulatory non-compliance
answers.B: Excessive latency
answers.C: Easier maintenance
answers.D: Model inversion attacks exposing training data

explanation: Transparent models with exposed structures may reveal sensitive training data patterns, risking inversion attacks.

stem: During user testing, explanations based only on model confidence scores are unhelpful. Which alternative best aids user understanding?

answers.A: Provide raw probability distributions
answers.B: Show training dataset size
answers.C: Offer top contributing features per prediction
answers.D: List all hyperparameters

explanation: Highlighting key features driving each decision gives users actionable insights beyond mere confidence levels.

stem: A marketing team wants to know if a text classification model considers banned words. Which transparency tool reveals word‐level influences?

answers.A: SageMaker Model Monitor
answers.B: SageMaker Clarify word‐attribution feature
answers.C: Model Card quantitative metrics
answers.D: Feature Store audit logs

explanation: SageMaker Clarify’s word-attribution identifies text tokens’ importance in predictions, revealing banned word influence.

stem: Your team uses a black-box ensemble. A stakeholder demands global explanations. Which technique provides global surrogate model insights?

answers.A: Train a decision tree surrogate on the ensemble’s inputs and outputs
answers.B: Generate local LIME explanations and average them
answers.C: Use integrated gradients
answers.D: Deploy attention mechanisms

explanation: A global surrogate decision tree approximates the ensemble’s decision surface, offering interpretable rules.

stem: A supply chain model’s Model Card lacks information on feature engineering. Why is this a transparency concern?

answers.A: Performance metrics might be inflated
answers.B: Cost estimates could be inaccurate
answers.C: Stakeholders cannot trace how raw inputs become features, hindering interpretability
answers.D: Model deployment will fail

explanation: Without feature engineering details, users can’t understand how inputs map to features, reducing model explainability.

stem: Which step best mitigates explanation risks when using third-party foundation models?

answers.A: Trust vendor documentation blindly
answers.B: Skip bias assessments to save time
answers.C: Only use models with closed-source weights
answers.D: Perform independent evaluations and review open-source Model Cards

explanation: Independent tests and reviewing Model Cards ensures third-party models meet transparency and bias requirements.

stem: A logistics company needs to explain anomaly detection alerts in real time. Which design is most suitable?

answers.A: Use an interpretable isolation forest with path length visualizations
answers.B: Deploy a deep autoencoder and log latent activations
answers.C: Train a GAN and inspect discriminator features
answers.D: Apply black-box clustering with post hoc clustering explanations

explanation: An interpretable isolation forest allows visualization of how anomalies are isolated, offering real‐time clarity.

stem: Which documentation practice supports transparency throughout the model lifecycle?

answers.A: Only logging final model metrics
answers.B: Maintaining versioned Model Cards with data and design decisions
answers.C: Archiving raw code without metadata
answers.D: Keeping hyperparameter settings private

explanation: Versioned Model Cards record evolving data sources, design rationale, and performance, ensuring transparency over time.

stem: Which explanation approach is least prone to misleading interpretations for correlated features?

answers.A: Individual conditional expectation plots
answers.B: Permutation feature importance
answers.C: SHAP dependence plots with interaction effects
answers.D: Linear model coefficients

explanation: SHAP dependence plots with interaction terms separate correlated feature effects, reducing misleading attributions.

stem: A customer disputes a decision and wants a human review. Which AWS service facilitates human-in-the-loop explainability?

answers.A: SageMaker Model Monitor
answers.B: AWS Config
answers.C: SageMaker Clarify
answers.D: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I)

explanation: Amazon A2I routes flagged predictions to human reviewers, providing an interface for explanation and correction.

stem: A company is planning to migrate its overburdened on-premises infrastructure to the AWS Cloud. They want to ensure minimal downtime, optimized costs, and high availability across multiple regions. Which AWS Cloud benefits should they prioritize to achieve these goals, and what strategies should they implement to maximize these benefits? Select the most comprehensive set of benefits and strategies.

answers.A: Speed of deployment, Local data storage, manual scaling; Use single region deployment, and static provisioning.
answers.B: Cost savings from reduced hardware investments, Extended data lifecycle management, manual failover; Rely on on-premises backups and manual scaling.
answers.C: Global reach and rapid deployment, High availability, Elasticity, Cost-efficiency; Use multi-region deployment, Auto Scaling, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC).
answers.D: Enhanced security, Fixed capacity planning, On-demand resource allocation; Implement rigid capacity planning and local data centers.

explanation: The most effective strategies involve leveraging AWS Cloud's global infrastructure for rapid and widespread deployment, implementing auto scaling for elasticity, and using IaC to automate deployments and updates. These strategies maximize the benefits of speed, cost efficiency, high availability, and global accessibility, aligning with the company's migration and business continuity goals.

stem: A startup is developing a web application with unpredictable traffic patterns. They want to deploy their application on AWS using a method that supports rapid provisioning, flexibility, and automation, while minimizing manual effort. Which deployment and operation method should they choose, and what are the key considerations to ensure scalable and resilient deployment?

answers.A: Manual deployment via AWS Management Console; manually modify resources as needed for scaling.
answers.B: Using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) with CloudFormation; deploy stacks once and update manually.
answers.C: Deploying directly via AWS CLI commands; script deployments without version control.
answers.D: Utilizing Infrastructure as Code (IaC) with tools like AWS CloudFormation or Terraform; automate deployment, updates, and scaling with version-controlled templates and pipelines.

explanation: IaC tools like CloudFormation or Terraform enable automation, repeatability, and version control, which are ideal for a startup with variable traffic. This approach supports rapid, automated provisioning and scaling, reduces manual errors, and enhances resilience and maintainability.

stem: A media company needs to run a large-scale transcoding application that requires high scalability, flexible resource management, and cost optimization. They also want to minimize operational overhead. Which AWS compute service best fits these requirements, and what are the key features that support their workload?

answers.A: AWS Lambda; serverless execution, automatic scaling, pay-per-use model.
answers.B: Amazon EC2; dedicated server management, manual scaling, custom AMIs.
answers.C: Amazon ECS; container orchestration, cluster management, integration with EC2 or Fargate.
answers.D: AWS Batch; batch job scheduling, managed compute environment, dynamic resource provisioning.

explanation: AWS Lambda offers serverless computing, automatically scales with workload, and charges based on actual runtime, making it highly suitable for batch transcoding tasks with unpredictable load patterns. It minimizes operational overhead, providing a highly scalable and cost-effective solution.

stem:
A company plans to migrate its legacy application to AWS and aims to design a solution that maximizes fault tolerance, scalability, and operational excellence. Considering the AWS Well-Architected Framework pillars, which combination of design principles best aligns with these goals? 

A) Choose a single Availability Zone for cost savings, implement manual failover procedures, and tightly couple services to reduce latency.
B) Design for high availability across multiple Availability Zones, automate deployment and recovery processes, and decouple services for resilience.
C) Focus on minimizing operational overhead by using a monolithic architecture, leverage manual scaling, and maintain tight integrations between components.
D) Optimize for performance by allocating dedicated resources, avoid automation to reduce complexity, and keep services tightly integrated for speed.

answers.A: Choose a single Availability Zone for cost savings, implement manual failover procedures, and tightly couple services to reduce latency.
answers.B: Design for high availability across multiple Availability Zones, automate deployment and recovery processes, and decouple services for resilience.
answers.C: Focus on minimizing operational overhead by using a monolithic architecture, leverage manual scaling, and maintain tight integrations between components.
answers.D: Optimize for performance by allocating dedicated resources, avoid automation to reduce complexity, and keep services tightly integrated for speed.

explanation: Option B aligns with the AWS Well-Architected Framework pillars by emphasizing high availability, automation, and decoupling of services, which collectively enhance fault tolerance, scalability, and operational excellence. Choices A, C, and D either compromise resilience, increase operational overhead, or reduce flexibility, making them less suitable for a robust, scalable cloud architecture.

stem:
In designing a new cloud-native application, an architect is considering the use of managed services and microservices architecture to ensure resilience and agility. Which key design principles should the architect prioritize according to the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

A) Monolith deployment, manual scaling, and tight service coupling.
B) Serverless computing, decoupled components, and automated deployment pipelines.
C) Fixed infrastructure, manual patching, and tightly integrated services.
D) Large, monolithic databases, vertical scaling, and low automation levels.

answers.A: Monolith deployment, manual scaling, and tight service coupling.
answers.B: Serverless computing, decoupled components, and automated deployment pipelines.
answers.C: Fixed infrastructure, manual patching, and tightly integrated services.
answers.D: Large, monolithic databases, vertical scaling, and low automation levels.

explanation: Option B advocates for serverless architectures, decoupled services, and automation, which are core principles of a modern, resilient, and scalable system as per AWS best practices. The other options reflect traditional or outdated practices that reduce agility and fault tolerance.

stem:
An organization is transitioning to a multi-region deployment model to improve disaster recovery and latency. They want to ensure their architecture adheres to AWS's high availability principles. Which approach best exemplifies this goal?

A) Deploy all resources in a single region using the same Availability Zone.
B) Use multiple regions with independent, replicated resources and automate failover mechanisms.
C) Centralize resources in one Region to simplify management, and manually replicate data to disaster recovery sites.
D) Deploy resources in different regions but avoid data replication to reduce complexity, relying on backups for disaster recovery.

answers.A: Deploy all resources in a single region using the same Availability Zone.
answers.B: Use multiple regions with independent, replicated resources and automate failover mechanisms.
answers.C: Centralize resources in one Region to simplify management, and manually replicate data to disaster recovery sites.
answers.D: Deploy resources in different regions but avoid data replication to reduce complexity, relying on backups for disaster recovery.

explanation: Option B employs multi-region deployment with replication and automated failover, which aligns with high availability and disaster resilience principles in AWS architecture. The other options lack sufficient redundancy or automation to ensure robust high availability.

stem: A global retail startup needs to launch identical test, staging, and production environments in three AWS Regions with minimal manual effort and ensure consistency across regions. Which AWS capability best addresses this requirement?

answers.A: Manually replicate resources in each Region using the AWS Management Console
answers.B: Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets with a common template across the three Regions
answers.C: Deploy AWS Elastic Beanstalk applications separately in each Region
answers.D: Use Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to copy EC2 instances to each Region

explanation: CloudFormation StackSets automates deployment of identical stacks across multiple Regions, ensuring consistency and minimal manual effort.

stem: A media streaming service must deliver live video to viewers worldwide with minimal latency. Which combination of AWS global infrastructure features and services provides both global reach and high availability?

answers.A: Deploy EC2 instances in one Region and use an Application Load Balancer
answers.B: Use AWS Wavelength in all major cities with CloudFront
answers.C: Use Amazon CloudFront with edge locations and deploy origin servers in multiple AWS Regions
answers.D: Deploy AWS Outposts in each data center and use Route 53 geolocation routing

explanation: CloudFront edge locations cache content close to viewers, and origin servers in multiple Regions ensure availability if one Region fails.

stem: A financial analytics firm expects unpredictable spikes in compute usage during market events. They want to pay only for what they use and to scale automatically without manual intervention. Which AWS benefit and service combination fulfills these requirements?

answers.A: Elasticity using Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
answers.B: High availability using Multi-AZ RDS
answers.C: Agility using AWS CloudFormation
answers.D: Global reach using Route 53 latency-based routing

explanation: Elasticity with EC2 Auto Scaling automatically adds or removes instances to match usage, ensuring they pay only for the capacity they consume.

stem: During a global product launch, a company needs DNS-based traffic routing that directs users to the lowest-latency Region and fails over if that Region becomes unavailable. Which AWS service and routing policy accomplish this with minimal configuration?

answers.A: AWS Global Accelerator with geoproximity routing
answers.B: Amazon CloudFront with origin failover
answers.C: AWS WAF with regional ACLs
answers.D: Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing with active-active endpoints in multiple Regions

explanation: Route 53 latency-based routing directs users to the Region with the lowest latency and supports health checks for failover.

stem: A robotics research team must spin up dozens of GPU-backed EC2 instances in under 10 minutes for machine learning training, then tear them down when finished. Which AWS advantage and feature align best with this need?

answers.A: High availability via Multi-AZ deployments
answers.B: Speed of deployment via Amazon EC2 and Elastic GPU
answers.C: Global reach via AWS Outposts
answers.D: Economies of scale via Reserved Instances

explanation: EC2’s rapid provisioning (minutes) and on-demand Elastic GPUs demonstrate agility and speed of deployment, enabling quick spin-up and tear-down.

stem: An enterprise with offices in Europe, Asia, and North America wants a single DNS record that automatically routes traffic based on user location for compliance and performance. Which AWS global infrastructure feature supports this?

answers.A: Amazon CloudFront with geo restriction
answers.B: Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing
answers.C: AWS Global Accelerator with endpoint groups
answers.D: AWS Direct Connect global network

explanation: Route 53 geolocation routing sends user requests to endpoints based on their geographic location for both compliance and reduced latency.

stem: A biotech startup must maintain a highly available data processing pipeline across two Regions. They require automatic failover if one Region loses connectivity. Which architecture best meets these requirements?

answers.A: Deploy all resources in one Region and back up data to another Region
answers.B: Use Amazon S3 cross‐Region replication and process data in a single Region
answers.C: Deploy active-active compute and database clusters in two Regions with Route 53 health checks for failover
answers.D: Use AWS Backup to replicate snapshots across Regions and manually promote

explanation: Active-active deployment across two Regions with Route 53 health checks ensures continuous availability and automatic failover.

stem: A software team needs to prototype a new application architecture in hours, iterate rapidly, and discard it without incurring ongoing cost. Which AWS characteristic and service combination is most aligned?

answers.A: Global reach using AWS Direct Connect
answers.B: High availability using RDS Multi-AZ
answers.C: Elasticity using EC2 Reserved Instances
answers.D: Agility using AWS CloudFormation and on-demand pricing

explanation: Agility with CloudFormation allows rapid prototyping and cleanup, and on-demand pricing prevents long-term costs for disposable environments.

stem: A gaming company wants to minimize latency for voice chat between players in South America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. Which AWS infrastructure feature combination should they adopt?

answers.A: Amazon CloudFront global edge network and AWS Global Accelerator
answers.B: Multi-Region Outposts deployments
answers.C: AWS Storage Gateway in each continent
answers.D: Amazon RDS Multi-AZ with cross-Region read replicas

explanation: CloudFront edge network reduces latency for user traffic, and Global Accelerator optimizes path selection across the AWS global network for real-time voice chat.

stem: A retail analytics platform must scale out automatically to handle unpredictable holiday traffic surges within seconds. Which two AWS benefits are primarily being utilized?

answers.A: Elasticity and agility
answers.B: High availability and economies of scale
answers.C: Global reach and cost savings
answers.D: Security and compliance

explanation: Automatic scaling in response to demand demonstrates elasticity, and rapid deployment/configuration changes demonstrate agility.

stem: A multinational corporation needs to ensure its application is served from multiple physical locations near users to meet data residency and performance requirements. Which AWS feature best satisfies both needs?

answers.A: Deploy Amazon WorkSpaces in each country
answers.B: Use multiple AWS Regions with Amazon Route 53 geoproximity routing
answers.C: Leverage AWS Outposts with per-country deployments
answers.D: Use a single Region with AWS CloudFront geofencing

explanation: Multiple Regions meet data residency, and Route 53 geoproximity routing directs traffic to the nearest regional endpoint for performance.

stem: A data analytics startup wants to process real-time IoT data streams in multiple geographic areas without managing servers. Which AWS service and benefit combination should they choose?

answers.A: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling for IoT applications
answers.B: AWS IoT Greengrass on on-premises gateways
answers.C: AWS Lambda@Edge with CloudFront for serverless global processing
answers.D: AWS Snowball Edge devices

explanation: Lambda@Edge allows serverless code execution at CloudFront edge locations, enabling real-time processing close to data sources without server provisioning.

stem: An organization subject to strict regulatory requirements must keep data within specific countries yet provide a single application interface. Which AWS global infrastructure feature supports compliance and agility?

answers.A: Amazon CloudFront with geo restriction
answers.B: AWS Snowball for data transfer
answers.C: AWS Direct Connect with public VIF
answers.D: Deploy Regions in required countries and use Route 53 geolocation routing with CloudFormation Templates for deployment automation

explanation: Deploying in specific Regions meets data residency, geolocation routing enforces compliance at DNS level, and templates automate deployment (agility).

stem: An online gaming company wants to ensure that all user actions and administrative changes are recorded and centrally viewable to support incident investigations and forensics. Which Well-Architected design principle best addresses this need?

answers.A: Enable traceability
answers.B: Apply security at all layers
answers.C: Perform operations as code
answers.D: Experiment more often

explanation: The security pillar’s Enable traceability principle ensures that all actions and changes are logged and monitored centrally for audit and forensic purposes. The other options address different concerns.

stem: A fintech startup needs to deploy daily updates with minimal risk and quick rollback in production. Which Well-Architected principle should they follow to meet this requirement?

answers.A: Stop spending money on undifferentiated heavy lifting
answers.B: Make frequent, small, reversible changes
answers.C: Test recovery procedures
answers.D: Democratize advanced technologies

explanation: Making small, reversible changes reduces blast radius and accelerates rollback, an operational excellence principle. The other choices do not directly address deployment risk.

stem: A social media platform anticipates unpredictable viral events and wants to automatically distribute traffic across multiple compute resources to maintain service availability. Which Well-Architected principle supports this?

answers.A: Scale horizontally to increase aggregate system availability
answers.B: Use serverless architectures
answers.C: Adopt a consumption model
answers.D: Learn from all operational failures

explanation: Scaling horizontally (adding more instances) is a reliability principle that increases aggregate availability. The other options address different aspects of the framework.

stem: An online retailer aims to avoid manual capacity forecasting and over-provisioning by allowing AWS services to provision resources automatically based on demand. Which principle are they applying?

answers.A: Stop guessing capacity
answers.B: Go global in minutes
answers.C: Use managed and application-level services to reduce cost of ownership
answers.D: Keep people away from data

explanation: Stop guessing capacity is a reliability principle that removes the need for manual forecast and over-provisioning. The other choices relate to different pillars.

stem: A photo-sharing application wants to minimize upfront investments and pay only for storage and compute when they actually use them. Which design principle should guide their architecture?

answers.A: Adopt a consumption model
answers.B: Automatically recover from failure
answers.C: Prepare for security events
answers.D: Use automated security best practices

explanation: Adopt a consumption model is a cost optimization principle encouraging pay-per-use. The other options address reliability or security concerns.

stem: A company building real-time ML inference workloads systematically tests different EC2 instance types, measuring CPU, GPU, and network utilization to optimize cost and throughput. Which Well-Architected principle are they applying?

answers.A: Consider mechanical sympathy
answers.B: Stop guessing capacity
answers.C: Use serverless architectures
answers.D: Annotate documentation

explanation: Consider mechanical sympathy is a performance efficiency principle that encourages understanding hardware characteristics to optimize performance. The others address different pillars.

stem: A biotech firm processes sporadic genomic data analysis using AWS Lambda functions and S3 to avoid provisioning servers for intermittent workloads. Which Well-Architected principle is illustrated?

answers.A: Use serverless architectures
answers.B: Scale horizontally to increase aggregate system availability
answers.C: Adopt a consumption model
answers.D: Perform operations as code

explanation: Use serverless architectures is a performance efficiency principle that allows workloads to run without managing servers. The other options relate to reliability, cost, and operations.

stem: A security team wants to ensure that only approved API calls invoke critical functions. They implement least-privilege IAM policies and centralized identity management. Which security design principle does this represent?

answers.A: Implement a strong identity foundation
answers.B: Keep people away from data
answers.C: Experiment more often
answers.D: Democratize advanced technologies

explanation: Implement a strong identity foundation is a security principle that emphasizes least-privilege access and centralized identity. The other options are unrelated to access control.

stem: An operations team uses AWS CloudFormation and version control for all infrastructure changes, enabling peer review and rollback. Which operational excellence principle is demonstrated?

answers.A: Perform operations as code
answers.B: Manage change in automation
answers.C: Use serverless architectures
answers.D: Analyze and attribute expenditure

explanation: Perform operations as code is an operational excellence principle promoting IaC and version control. The others address reliability, performance, or cost.

stem: A healthcare application must ensure that patient data is encrypted both when stored and when transmitted. Which Well-Architected principle covers this requirement?

answers.A: Protect data in transit and at rest
answers.B: Keep people away from data
answers.C: Annotate documentation
answers.D: Scale horizontally to increase aggregate system availability

explanation: Protect data in transit and at rest is a security principle that mandates encryption. The other choices do not directly mandate encryption.

stem: To reduce operational toil, a tech company automates security patching and vulnerability scanning across all accounts using AWS Systems Manager. Which design principle is addressed?

answers.A: Apply security at all layers
answers.B: Automate security best practices
answers.C: Manage change in automation
answers.D: Adopt a consumption model
