stem: A retail company's web application is repeatedly targeted by a DDoS attack that floods the Application Load Balancer with HTTP floods at Layer 7. Basic infrastructure-level protection is already in place. Which AWS service should be added to detect and mitigate Layer 7 DDoS attacks automatically?

answers.A: AWS Shield Standard, which automatically protects against Layer 7 attacks at no extra cost.
answers.B: AWS WAF with rate-based rules attached to the Application Load Balancer, combined with AWS Shield Advanced for enhanced DDoS protection and access to the AWS DDoS Response Team.
answers.C: Amazon GuardDuty, which monitors CloudTrail logs for DDoS indicators and blocks attackers.
answers.D: AWS Network Firewall deployed in the VPC to block malicious HTTP requests.

explanation: AWS WAF with rate-based rules limits the number of requests from a single IP and blocks HTTP floods at Layer 7. Shield Advanced provides advanced DDoS protection, real-time visibility, and access to the DDoS Response Team. Shield Standard protects at Layers 3/4 only. GuardDuty detects threats but doesn't block traffic. Network Firewall operates at Layer 3/4.

stem: A company stores database passwords and API keys in EC2 instance environment variables. A security audit flags this as a risk. The company wants to centrally store, rotate, and audit access to all secrets without changing how the application retrieves them significantly. Which service is most appropriate?

answers.A: Store secrets in an S3 bucket with server-side encryption and restrict access with bucket policies.
answers.B: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store Standard tier to store secrets as plain text.
answers.C: Use AWS Secrets Manager to store and automatically rotate secrets, and update the application to call the Secrets Manager API to retrieve secrets at runtime.
answers.D: Encrypt secrets using AWS KMS and embed the encrypted values in the application's source code.

explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is purpose-built for secret lifecycle management: it stores secrets with encryption, rotates them automatically (for supported services like RDS), and provides audit logging via CloudTrail. Parameter Store Standard doesn't support automatic rotation. S3 is not a secrets management service. Embedding encrypted secrets in source code is a security anti-pattern.

stem: An organization has multiple AWS accounts. Developers federate into accounts using IAM Identity Center (SSO). The security team wants to enforce MFA for all federated users accessing the AWS Management Console. Where should MFA be enforced?

answers.A: In IAM Identity Center, enable MFA for all users in the Identity Center user portal. This enforces MFA at the federation layer before any account access.
answers.B: Enable MFA on every IAM user in every account individually.
answers.C: Create an SCP in AWS Organizations that denies all actions if MFA is not present in the request context.
answers.D: Configure AWS CloudTrail to alert when users access the console without MFA and manually revoke sessions.

explanation: IAM Identity Center is the central authentication layer for federated access across multiple accounts. Enforcing MFA there applies it universally before any account-level access. Enabling MFA per IAM user is impractical if users are federated (they have no IAM user). SCPs can reinforce but cannot substitute for MFA at the authentication layer. CloudTrail alerts are detective, not preventive.

stem: A company wants to run a backend API that handles between 0 and 10,000 requests per minute with unpredictable traffic patterns. The team wants to minimize server management and pay only for actual usage. Which compute option best fits this requirement?

answers.A: AWS Lambda with Amazon API Gateway, which scales automatically from zero to high concurrency with no idle costs.
answers.B: Amazon EC2 with an Auto Scaling group that scales between 0 and 10 instances based on CPU.
answers.C: Amazon ECS on EC2 with a minimum cluster size of 2 and Auto Scaling policies.
answers.D: An Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance sized for peak capacity.

explanation: Lambda scales instantly from zero with no minimum idle cost, making it ideal for variable, unpredictable workloads. API Gateway provides a serverless HTTP front end. EC2 Auto Scaling cannot scale to zero (minimum 1 instance), incurring idle cost. ECS on EC2 requires a baseline cluster. Reserved Instances are appropriate for predictable, steady workloads.
tags: API creation and management (for example, Amazon API Gateway, REST API)
Serverless technologies and patterns (for example, AWS Fargate, AWS Lambda)

stem: A company is choosing between AWS Lambda and Amazon ECS on Fargate to run a new microservice. The microservice processes images, takes 8 minutes per image, and requires 6 GB of memory. Which service is more appropriate?

answers.A: AWS Lambda, because it is serverless and requires no container management.
answers.B: Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate, because Lambda has a maximum execution timeout of 15 minutes and a 10 GB memory limit, and longer or memory-intensive tasks are better suited to container-based execution.
answers.C: AWS Lambda with provisioned concurrency to avoid cold starts for the 8-minute jobs.
answers.D: AWS Lambda using Lambda Container Images to extend the runtime limits.

explanation: While Lambda supports up to 15 minutes and 10 GB of memory, 8-minute image processing at 6 GB is pushing Lambda's boundaries and would be better suited to ECS on Fargate, which has no timeout or memory constraints. Lambda is better for short-duration, event-driven tasks. Lambda Container Images don't extend execution limits.
tags: AWS managed services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Transfer Family, Amazon SQS, AWS Secrets Manager)

stem: A team has a monolithic Node.js application running on EC2 that they want to decompose into microservices. One component is a user authentication function called on every request (milliseconds of compute, thousands of times per day). Which decomposition approach uses serverless most appropriately?

answers.A: Move the entire monolith to Lambda by packaging it as a single Lambda function.
answers.B: Keep all components on EC2 but trigger them via SQS to decouple them.
answers.C: Extract the authentication function to a Lambda function behind an API Gateway authorizer, while keeping other components that require persistent connections on EC2 or ECS.
answers.D: Deploy each function of the monolith as a separate Lambda function, regardless of execution time or resource requirements.

explanation: Serverless is most appropriate for small, stateless, event-driven functions. Lambda Authorizers are a perfect fit for authentication logic: triggered per request, milliseconds of execution, no idle cost. Monoliths should not be moved wholesale to a single Lambda. Components requiring persistent state or long execution are better left on EC2/ECS. Not all functions should be moved to Lambda indiscriminately.
tags: Design principles for microservices (for example, stateless workloads compared with stateful workloads)

stem: A company runs an in-memory database (Redis) on a single EC2 instance. The database holds 500 GB of data in RAM and requires consistent, low-latency access. Which EC2 instance family is most appropriate?

answers.A: Compute optimized (C-family): designed for CPU-intensive workloads.
answers.B: Memory optimized (R or X-family): designed for workloads that process large datasets in memory, offering high RAM-to-vCPU ratios.
answers.C: Storage optimized (I-family): designed for high I/O throughput to local NVMe storage.
answers.D: General purpose (M-family): balanced CPU, memory, and networking.

explanation: Memory-optimized instances (R and X families) offer high RAM-to-vCPU ratios specifically for memory-intensive workloads like in-memory databases. 500 GB of RAM requires an R6g.16xlarge or X-family instance. Compute-optimized instances have less RAM per vCPU. Storage-optimized instances are for I/O-intensive workloads, not in-memory workloads. General purpose instances are less cost-effective for memory-heavy workloads.
tags: AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Batch, Amazon EMR, AWS Fargate)
Selecting the appropriate compute options and features (for example, EC2 instance types) to meet business requirements

stem: A genomics company runs compute-intensive DNA sequence alignment jobs that are CPU-bound and require no significant memory or storage. Jobs run for 4 hours and are submitted in batches. Which instance type and purchasing strategy is most appropriate?

answers.A: R5.8xlarge On-Demand: memory optimized for genomics data analysis.
answers.B: I3.4xlarge On-Demand: storage optimized for sequence file I/O.
answers.C: C5.9xlarge Spot Instances: compute optimized for CPU-intensive workloads at lowest cost, with re-run tolerance if interrupted.
answers.D: T3.2xlarge Reserved: general purpose burstable instances for variable workloads.

explanation: Compute-optimized (C-family) instances have the highest vCPU-to-memory ratio and are purpose-built for CPU-bound workloads like sequence alignment. Spot Instances offer up to 90% savings and are appropriate for batch jobs that can be rerun if interrupted. R-family instances are memory-optimized (overkill and more expensive). T3 burstable instances throttle CPU under sustained load, unsuitable for 4-hour CPU-bound jobs.
tags: AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Batch, Amazon EMR, AWS Fargate)
Selecting the appropriate compute options and features (for example, EC2 instance types) to meet business requirements

stem: A startup is building a real-time video transcoding service. Jobs are CPU-bound, run for 10 minutes, and must be completed within 15 minutes of submission. Traffic is unpredictable and can spike 10x. Which compute strategy ensures latency SLAs are met at lowest cost?

answers.A: Use Reserved C-family instances at peak capacity to guarantee availability.
answers.B: Use On-Demand M-family general purpose instances with Auto Scaling.
answers.C: Use Lambda functions for transcoding with Provisioned Concurrency.
answers.D: Use a mixed fleet Auto Scaling group of On-Demand and Spot C-family instances, with On-Demand as base capacity and Spot for burst, using Spot interruption handling to re-queue interrupted jobs to On-Demand capacity.

explanation: A mixed fleet with On-Demand base + Spot burst provides cost savings during spikes while maintaining SLAs: if a Spot instance is interrupted, the job re-queues to On-Demand capacity. C-family instances are right for CPU-bound transcoding. Reserved Instances at peak capacity over-provisions for normal traffic. Lambda has a 15-minute limit and limited CPU, not suited for video transcoding.
tags: AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Batch, Amazon EMR, AWS Fargate)
Selecting the appropriate compute options and features (for example, EC2 instance types) to meet business requirements

stem: A web application experiences high read latency on an Amazon RDS MySQL database. The read traffic is 90% repetitive queries for the same product catalog data, which changes once per day. Which caching strategy reduces database load most effectively?

answers.A: Add Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached in front of RDS. Cache product catalog query results with a TTL of 24 hours and invalidate the cache when the catalog is updated.
answers.B: Enable RDS read replicas to distribute read traffic across multiple instances.
answers.C: Enable RDS Performance Insights to identify slow queries and optimize them.
answers.D: Increase the RDS instance size to handle higher read throughput.

explanation: ElastiCache for Memcached caches frequently accessed, rarely changing data like product catalogs, serving results from memory in microseconds vs. milliseconds for RDS. A 24-hour TTL matches the update frequency. Read replicas reduce per-replica load but still hit the database; they don't eliminate repeated identical queries. Performance Insights and instance upgrades don't reduce query count.
tags: Configuring read replicas to meet business requirements

stem: A read-heavy e-commerce application uses Amazon DynamoDB. Over time, 80% of read traffic is for the same 1,000 popular item records (hot keys) while the rest is for millions of other items. DynamoDB throttling errors are occurring. Which caching approach specifically addresses hot-key throttling?

answers.A: Increase DynamoDB read capacity units (RCUs) to handle the hot-key traffic.
answers.B: Add Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) as an in-memory cache in front of DynamoDB. DAX caches individual item reads and reduces hot-key reads to microseconds without any application code changes.
answers.C: Use DynamoDB Streams to pre-populate ElastiCache for Redis with hot items.
answers.D: Enable DynamoDB auto scaling to increase RCUs during traffic spikes automatically.

explanation: DAX is a purpose-built DynamoDB-compatible in-memory cache that intercepts hot-key reads before they hit DynamoDB, eliminating throttling on frequently accessed items with zero application code changes (it uses the same DynamoDB SDK calls). Increasing RCUs is expensive for hot-key patterns. ElastiCache works but requires application code changes. Auto scaling addresses capacity but not hot-key concentration.
tags: Caching strategies and services (for example, Amazon ElastiCache)
Data access patterns (for example, read-intensive compared with write-intensive)

stem: A company is ingesting 1 TB of data per day from IoT sensors into AWS for analytics. They need to determine the correct data ingestion service. The data arrives as a continuous stream of small JSON messages at ~50,000 events/second. Which service is most appropriate for this throughput requirement?

answers.A: AWS Snowball Edge: physically ship data weekly for batch ingestion.
answers.B: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with enough shards to handle 50,000 records/second, delivering to Amazon S3 via Kinesis Data Firehose.
answers.C: AWS Direct Connect with a 1 Gbps connection for dedicated high-speed ingestion.
answers.D: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to upload JSON files directly from IoT devices.

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams is designed for real-time streaming ingestion at high throughput. Each shard handles up to 1,000 records/second or 1 MB/second; 50 shards handle 50,000 records/second. Firehose then delivers batched data to S3. Snowball is for offline bulk transfer. Direct Connect is for hybrid connectivity, not streaming ingestion. S3 Transfer Acceleration is for large file uploads, not event streams.
tags: Data transfer services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS DataSync, AWS Storage Gateway)

stem: A company must transfer 500 TB of historical data from on-premises to Amazon S3 within 2 weeks. Their internet connection is 1 Gbps and is fully utilized by production workloads. What is the most practical transfer solution?

answers.A: Use AWS DataSync over the existing internet connection to transfer data in the background.
answers.B: Upgrade the internet connection to 10 Gbps and use aws s3 sync for the transfer.
answers.C: Order multiple AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices to physically transport the data to AWS.
answers.D: Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to speed up uploads over the existing connection.

explanation: Transferring 500 TB over a 1 Gbps link (even at full utilization) would take over 45 days. Snowball Edge devices each hold up to 80 TB; 7 devices would move 500 TB physically within days. DataSync and aws s3 sync are limited by internet bandwidth. Upgrading connectivity takes longer than 2 weeks to provision. Transfer Acceleration improves upload performance but is still constrained by the 1 Gbps pipe.
tags: Data transfer services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS DataSync, AWS Storage Gateway)

stem: A retail company needs to deliver real-time inventory updates to their mobile app. Updates arrive at 10,000 events/second and must be delivered to clients within 500 milliseconds. Downstream systems consume the data for analytics and fraud detection simultaneously. Which architecture meets the throughput and latency requirements?

answers.A: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (multiple shards) to ingest events, with multiple consumer applications (Lambda for mobile push, Kinesis Data Analytics for fraud detection, Kinesis Data Firehose for analytics) each reading from the stream independently.
answers.B: Amazon SQS standard queue to buffer events, with Lambda polling the queue for each consumer.
answers.C: Amazon SNS to fan out events to multiple SQS queues, each with a Lambda consumer reading at its own pace.
answers.D: Write events directly to Amazon DynamoDB and have each consumer application poll DynamoDB for new records.

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams supports multiple independent consumers reading from the same stream simultaneously (Enhanced Fan-Out provides dedicated throughput per consumer), meeting both the 10,000 events/second ingest and the 500ms delivery requirement. SQS doesn't support multiple independent consumers without SNS fan-out. SNS/SQS fan-out adds latency and is harder to manage at this scale. DynamoDB polling adds latency and is not a streaming architecture.
tags: Streaming data services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon Kinesis)

stem: A company is running a big data analytics workload on Amazon EMR that reads and writes large sequential files. The workload does not require high IOPS. Which Amazon EBS volume type is the most cost-effective for this use case?

answers.A: io2 Block Express: highest IOPS and lowest latency.
answers.B: gp3: general purpose SSD balancing price and performance.
answers.C: st1 (Throughput Optimized HDD): designed for large, sequential I/O workloads like big data and log processing at a lower cost per GB than SSD.
answers.D: sc1 (Cold HDD): lowest-cost EBS option for infrequently accessed data.

explanation: st1 is optimized for large sequential reads and writes (up to 500 MB/s throughput) at a significantly lower cost per GB than SSD volumes. It is the standard choice for EMR, data warehouses, and log processing. io2 and gp3 are designed for random I/O workloads. sc1 is for cold, infrequently accessed data with lower throughput limits.
tags: Selecting the most cost-effective storage service for a workload

stem: A startup runs a content archiving application that stores infrequently accessed files. Files are read at most once a month for review. The primary requirement is the lowest possible EBS storage cost. Which volume type is most appropriate?

answers.A: gp3 SSD: cost-effective general purpose storage.
answers.B: st1 HDD: throughput-optimized for sequential workloads.
answers.C: io1 SSD: provisioned IOPS for high-performance workloads.
answers.D: sc1 (Cold HDD): the lowest-cost EBS volume type, designed for infrequently accessed sequential workloads.

explanation: sc1 is the cheapest EBS volume type, priced around $0.015/GB/month vs $0.025/GB for st1. It suits cold storage workloads where data is accessed rarely. The lower throughput ceiling (up to 250 MB/s) is acceptable for once-a-month access. gp3, io1, and st1 are all more expensive and designed for more frequent or higher-performance access patterns.
tags: Access options (for example, an S3 bucket with Requester Pays object storage)

stem: A company is migrating from Oracle Database Enterprise Edition (on-premises) to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL as part of a cost-reduction initiative. This is classified as which type of migration?

answers.A: Homogeneous migration: both databases are relational.
answers.B: Heterogeneous migration: the source and target use different database engines (Oracle to PostgreSQL), requiring schema and code conversion.
answers.C: Lift-and-shift migration: the database is moved to EC2 with no engine change.
answers.D: In-place migration: the database engine is upgraded in place on the same infrastructure.

explanation: A heterogeneous migration involves different source and target database engines (Oracle → PostgreSQL), requiring schema and stored procedure conversion using AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) and data migration via DMS. A homogeneous migration uses the same engine (e.g., MySQL → MySQL). Lift-and-shift and in-place migrations don't involve engine changes.
tags: Migrating database schemas and data to different locations and/or different database engines
Database engines with appropriate use cases (for example, heterogeneous migrations, homogeneous migrations)

stem: A company is migrating a SQL Server database to Amazon RDS for SQL Server. Which type of migration is this, and which AWS tools are needed?

answers.A: Homogeneous migration (same engine, SQL Server to SQL Server). AWS DMS can migrate the data without schema conversion. AWS SCT is not required.
answers.B: Heterogeneous migration. AWS SCT must convert the schema from SQL Server to RDS SQL Server dialect, then DMS migrates data.
answers.C: Homogeneous migration. AWS SCT is required to optimize the schema for RDS.
answers.D: Heterogeneous migration. Only pg_dump/pg_restore can perform this type of migration.

explanation: Migrating SQL Server to RDS for SQL Server is a homogeneous migration — the database engine is unchanged. DMS can handle the data transfer directly without schema conversion. SCT is needed for heterogeneous migrations (different source and target engines). pg_dump/pg_restore is for PostgreSQL only.
tags: Determining an appropriate database engine (for example, MySQL compared with PostgreSQL)

stem: After migrating a MySQL database from on-premises to Amazon Aurora MySQL using AWS DMS, the team notices that some Oracle-specific functions referenced in views are failing. What is the most likely explanation?

answers.A: The DMS replication instance ran out of storage during the migration.
answers.B: Aurora MySQL does not support views.
answers.C: The original database was likely Oracle, not MySQL, and object references in views used Oracle-specific syntax not compatible with Aurora MySQL. SCT was not used to convert these objects.
answers.D: Amazon Aurora MySQL has a different MySQL dialect that doesn't support standard views.

explanation: Oracle-specific functions in views indicate the source was Oracle, not MySQL. This is a heterogeneous migration that requires AWS SCT to convert schema objects including views. DMS migrates data but not incompatible schema objects. Aurora MySQL fully supports MySQL-compatible views and functions.
tags: Migrating database schemas and data to different locations and/or different database engines

stem: A company's web application has recently suffered a SQL injection attack that extracted customer data from an Amazon RDS database. The application is behind an Application Load Balancer. Which combination of AWS services prevents future SQL injection attacks?

answers.A: Enable AWS Shield Advanced on the ALB to detect and block SQL injection at Layer 7.
answers.B: Deploy AWS WAF on the ALB with a managed rule group for SQL injection (e.g., AWS Managed Rules SQL database rule group) to inspect and block HTTP requests containing SQL injection payloads.
answers.C: Enable Amazon Inspector on the EC2 instances running the application to scan for vulnerabilities.
answers.D: Use Amazon GuardDuty to detect SQL injection attempts in real time and automatically update security groups.

explanation: AWS WAF with the SQL database managed rule group inspects incoming HTTP/HTTPS requests for SQL injection patterns and blocks matching requests before they reach the application. Shield Advanced is a DDoS protection service, not a WAF. Inspector assesses EC2 vulnerabilities — it doesn't block runtime attacks. GuardDuty detects threats via log analysis but doesn't actively block requests.
tags: Integrating AWS services to secure applications (for example, AWS Shield, AWS WAF, IAM Identity Center, AWS Secrets Manager)

stem: An application is experiencing a volumetric DDoS attack that is saturating the network interface of the EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer. The attack involves SYN floods and UDP reflection. Which AWS protection is appropriate?

answers.A: AWS Shield Standard, which is automatically enabled on all AWS accounts at no cost, protects against common Layer 3 and Layer 4 DDoS attacks including SYN floods and UDP reflection.
answers.B: AWS WAF with rate-based rules to block the attacking IPs.
answers.C: Amazon GuardDuty to detect the attack and automatically update NACLs to block the source IPs.
answers.D: Amazon CloudWatch alarms to alert the team when network traffic exceeds a threshold.

explanation: AWS Shield Standard is automatically enabled for all AWS customers and provides protection against common infrastructure-level DDoS attacks (Layers 3 and 4), including SYN floods and UDP amplification, at no additional charge. WAF operates at Layer 7 and doesn't handle volumetric Layer 3/4 attacks. GuardDuty and CloudWatch are detective tools, not active protections.
tags: Control ports, protocols, and network traffic on AWS

stem: A company runs a public REST API behind Amazon API Gateway. A security audit identifies that the API is vulnerable to HTTP parameter tampering where attackers modify request parameters to access other users' data. Which service and feature helps mitigate this at the API layer?

answers.A: Enable AWS Shield Advanced on the API Gateway to detect parameter manipulation.
answers.B: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor API Gateway access logs for suspicious parameter patterns.
answers.C: Deploy AWS WAF on the API Gateway with custom rules or managed rule groups that validate and restrict request parameter values, blocking requests with suspicious or out-of-range parameter values.
answers.D: Use Amazon Cognito to authenticate all API requests, which prevents parameter tampering.

explanation: AWS WAF custom rules can validate request parameters (size constraints, regex patterns, value ranges) and block requests that violate expected patterns, directly mitigating parameter tampering at the API layer. Shield Advanced is for DDoS protection. GuardDuty is detective only. Cognito authentication prevents unauthorized access but doesn't validate the content of authenticated requests.

stem: A company wants to ensure their EC2 instances always run a known, tested AMI and that configuration drift (manual changes to running instances) is automatically detected and remediated. Which approach implements immutable infrastructure with automated integrity checks?

answers.A: Use AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to patch running EC2 instances in place.
answers.B: Use EC2 Image Builder to build and test golden AMIs, deploy new instances from those AMIs via Auto Scaling launch templates, and use AWS Config rules to detect and alert on configuration drift.
answers.C: Use AWS CloudTrail to log all API calls and manually review changes to EC2 instances weekly.
answers.D: Deploy AWS Inspector on all instances to continuously scan for configuration issues.

explanation: Immutable infrastructure means replacing instances rather than modifying them: EC2 Image Builder creates tested golden AMIs, Auto Scaling deploys from those AMIs, and AWS Config continuously evaluates resource configurations against desired state. Patch Manager modifies running instances (mutable). CloudTrail provides audit logs but not automated remediation. Inspector assesses security vulnerabilities, not configuration drift.
tags: AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions, Amazon Route 53)

stem: A company wants to automatically detect and remediate EC2 instances whose security group configurations have changed from the approved baseline (e.g., a port 22 rule was added). Which AWS service automates this?

answers.A: Amazon GuardDuty, which detects security misconfigurations and automatically reverts them.
answers.B: AWS CloudTrail, which logs security group changes and triggers a Lambda to revert them via an EventBridge rule.
answers.C: AWS Config with a managed rule (restricted-ssh) and an automatic remediation action via AWS Systems Manager Automation to revert unauthorized security group changes.
answers.D: Amazon Inspector, which scans security groups and removes unauthorized rules automatically.

explanation: AWS Config continuously evaluates resource configurations against rules (e.g., restricted-ssh checks for unrestricted SSH access). When a rule is non-compliant, Config can trigger automatic remediation via SSM Automation documents to revert the change. CloudTrail logs changes and can trigger Lambda via EventBridge but requires custom implementation. GuardDuty and Inspector don't automatically revert security group changes.
tags: AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions, Amazon Route 53)
Service quotas and throttling (for example, how to configure the service quotas for a workload in a standby environment)

stem: A company needs to guarantee that all S3 buckets in their AWS account never have public access enabled. New buckets are created regularly by developers. Which automation strategy enforces this at scale?

answers.A: Enable S3 Block Public Access at the AWS account level in the S3 console, which prevents any bucket or object in the account from being made public, and use an AWS Config rule to detect and remediate any buckets where it is disabled.
answers.B: Write a daily Lambda function that checks all S3 buckets and removes public access policies.
answers.C: Apply a Service Control Policy (SCP) in AWS Organizations that denies s3:PutBucketPolicy on all member accounts.
answers.D: Use Amazon Macie to detect publicly accessible S3 buckets and alert the security team.

explanation: Account-level S3 Block Public Access is the most effective preventive control — it overrides bucket and object ACLs regardless of what developers configure. AWS Config continuously monitors compliance. An SCP can complement this but denying PutBucketPolicy would prevent legitimate bucket policies. Daily Lambda checks are reactive, not preventive. Macie is a detective tool.
tags: AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions, Amazon Route 53)
Using AWS services that improve the reliability of legacy applications and applications not built for the cloud (for example, when application changes are not possible)

stem: A company runs an application on EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone. They need to make the application highly available against AZ failures with no data loss and automatic failover. Which architecture achieves this?

answers.A: Use EC2 Auto Scaling to replace failed instances within the same AZ automatically.
answers.B: Deploy EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer, with an RDS Multi-AZ database. Configure the Auto Scaling group to span all AZs.
answers.C: Deploy instances in two AZs using Route 53 health checks for DNS failover.
answers.D: Replicate EC2 instances using AWS Backup across AZs to restore quickly if an AZ fails.

explanation: An ALB spans multiple AZs and automatically routes traffic to healthy instances. Auto Scaling across multiple AZs ensures capacity is maintained if an AZ fails. RDS Multi-AZ provides synchronous replication and automatic failover. Auto Scaling within a single AZ only replaces instances, not AZ failures. DNS failover adds propagation delay. AWS Backup provides recovery, not active failover.
tags: Determining the AWS services required to provide a highly available and/or fault-tolerant architecture across AWS Regions or Availability Zones

stem: A company must ensure their application remains available even if an entire AWS Region becomes unavailable. They require an RTO of under 1 hour. Which multi-region architecture pattern achieves this at the lowest cost?

answers.A: Active-active multi-region: deploy the full application stack in two regions and route 50% of traffic to each region continuously.
answers.B: Backup and restore: take daily RDS snapshots and copy to a second region; restore if the primary region fails.
answers.C: Pilot light: replicate core data (RDS read replica in second region) and keep a minimal compute footprint ready. Scale out the application in the secondary region in under 1 hour when a failover is triggered.
answers.D: Warm standby: run a fully scaled-down but active replica of the production stack in the secondary region at 50% capacity, continuously routing 10% of traffic there.

explanation: Pilot light keeps the data continuously replicated but computes at minimal cost. Scaling out within 1 hour is feasible with automation. It's cheaper than active-active or warm standby. Backup and restore typically exceeds a 1-hour RTO for large databases. Active-active provides the lowest RTO but at double the infrastructure cost.
tags: AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions, Amazon Route 53)
Determining automation strategies to ensure infrastructure integrity

stem: An application uses Amazon DynamoDB as its database and must be highly available across two AWS Regions with active-active read/write capability. Which DynamoDB feature enables this?

answers.A: DynamoDB Global Tables, which replicate table data across multiple Regions in real time and support multi-region, multi-active write capability.
answers.B: DynamoDB Streams, which can be read by Lambda functions in multiple regions to replicate data.
answers.C: DynamoDB DAX clusters deployed in each region for low-latency reads.
answers.D: DynamoDB On-Demand mode, which automatically scales to accommodate multi-region traffic.

explanation: DynamoDB Global Tables is the native multi-region, multi-active feature that replicates table data across chosen Regions in near-real time, enabling reads and writes in all configured Regions. DynamoDB Streams + Lambda can build custom replication but with added complexity and latency. DAX is a read cache, not a replication mechanism. On-Demand mode governs billing, not replication.
tags: AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions, Amazon Route 53)
Determining the AWS services required to provide a highly available and/or fault-tolerant architecture across AWS Regions or Availability Zones

stem: A company's application stores and retrieves millions of small objects (average 50 KB) from Amazon S3. Read performance is poor. A solutions architect is evaluating options to improve throughput without changing the application's S3 API calls. Which configuration change most improves S3 read performance?

answers.A: Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication to keep a copy in a closer region.
answers.B: Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration for uploads and implement a CloudFront distribution in front of S3 for reads, caching objects at edge locations.
answers.C: Change the S3 bucket to use the S3 Express One Zone storage class for lower latency.
answers.D: Increase the S3 request rate by using multiple prefixes in object key names to parallelize requests.

explanation: CloudFront caches S3 objects at edge locations, reducing latency for repeated reads of the same objects and offloading requests from S3. This is the most impactful change for read performance with no application changes. S3 Express One Zone provides lower latency but is a different storage class requiring a different API. Multiple prefixes improve S3 request rate limits but not end-user latency. Transfer Acceleration improves upload speed.
tags: Hybrid storage solutions to meet business requirements
Determining storage services and configurations that meet performance demands

stem: A video production company uses Amazon EFS to share video project files across 20 EC2 instances. They observe poor throughput when multiple instances simultaneously read large files. Which EFS configuration change improves throughput performance?

answers.A: Switch EFS to use the Infrequent Access storage class to reduce latency.
answers.B: Change the EFS performance mode from General Purpose to Max I/O.
answers.C: Switch to EFS Elastic Throughput mode (or Provisioned Throughput) and choose Max I/O performance mode to handle high aggregate throughput from many concurrent clients.
answers.D: Reduce the number of EC2 instances accessing EFS to below 10 to stay within the file system's throughput limits.

explanation: Max I/O performance mode is designed for highly parallelized workloads with many clients, providing higher aggregate throughput at the cost of slightly higher per-operation latency. Elastic or Provisioned Throughput allows the file system to scale or guarantee throughput independent of storage size. Infrequent Access increases latency. Reducing concurrent clients defeats the purpose of shared storage.
tags: Determining storage services and configurations that meet performance demands
Determining storage services that can scale to accommodate future needs

stem: A company wants to run containerized microservices on AWS. The team is familiar with Kubernetes and wants to use standard Kubernetes APIs and tooling (kubectl, Helm, etc.) while minimizing cluster management overhead. Which service is most appropriate?

answers.A: Amazon ECS on EC2 with a custom task definition that supports kubectl commands.
answers.B: Amazon EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service), which runs managed Kubernetes control plane and supports standard Kubernetes APIs, kubectl, and Helm.
answers.C: AWS Fargate without an orchestrator, running containers directly on serverless compute.
answers.D: AWS Elastic Beanstalk, which supports Docker containers with automatic orchestration.

explanation: EKS is AWS's managed Kubernetes service that runs a compliant Kubernetes control plane and supports all standard Kubernetes tooling. Teams already familiar with Kubernetes can use EKS with no tooling changes. ECS uses AWS-specific task definitions and does not support kubectl. Fargate is a compute engine used with ECS or EKS, not a standalone orchestrator. Elastic Beanstalk is not a Kubernetes-compatible service.
tags: AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Batch, Amazon EMR, AWS Fargate)
Selecting the appropriate compute options and features (for example, EC2 instance types) to meet business requirements

stem: A startup is containerizing a simple web application and wants the fastest path to production with containers on AWS. The team has no Kubernetes experience and wants to minimize infrastructure management. Which orchestration service is most appropriate?

answers.A: Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate: a serverless container orchestration service with a simpler model than Kubernetes, requiring no cluster management or Kubernetes expertise.
answers.B: Amazon EKS on AWS Fargate: runs Kubernetes without managing nodes, but still requires Kubernetes knowledge.
answers.C: Amazon EKS on EC2: provides full Kubernetes control with self-managed worker nodes.
answers.D: AWS App Runner: fully managed container deployment service requiring no orchestration knowledge, but limited to simple web applications and APIs.

explanation: ECS on Fargate is the simplest AWS container orchestration option: it abstracts away the underlying infrastructure, has a straightforward task/service model, and requires no Kubernetes expertise. EKS on Fargate still requires Kubernetes knowledge. EKS on EC2 requires managing worker nodes. App Runner is even simpler but limited in capabilities for production microservices.
tags: The orchestration of containers (for example, Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS)
Scalability capabilities with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, AWS Auto Scaling)

stem: A company runs 200 microservices across Amazon ECS and wants to migrate to Kubernetes for standardized tooling and better portability. They want to run Kubernetes without managing the control plane. Which option is correct?

answers.A: Self-install Kubernetes on EC2 using kubeadm and manage the control plane manually.
answers.B: Use Amazon ECS with Kubernetes compatibility mode enabled.
answers.C: Use Amazon EKS, which provides a fully managed Kubernetes control plane (etcd, API server, scheduler) with automatic updates and high availability.
answers.D: Use AWS App Mesh to orchestrate the existing ECS microservices with Kubernetes-compatible APIs.

explanation: Amazon EKS manages the Kubernetes control plane (etcd, API server, controller manager, scheduler) including high availability and version upgrades, so the team only manages worker nodes (or uses Fargate for serverless nodes). ECS has no Kubernetes compatibility mode. Self-managed Kubernetes on EC2 requires full control plane management. App Mesh is a service mesh, not a container orchestrator.
tags: Decoupling workloads so that components can scale independently
AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Batch, Amazon EMR, AWS Fargate)

stem: A company wants to migrate from a commercial Oracle database to reduce licensing costs. They are willing to refactor stored procedures. Which AWS-managed database service is the most Oracle-compatible, offering Oracle-to-Aurora migration tooling?

answers.A: Amazon DynamoDB: a NoSQL database that eliminates licensing costs entirely.
answers.B: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: supports most Oracle SQL syntax through compatibility features and is supported by AWS SCT for schema conversion from Oracle.
answers.C: Amazon RDS for SQL Server: a different commercial engine with similar licensing costs.
answers.D: Amazon Redshift: a data warehouse optimized for analytical queries, not OLTP.

explanation: Aurora PostgreSQL is the most common Oracle migration target for OLTP workloads, offering strong SQL compatibility and supported by AWS SCT and DMS for heterogeneous migrations. DynamoDB requires significant application refactoring and is not SQL-compatible. RDS for SQL Server still requires Microsoft licensing. Redshift is for analytics, not transactional workloads.
tags: AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions)

stem: A company runs a MySQL 5.7 database on EC2. They want to migrate to a managed service without changing the MySQL engine. Which migration is homogeneous and which tool migrates the data with minimal downtime?

answers.A: Migrate to Amazon RDS for MySQL or Amazon Aurora MySQL (homogeneous migration). Use AWS DMS with Full Load + CDC to replicate data continuously until cutover.
answers.B: Migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (heterogeneous migration). Use AWS SCT to convert the schema and DMS to migrate data.
answers.C: Migrate to Amazon Redshift (heterogeneous migration). Use AWS Glue to transform and load MySQL data.
answers.D: Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB (heterogeneous migration). Use AWS Database Migration Service in NoSQL migration mode.

explanation: MySQL to RDS/Aurora MySQL is a homogeneous migration — same engine family, no schema conversion required. DMS with Full Load + CDC provides near-zero-downtime migration. Aurora PostgreSQL and DynamoDB are heterogeneous targets requiring additional conversion. Redshift is an analytical data warehouse, not a drop-in MySQL replacement.
tags: Determining an appropriate database engine (for example, MySQL compared with PostgreSQL)

stem: A financial company currently runs a Microsoft SQL Server database for OLTP workloads and pays significant licensing fees. They want to evaluate a PostgreSQL-compatible managed service to reduce costs. Which AWS service provides the highest PostgreSQL compatibility with enterprise features like global replication?

answers.A: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL: fully managed PostgreSQL with standard features.
answers.B: Amazon DynamoDB: eliminates SQL licensing costs with a NoSQL model.
answers.C: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: a PostgreSQL-compatible engine with up to 5x the performance of standard PostgreSQL, Global Database for cross-region replication, and Serverless v2 for variable workloads.
answers.D: Amazon Redshift with Spectrum: PostgreSQL-compatible analytical queries on S3.

explanation: Aurora PostgreSQL provides PostgreSQL compatibility with enterprise-grade features (Global Database, Multi-AZ, Serverless v2, automated backups) at lower licensing cost than SQL Server. RDS for PostgreSQL is also valid but lacks Aurora's performance and Global Database features. DynamoDB requires significant application changes. Redshift is an analytical warehouse, not an OLTP replacement.
tags: AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions)

stem: A company wants to build a data lake on Amazon S3 that aggregates data from multiple sources. They need to control which teams can access which datasets, enforce column-level security on sensitive tables, and provide a central data catalog. Which AWS service simplifies these data lake governance requirements?

answers.A: Amazon Macie, to classify and protect sensitive data in S3.
answers.B: AWS Lake Formation, which provides centralized data lake access control, column-level and row-level security, fine-grained permissions, and integration with the AWS Glue Data Catalog.
answers.C: Amazon S3 bucket policies with prefix-based access control for each team.
answers.D: AWS IAM policies with resource-level permissions on each S3 prefix.

explanation: AWS Lake Formation is purpose-built for data lake governance: it manages a central Data Catalog, enforces table/column/row-level access control on top of S3 data, and integrates with Athena, Redshift Spectrum, and EMR. Macie detects sensitive data but doesn't enforce access. S3 bucket policies and IAM policies operate at the object/prefix level and don't support column-level security.

stem: A company is building a data lake in Amazon S3. Raw data from various sources lands in S3 and must be catalogued automatically so analysts can discover and query it with Amazon Athena. Which AWS service should be used to crawl the S3 data and populate a metadata catalog?

answers.A: AWS Glue Crawlers, which automatically scan S3 data, infer schemas, and create/update tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog.
answers.B: Amazon Macie, which classifies S3 data and creates a data inventory.
answers.C: Amazon Athena, which can directly infer schemas from S3 files without a catalog.
answers.D: AWS Lake Formation Blueprint, which automatically imports data from databases into S3 and creates catalog entries.

explanation: Glue Crawlers scan S3 paths, detect file formats and schemas, and populate the Glue Data Catalog with table definitions that Athena uses for queries. Macie is a security service for sensitive data detection. Athena requires pre-defined table definitions (via Glue Data Catalog or manual DDL). Lake Formation Blueprints import data from databases into S3 but don't crawl existing S3 data.
tags: Transforming data between formats (for example, .csv to .parquet)

stem: A security team needs to ensure that sensitive customer PII data stored in a data lake on Amazon S3 is encrypted at rest and that only authorized ETL jobs (running on AWS Glue) can access the raw data. Which combination of controls achieves this?

answers.A: Enable S3 default encryption with SSE-S3 and use S3 ACLs to restrict access to the Glue service role.
answers.B: Enable Amazon Macie on the S3 bucket to block unauthorized access automatically.
answers.C: Enable S3 default encryption with SSE-KMS using a customer-managed KMS key, restrict KMS key usage to the Glue IAM role, and use Lake Formation permissions to grant table access only to the Glue ETL job's IAM role.
answers.D: Use S3 Block Public Access and restrict the bucket policy to deny all principals except the Glue service.

explanation: SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key provides encryption with fine-grained access control (only the Glue role's key policy allows decryption). Lake Formation adds table/column-level permissions on top of the S3 access. SSE-S3 provides encryption but uses AWS-managed keys with less access control. Macie is detective, not preventive. S3 Block Public Access + bucket policies operate at the object level, not table/column level.

stem: A company collects temperature sensor readings every second from 10,000 sensors and needs to query trends over time (e.g., average temperature per hour per sensor over the last 30 days). Which database type and AWS service is most cost-effective for this workload?

answers.A: Amazon RDS for MySQL with a timestamp index on the readings table.
answers.B: Amazon DynamoDB with a partition key of sensor ID and sort key of timestamp.
answers.C: Amazon Timestream, a purpose-built time series database optimized for ingesting and querying time-stamped data with automatic data tiering from memory to magnetic storage.
answers.D: Amazon Redshift for analytical queries on time-series data.

explanation: Amazon Timestream is AWS's managed time series database, purpose-built for IoT and telemetry data. It automatically tiers data from in-memory (recent) to cost-effective magnetic storage (historical), and supports time series functions natively. RDS and DynamoDB can store time series data but are not optimized for time-based aggregations at this scale. Redshift works but requires manual data tiering and is more expensive.
tags: Determining cost-effective AWS database types (for example, time series format, columnar format)
AWS cost management service features (for example, cost allocation tags, multi-account billing)

stem: A data analytics team runs complex aggregation queries on a 10 TB dataset that joins multiple large tables. Query performance is poor on their Amazon RDS PostgreSQL instance. They need a database optimized for analytical (OLAP) workloads at the lowest cost. Which AWS service is most appropriate?

answers.A: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with read replicas to distribute analytical query load.
answers.B: Amazon Redshift, a columnar, massively parallel processing (MPP) data warehouse optimized for OLAP analytical queries on large datasets.
answers.C: Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity mode to handle analytical query spikes.
answers.D: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to cache query results and reduce RDS load.

explanation: Amazon Redshift uses columnar storage and MPP execution, making it orders of magnitude faster and more cost-effective than row-based RDS for analytical queries on large datasets. RDS read replicas reduce per-replica load but don't change the OLTP query execution model. DynamoDB is a key-value/document NoSQL store, not suited for complex SQL analytics. ElastiCache can cache results but doesn't solve the underlying query performance issue.
tags: Determining cost-effective AWS database types (for example, time series format, columnar format)
Determining cost-effective AWS database services with appropriate use cases (for example, DynamoDB compared with Amazon RDS, serverless)

stem: A global media company hosts a popular news website with millions of daily visitors worldwide. Most of the page content changes infrequently (articles are published once and rarely updated). The origin servers in us-east-1 are experiencing high load and latency for global users. Which cost optimization strategy has the greatest impact?

answers.A: Deploy Amazon CloudFront in front of the origin servers with appropriate cache-control headers (long TTLs for static content). CloudFront serves cached content from edge locations globally, reducing origin load and improving latency.
answers.B: Deploy EC2 instances in each AWS Region where users are located and use Route 53 latency-based routing.
answers.C: Use AWS Global Accelerator to route all traffic over the AWS backbone network to us-east-1.
answers.D: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the origin S3 bucket to speed up content delivery.

explanation: CloudFront caches content at 400+ edge locations globally. For infrequently changing content with long TTLs, the majority of requests are served from cache, dramatically reducing origin load and cost while improving global latency. Multi-region EC2 deployment requires replication and significantly higher infrastructure cost. Global Accelerator routes to the origin (us-east-1) faster but doesn't cache content. S3 Transfer Acceleration improves upload speeds, not download/delivery performance.
tags: Determining strategic needs for content delivery networks (CDNs) and edge caching
Load balancing concepts (for example, Application Load Balancer)

stem: A company wants to decide whether to use Amazon CloudFront or AWS Global Accelerator to improve performance for their application. The application is an API that handles personalized, non-cacheable requests. Which service is more appropriate and why?

answers.A: Amazon CloudFront: it can cache API responses at edge locations to reduce origin load.
answers.B: AWS Global Accelerator: it routes non-cacheable API traffic over the AWS global backbone network to the origin in the optimal Region, reducing latency without caching.
answers.C: Amazon CloudFront with cache TTL set to 0: it proxies requests to the origin with no caching, providing the same benefit as Global Accelerator.
answers.D: Neither; both services only benefit static content delivery and have no value for dynamic APIs.

explanation: Global Accelerator is designed for dynamic, non-cacheable traffic: it uses anycast routing to direct users to AWS edge locations and then forwards traffic over the low-latency AWS backbone to the application. CloudFront is optimized for cacheable content; setting TTL to 0 wastes the caching infrastructure and adds CloudFront overhead without benefit. Both services provide value for dynamic content — Global Accelerator is the right choice.
tags: Network services with appropriate use cases (for example, DNS)
AWS cost management service features (for example, cost allocation tags, multi-account billing)

stem: A retail company serves product images globally from an S3 bucket in us-east-1. They want to reduce costs by minimizing S3 data transfer charges and improving load times for users in Asia and Europe. What is the most cost-effective strategy?

answers.A: Replicate the S3 bucket to additional regions using S3 Cross-Region Replication and use Route 53 geolocation routing.
answers.B: Use AWS Global Accelerator to route image requests to the S3 bucket in us-east-1.
answers.C: Create a CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin. CloudFront caches images at edge locations globally, reducing repeated S3 GET requests and inter-regional data transfer charges.
answers.D: Use S3 Transfer Acceleration to speed up image delivery to global users.

explanation: CloudFront caches S3 objects at edge locations. Once cached, subsequent requests are served from the edge with no additional S3 GET or inter-regional data transfer charge. S3 CRR replicates data to multiple regions at replication cost plus ongoing S3 storage cost. Global Accelerator routes to the origin without caching. S3 Transfer Acceleration improves upload performance, not download delivery.
tags: Configuring appropriate network routes to minimize network transfer costs (for example, Region to Region, Availability Zone to Availability Zone, private to public, AWS Global Accelerator, VPC endpoints)
Determining strategic needs for content delivery networks (CDNs) and edge caching

stem: A startup is building an image-processing pipeline that receives unpredictable bursts from 0 to 8,000 requests per minute. Each request runs for 2-4 seconds, must complete within 15 seconds end-to-end, and requires occasional access to a VPC-hosted PostgreSQL database. The team has only two engineers and wants to minimize operational overhead while keeping cost low during idle periods. Which architecture is MOST appropriate?

answers.A: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions in a VPC, decouple work with Amazon SQS, and scale Lambda concurrency with reserved concurrency controls.
answers.B: Run a continuously provisioned Amazon ECS service on Fargate behind an ALB and scale tasks on CPU utilization.
answers.C: Deploy Amazon EKS with Karpenter and HPA to autoscale pods based on queue depth.
answers.D: Run EC2 Auto Scaling instances with a custom AMI and process requests through an NLB.

explanation: This is a classic bursty, short-lived workload with long idle periods and small team capacity constraints. API Gateway + Lambda + SQS provides serverless elasticity, low idle cost, and simpler operations while still supporting VPC access. ECS/Fargate and EKS can work but generally introduce more operational tuning and baseline cost for this request profile. EC2 adds the most management burden.
tags: API creation and management (for example, Amazon API Gateway, REST API)
Serverless technologies and patterns (for example, AWS Fargate, AWS Lambda)

stem: A media company runs a workflow that ingests uploaded videos, triggers parallel transcode and metadata extraction steps, retries failed steps with exponential backoff, and sends a final callback only after all branches succeed. The workload volume fluctuates heavily, and the team wants minimal infrastructure management. Which design BEST fits the requirement?

answers.A: Use Amazon ECS services for each stage with EventBridge rules and custom state-tracking tables in DynamoDB.
answers.B: Use AWS Batch for all steps and poll job states from an AWS Lambda coordinator.
answers.C: Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate parallel branches and retries, with AWS Lambda and service integrations for each task.
answers.D: Use Amazon MQ with worker consumers and implement workflow state transitions in application code.

explanation: The requirement is orchestration-centric: parallel branches, retries, backoff, and completion coordination with minimal ops. Step Functions is purpose-built for this serverless pattern and reduces custom state-management code. Other options can implement the behavior but require significant custom orchestration logic and operational overhead.
tags: Workflow orchestration (for example, AWS Step Functions)
The orchestration of containers (for example, Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS)

stem: A company is modernizing a monolithic Java application that requires sidecar agents for service mesh, custom kernel tuning, and strict control over container runtime behavior. Teams already run Kubernetes on-prem and need workload portability between on-prem and AWS with minimal re-platforming risk. Which compute strategy is MOST suitable?

answers.A: Refactor into AWS Lambda functions and use API Gateway for all service endpoints.
answers.B: Adopt Amazon EKS and deploy the existing Kubernetes manifests with incremental adjustments.
answers.C: Use Amazon ECS on Fargate because it removes all cluster management and supports all Kubernetes-native controls.
answers.D: Migrate directly to AWS App Runner to preserve all current sidecar and runtime controls.

explanation: The key signal is Kubernetes portability plus deep runtime control requirements. EKS aligns best with existing K8s operations and minimizes migration risk from on-prem Kubernetes. Lambda is a major re-architecture; Fargate/ECS simplifies operations but does not provide Kubernetes-native portability and control parity; App Runner is not designed for this level of runtime customization.
tags: Determining the AWS services required to achieve loose coupling based on requirements
Recommending appropriate compute, storage, networking, and database technologies based on requirements

stem: An organization wants to reduce EC2 spend across 40 accounts. They need to identify which instance families drive the highest compute costs by environment tag, forecast month-end spend, and alert when projected spend exceeds team budgets. Which approach provides the MOST complete solution with minimal custom tooling?

answers.A: Activate cost allocation tags, use AWS Cost Explorer for service and instance-family analysis plus forecasting, and configure AWS Budgets with forecasted cost alerts per team.
answers.B: Use CloudWatch metrics and alarms on CPUUtilization, then notify teams when utilization is low.
answers.C: Enable Trusted Advisor checks and notify teams when underutilized EC2 instances are detected.
answers.D: Use AWS Compute Optimizer only, and rely on its recommendations as a budgeting and forecasting replacement.

explanation: The question asks for cost attribution, forecasting, and threshold alerting. Cost allocation tags + Cost Explorer + Budgets directly address all three. CloudWatch utilization is operational telemetry, not cost allocation/forecasting. Trusted Advisor and Compute Optimizer are useful optimization inputs but do not replace budgeting and forecast governance.
tags: Optimization of compute utilization (for example, containers, serverless computing, microservices)
Instance types, families, and sizes (for example, memory optimized, compute optimized, virtualization)

stem: A platform team must enforce compute cost accountability. Any new EC2, Auto Scaling group, or ECS service must include CostCenter and Environment tags, or creation should fail. They also need monthly chargeback reporting by those tags. Which design BEST satisfies both control and reporting?

answers.A: Use AWS Config required-tags rules and auto-remediate missing tags with Lambda.
answers.B: Use SCPs that deny all compute actions unless principal tags are present.
answers.C: Use tag policies and IAM/SCP condition keys to deny untagged create actions, activate cost allocation tags, and report using Cost Explorer/CUR.
answers.D: Use CloudTrail Lake queries to find untagged resources and send weekly reports.

explanation: Prevention plus reporting is required. Deny-on-create controls with tag condition keys (in IAM/SCP patterns), reinforced by tag policy governance, prevent drift at creation time. Cost allocation tags with Cost Explorer/CUR provide chargeback reporting. Config or CloudTrail-only approaches are mostly detective and allow noncompliant creates before remediation.
tags: Scaling strategies (for example, auto scaling, hibernation)
AWS cost management service features (for example, cost allocation tags, multi-account billing)

stem: A high-throughput TCP gaming backend must expose static anycast IPs globally and handle millions of long-lived connections. The team is evaluating ALB, NLB, and GWLB, and wants the most cost-efficient service that still meets protocol and latency requirements. Which choice is MOST appropriate?

answers.A: Use ALB because L7 routing is cheaper for all connection types and supports static IPs natively.
answers.B: Use NLB because it supports L4 TCP at high scale with static IP/EIP support and lower overhead for this traffic profile.
answers.C: Use GWLB because it is optimized for distributing internet-facing application traffic directly to containers.
answers.D: Use ALB plus Global Accelerator because ALB is required for all long-lived TCP sessions.

explanation: For massive TCP workloads needing static IP semantics, NLB is the right fit and is typically more cost-effective than ALB for pure L4 forwarding at scale. ALB is L7 and does not natively provide the same static IP model. GWLB is for transparent appliance insertion, not general application load balancing.
tags: Determining an appropriate load balancing strategy (for example, Application Load Balancer [Layer 7] compared with Network Load Balancer [Layer 4] compared with Gateway Load Balancer)
AWS cost management service features (for example, cost allocation tags, multi-account billing)
Determining cost-effective AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Lambda, Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate)

stem: A workload runs continuously at 20-30% CPU on c6i.4xlarge instances, with memory utilization under 40%. Performance tests show c6i.2xlarge meets latency SLOs with 55% CPU at peak. Which action provides the BEST cost optimization with controlled risk?

answers.A: Keep the current size and purchase a 3-year Compute Savings Plan immediately.
answers.B: Switch to t3 instances because burst credits always lower cost for steady workloads.
answers.C: Move to Spot Instances only because interruption risk is negligible for all production traffic.
answers.D: Right-size to c6i.2xlarge in a phased rollout with CloudWatch alarms and rollback thresholds.

explanation: The data indicates systematic over-provisioning, and validated load tests show smaller instances still meet SLOs. Right-sizing with phased deployment and rollback controls is the best cost/risk tradeoff. Savings Plans optimize pricing but do not solve over-sizing. T-class and Spot-only choices introduce different performance/availability risks for a steady production profile.
tags: Optimization of compute utilization (for example, containers, serverless computing, microservices)
Determining the required availability for different classes of workloads (for example, production workloads, non-production workloads)

stem: A company stores sensitive files in Amazon S3 with server-side encryption and versioning enabled. During an audit, the security lead asks who is responsible for patching the underlying storage hardware, rotating application IAM access keys, and configuring bucket policies to block public access. Which answer correctly maps responsibilities under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?

answers.A: Customer is responsible for patching storage hardware; AWS is responsible for IAM key rotation and bucket policies.
answers.B: AWS is responsible for storage hardware patching; customer is responsible for IAM key rotation and S3 bucket policy/public access settings.
answers.C: AWS is responsible for all three because S3 is a fully managed service.
answers.D: Customer and AWS share equal responsibility for all three tasks.

explanation: For managed services like S3, AWS handles security of the cloud (infrastructure, physical hosts, foundational services). Customers handle security in the cloud, including IAM credential hygiene and resource policies such as bucket policies and public access controls.
tags: Determining the appropriate use of resource policies for AWS services

stem: A SaaS platform has synchronous checkout calls to a payment microservice. During downstream slowness, thread pools saturate and checkout availability drops across the stack. The team needs a resilience design that limits cascading failure and recovers automatically with minimal custom infrastructure. Which option BEST addresses this?

answers.A: Implement circuit breaker behavior with AWS App Mesh retries/timeouts and route asynchronous fallback events through SQS for deferred processing.
answers.B: Scale up checkout EC2 instances vertically to absorb downstream latency spikes.
answers.C: Increase client-side HTTP timeout from 2 seconds to 30 seconds to avoid early failures.
answers.D: Move payment and checkout into the same EC2 Auto Scaling group to reduce inter-service calls.

explanation: The failure mode is cascading dependency failure. Circuit breakers, bounded retries/timeouts, and asynchronous decoupling are core resilience patterns that isolate downstream faults and preserve availability. Vertical scaling and longer timeouts often worsen saturation. Co-locating services does not solve dependency failure semantics.
tags: AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions, Amazon Route 53)

stem: A manufacturing company must ingest 250 TB of historical data from an on-prem NFS environment, then continuously sync daily deltas (~4 TB/day) for analytics in S3. The WAN link cannot complete the initial transfer within the deadline. Which solution is MOST appropriate?

answers.A: Use AWS DataSync for both the initial load and deltas over the WAN link.
answers.B: Use AWS Transfer Family SFTP for historical load and deltas.
answers.C: Use AWS Snowball Edge for the bulk historical transfer, then use AWS DataSync for ongoing incremental synchronization.
answers.D: Use S3 Transfer Acceleration for historical load and AWS Glue jobs for deltas.

explanation: When network bandwidth cannot meet a large initial migration deadline, Snowball Edge is the best fit for bulk transfer. DataSync is then ideal for automated, recurring incremental sync. Transfer Family targets protocol-based file transfer use cases, not petabyte-scale seeding.
tags: Data transfer services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS DataSync, AWS Storage Gateway)
Data analytics and visualization services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon Athena, AWS Lake Formation, Amazon QuickSuite)

stem: A team ingests sensitive clickstream data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams from private subnets. They must avoid internet egress, enforce least-privilege producer permissions, and encrypt records with customer-managed keys. Which design is MOST secure and operationally efficient?

answers.A: Route producer traffic through a NAT gateway to the public Kinesis endpoint and use SSE-S3 encryption.
answers.B: Use an internet gateway, allow egress only to AWS IP ranges, and rely on default Kinesis encryption.
answers.C: Use VPC peering to a shared services VPC and publish with wildcard IAM permissions on all streams.
answers.D: Use an interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) for Kinesis, grant producers IAM permissions scoped to specific stream ARNs, and enable KMS CMK encryption on the stream.

explanation: PrivateLink removes internet egress dependency for Kinesis access from private subnets. Stream-level IAM scoping enforces least privilege, and CMK-backed encryption meets strict key-control requirements. NAT/internet-based options increase exposure and operational/cost overhead.
tags: Secure access to ingestion access points

stem: A company must migrate 120 TB of archived compliance files to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval at the lowest total cost. Most files are on-prem and disconnected from applications; no incremental sync is needed after migration. The site has only a 200 Mbps link and a 3-week deadline. Which option is MOST cost-effective and feasible?

answers.A: Use AWS DataSync continuously over the 200 Mbps link until all files are uploaded.
answers.B: Use AWS Snowball Edge for bulk transfer, then lifecycle objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
answers.C: Use AWS Transfer Family SFTP endpoints and ask teams to upload archives manually.
answers.D: Use S3 Transfer Acceleration from on-prem clients with multipart uploads.

explanation: The constrained bandwidth and deadline make network transfer impractical. Snowball Edge is designed for large offline bulk migration and minimizes transfer time risk. DataSync and Transfer Acceleration are network dependent; Transfer Family is not suited for this bulk archival migration model.
tags: Selecting the most cost-effective storage service for a workload

stem: A database platform team needs monthly chargeback for Amazon RDS, Aurora, and DynamoDB by business unit across 30 accounts. They also need queryable historical cost detail (resource IDs and usage types) for finance audits. Which approach BEST meets the requirement?

answers.A: Use CloudWatch billing alarms and export alarm history for audit evidence.
answers.B: Use only AWS Budgets per account and email monthly totals to finance.
answers.C: Activate cost allocation tags, enable CUR delivery to S3, and query CUR with Athena for database-specific chargeback and audit reporting.
answers.D: Use Trusted Advisor cost checks and manually map findings to business units.

explanation: The requirement needs granular, historical, queryable billing data by tagged ownership and resource attributes. CUR in S3 with Athena is the standard foundation for detailed finance analytics, while cost allocation tags enable business-unit chargeback. Budgets and alarms are useful for thresholds but lack detailed audit-grade queryability.

stem: A company is migrating from Oracle on-premises to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Management wants to minimize migration licensing and transformation cost while reducing cutover risk. Which DMS strategy is MOST cost-effective and appropriate?

answers.A: Use homogeneous migration tooling because both engines are relational and require no conversion.
answers.B: Use AWS DMS with AWS SCT for heterogeneous schema conversion and ongoing CDC until cutover.
answers.C: Export Oracle tables to CSV and bulk load manually into Aurora to avoid DMS costs.
answers.D: Replicate Oracle block storage with AWS DataSync and attach it directly to Aurora.

explanation: Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL is a heterogeneous migration, so schema and code conversion is needed. AWS SCT + DMS (with CDC) is typically the most controlled and cost-effective AWS-native path for minimizing downtime and migration risk. Homogeneous assumptions are incorrect, and manual CSV pipelines increase operational risk and transformation effort.

Finance wants to reduce compute spend by at least 40% without impacting availability. Which combination of purchasing options best achieves this?

answers.A: Purchase 40 Standard Reserved Instances (1-year, all-upfront) for web, 200 Scheduled Reserved Instances for batch, and On-Demand for dev/test.
answers.B: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan covering 40 instances for web and 200 instances for batch combined; use On-Demand for overflow and dev/test.

answers.D: Purchase 240 Standard Reserved Instances (3-year, no-upfront) to cover peak capacity for all tiers and use On-Demand when reservations are exhausted.

explanation: Compute Savings Plans provide the broadest flexibility across instance families and regions and should cover the predictable baseline. Spot Instances are ideal for fault-tolerant batch bursting and deliver up to 90% savings. Dev/test is unpredictable, so On-Demand or Spot avoids waste. stem: A solutions architect reviews AWS Cost Explorer and finds that 60% of monthly AWS spend is data transfer charges. Cross-AZ traffic accounts for the majority of the data transfer cost. Which combination of changes provides the greatest cost reduction?

answers.A: Enable cross-zone load balancing only at the NLB level if needed, add VPC Gateway Endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB, pin each AZ's EC2 instances to serve requests from the same AZ using AZ-aware routing, and use AWS Direct Connect for the on-premises data warehouse.
answers.B: Replace NLB with ALB (which has no cross-AZ charge), move S3 and DynamoDB to the same Region, and use a Site-to-Site VPN for on-premises transfer.
answers.C: Use CloudFront in front of the NLB to cache responses and reduce origin hits, add S3 Transfer Acceleration to reduce upload cost, and compress report files before sending on-premises.
answers.D: Consolidate all EC2 instances into a single AZ to eliminate cross-AZ charges and use a NAT Gateway in that AZ for on-premises connectivity.

explanation: Cross-AZ charges dominate; AZ-aware routing avoids unnecessary cross-AZ hops. VPC Gateway Endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB eliminate data processing charges through NAT and inter-AZ paths. Direct Connect reduces per-GB on-premises transfer cost vs. internet. ALB also incurs cross-AZ charges; VPN doesn't reduce per-GB cost significantly. stem: An enterprise operates 80 AWS accounts under AWS Organizations. The security team mandates that all S3 buckets must have server-side encryption enabled and public access blocked, all EC2 instances must belong to approved AMIs, and all non-compliant resources must trigger automated remediation within 15 minutes. They want centralized visibility and minimal per-account configuration. What is the MOST operationally efficient approach?

answers.A: Deploy individual AWS Config rules in each account using CloudFormation StackSets, aggregate findings in a central S3 bucket via a Lambda function, and configure SNS notifications for non-compliance.
answers.B: Enable AWS Config with a delegated administrator account, deploy an Organization-level Conformance Pack containing the required managed rules and automatic remediation SSM Automation documents, and use the Config Aggregator to view compliance centrally.
answers.C: Use AWS Security Hub with CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark across all accounts, configure EventBridge rules to trigger Lambda for remediation, and store findings in a central Security Hub master account.
answers.D: Write custom AWS Lambda functions in each account to evaluate resource configuration on a schedule, publish results to Amazon CloudWatch, and use CloudWatch Alarms for out-of-compliance notifications.

explanation: Organization-level Conformance Packs deploy managed Config rules and remediation actions to all accounts simultaneously from a delegated administrator, providing centralized governance with minimal per-account work. Config Aggregators provide cross-account visibility. Security Hub provides findings but doesn't natively enforce Config-rule-based remediation at org level; individual rule deployment via StackSets requires more per-account management.

stem: A company is decomposing a monolith into microservices on Amazon ECS. One downstream payment service is intermittently slow (p99 latency spikes to 30 seconds), causing upstream services to exhaust their thread pools and cascade-fail across the entire system. The team wants to implement a circuit-breaker pattern with automatic recovery, without modifying application code. Which solution achieves this?

answers.A: Deploy AWS App Mesh with an Envoy sidecar proxy for each ECS task. Configure an Envoy circuit-breaker policy with outlier detection (consecutive 5xx errors) and a retry policy with exponential backoff on the virtual service for the payment service.
answers.B: Place an Application Load Balancer in front of the payment service and configure ALB target group health checks with a threshold of 2 consecutive failures; unhealthy targets are removed and the upstream receives 502 errors.
answers.C: Use Amazon API Gateway with a usage plan and throttling limits to cap requests to the payment service; when limits are exceeded, API Gateway returns 429 errors to prevent cascade failures.
answers.D: Implement AWS Step Functions with a Wait state and retry logic to orchestrate calls to the payment service with exponential backoff at the workflow orchestration layer.

explanation: App Mesh with Envoy sidecars implements the circuit-breaker pattern transparently at the proxy layer—no application code changes needed. Envoy's outlier detection ejects unhealthy endpoints and its circuit-breaker limits pending requests. ALB health checks remove instances but don't implement circuit-breaker semantics (open/half-open/closed). API Gateway throttling protects the gateway, not the inter-service call path. Step Functions adds workflow orchestration but requires application-level changes.
