stem: A company evaluates three workloads for compute selection: (A) a web scraping job that processes 10,000 URLs/day, each taking 30-120 seconds and requiring 2 GB RAM and a headless browser (250 MB binary); (B) a real-time image thumbnail generator triggered by S3 uploads, each invocation takes < 3 seconds and uses < 512 MB RAM; (C) a 24/7 TCP socket server handling 50,000 persistent WebSocket connections with state in memory. Which compute service best fits each workload?

answers.A: Lambda for all three: Lambda supports 15-minute timeouts, up to 10 GB RAM, and container images up to 10 GB for the scraper. Lambda scales to 50,000 concurrent connections with provisioned concurrency.
answers.B: Fargate for web scraping (container with browser), Lambda for thumbnails, and EC2 for the WebSocket server.
answers.C: EC2 for all three: consistent pricing is better than per-invocation costs at high volume, and EC2 supports all three workload types.
answers.D: Fargate for web scraping (long-running tasks, large binary, variable duration fits container model well); Lambda for thumbnail generation (short-duration, event-driven, low memory); EC2 or ECS Fargate with a load balancer for WebSocket server (persistent connections, stateful, 24/7 operation).

explanation: Web scraping with 30-120 second duration fits Lambda (within 15-min limit) but the 250 MB headless browser binary and 2 GB RAM make a container (Fargate) more practical and portable. Lambda thumbnails are a textbook use case: event-driven, short, lightweight. The WebSocket server requires persistent connections and stateful in-memory data—Lambda is stateless and doesn't maintain persistent TCP connections; EC2 or ECS (long-running container) is appropriate. Fargate can also serve WebSockets when fronted by ALB/NLB with stickiness.

stem: A company needs to build an order processing workflow: validate order → charge payment (external API, can take up to 5 minutes) → update inventory → send confirmation email → archive order. If payment fails, the order must be cancelled and the customer notified. If inventory update fails after payment, the payment must be reversed. The workflow must be auditable (full execution history). Which orchestration approach is most appropriate?

answers.A: Chain Lambda functions: each Lambda invokes the next step synchronously. Use DynamoDB to track workflow state. Each Lambda implements retry and compensation logic. Use CloudWatch Logs for audit trail.
answers.B: Use AWS Step Functions Standard Workflow with Task states for each step. Implement Catch blocks for payment and inventory failures with compensating transactions (cancel/reverse payment). Step Functions natively maintains full execution history for auditability, supports waits for async operations (payment callback), and handles retries with exponential backoff.
answers.C: Use Amazon SQS queues between each step. Each step's Lambda consumes from a queue, processes, and enqueues the next step. Use DLQs for failures and a separate compensation SQS queue for rollback.
answers.D: Use AWS EventBridge to choreograph the workflow. Each service publishes events on completion/failure. Subscribe services to relevant events. Store event history in EventBridge Archive for auditability.

explanation: Step Functions Standard Workflows are designed for long-running, auditable business processes with complex branching, error handling, and compensation. The 5-minute payment step fits within Standard Workflow's 1-year maximum execution time (unlike Express Workflows). Catch/compensate patterns are native. Full execution history is built-in. Lambda chaining (A) creates tight coupling and difficult error handling. SQS-based choreography (C) distributes state across queues making compensation complex. EventBridge choreography (D) lacks native compensation flow and execution history.

stem: A company wants to build a visualization solution for two audiences: (1) Business analysts who need interactive dashboards with drill-down capabilities on aggregated sales data (100 GB in Redshift), updated daily; (2) Security operations team who need real-time log search and dashboards on VPC Flow Logs and CloudTrail (1 TB/day streaming from Kinesis). Which services best serve each audience?

answers.A: Amazon QuickSight with SPICE for the business analysts (Redshift data imported to SPICE for fast interactive queries, daily refresh schedule). Amazon OpenSearch Service with OpenSearch Dashboards for the security team (Kinesis Data Firehose delivers logs to OpenSearch in near-real-time; OpenSearch Dashboards provides log search, time-series visualization, and anomaly detection).
answers.B: Amazon QuickSight for both audiences. Configure QuickSight with Kinesis as a data source for the security team's real-time logs and Redshift for business analysts.
answers.C: Amazon OpenSearch Service for both audiences. Use Redshift Spectrum to query Redshift data in OpenSearch Dashboards. Configure log ingestion for the security team via Kinesis.
answers.D: Amazon Managed Grafana for both audiences. Connect Grafana to Redshift using the Amazon Redshift data source plugin and to OpenSearch for security logs.

explanation: QuickSight with SPICE is purpose-built for business intelligence with pre-built chart types, ad hoc exploration, and scheduled refreshes—ideal for daily sales reporting. OpenSearch Dashboards (formerly Kibana) is purpose-built for log analytics, near-real-time search, and security monitoring with Kinesis Firehose integration—ideal for the SOC. QuickSight cannot ingest Kinesis streams in real time (B). OpenSearch doesn't natively query Redshift (C). Managed Grafana works for both but requires more configuration and is better suited for metrics/operational data than business BI (D).
tags: Determine high-performing data ingestion and transformation solutions
Data analytics and visualization services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon Athena, AWS Lake Formation, Amazon QuickSuite)
Streaming data services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon Kinesis)

stem: A SaaS company wants to embed Amazon QuickSight dashboards in their customer-facing web application. Customers must see only their own data, and the embedding must work without customers having QuickSight accounts. The application authenticates customers via Amazon Cognito User Pools. Dashboard load time must be under 2 seconds. Which embedding approach is correct?

answers.A: Use QuickSight's public embedding feature. Generate a public embed URL for each dashboard. Control data visibility using URL parameters passed to QuickSight.
answers.B: Create one QuickSight user per customer using the QuickSight CreateUser API during customer registration. Use GenerateEmbedUrlForRegisteredUser to generate per-customer embed URLs. Apply Row-Level Security using a dataset with user-to-data mappings.
answers.C: Use QuickSight anonymous embedding (no QuickSight user accounts needed). From your application backend, call GenerateEmbedUrlForAnonymousUser using a Cognito-authenticated backend call. Pass the customer's identifier as a session tag. Configure RLS on the dataset using ${sessionTag:customerId}. Import datasets into SPICE for sub-2-second load times.
answers.D: Use QuickSight Namespaces—create one namespace per customer. In each namespace, create one user and assign permissions to the relevant dataset filtered by customer ID. Generate namespace-scoped embed URLs.

explanation: Anonymous embedding with session tags is purpose-built for SaaS multi-tenancy: no QuickSight user accounts per customer, tenant isolation via session-tag-based RLS, and the backend generates embed URLs using Cognito credentials. SPICE import ensures fast load times. Public embedding (A) has no authentication and allows URL parameter tampering. Per-user accounts (B) require managing potentially thousands of QuickSight users. Namespaces (D) provide isolation but still require user provisioning per customer.
tags: Security services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Cognito, AWS GuardDuty, AWS Macie)
Integrating AWS services to secure applications (for example, AWS Shield, AWS WAF, IAM Identity Center, AWS Secrets Manager)

stem: A company evaluates streaming ingestion services for a new analytics platform. Requirement A: Ingest 50 MB/s of clickstream data from a web application, process with Lambda, load results to S3 and Redshift, require managed scaling with no broker management. Requirement B: Ingest 500 MB/s of financial transactions from 200 microservices, each consuming the same stream independently with different consumer groups, with message retention up to 7 days and support for exactly-once semantics. Which services fit each requirement?

answers.A: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for A (managed, Lambda integration, direct S3 and Redshift delivery). Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Enhanced Fan-Out for B (multiple independent consumers, configurable retention).
answers.B: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose for A (fully managed, auto-scales, native S3 and Redshift delivery, no consumer group management needed). Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka) for B (Kafka's consumer group model supports 200+ independent consumers, 7-day retention, and exactly-once semantics via Kafka transactions).
answers.C: Amazon SQS for A (managed, Lambda integration). Amazon MSK for B (Kafka consumer groups, retention, exactly-once).
answers.D: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose for both. Firehose supports multiple destinations and can fanout to multiple S3 prefixes for independent consumers.

explanation: Kinesis Firehose is fully managed (no shard management), auto-scales, and has native S3/Redshift delivery—perfect for Requirement A. Kafka (MSK) is ideal for Requirement B: consumer groups allow each of 200 microservices to maintain independent offsets, 7-day retention is configurable, and Kafka transactions provide exactly-once semantics. Kinesis with Enhanced Fan-Out (A) supports multiple consumers but has a 7-day max retention and doesn't match Kafka's consumer group model at 200 consumers. SQS (C) is a message queue, not a streaming platform with replay and consumer groups.
tags: Determine high-performing data ingestion and transformation solutions
Streaming data services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon Kinesis)
Queuing and messaging concepts (for example, publish/subscribe)
Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK)

stem: A company needs to ingest data from two sources: (1) A third-party partner uploads daily CSV files via SFTP from their on-premises system; (2) The company's own data center generates 10 TB of log files nightly that must be transferred to S3 for analytics. Which AWS ingestion services are most appropriate for each source?

answers.A: AWS Transfer Family (SFTP endpoint backed by S3) for the third-party partner SFTP uploads—partners use existing SFTP clients, files land directly in S3. AWS DataSync with an on-premises agent for the nightly log transfer—DataSync optimizes transfer performance, handles file checksums, and can schedule recurring transfers.
answers.B: AWS DataSync for both: deploy an on-premises DataSync agent, configure it to accept SFTP connections from the partner, and schedule nightly log transfers.
answers.C: AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway for both: partners mount the file share via NFS/SMB, and the on-premises data center uses the same gateway for log uploads.
answers.D: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose for log ingestion (streaming) and S3 pre-signed URLs shared with the partner for CSV uploads. No SFTP support needed if partners switch to HTTPS.

explanation: AWS Transfer Family provides fully managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP endpoints that write directly to S3, allowing third-party partners to use their existing SFTP tools without change. AWS DataSync is purpose-built for high-performance, scheduled bulk file transfer from on-premises to AWS, with an agent installed on-premises to optimize 10 TB nightly transfers. DataSync doesn't accept inbound SFTP connections (B). Storage Gateway is for hybrid storage (NFS/SMB access to S3), not SFTP and not optimized for bulk nightly transfers (C). Kinesis Firehose is for streaming data, not file-based transfer, and requiring partners to change from SFTP is disruptive (D).
tags: Determine high-performing data ingestion and transformation solutions
Data transfer services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS DataSync, AWS Storage Gateway)

stem: A genomics research company uploads large sequencing files (average 50 GB, maximum 500 GB) to S3. Uploads currently fail intermittently for large files due to network instability, requiring complete restarts. The team wants to: (1) maximize upload resilience and resume failed uploads; (2) reduce time-to-upload for 500 GB files; (3) minimize S3 storage costs during the upload process. Which upload strategy achieves all three objectives?

answers.A: Use S3 Transfer Acceleration to reduce upload latency by routing through CloudFront edge locations. Use single-part uploads with retry logic in the application.
answers.B: Use S3 Multipart Upload: split files into 100-500 MB parts, upload parts in parallel (using multiple threads), and retry only failed parts on interruption. Set an S3 lifecycle rule to abort incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days to avoid storage charges for partial uploads.
answers.C: Use AWS DataSync with an on-premises agent to handle the uploads. DataSync automatically handles multipart upload, retries, and verification checksums.
answers.D: Use S3 Batch Operations to upload files in batch mode, which provides automatic retry and parallel upload capabilities.

explanation: S3 Multipart Upload splits large objects into parts that upload independently and in parallel, dramatically reducing upload time and allowing resume of failed parts without restarting the entire upload. The lifecycle rule for aborting incomplete multipart uploads prevents orphaned parts from accumulating storage costs. Transfer Acceleration (A) reduces latency but doesn't address resilience for large files with single-part uploads. DataSync (C) is for bulk transfer from NFS/SMB storage, not for application-level S3 uploads from a client. S3 Batch Operations (D) processes existing S3 objects, not new uploads.
tags: Determine high-performing and/or scalable storage solutions
Storage services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS)
Implementing strategies to ensure the durability and availability of data (for example, backups)

stem: An IoT platform receives telemetry from 100,000 devices. Each device sends 1 KB sensor readings every 10 seconds. The readings must be stored in S3 for long-term analytics with Athena. Storing each reading as an individual S3 object results in 10,000 S3 PUT requests per second and S3 storage costs dominated by per-object overhead (minimum 128 KB billing size). Which architecture reduces cost and improves query performance?

answers.A: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically reduce storage costs. The per-object overhead is managed by S3 Intelligent-Tiering's monitoring fee optimization.
answers.B: Use Amazon DynamoDB to store individual readings in real time. Configure DynamoDB export to S3 weekly for Athena analytics.
answers.C: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to buffer device telemetry (via Kinesis Data Streams or direct PUT). Configure Firehose to batch records by 5-minute time window or 128 MB size, convert to Parquet with GZIP compression, and partition by device_type/date in S3. Athena queries the columnar, partitioned Parquet files efficiently.
answers.D: Use S3 Object Lambda to aggregate individual small objects into larger compound objects when Athena queries them. Individual PUTs remain but query cost is reduced.

explanation: Batching 1 KB readings into time-windowed, Parquet-compressed files via Firehose solves both problems: S3 PUT requests drop from 10,000/sec to a few per minute (reducing API cost and per-object overhead), and columnar Parquet with partitioning dramatically improves Athena query performance and reduces per-query cost. S3 Intelligent-Tiering (A) manages access-tier costs but doesn't address per-object overhead or query efficiency. DynamoDB (B) adds cost and weekly export creates stale data. S3 Object Lambda (D) applies transformations at read time and doesn't reduce the write-time per-object cost.
tags: Determine high-performing data ingestion and transformation solutions

stem: A company runs a multi-tier application using EC2 (with EBS), RDS Aurora, EFS, and DynamoDB across 3 accounts under Organizations. Compliance requires: daily backups with 35-day retention, cross-account backup copies, and immutable backup vaults (no deletion for 7 years). Which backup strategy achieves all requirements with the least operational overhead?

answers.A: Create native snapshots for EBS, RDS, and DynamoDB using CloudWatch Events scheduled rules in each account. Use S3 lifecycle policies for EFS backup data. Manually copy snapshots cross-account via AWS CLI scripts.
answers.B: Use AWS Backup with a backup plan defining daily backups and 35-day retention. Configure cross-Region copy. Enable AWS Backup Audit Manager for compliance monitoring.
answers.C: Use AWS Backup with Organizations integration (delegated administrator). Create a backup policy applied at the organization root. Configure daily backup rules with 35-day retention for all supported resource types (EC2, RDS, EFS, DynamoDB). Add a copy rule to a central backup account's vault. Enable Backup Vault Lock (Compliance mode) with a 7-year minimum retention period on the destination vault.
answers.D: Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM) for EBS and RDS snapshots. Use AWS Backup for EFS and DynamoDB. Configure cross-account snapshot sharing via KMS key policies and snapshot sharing APIs.

explanation: AWS Backup with Organizations support applies a single backup policy across all accounts. Backup Vault Lock in Compliance mode creates WORM (write once, read many) immutable vaults that cannot be deleted even by root—meeting the 7-year immutability requirement. Cross-account copies to a central vault fulfill the cross-account requirement. All specified services (EC2, RDS Aurora, EFS, DynamoDB) are supported natively. Native snapshots + CLI (A) require custom code and don't provide Vault Lock. Option B lacks cross-account support and Vault Lock. DLM+Backup mix (D) adds complexity and lacks centralized governance.

stem: A company archives three types of data to Amazon S3 Glacier: (1) Medical records that must be retrieved within 1 hour when requested (rare, ~10 retrievals/year per 1 million records); (2) Financial audit logs that regulators may request within 24 hours (very rare, 1-2 requests/year); (3) Raw video footage that is almost never accessed but must be retained for 10 years (0-1 retrieval/decade). Which S3 Glacier storage classes are most cost-effective for each type?

answers.A: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval for medical records (millisecond retrieval, highest storage cost among Glacier tiers); S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval for audit logs (Standard retrieval: 3-5 hours, or Expedited: 1-5 minutes—within 24 hours; lower storage cost); S3 Glacier Deep Archive for video footage (12-48 hour retrieval, lowest storage cost).
answers.B: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval for all three: Standard retrieval (3-5 hours) satisfies all requirements. One storage class simplifies management.
answers.C: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval for all three: all data can be retrieved within 1 hour, and the cost difference is minimal compared to retrieval flexibility.
answers.D: S3 Glacier Deep Archive for medical records and audit logs (cost priority), S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval for video footage (it's never accessed so retrieval speed doesn't matter).

explanation: Glacier Instant Retrieval (millisecond access) fits medical records' 1-hour SLA requirement and is the only Glacier tier supporting it natively. Glacier Flexible Retrieval's Expedited or Standard tiers satisfy audit logs' 24-hour requirement at lower storage cost. Glacier Deep Archive's 12-48 hour retrieval is acceptable for video footage with decade-scale access and minimizes the storage cost for 10 years. Using one class for all (B) pays for instant retrieval when it's not needed. All Instant Retrieval (C) is unnecessarily expensive for rarely-accessed data. Deep Archive for medical records (D) violates the 1-hour RTO.

stem: An e-commerce platform uses EC2 Auto Scaling for its web tier. Traffic patterns show: a gradual increase from 6 AM to noon, a relatively stable high-traffic period from noon to 8 PM, and a sharp predictable spike at 8 PM (flash sale) lasting 30 minutes. After the spike, traffic drops sharply. The current scaling policy (simple scaling with CloudWatch alarms) causes over-provisioning during gradual ramp-up and under-provisioning at the start of the flash sale spike. Which combination of scaling policies optimizes this workload?

answers.A: Use target tracking scaling (CPU at 60%) for all scenarios. The target tracking policy continuously adjusts capacity to maintain the target, handling both gradual ramp-up and the flash sale spike.
answers.B: Use predictive scaling with CPU utilization metric for the gradual ramp-up and afternoon steady state. Use a simple scaling policy with a large step size for the flash sale spike.
answers.C: Use a combination: target tracking scaling (CPU at 60%) for the gradual ramp-up and steady state periods. Add a scheduled scaling action to pre-scale to peak flash sale capacity at 7:50 PM (10 minutes before the spike). After the sale, the target tracking policy gradually scales in as CPU drops.
answers.D: Use step scaling with small step sizes for the gradual ramp-up and large step sizes for the spike. Configure three separate step scaling alarms with different thresholds for different time periods.

explanation: Target tracking handles gradual, continuous load changes efficiently. Scheduled scaling solves the predictable flash sale spike by pre-provisioning capacity before the spike hits (since reactive scaling has a lag of several minutes, causing under-provisioning at spike onset). Combined, these handle all three traffic patterns. Target tracking alone (A) cannot pre-provision for known spikes; scaling lag causes under-provisioning at spike start. Predictive + simple (B) adds complexity; simple scaling has cooldown delays. Step scaling (D) is complex to tune across multiple time periods and still suffers from reactive lag at spike onset.

stem: A data processing application runs long-running computations on EC2 instances (m5.4xlarge). Each job takes 6-8 hours and maintains large in-memory datasets (60 GB). Jobs run during business hours. To reduce costs, the operations team wants to stop instances when jobs aren't running but cannot afford the time to rebuild in-memory state (takes 2 hours) when instances restart. Which EC2 feature addresses this requirement, and what constraints must be considered?

answers.A: Use EC2 Auto Scaling with lifecycle hooks to save in-memory state to S3 before termination and restore on startup. This recreates the in-memory state automatically without requiring EC2 Hibernation.
answers.B: Use EC2 Hibernation. When hibernated, the instance's RAM contents are saved to an encrypted EBS root volume. On restart, RAM state is restored, avoiding the 2-hour rebuild. Constraints: the EBS root volume must be large enough for RAM (60 GB+) and encrypted; the instance must be an On-Demand or Reserved Instance (not Spot for all scenarios); hibernation must be enabled at launch time.
answers.C: Use EC2 instance store-backed instances. Stop the instance to pause billing; instance store preserves data between stop/start cycles.
answers.D: Use AWS Lambda with a 15-minute maximum execution time. Split the computation into 15-minute chunks using DynamoDB to checkpoint state between invocations.

explanation: EC2 Hibernation saves RAM to the encrypted EBS root volume on hibernate and restores it on start, preserving in-memory state. This avoids the 2-hour rebuild. Key constraints: hibernation must be configured at launch, root EBS must be encrypted and large enough for RAM contents, supported on specific instance families (m5 is supported), and only for On-Demand/Reserved instances (Spot hibernation support is limited). Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks (A) require the application to implement state serialization/deserialization—the customer specifically cannot afford rebuild time. Instance store (C) does NOT persist between stop/start (it's cleared on stop). Lambda (D) doesn't support 6-8 hour jobs.

stem: A company currently uses a single 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection for all hybrid traffic. Peak utilization consistently hits 95%, causing latency spikes. The company needs to increase bandwidth to 5 Gbps while also requiring the connection to remain available if a single physical link fails. Which Direct Connect configuration meets both requirements at the lowest cost?

answers.A: Provision a single 10 Gbps Direct Connect dedicated connection. This provides headroom above the 5 Gbps requirement and a single physical connection at lower cost than multiple connections.
answers.B: Add four additional 1 Gbps Direct Connect connections (total 5 x 1 Gbps = 5 Gbps). Configure each independently with separate BGP sessions. If one fails, the remaining four maintain 4 Gbps.
answers.C: Create a Link Aggregation Group (LAG) with multiple Direct Connect connections of the same speed. A LAG bundles connections into a single logical connection with LACP. If configured with a minimum links setting that allows one link failure, the LAG continues operating at reduced capacity. Calculate the number of connections needed to achieve 5 Gbps+ with one link failed.
answers.D: Use AWS Transit Gateway with two separate Direct Connect Gateways and two 1 Gbps connections each. Configure Equal-Cost Multipath (ECMP) on the Transit Gateway to aggregate bandwidth to 4 Gbps total.

explanation: A Direct Connect LAG bundles multiple connections of the same speed into a single logical connection, aggregating bandwidth (LACP/802.3ad). Setting the minimum links parameter allows the LAG to continue if one link fails. For 5 Gbps with one-link-failure resilience: 3 x 2 Gbps LAG = 6 Gbps (5 Gbps with one link down) or 6 x 1 Gbps LAG = 6 Gbps (5 Gbps with one down). A single 10 Gbps connection (A) has no resilience to physical failure. Independent connections (B) work but lack LACP bonding and don't form a LAG. TGW ECMP (D) requires VPN or individual VIFs per connection and is for VPN, not Direct Connect aggregation.

stem: A company uses a single AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection (two tunnels) for on-premises connectivity. Maximum VPN throughput per tunnel is 1.25 Gbps. Peak traffic reaches 2.8 Gbps, causing packet drops. The company cannot deploy Direct Connect due to budget constraints. They need to increase effective VPN throughput to at least 3 Gbps with redundancy. Which configuration achieves this?

answers.A: Enable VPN acceleration (AWS Global Accelerator) on the existing VPN connection to increase throughput beyond 1.25 Gbps per tunnel.
answers.B: Attach multiple Site-to-Site VPN connections (each with 2 tunnels at 1.25 Gbps each) to an AWS Transit Gateway. Enable ECMP (Equal-Cost Multipath routing) on the Transit Gateway. With 3 VPN connections and ECMP, BGP advertises the same route over all tunnels and the on-premises router distributes traffic, achieving ~7.5 Gbps aggregate throughput (6 tunnels x 1.25 Gbps).
answers.C: Upgrade to a VPN connection with higher throughput. AWS offers 10 Gbps Site-to-Site VPN connections as a premium option.
answers.D: Use AWS CloudHub to connect multiple VPN connections to a Virtual Private Gateway. CloudHub automatically load-balances traffic across all connected VPN tunnels.

explanation: AWS Transit Gateway with ECMP allows multiple VPN connections to be attached, with traffic distributed across all active tunnels using ECMP routing. Each VPN connection provides 2 tunnels at 1.25 Gbps each; with ECMP enabled and BGP configured, on-premises routers distribute load across all tunnels. This is the documented method to exceed the single VPN 1.25 Gbps limit. Global Accelerator (A) doesn't increase VPN tunnel throughput. AWS doesn't offer higher-throughput VPN connections beyond the 1.25 Gbps per tunnel limit (C). CloudHub (D) connects branch offices (hub-and-spoke VPNs), not for throughput aggregation to a single on-premises site.

stem: A solutions architect is auditing a three-tier VPC design. Match each behavioral statement to the VPC security component it BEST describes. Each component is used once.

answers.A: Security Group
answers.B: Network ACL (NACL)
answers.C: Route Table

subquestions.prompt: Operates at the subnet boundary, evaluates rules in ascending numeric order (first match applies), and supports explicit DENY rules — enabling a blanket block of a specific IP range before any ALLOW rule can match it.
Is stateful: once an inbound connection passes the inbound rule, all corresponding return traffic is automatically allowed without requiring a matching outbound rule.

Associates destination CIDR blocks with specific targets (internet gateway, NAT gateway, transit gateway attachment) and determines how packets exiting a subnet are forwarded toward their destination.

Rules are evaluated simultaneously (no ordering), only ALLOW rules exist, and another instance of the same resource type can be cited as a source/destination — enabling dynamic group-based access within a VPC.

explanation: NACLs are stateless and subnet-level: numbered rules are evaluated in order; the first match wins; both ALLOW and DENY are supported — making them the right tool for explicit IP-range blocks. Security Groups are stateful and ENI-level: they track connection state so return traffic is implicitly allowed; rules are evaluated simultaneously (all rules, not first-match); only ALLOW is supported; and other security group IDs can be used as sources/destinations. Route Tables control packet forwarding out of a subnet by mapping destination CIDRs to gateway targets.

stem: An enterprise must establish a private 10 Gbps connection from its on-premises data center to six Amazon VPCs spread across three AWS Regions. The connection must never traverse the public internet, and ALL six VPCs must be reachable over a SINGLE physical AWS port simultaneously. Which TWO services are REQUIRED to satisfy these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: AWS Direct Connect with a dedicated connection (10 Gbps port speed)
answers.B: AWS Site-to-Site VPN with BGP routing configured on a Virtual Private Gateway
answers.C: AWS Direct Connect Gateway associated with a Virtual Private Gateway in each target VPC
answers.D: AWS Transit Gateway deployed in each Region with an SD-WAN attachment for on-premises routing
answers.E: AWS PrivateLink endpoint services created in each VPC for private IP access

explanation: A Direct Connect dedicated connection (1, 10, or 100 Gbps) provides the private physical circuit between on-premises and AWS without traversing the internet. A Direct Connect Gateway enables a single Direct Connect connection to reach VPCs in multiple AWS Regions simultaneously through their associated Virtual Private Gateways — eliminating the need for separate connections per Region. Site-to-Site VPN travels over the public internet and offers at most 1.25 Gbps per tunnel. PrivateLink exposes specific services, not general VPC connectivity. Transit Gateway adds flexibility but is not strictly required to meet the stated requirements and adds cost.

answers.A: gp3 (General Purpose SSD)

answers.C: st1 (Throughput Optimized HDD)
answers.D: sc1 (Cold HDD)

subquestions.prompt: A SAP HANA in-memory database requiring 64,000 IOPS, sub-millisecond latency, 99.999% durability, and the ability to provision IOPS completely independently of volume size up to 256,000 IOPS.

An application server boot volume (200 GiB) that needs a consistent 4,000 IOPS baseline. The team wants to set IOPS independently of size to avoid over-provisioning while keeping the lowest-cost SSD tier.
A Hadoop cluster performing large sequential reads of multi-hundred-GiB log files daily. Throughput of up to 500 MiB/s is needed; random IOPS requirements are minimal.
A compliance archive storing 50 TB of audit logs accessed fewer than twice per year. The lowest per-GB monthly block-storage cost is the primary requirement; retrieval latency is not a concern.

explanation: io2 Block Express supports up to 256,000 IOPS, 4,000 MiB/s throughput, sub-millisecond latency, and 99.999% durability — the only EBS type suitable for mission-critical databases like SAP HANA. gp3 lets you configure IOPS (up to 16,000) and throughput independently of volume size, making it cost-effective for general workloads without gp2's implicit IOPS-per-GiB coupling. st1 is a Throughput Optimized HDD designed for frequently accessed sequential workloads (Hadoop, ETL) with up to 500 MiB/s — cost-effective for big sequential reads. sc1 (Cold HDD) offers the lowest per-GB EBS price and suits infrequently accessed sequential data where throughput can be as low as 80–250 MiB/s.

stem: A company is architecting a three-tier e-commerce application. The web tier must absorb sudden traffic spikes without dropping requests. The application tier performs variable-duration order-processing tasks and must scale independently of the web tier. The database tier must survive an Availability Zone failure with automatic failover and no data loss. Which TWO design choices BEST address ALL three requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Front the web tier with an Application Load Balancer; configure the application tier to poll ALB access logs stored in S3 to determine current load and scale accordingly
answers.B: Insert Amazon SQS between the web and application tiers so the web tier enqueues order requests and the application tier polls the queue, enabling each tier to scale and fail independently
answers.C: Deploy the application tier as a single xl instance type to reduce inter-tier networking and eliminate the need for a queue by processing requests faster
answers.D: Deploy Amazon RDS for MySQL with Multi-AZ enabled; the synchronous standby in a second AZ promotes automatically within 60–120 seconds if the primary fails
answers.E: Deploy cross-AZ Amazon RDS Read Replicas and configure the application to promote a read replica to primary manually when the primary instance becomes unavailable

explanation: SQS durably buffers requests between tiers: the web tier enqueues at any rate, the application tier polls at its own pace, and no requests are dropped during spikes — this is the canonical AWS loose-coupling pattern for multi-tier architectures. RDS Multi-AZ uses synchronous replication to a standby replica in a different AZ; AWS orchestrates automatic failover with no manual intervention, and the synchronous replication ensures zero data loss. Polling ALB access logs from S3 introduces unacceptable lag (logs are delivered every 5 minutes). A single large instance is a single point of failure and cannot scale elastically. Read Replicas use asynchronous replication (possible data loss) and require manual promotion — they do not provide automatic failover.

answers.A: Amazon Neptune

An IoT fleet platform currently runs Apache Cassandra on-premises with wide-column tables and CQL-based queries. The team wants a fully managed cloud migration with minimal application code changes.

A mobile gaming leaderboard needs guaranteed single-digit millisecond latency at millions of reads per second, a serverless On-Demand capacity mode to eliminate capacity planning, and multi-region active-active replication via Global Tables.

explanation: Neptune is AWS's managed graph database (Gremlin and SPARQL), optimised for traversing dense relationship networks — the correct choice for fraud detection graph queries. Keyspaces is a serverless Cassandra-compatible service: CQL queries work unchanged, enabling lift-and-shift migrations. DocumentDB provides MongoDB wire-protocol compatibility with ACID transactions and rich aggregation support — ideal for MongoDB migrations. DynamoDB delivers guaranteed single-digit millisecond performance at any scale, a serverless On-Demand mode, and Global Tables for multi-region active-active replication.

stem: A team is troubleshooting intermittent latency spikes in a distributed application spanning Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and containerized microservices on Amazon ECS. They need end-to-end request traces, service dependency maps, and the ability to pinpoint which downstream component is responsible for the added latency. Which TWO actions should the solutions architect take to enable this capability? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Enable X-Ray active tracing on the API Gateway stage and set the Lambda function tracing mode to Active so that X-Ray captures traces for every invocation
answers.B: Create a CloudWatch dashboard with p99 latency metrics from API Gateway, Lambda, and ECS to identify the slowest service tier in aggregate
answers.C: Add the X-Ray daemon as a sidecar container in each ECS task definition and instrument the application code with the X-Ray SDK to emit subsegments for each downstream service call
answers.D: Enable AWS CloudTrail data event logging for Lambda invocations and use Amazon Athena to parse trace IDs from CloudTrail logs and reconstruct call chains
answers.E: Configure Amazon CloudWatch Contributor Insights on Lambda logs to rank function invocations by duration and correlate high-duration entries across services by request ID

explanation: Enabling X-Ray active tracing on API Gateway propagates the trace header downstream; setting Lambda tracing mode to Active records traces for every invocation automatically. For ECS, the X-Ray daemon must run as a sidecar container (sharing the task's network namespace on UDP port 2000) to receive trace segments emitted by the X-Ray SDK in application code — producing the subsegments and annotations needed for per-request service maps and latency breakdowns. CloudWatch metrics show aggregate percentiles but not per-request causality across service boundaries. CloudTrail records API call metadata, not performance traces. Contributor Insights ranks log entries but cannot stitch cross-service call chains into a dependency map.

stem: A business-continuity team must assign a disaster recovery strategy to each application based on recovery objectives and budget. Match each application profile to the DR strategy that meets its RTO/RPO at the LOWEST cost. Each strategy is used once.

answers.A: Backup and Restore
answers.B: Pilot Light
answers.C: Warm Standby
answers.D: Multi-site Active-Active

subquestions.prompt: An internal reporting tool with an RTO of 48 hours and RPO of 24 hours. Nightly database snapshots and AMIs are copied to a secondary Region; no infrastructure runs there normally.
A customer-facing REST API with RTO of 4 hours and RPO of 1 hour. The production database replicates continuously to a DR Region, but no application servers are running there.

An order-management system with RTO of 15 minutes and RPO of 5 minutes. A scaled-down but fully operational environment (25% of production capacity) runs continuously in a DR Region and can be rapidly scaled out on failover.

A global payment platform with RTO of seconds and RPO of zero. Live traffic is distributed across two Regions simultaneously using Route 53 latency routing; data is synchronously replicated between Regions.

explanation: Backup and Restore has the highest RTO/RPO tolerance (hours to days) and lowest cost — infrastructure is recreated entirely from snapshots on failover. Pilot Light keeps only the most critical core (typically the database) running in the DR Region; application servers are launched only when needed, achieving an RTO of hours. Warm Standby runs a fully functional but scaled-down replica continuously, reducing failover to minutes by scaling out rather than provisioning from scratch. Multi-site Active-Active distributes production traffic across all Regions simultaneously, providing near-zero RTO/RPO at the highest cost.

stem: A security team must ensure that the AWS KMS customer managed key (CMK) used for data encryption and the TLS certificate on an Application Load Balancer are both rotated automatically with zero service interruption and no manual steps. Which TWO actions achieve this? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Export the ACM public certificate and private key, store the key in AWS Secrets Manager with a rotation Lambda, and configure the ALB listener to retrieve the certificate from Secrets Manager on each TLS handshake
answers.B: Enable automatic key rotation on the CMK; AWS rotates the backing key material annually while preserving the key ID, ARN, and aliases — all existing ciphertexts remain decryptable without re-encryption
answers.C: Write a scheduled Lambda function that calls the KMS GenerateDataKey API monthly to produce a new data key, stores it in S3, and updates the application configuration with the new key ARN
answers.D: Use AWS Certificate Manager to request a public TLS certificate, associate it with the ALB HTTPS listener, and rely on ACM's fully managed renewal — ACM renews and redeploys the certificate before expiration without downtime
answers.E: Use AWS Certificate Manager Private CA to issue a certificate for the public ALB listener so the security team retains full control over the renewal schedule and can rotate on demand

explanation: KMS automatic rotation rotates the underlying backing key material on a yearly schedule. The key ID, ARN, and all aliases remain unchanged, so applications need no configuration updates; KMS tracks which key version encrypted each ciphertext and uses the correct version for decryption automatically — zero re-encryption and zero downtime. ACM manages the complete lifecycle of public TLS certificates: it provisions, deploys to ALB listeners, and renews certificates automatically 60 days before expiration with no service interruption. ACM public certificates cannot have their private keys exported; the ALB integrates with ACM directly without Secrets Manager. Generating data keys manually does not rotate the CMK. Private CA is for internal/private PKI use cases, not public-facing load balancers.

stem: A solutions architect is recommending EC2 scaling strategies for three different workloads. Match each workload to the MOST appropriate scaling strategy. Each strategy is used once.

answers.A: Horizontal scaling (EC2 Auto Scaling group adding or removing instances)
answers.B: Vertical scaling (moving to a larger EC2 instance type)
answers.C: EC2 Hibernation

subquestions.prompt: A stateless web API stores all session state in Amazon ElastiCache and experiences 10× traffic spikes on weekday mornings. Cost must be minimised during overnight low-traffic periods.
A legacy Oracle database runs on a single EC2 instance with a per-instance license. The application cannot be distributed across nodes but is hitting CPU and memory ceilings as the dataset grows.

A developer's build server takes 25 minutes to warm up an in-memory compilation cache after a cold start. The team stops the instance overnight and wants it to resume instantly each morning with all in-memory state intact, without a full OS boot.

explanation: Horizontal scaling (Auto Scaling) is ideal for stateless workloads where any instance can serve any request — session state in ElastiCache means no affinity is required, so instances can be added or removed freely. Vertical scaling (instance resize) is the only option for workloads that cannot be distributed — such as single-node licensed databases — though it requires a stop/start cycle. EC2 Hibernation saves the full RAM contents to the encrypted EBS root volume on stop; on restart, memory is restored and the process resumes exactly where it left off — eliminating cold-start initialisation costs.

stem: A healthcare company stores patient scan files in Amazon S3. Scans are actively accessed for the first 30 days, then accessed occasionally and unpredictably between 31 and 90 days, then rarely after 90 days. After 365 days, files must be retained for 6 additional years for HIPAA compliance and will never be accessed in normal operations — though retrieval within 12 hours must be possible when required. The company wants to minimise S3 costs. Which TWO lifecycle actions should the architect configure? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Transition objects to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval at 30 days to immediately reduce costs for the unpredictable access window
answers.B: Transition objects to S3 Intelligent-Tiering at 30 days so AWS automatically moves files between Frequent and Infrequent Access tiers based on actual usage patterns
answers.C: Transition objects to S3 One Zone-IA at 90 days to minimise storage costs while still supporting occasional retrieval
answers.D: Set an S3 expiration action to delete objects after 365 days to avoid long-term archive costs
answers.E: Transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive at 365 days, which provides the lowest per-GB storage cost and supports standard retrieval within 12 hours

explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between Frequent Access and Infrequent Access tiers (and optionally Archive tiers) based on access patterns, making it optimal for the 31–90 day window where access is occasional and unpredictable — no retrieval fees for monitored tiers. S3 Glacier Deep Archive ($0.00099/GB-month) is the lowest-cost S3 storage class; it supports standard retrieval in 12 hours, satisfying the compliance retrieval requirement. Glacier Instant Retrieval has a 90-day minimum storage duration charge and per-retrieval costs, making it poorly suited to occasional access at 30 days. S3 One Zone-IA stores data in only one Availability Zone (99.5% availability, 99.999999999% durability on paper but AZ loss risks data), which is inappropriate for medical records requiring high durability. Expiring objects after 365 days would violate the 7-year HIPAA retention requirement.

stem: A solutions architect is selecting the appropriate load balancer for each architectural scenario. Match each scenario to the correct AWS load balancer type. Each type is used once.

answers.A: Application Load Balancer (ALB)
answers.B: Network Load Balancer (NLB)
answers.C: Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)

subquestions.prompt: A microservices platform routes HTTP/HTTPS requests to different backend services based on the URL path (/orders/* → Order Service, /catalog/* → Catalog Service) and must terminate TLS at the load balancer.

A financial trading application handles millions of concurrent TCP connections and requires static IP addresses per Availability Zone for firewall whitelisting, ultra-low latency, and the ability to preserve client IP addresses at the transport layer.

A security team must route ALL ingress and egress VPC traffic through a fleet of third-party virtual firewall appliances for deep packet inspection before any traffic reaches its final destination, without changing IP addresses or requiring application changes.

explanation: ALB operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS), supporting content-based routing rules (path, host, header, query string), WebSocket, and TLS termination — the standard choice for web applications and microservices. NLB operates at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP/TLS), provides static Elastic IP addresses per AZ (suitable for firewall whitelisting), preserves source IP, and handles millions of connections with microsecond latency. Gateway Load Balancer operates at Layer 3 and uses the GENEVE protocol to transparently bump-in-the-wire traffic through third-party security appliance fleets, making it the purpose-built choice for inline network security inspection.
tags: Load balancing concepts (for example, Application Load Balancer [ALB])
Designing VPC architectures with security components (for example, security groups, route tables, network ACLs, NAT gateways)

stem: A security audit reveals that the AWS root account has no MFA configured and that IAM users in member accounts can perform any API action from the console without MFA. The security team must immediately enforce MFA for both root and IAM user activity with the least operational overhead. Which TWO actions should the solutions architect take FIRST? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Immediately enable a virtual or hardware MFA device on the AWS management account root user and store the recovery codes in a physical secure location
answers.B: Create new root account access keys and share them only with trusted administrators who have their own MFA devices, then delete the old keys
answers.C: Attach an IAM managed policy to all IAM groups that includes a Deny on all actions ('*') when the condition 'aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent' is false, while exempting MFA-enrollment actions so users can self-enroll
answers.D: Deploy Amazon GuardDuty in all accounts to detect and alert on console logins performed without MFA, then use EventBridge to trigger a Lambda that disables the offending IAM user
answers.E: Rotate all existing IAM user passwords immediately to force re-authentication, then rely on the identity provider's MFA enforcement for subsequent logins

explanation: The root account MFA gap is the most critical vulnerability — enabling MFA on the root user (virtual authenticator or hardware device) directly closes the highest-risk attack surface. A deny-based IAM policy conditioned on 'aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent: false' is the standard pattern to enforce MFA for IAM user console and API access; attaching it to groups ensures coverage without per-user management, and carving out iam:CreateVirtualMFADevice and iam:EnableMFADevice lets users self-enroll. Root account access keys should never exist (create or distribute them); GuardDuty detects threats but does not prevent non-MFA logins; password rotation does not enforce MFA for subsequent logins.
tags: Applying AWS security best practices to IAM users and root users (for example, multi-factor authentication [MFA])
AWS security best practices (for example, the principle of least privilege)

stem: A solutions architect must recommend the appropriate AWS service for each data migration scenario. Match each scenario to the MOST appropriate service. Each service is used once.

answers.A: AWS DataSync
answers.B: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS)
answers.C: AWS Snow Family (Snowball Edge)
answers.D: AWS Transfer Family

subquestions.prompt: A company must migrate 3 PB of on-premises NAS file data to Amazon S3. Its internet connection is 200 Mbps, meaning an online transfer would take over a year. The migration must complete within 8 weeks.

A team must migrate a production Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL while keeping both systems in sync during a 2-week parallel-run window, using change data capture (CDC) to minimise cutover downtime.

An analytics team needs to copy 50 TB of NFS file shares from on-premises to Amazon EFS over the network, with automatic bandwidth throttling, per-file checksum verification, and a configurable schedule.

A financial institution's external partners deliver daily settlement files using SFTP clients. The institution wants to receive these files directly into Amazon S3 without changing partner-side tooling or credentials.

explanation: AWS Snow Family (Snowball Edge) is the appropriate choice when the data volume makes online transfer impractical — physical devices are shipped to the customer, loaded offline, then shipped back to AWS. AWS DMS supports homogeneous and heterogeneous database migrations with CDC, keeping source and target in sync during cutover windows. AWS DataSync is a managed online file-transfer service that accelerates NFS/SMB/S3/EFS migrations with scheduling, checksums, and bandwidth throttling. AWS Transfer Family provides fully managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP endpoints backed by S3 or EFS, so external partners continue to use their existing SFTP workflows without any client-side changes.
tags: Selecting the appropriate service for data migration to storage services
Hybrid storage options (for example, AWS DataSync, AWS Transfer Family, AWS Storage Gateway)

stem: A platform team manages infrastructure across 60 AWS accounts in an AWS Organisation. They must ensure identical VPC configurations (subnets, NACLs, security groups) are deployed in every account and that any out-of-band manual changes to those resources are automatically detected and reverted. Which TWO actions should the solutions architect implement? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions to deploy and maintain the VPC stack across all Organisation member accounts automatically, including accounts added in future
answers.B: Run CloudFormation drift detection on each stack daily via a scheduled Lambda and send SNS email notifications to administrators whenever drift is detected
answers.C: Enable AWS Config with relevant managed rules (e.g. vpc-sg-open-only-to-authorized-ports) and configure automatic remediation using AWS Systems Manager Automation documents to revert unauthorised changes
answers.D: Attach IAM deny policies in each account that block all VPC modification API calls (ec2:ModifyVpcAttribute, ec2:DeleteSubnet, etc.) to prevent manual changes entirely
answers.E: Use AWS Service Catalog to create a VPC portfolio product and require all teams to provision VPCs exclusively through the catalog, preventing direct console creation

explanation: CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions integrates with AWS Organisations to automatically deploy stacks to existing and future member accounts, ensuring consistent baseline configurations at scale. AWS Config continuously evaluates resource configurations against defined rules; pairing rules with SSM Automation remediation documents creates a detect-and-remediate loop that automatically reverts unauthorised changes — this is the canonical pattern for enforcing infrastructure integrity. Drift detection alone only notifies; it does not revert changes. Blanket IAM deny policies break legitimate operational workflows. Service Catalog governs provisioning but does not prevent or remediate out-of-band changes made directly via the console or API.
tags: Determining automation strategies to ensure infrastructure integrity

stem: A solutions architect is selecting network connectivity options for four different connectivity requirements. Match each requirement to the MOST appropriate AWS networking service. Each service is used once.

answers.A: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
answers.B: AWS Direct Connect
answers.C: AWS PrivateLink
answers.D: VPC Peering

subquestions.prompt: Two VPCs in the same Region must route traffic between their private CIDR ranges with low latency and no bandwidth throttling. The connection must not traverse the internet and there is no overlapping IP space.

A company needs encrypted connectivity from its on-premises data centre to an AWS VPC within hours, without waiting for months of physical circuit provisioning, accepting that traffic will traverse the public internet.

A SaaS provider wants to expose a specific service running in their VPC to thousands of customer VPCs across different AWS accounts and Regions without peering VPCs, advertising CIDR routes, or exposing the service to the public internet.
A bank requires a private, dedicated 10 Gbps connection to AWS with consistent, low-latency performance that never traverses the public internet and supports a Service Level Agreement with AWS.

explanation: VPC Peering creates a direct private connection between two VPCs (same or different accounts/Regions) using private IP addresses, with no internet traversal and no bandwidth cap — ideal for same-Region private routing with non-overlapping CIDRs. Site-to-Site VPN is an encrypted IPSec tunnel over the public internet that can be provisioned in hours, making it the fastest path to on-premises connectivity. PrivateLink exposes services through Network Load Balancer endpoints that consumers access via Interface VPC Endpoints, enabling service-specific private access without VPC routing or CIDR overlap concerns. Direct Connect is a dedicated physical circuit (1/10/100 Gbps) with consistent network performance and no public internet traversal, suitable for demanding enterprise workloads with SLA requirements.
tags: Securing external network connections to and from the AWS Cloud (for example, VPN, AWS Direct Connect)
Reviewing existing workloads for network optimizations
Network services with appropriate use cases (for example, DNS)

stem: A manufacturing company runs containerised workloads on-premises for data-residency reasons and also runs workloads on AWS. Some applications use Kubernetes (managed via Amazon EKS in the cloud) and others use Amazon ECS. The team wants a unified AWS-native control plane for BOTH on-premises Kubernetes and on-premises ECS workloads using their existing on-premises servers — without purchasing additional dedicated hardware from AWS. Which TWO services satisfy this requirement? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Amazon EKS Anywhere — deploys and manages Kubernetes clusters on the company's existing on-premises infrastructure using the same EKS tooling and control plane APIs
answers.B: AWS Outposts rack — delivers fully AWS-managed infrastructure (EC2, EKS, ECS) deployed at the company's data centre on dedicated AWS-supplied hardware
answers.C: Amazon ECS Anywhere — registers the company's existing on-premises servers as ECS external instances that are managed through the same ECS control plane in the AWS console
answers.D: AWS Fargate — runs ECS and EKS tasks on AWS-managed infrastructure so the company no longer needs to manage any servers
answers.E: Amazon EC2 instances in AWS Local Zones configured as ECS container instances, placed closer to the on-premises facility to reduce latency

explanation: EKS Anywhere extends the Amazon EKS control plane to customer-owned infrastructure (on-premises bare metal, VMware vSphere, etc.) so teams manage on-premises Kubernetes clusters using the same eksctl, kubectl, and AWS Console workflows as cloud EKS clusters. ECS Anywhere registers any Linux server (physical or VM) as an ECS external instance via the SSM agent; it appears in the ECS control plane alongside cloud instances, enabling unified task scheduling and management. AWS Outposts requires purchasing and installing AWS-supplied rack hardware — this contradicts the 'no additional hardware' requirement. Fargate is a serverless AWS-only compute engine and does not extend to on-premises servers. Local Zone instances still run in AWS infrastructure and are not physically on-premises.
tags: Hybrid compute options (for example, AWS Outposts)
Determining the appropriate placement of resources to meet business requirements

stem: A solutions architect must recommend the correct AWS storage service for each hybrid storage scenario. Match each scenario to the MOST appropriate service. Each service is used once.

answers.A: AWS Storage Gateway – File Gateway
answers.B: AWS Storage Gateway – Volume Gateway (Cached mode)
answers.C: AWS DataSync
answers.D: AWS Transfer Family

subquestions.prompt: A video-production studio needs on-premises NFS and SMB shares that transparently back to Amazon S3, allowing editing workstations to read and write cloud-stored video files without any application changes.

A hospital's legacy PACS imaging system uses iSCSI block storage. The team wants to keep a frequently accessed local cache on-premises while durably storing all primary volumes in AWS for disaster recovery.

A company is migrating 80 TB of on-premises NFS data to Amazon EFS over a 3-week window. The migration must include per-file checksum verification, bandwidth throttling to protect production traffic, and automated scheduling.

External trading partners transmit daily settlement files using SFTP client software. The company wants to receive these files into Amazon S3 without requiring any partner-side reconfiguration of SFTP endpoints or credentials.

explanation: File Gateway presents S3 buckets as NFS/SMB file shares on-premises with a local cache, making S3 appear as a network file system to existing applications. Volume Gateway (Cached mode) presents iSCSI block volumes on-premises with frequently accessed data cached locally and all data stored durably in AWS — ideal for legacy block-storage applications needing cloud backup. DataSync is a managed online migration service with scheduling, per-file checksums, bandwidth throttling, and filtering — purpose-built for large-scale file migrations. Transfer Family provides managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP endpoints that store files directly in S3 or EFS, letting external partners continue using their existing SFTP tooling unchanged.
tags: Hybrid storage options (for example, AWS DataSync, AWS Transfer Family, AWS Storage Gateway)
Storage options and characteristics (for example, durability, replication)

stem: A security team requires continuous assessment of EC2 instances and Amazon ECR container images for known CVEs and must automatically patch EC2 instances that fall outside the approved patch baseline without manual intervention. Which TWO services should the solutions architect implement to fulfil BOTH requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Enable Amazon Inspector v2 to continuously scan EC2 instances and ECR container images for software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and unintended network exposure, generating prioritised findings
answers.B: Enable Amazon GuardDuty to detect unusual API calls and network anomalies that may indicate active exploitation of a software vulnerability
answers.C: Create an AWS Config managed rule (ec2-instance-managed-by-systems-manager) and configure auto-remediation to terminate non-compliant instances
answers.D: Use AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to define a patch baseline and maintenance window; SSM automatically installs approved patches on non-compliant EC2 instances on schedule
answers.E: Use AWS Trusted Advisor security checks to identify EC2 instances running outdated AMIs and trigger an EventBridge rule to invoke Lambda for remediation

explanation: Amazon Inspector v2 is the purpose-built continuous vulnerability assessment service: it scans EC2 instances (via the SSM agent) and ECR images for CVEs and network reachability issues, generating prioritised findings with CVSS scores. AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager closes the remediation loop: administrators define a patch baseline (approved patches), create a maintenance window, and SSM automatically installs missing patches on EC2 instances on the defined schedule — no manual intervention required. GuardDuty detects active threats and anomalies but does not assess or remediate software vulnerabilities. Config rules and instance termination are too disruptive as a remediation for patch compliance. Trusted Advisor security checks are not designed for continuous CVE scanning and do not provide CVSS-prioritised vulnerability findings.
tags: Determining automation strategies to ensure infrastructure integrity

stem: A solutions architect must recommend the appropriate deployment model for four workloads with different availability requirements. Match each workload profile to the MOST cost-effective deployment model that meets its requirements. Each model is used once.

answers.A: Single-AZ deployment with no cross-AZ redundancy
answers.B: Multi-AZ deployment within a single AWS Region
answers.C: Multi-Region active-passive (primary Region serves traffic; DR Region on standby)
answers.D: Multi-Region active-active (all Regions simultaneously serve live traffic)

subquestions.prompt: A development and QA environment used only during business hours by an internal team of eight engineers. Occasional downtime is acceptable; minimising monthly cost is the primary driver.
A customer-facing e-commerce site with a 99.99% monthly availability SLA serving a single country. The architecture must survive an Availability Zone outage with automatic failover and no data loss.

A financial regulatory reporting system with an RTO of 4 hours and RPO of 1 hour that must survive a complete AWS Region failure. The system does not need to serve traffic from the DR Region during normal operations.
A globally distributed payment platform serving North America and Europe with an SLA of 99.999% and zero-data-loss requirements. Any single Region failure must be invisible to end users.

explanation: A single-AZ deployment offers the lowest cost but no redundancy — acceptable for non-production environments where downtime has no business impact. Multi-AZ within a Region provides automatic failover across AZs (each AZ is a separate physical data centre) with synchronous replication — the standard pattern for high-availability production workloads in one geography. Multi-Region active-passive maintains a standby environment in a second Region that is activated on failover; it meets multi-hour RTO targets at lower cost than active-active. Multi-Region active-active distributes live traffic globally with synchronous or near-synchronous replication, achieving the highest availability (99.999%+) and zero-data-loss at the highest cost.
tags: Determining the required availability for different classes of workloads (for example, production workloads, non-production workloads)
Disaster recovery (DR) strategies (for example, backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, active-active failover, recovery point objective [RPO], recovery time objective [RTO])
Determining the appropriate placement of resources to meet business requirements

stem: A company runs two EC2-based workloads. The first is a large-scale ML training job that can tolerate interruptions, checkpoints its progress every 30 minutes to Amazon S3, and runs 8–12 hours per job with 20 jobs per month. The second is a real-time inference API that has run 24/7 for two years with stable, predictable compute requirements and cannot tolerate interruptions. Which TWO purchasing options minimise total EC2 cost for BOTH workloads? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Use EC2 Spot Instances for the ML training workload; if interrupted, the checkpoint in S3 limits recomputation to at most 30 minutes
answers.B: Use EC2 On-Demand Instances for both workloads to ensure maximum availability and simplify cost forecasting
answers.C: Purchase a 1-year Compute Savings Plan or Reserved Instances for the inference API to reduce the steady-state 24/7 compute bill by up to 72% compared to On-Demand
answers.D: Use EC2 Dedicated Hosts for the inference API; the per-host billing model reduces cost for stable, long-running workloads compared to On-Demand per-instance pricing
answers.E: Use EC2 Spot Instances for the real-time inference API, applying Spot capacity pools across multiple instance families and Availability Zones to minimise interruption risk

explanation: Spot Instances offer up to 90% savings over On-Demand for interruption-tolerant workloads. Because the ML training job checkpoints every 30 minutes, a Spot interruption causes at most 30 minutes of lost work — a low risk-to-savings trade-off. A Compute Savings Plan (or EC2 Reserved Instance) provides 40–72% savings for workloads with stable, predictable usage — the 24/7 inference API is a textbook candidate. On-Demand pricing for both workloads is the most expensive option. Dedicated Hosts are primarily for BYOL licensing compliance (e.g., Windows Server, SQL Server per-core licensing); their per-host cost does not inherently provide savings over RIs/Savings Plans for general workloads. Spot Instances are inappropriate for real-time inference APIs that cannot tolerate interruption — a Spot reclaim would take the endpoint offline immediately.
tags: Determining appropriate scaling methods and strategies for elastic workloads (for example, horizontal compared with vertical, EC2 hibernation)
Determining the required availability for different classes of workloads (for example, production workloads, non-production workloads)
AWS purchasing options (for example, Spot Instances, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans)

stem: A solutions architect is selecting AWS AI/ML services for five separate application requirements. Match each requirement to the MOST appropriate AWS managed AI service. Each service is used once.

answers.A: Amazon Rekognition
answers.B: Amazon Transcribe
answers.C: Amazon Textract
answers.D: Amazon Comprehend
answers.E: Amazon Translate

subquestions.prompt: A compliance system analyzes millions of customer feedback emails to automatically detect sentiment (positive/negative/mixed), extract named entities (person, organization, date), identify dominant language, and flag any personally identifiable information (PII).
A call center platform converts recorded customer service calls to searchable text transcripts with speaker diarization (who spoke when) and a custom vocabulary for industry-specific terminology.

A content moderation system processes images uploaded by users of a social platform, detecting unsafe content, recognizing celebrity faces, and identifying objects and scenes — returning confidence scores for each.

A finance team automates accounts payable by extracting structured data (vendor name, invoice number, line items, totals) from scanned PDF invoices without pre-defining templates or training a custom model.
A global e-commerce platform automatically converts English product descriptions into 50 other languages in real time when a new listing is created, using neural machine translation.

explanation: Comprehend is AWS's NLP service for text analysis: sentiment, entity extraction, key phrases, language detection, and PII redaction. Transcribe converts audio to text (ASR) with speaker diarization, custom vocabularies, and custom language models. Rekognition analyzes images and videos for faces, objects, scenes, text, and moderation labels. Textract extracts structured data (key-value pairs, tables, form fields) from documents and PDFs without requiring template definitions. Translate provides neural machine translation supporting 75+ languages.

stem: A financial services company stores sensitive payment card data in Amazon S3. The security team has two requirements: (1) automatically discover and alert on any S3 bucket containing unprotected PII or financial data, and (2) encrypt data using cryptographic keys stored in FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware where AWS has NO access to the key material. Which TWO services satisfy these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Amazon Macie — uses ML to automatically discover, classify, and alert on sensitive data (PII, financial records, credentials) stored in S3 buckets
answers.B: Amazon GuardDuty — detects threats such as unusual S3 API calls and data exfiltration patterns indicative of a breach in progress
answers.C: AWS CloudHSM — provides single-tenant, FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware security modules where the customer manages all key material and AWS has zero access to the HSMs
answers.D: AWS KMS with customer managed keys (CMKs) — encrypts data using FIPS 140-2 Level 2 validated HSMs managed by AWS, where the customer controls the key policy
answers.E: AWS Secrets Manager — stores and rotates database credentials and API keys, with automatic integration for RDS and Redshift secrets

explanation: Amazon Macie is purpose-built for discovering and protecting sensitive data in S3: it uses ML to detect PII, financial data, and credentials, generates findings, and can alert via EventBridge or Security Hub — exactly what requirement 1 needs. AWS CloudHSM provides single-tenant, FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated HSMs where the customer controls the HSM partition and AWS has no ability to extract key material — satisfying requirement 2. KMS CMKs use FIPS 140-2 Level 2 HSMs managed by AWS; while very secure, AWS technically manages the underlying hardware and the key material never leaves KMS-managed HSMs. GuardDuty detects active threats and anomalies but does not discover stored PII. Secrets Manager manages credentials, not arbitrary customer-controlled encryption keys.
tags: Implementing policies for data access, lifecycle, and protection

stem: A solutions architect is selecting serverless AWS services for four different application patterns. Match each pattern to the MOST appropriate serverless service. Each service is used once.

answers.A: AWS Lambda
answers.B: AWS Fargate
answers.C: AWS AppSync
answers.D: AWS Serverless Application Repository (SAR)

subquestions.prompt: A team builds a reusable, pre-tested serverless data-ingestion pipeline and wants to publish it so other AWS accounts in the organisation can discover and deploy it in one click without writing CloudFormation.
A mobile app needs real-time data synchronization via GraphQL subscriptions, offline data support when the device has no connectivity, and automatic conflict resolution — backed by DynamoDB.
A batch image-processing job runs Docker containers requiring 30 GiB RAM and 8 vCPUs per task, takes up to 4 hours to complete, and is triggered from an SQS queue — with no EC2 instances to manage.
An S3 event triggers lightweight JSON transformation and routing logic that runs for under 10 seconds and forwards the result to an SNS topic. No persistent infrastructure should be provisioned.

explanation: SAR is a managed repository for sharing and deploying serverless applications — publishers upload SAM templates and code, and consumers deploy them with one click without touching CloudFormation directly. AppSync is a fully managed GraphQL service with built-in real-time WebSocket subscriptions, DynamoDB resolvers, and offline sync (via Amplify DataStore), making it ideal for mobile apps. Fargate runs containerised workloads without managing EC2 instances — it supports large memory (up to 120 GiB) and long-running tasks (hours) that exceed Lambda's constraints. Lambda is ideal for short-lived (max 15 minutes), event-driven functions triggered by S3, SNS, SQS, or API Gateway — with no infrastructure to provision or manage.
tags: Serverless technologies and patterns (for example, AWS Lambda, Fargate)

stem: A FinOps team has two requirements: (1) build custom Amazon Athena queries and Amazon QuickSight dashboards against the most granular AWS billing data available (hourly, resource-level, with usage type and tags), and (2) automatically send an SNS alert when monthly spend for a specific AWS service exceeds a defined dollar threshold. Which TWO services should they configure? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) delivered to an S3 bucket in Parquet format, enabling Athena queries with an AWS Glue crawler-generated table for granular resource-level cost analysis
answers.B: AWS Cost Explorer with CSV export scheduled by a Lambda function, processed by Glue ETL, and loaded into Redshift for visualization
answers.C: AWS Budgets configured with a Cost budget scoped to a specific AWS service, with an SNS alert action triggered when actual monthly spend exceeds the defined threshold
answers.D: AWS Trusted Advisor to generate weekly cost-optimization recommendations and automatically email the savings summary to the billing team
answers.E: Amazon CloudWatch Billing Alarm on the EstimatedCharges metric to notify via SNS when total estimated charges exceed the threshold

explanation: AWS Cost and Usage Report is the most comprehensive billing dataset AWS offers — it provides hourly, resource-level cost and usage data with all cost allocation tags, delivered to S3 in CSV or Parquet format. Pairing CUR with an Athena table (via a Glue crawler) and QuickSight is the standard AWS FinOps architecture for custom granular analysis. AWS Budgets supports service-scoped cost budgets with SNS alert actions — the most direct mechanism for service-specific spend thresholds. Cost Explorer provides pre-built 13-month visualizations and CSV exports but does not provide the hourly resource-level granularity needed for custom Athena queries. Trusted Advisor provides general cost optimization checks, not configurable dollar thresholds. CloudWatch Billing Alarms monitor estimated total charges and cannot be filtered to a specific service the way Budgets can.

stem: A solutions architect is assigning AWS security services to four operational scenarios. Match each scenario to the MOST appropriate security service. Each service is used once.

answers.A: Amazon GuardDuty
answers.B: Amazon Detective
answers.C: AWS Security Hub
answers.D: Amazon Inspector

subquestions.prompt: A SOC team receives hundreds of daily findings from GuardDuty, Macie, and Inspector across 40 accounts. They need a single aggregated dashboard that normalizes all findings to the Amazon Security Finding Format (ASFF), prioritizes them by severity, and maps them to compliance frameworks.

An analyst must investigate a GuardDuty finding about an EC2 instance making outbound calls to a known command-and-control server. The analyst needs a visual, graph-based timeline of all related API calls, VPC flow records, and CloudTrail events over the past 90 days.

A security operations team needs continuous, automated detection of anomalous behaviors across the AWS environment: unusual IAM role assumptions, EC2 instances communicating with known malicious IPs, and S3 data exfiltration patterns — without deploying any agents.

A DevSecOps team requires continuous assessment of EC2 instances and ECR container images for known CVEs (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) with CVSS-scored findings that integrate into Security Hub for centralised tracking.

explanation: Security Hub is the centralised findings aggregation service: it collects findings from GuardDuty, Macie, Inspector, Firewall Manager, and partner tools; normalizes them to ASFF; scores them; and maps them to CIS, PCI DSS, and NIST frameworks. Amazon Detective is the post-incident investigation service: it uses ML and graph analysis to build interactive visualizations of API call sequences, network flows, and user sessions — enabling root-cause analysis of security incidents. GuardDuty is the always-on threat detection service: it analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and Kubernetes audit logs for anomalous behavior and known malicious indicators without requiring agents. Inspector v2 is the vulnerability management service that continuously scans EC2 (via SSM agent) and ECR images for CVEs.
tags: Designing VPC architectures with security components (for example, security groups, route tables, network ACLs, NAT gateways)

stem: A company with 35 AWS accounts must enforce consistent AWS WAF web ACL rules across ALL public-facing Application Load Balancers and Amazon CloudFront distributions. New ALBs created in any member account must be automatically protected without requiring the individual account team to take any action. Which TWO services should the solutions architect configure? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: AWS WAF — create web ACLs containing AWS Managed Rules groups (e.g., AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet, AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet) that define the actual filtering rules
answers.B: AWS Firewall Manager — create WAF security policies at the Organisation root that reference the WAF web ACLs and automatically deploy them to all existing and future ALBs and CloudFront distributions in member accounts
