stem: A security architect is designing identity federation for different use cases. Match each federation scenario to the correct AWS authentication mechanism.

answers.A: SAML 2.0 federation with STS AssumeRoleWithSAML
answers.B: Web Identity federation with STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
answers.C: AWS IAM Identity Center (SSO) with SAML/OIDC
answers.D: AWS Directory Service AD Connector
answers.E: AWS Directory Service Managed Microsoft AD

subquestions.prompt: 5,000 employees use Microsoft Active Directory on-premises. They need single sign-on to the AWS Management Console using their corporate credentials, with role assignments based on AD group membership.
A mobile app allows users to sign in with their Google account. After authentication, the app needs temporary AWS credentials to upload photos directly to S3 from the mobile device.
An on-premises ADFS (Active Directory Federation Services) deployment issues SAML assertions. Developers must be able to assume AWS IAM roles using their ADFS credentials via the AWS CLI.
On-premises Linux servers running workloads need to use their existing Active Directory accounts to authenticate to AWS services. The AD must remain on-premises without migrating to AWS.

A company moving entirely to AWS needs a new managed Microsoft Active Directory in the cloud for EC2 Windows domain join, Group Policy, and LDAP/Kerberos authentication — with no on-premises AD dependency.

explanation: IAM Identity Center (formerly SSO) is the recommended service for workforce federation — integrates with external IdPs via SAML/OIDC and provides a centralized portal with automatic role assignment. Web Identity federation (OIDC) is for mobile/web apps authenticating with Google, Apple, Facebook, and exchanging tokens for AWS credentials. SAML 2.0 federation with STS is used for programmatic (CLI) access via ADFS. AD Connector proxies authentication requests to on-premises AD without synchronizing directory data to AWS. Managed Microsoft AD is a fully managed AD in AWS for new cloud-native deployments.

stem: An analytics team queries a 50 TB S3 data lake using Athena. Queries scan the full dataset every time, resulting in $500/day in query costs and 10-minute query times. The data is stored as JSON, partitioned only by year. Which TWO optimizations will have the largest impact on both cost and query performance?

answers.A: Convert the JSON data to Apache Parquet or ORC columnar format and compress with Snappy. Athena charges per TB of data scanned, and columnar formats allow column pruning to scan only referenced columns.
answers.B: Add more granular partitioning (year/month/day/hour) to the S3 prefix structure and update the Glue Data Catalog table to register new partition keys. Use partition projection to eliminate the need to run MSCK REPAIR TABLE.
answers.C: Enable Athena query result reuse to cache query results for 24 hours, reducing scanned data for identical queries.
answers.D: Use Athena workgroups to set per-query data scan limits, preventing individual queries from scanning more than 1 TB and alerting when thresholds are exceeded.
answers.E: Migrate the S3 data to an Amazon Redshift cluster and run the queries there instead, as Athena is not designed for large datasets.

explanation: Converting to Parquet/ORC (option A) is typically the single largest optimization for Athena costs and speed. Columnar formats allow Athena to read only the columns referenced in the SELECT clause and predicate pushdown eliminates entire row groups. Combined with Snappy compression, data scanned drops by 70-90% — transforming a 50 TB scan into 5-15 TB. Granular partitioning (option B) enables partition pruning: a query filtered on a specific day scans only that day's data rather than the full year's partition. Combining year/month/day/hour partitions with a date range filter can reduce scanned data by 99%. Partition projection avoids the need to sync partition metadata with Glue. Options A and B together routinely achieve 10-100x cost reduction. Option C (result reuse) only helps for identical repeated queries. Option D (scan limits) prevents expensive queries but doesn't reduce cost for necessary queries. Option E (Redshift) is a valid alternative but represents a complete architecture change — the question asks for optimizations.

stem: A network architect is configuring ALB and NLB behavior for various requirements. Match each requirement to the correct load balancer configuration feature.

answers.A: ALB listener rules with weighted target groups
answers.B: ALB sticky sessions (duration-based)
answers.C: NLB with cross-zone load balancing
answers.D: ALB health check with a custom path and threshold
answers.E: ALB with host-based routing

subquestions.prompt: Send 5% of production traffic to a new application version target group and 95% to the current version, enabling a canary deployment with precise traffic splitting.
Ensure that a user's requests within a 1-hour session are always routed to the same EC2 instance, because the application stores session state locally on the server.
An NLB has three targets: 2 in us-east-1a and 1 in us-east-1b. With this feature enabled, each target receives an equal 33% share of traffic regardless of which AZ the client connects to.
Mark a target as unhealthy only after it fails three consecutive HTTP 200 checks at /health every 30 seconds, and re-mark it healthy only after two consecutive successful checks.
Route requests to api.example.com to a microservices target group and requests to app.example.com to a monolith target group — both hosted behind a single ALB and IP address.

explanation: Weighted target groups on ALB listener rules allow precise percentage-based traffic splitting between target groups — the standard mechanism for canary/blue-green deployments. Duration-based sticky sessions use a cookie to route a user's requests to the same target for a configured period. NLB cross-zone load balancing distributes traffic evenly across all registered targets regardless of AZ, compensating for uneven target distribution. ALB health check configuration allows custom paths, success codes, interval, healthy/unhealthy thresholds. Host-based routing uses the HTTP Host header to route to different target groups from a single ALB.

stem: An application has two components: a stateless API tier (currently 4x m5.2xlarge) handling 10,000 req/sec at peak, and a stateful database tier (1x r5.8xlarge RDS) that is CPU-bound at peak. The team needs to scale both tiers cost-effectively. Which TWO scaling strategies are correct for each tier?

answers.A: Scale the API tier horizontally by adding more m5.2xlarge instances behind an ALB with Auto Scaling target tracking (ALBRequestCountPerTarget), using Spot Instances for cost reduction.
answers.B: Scale the API tier vertically by upgrading to m5.8xlarge instances, as horizontal scaling requires refactoring the stateless application.
answers.C: Scale the database tier vertically by upgrading to r5.16xlarge or r5.24xlarge to add CPU capacity, then add Read Replicas to offload read traffic if reads dominate the workload.
answers.D: Scale the database tier horizontally by adding four r5.8xlarge RDS instances in a cluster and distributing writes across them using application-level sharding.
answers.E: Scale the database tier by enabling RDS Multi-AZ, which provides additional compute capacity from the standby instance to handle peak CPU load.

explanation: The stateless API tier (option A) is perfectly suited for horizontal scaling — stateless services share no session state between instances, so adding instances behind an ALB is architecturally correct. Target tracking on ALBRequestCountPerTarget automatically adjusts instance count to maintain a target request rate. Spot Instances provide up to 90% savings for Auto Scaling groups that can replace instances quickly. The stateful RDS database (option C) is not horizontally scalable using vanilla RDS (no write sharding support without Aurora or custom sharding) — the correct approach is vertical scaling (larger instance type) to add CPU, plus Read Replicas to offload read queries. Option B is incorrect because stateless APIs scale better horizontally at lower cost. Option D (application-level sharding across 4 RDS instances) requires significant application refactoring and is not appropriate for a standard RDS deployment. Option E (Multi-AZ standby) does NOT provide additional compute capacity — the standby is passive and does not serve traffic.

stem: A solutions architect is selecting the correct AWS database for five different application data models. Match each data model to the most appropriate AWS database service.

answers.A: Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL-compatible)
answers.B: Amazon DynamoDB
answers.C: Amazon Neptune
answers.D: Amazon Timestream
answers.E: Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (QLDB)

subquestions.prompt: An online retail platform stores orders, customers, products, and inventory with complex multi-table JOIN queries, ACID transactions across tables, and reporting with GROUP BY aggregations.
A gaming application stores per-user session data and leaderboards that require single-millisecond read latency at 1 million requests per second, with a flexible schema that varies by game mode.

A social network stores user profiles and relationships (follows, friends, likes). Queries like 'find all friends of friends who share common interests' require traversing relationship edges efficiently.
An IoT platform ingests 10 million sensor readings per second and needs to query time-series data with time-based aggregations, downsampling, and interpolation using built-in time-series functions.

A financial application requires an immutable, cryptographically verifiable audit log of all balance changes. The history must be provable and tamper-evident — any modification to historical records must be detectable.

explanation: Aurora (PostgreSQL/MySQL-compatible) is the correct relational database for multi-table JOINs, ACID transactions, and SQL aggregations. DynamoDB provides single-digit millisecond performance at any scale with flexible schema. Neptune is the managed graph database supporting Gremlin and SPARQL for traversal-heavy relationship queries. Timestream is purpose-built for time-series data with built-in time-series functions, automatic data tiering, and massive ingestion rates. QLDB provides a cryptographically verifiable transaction log using a SHA-256 hash chain — suitable for regulatory audit trails.

stem: An order management system uses SQS to decouple order submission from fulfillment. Orders within the same customer account must be processed in the sequence they were submitted (FIFO per customer), but orders from different customers can be processed in parallel. The system must process 15,000 messages per second at peak. Which TWO features of SQS FIFO queues must be configured to meet these requirements while achieving maximum throughput?

answers.A: Use a message group ID set to the customer account ID in each message. Within the same MessageGroupId, FIFO queues guarantee strict ordering and deliver messages one at a time to a consumer.
answers.B: Set a content-based deduplication attribute on each message so that identical order submissions within the 5-minute deduplication window are automatically discarded.
answers.C: Enable high-throughput FIFO mode (SQS FIFO with partitions) to increase throughput to up to 70,000 TPS per partition, allowing the queue to handle 15,000 messages/second across multiple message groups.
answers.D: Create multiple SQS Standard queues (one per customer) and use a Lambda function to route messages to the correct queue based on customer ID.
answers.E: Use a single SQS Standard queue with a Lambda consumer that re-orders messages by submission timestamp within a 500ms window before processing.

explanation: MessageGroupId (option A) is the FIFO queue feature that enables per-group ordering — all messages with the same MessageGroupId (customer account ID) are processed in strict FIFO order, while different groups are processed in parallel by different consumers. This exactly matches the requirement. High-throughput FIFO mode (option C) uses multiple partitions to overcome the standard FIFO limit of 3,000 TPS (with batching) and supports up to 70,000 TPS — required to handle 15,000 messages/second. Option B (content-based deduplication) is about preventing duplicate messages using SHA-256 of the body — not related to ordering or throughput. Option D (multiple Standard queues) achieves ordering but requires maintaining per-customer queues (complex, doesn't scale to millions of customers). Option E (Standard queue + re-ordering in Lambda) is not reliable — SQS Standard doesn't guarantee delivery order, and 500ms windowing doesn't guarantee correct ordering under load.

stem: A data warehouse team is optimizing Amazon Redshift for a large-scale analytics workload. Match each performance or scalability challenge to the correct Redshift feature.

answers.A: Redshift Spectrum
answers.B: Redshift Concurrency Scaling
answers.C: Redshift Materialized Views
answers.D: Redshift AQUA (Advanced Query Accelerator)
answers.E: Redshift sort keys and distribution styles

subquestions.prompt: Query 500 TB of historical data stored in S3 in Parquet format without loading it into Redshift, joining it with 10 TB of current data in the Redshift cluster.
During month-end reporting, 200 concurrent users submit queries simultaneously. Normal cluster handles 50 users, but month-end demand spikes 4x without adding permanent cluster nodes.

A BI dashboard runs the same 20 complex aggregation queries every 5 minutes. Pre-compute and cache these query results so dashboard loads are sub-second, refreshing automatically when underlying data changes.
Offload compute-intensive query processing to a distributed hardware-accelerated layer close to S3 storage, reducing the load on Redshift's main cluster compute nodes for I/O-bound queries.
Optimize a frequently executed JOIN between a 1 TB 'orders' fact table and a 5 MB 'products' dimension table. Configure the distribution and sort strategies to eliminate data movement between nodes.

explanation: Redshift Spectrum extends queries to S3 data lake without ETL. Concurrency Scaling adds transient clusters automatically during peak concurrent query periods. Materialized Views pre-compute and cache query results with incremental refresh. AQUA is a hardware-accelerated distributed cache layer that processes queries closer to S3 storage for RA3 node clusters. Sort keys determine physical row ordering on disk (enabling zone map pruning); distribution styles (KEY, ALL, EVEN) control how rows are distributed across nodes to minimize shuffle — distributing the small dimension table as ALL eliminates broadcast joins.

stem: A company is migrating 200 applications to AWS. Application A is a legacy Oracle database (approaching end-of-support) with tightly coupled stored procedures that drive significant business logic. Application B is a Java EE application on WebLogic running on on-premises VMs that the team wants on AWS quickly with minimal code changes, taking advantage of managed services. Which TWO migration strategies are correct for each application?

answers.A: Refactor (re-architect) Application A: migrate from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL, rewrite stored procedures as application logic or Lambda functions, and modernize the data layer.
answers.B: Rehost (lift-and-shift) Application A: use AWS Application Migration Service to replicate the Oracle VM to EC2 without changes.
answers.C: Replatform Application B: migrate from WebLogic on VMs to Amazon ECS with containerized Java EE, or to AWS Elastic Beanstalk with Tomcat, gaining managed infrastructure without full refactoring.
answers.D: Rehost Application B by replicating the WebLogic VMs to EC2, retaining the existing WebLogic license and configuration exactly as-is.
answers.E: Retire Application B: the Java EE stack is outdated and should be decommissioned and replaced with a new microservices architecture before migration.

explanation: Application A (Oracle approaching EoS with stored procedure business logic) is a Refactor candidate — the business pressure of EoS combined with cost and licensing creates the ROI for a deeper migration to Aurora PostgreSQL with SCT (Schema Conversion Tool). This is more work but eliminates Oracle licensing costs and technical debt. Application B (Java EE on WebLogic, needs AWS quickly with minimal changes) is a Replatform candidate — moving to ECS containers or Elastic Beanstalk removes VM management overhead without requiring application code changes, gaining managed patching, auto-scaling, and monitoring. Option B (rehosting Oracle) misses the EoS problem and perpetuates expensive licensing. Option D (rehosting WebLogic to EC2) is a rehost — valid but slower and doesn't take advantage of managed services as specified. Option E (retiring the Java app) is a business decision, not a migration strategy — the question specifies the team wants it on AWS.

stem: A company is building NLP-powered features using Amazon Comprehend. Match each application requirement to the correct Comprehend capability.

answers.A: Comprehend Sentiment Analysis
answers.B: Comprehend Entity Recognition
answers.C: Comprehend Topic Modeling
answers.D: Comprehend PII Detection and Redaction
answers.E: Comprehend Custom Classifier

subquestions.prompt: Analyze 500,000 product reviews to determine whether each review is positive, negative, neutral, or mixed, and calculate an aggregate satisfaction score per product category.
Extract mentions of company names, stock tickers, people, dates, monetary amounts, and locations from news articles to populate a financial knowledge graph.
Analyze 100,000 customer support tickets to automatically discover the 20 most common themes and categories without predefined labels or training data.
Scan customer emails before archiving them and automatically redact Social Security numbers, credit card numbers, and email addresses to comply with data minimization requirements.
Classify legal documents into categories (contract, NDA, patent, litigation) that are specific to the company's taxonomy. The model must be trained on 500 labeled examples of each category.

explanation: Comprehend Sentiment Analysis classifies text as POSITIVE/NEGATIVE/NEUTRAL/MIXED with confidence scores. Entity Recognition extracts structured entities (PERSON, ORGANIZATION, DATE, MONEY, LOCATION) from unstructured text. Topic Modeling (LDA) discovers latent themes in large document collections without labeled training data — unsupervised. PII Detection identifies and optionally redacts 18+ PII entity types. Custom Classifier trains a multi-class or multi-label text classifier on your own taxonomy using labeled training documents.

stem: A solutions architect is designing a VPC for a three-tier application across three Availability Zones. The VPC CIDR is 10.0.0.0/16 (65,536 addresses). The design requires: public subnets for ALB (needs ~50 IPs each), private subnets for EC2 (needs ~500 IPs each), and database subnets for RDS (needs ~10 IPs each). Which TWO statements correctly describe AWS VPC subnetting constraints that must be accounted for in this design?

answers.A: AWS reserves 5 IP addresses in every subnet (the first 4 and the last). A /28 subnet (16 addresses) provides only 11 usable IPs — insufficient for the database subnet requiring 10 IPs with headroom.
answers.B: VPC subnets must be sized in powers of 2. A /23 subnet (512 addresses) provides 507 usable IPs, which satisfies the 500-IP requirement for EC2 private subnets with minor headroom.
answers.C: The VPC's DNS resolver (Route 53 Resolver) occupies the .2 address in the VPC CIDR, but this address is included in AWS's 5 reserved addresses per subnet and does not reduce usable IPs in subnets beyond those 5.
answers.D: Subnets in different Availability Zones can overlap CIDR ranges within the same VPC, enabling IP address reuse across AZs.
answers.E: The minimum subnet size in a VPC is /28 (16 addresses, 11 usable). The maximum subnet size must be smaller than the VPC CIDR block, so a /16 VPC can have at most a /17 subnet.

explanation: AWS reserves exactly 5 addresses per subnet: .0 (network), .1 (VPC router), .2 (DNS), .3 (future use), and the last address (broadcast). A /28 has 16 total, 11 usable — correct for the database subnets but with minimal headroom for the 10-IP requirement. A /23 has 512 total, 507 usable — correct for 500-IP EC2 requirements. Option C is partially true about .2 being the DNS resolver but the statement about it being included in the 5 reserved is correct — this is informational, not a trap answer. Option D is false — subnet CIDRs within a VPC CANNOT overlap. Option E is partially correct about minimum /28 and maximum being smaller than VPC, but the claim about /16 VPC limiting to /17 is correct only if you want a single subnet covering half the VPC — you can have many subnets of any size that together don't exceed the VPC CIDR.

stem: A platform team is optimizing AWS Lambda functions for production workloads. Match each operational requirement to the correct Lambda feature.

answers.A: Lambda Provisioned Concurrency
answers.B: Lambda Layers
answers.C: Lambda Destinations
answers.D: Lambda Function URLs
answers.E: Lambda SnapStart (for Java)

subquestions.prompt: A Java Lambda function serving user-facing API requests has p99 latency of 3 seconds due to cold starts (JVM initialization takes 2.5 seconds). The team needs consistently low latency for all invocations.

15 Lambda functions all use the same 50 MB NumPy/Pandas Python library. Packaging the library in each function zip increases deployment size and update time. Share the library as a reusable component.

An asynchronously invoked Lambda function (triggered by S3 events) must route its success result to an SQS queue for auditing and send failed invocations (after all retries) to a separate SQS DLQ for analysis.
Expose a Lambda function as a simple HTTPS endpoint without deploying an API Gateway. The endpoint must support request/response payloads and be accessible directly by a third-party webhook sender.

A Java 11 Lambda function initializes a Spring Boot application context, taking 8 seconds on cold start. Reduce cold start to under 1 second by taking a snapshot of the initialized execution environment.

explanation: Provisioned Concurrency keeps Lambda execution environments initialized and warm, eliminating cold start latency entirely — billed per concurrency-hour. Layers share common dependencies (libraries, runtimes) across multiple functions as reusable zip packages. Destinations route asynchronous invocation outcomes (success/failure) to SQS, SNS, EventBridge, or other Lambda functions — more flexible than DLQ alone. Function URLs provide HTTPS endpoints for Lambda without API Gateway. SnapStart (Java) takes a snapshot of the initialized execution environment after the init phase, restoring it for cold starts — reduces Java cold starts from seconds to milliseconds.

stem: A security engineer is hardening an Amazon EKS cluster. The cluster runs multi-tenant workloads where different teams' pods must not be able to communicate with each other's pods, and each team's pods must only have the AWS IAM permissions needed for their specific workload. Which TWO controls correctly implement network isolation and IAM least privilege at the pod level in EKS?

answers.A: Deploy the AWS VPC CNI with Kubernetes NetworkPolicy support (using a network policy engine like Calico or the VPC CNI network policy controller) to enforce pod-to-pod traffic restrictions based on namespace and label selectors.
answers.B: Configure EKS security groups at the node group level so that different teams' node groups use separate security groups, preventing cross-team pod communication at the EC2 level.
answers.C: Use IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) to associate specific IAM roles with each team's Kubernetes Service Account, providing pod-level AWS credential scoping via OIDC federation.
answers.D: Enable EKS Managed Node Groups with Bottlerocket AMI to use an immutable OS that prevents pods from modifying host system files.
answers.E: Configure Kubernetes RBAC ClusterRoles to restrict which AWS API calls each team can make from within the cluster.

explanation: Kubernetes NetworkPolicy (option A) with a compatible CNI plugin enforces Layer 3/4 traffic rules between pods based on label selectors and namespace selectors. Without a policy engine, pods in the same VPC can communicate freely. The VPC CNI's network policy controller (or Calico) enforces these rules at the pod ENI level. IRSA (option C) scopes AWS IAM permissions per Kubernetes Service Account — pods using Team A's service account assume Team A's IAM role, while Team B's pods assume a different role. This provides the AWS-level least privilege without over-granting node-level IAM permissions. Option B (node-level security groups) is coarser granularity — teams sharing a node group cannot be isolated without awsvpc mode and per-pod security groups. Option D (Bottlerocket) hardens the OS but doesn't control pod-to-pod networking or AWS IAM. Option E (RBAC) controls Kubernetes API access, not AWS API access.

stem: A security team is implementing comprehensive audit logging using AWS CloudTrail. Match each audit logging requirement to the correct CloudTrail feature.

answers.A: CloudTrail Management Events
answers.B: CloudTrail Data Events
answers.C: CloudTrail Insights
answers.D: AWS CloudTrail Lake
answers.E: CloudTrail Organization Trail

subquestions.prompt: Record all API calls to create, modify, or delete AWS resources (EC2 instance launches, IAM role changes, S3 bucket creation) across the account. This is the default audit log that tracks control plane operations.
Record every GetObject, PutObject, and DeleteObject API call on a specific S3 bucket containing sensitive medical records. This generates high-volume events not included in the default trail.
Automatically detect when the rate of IAM DeleteRole API calls spikes from a baseline of 2 per hour to 50 per hour, and send an SNS notification when an unusual activity pattern is detected.
Run SQL queries directly against CloudTrail event history spanning the last 7 years without exporting logs to S3 and Athena first. The events are stored in an immutable, managed data store.
Centralize CloudTrail logs from all 60 accounts in an AWS Organization into a single S3 bucket in the security account, with a single configuration that automatically includes new accounts.

explanation: Management Events (control plane) are logged by default and cover resource creation/modification/deletion. Data Events (data plane) cover object-level operations on S3, Lambda invocations, DynamoDB operations — high-volume and not logged by default. CloudTrail Insights detects unusual API activity patterns using ML baselines (unusual write activity, error rates). CloudTrail Lake is a managed event data store with built-in SQL query capability — no S3 + Athena pipeline required, with configurable retention up to 7 years. Organization Trails create a single trail that captures events from all accounts in an Organization automatically.

stem: A team is building two APIs: (1) a public REST API that needs request validation, usage plans with API key throttling, and a WAF integration for security, and (2) a real-time bidirectional communication API for a browser-based chat application. Which TWO API Gateway types correctly satisfy each requirement?

answers.A: API Gateway REST API (Regional endpoint) with request validators for body/parameters, usage plans linked to API keys for per-client throttling, and WAF Web ACL association.
answers.B: API Gateway HTTP API, which supports WAF integration, usage plans, and request validation at lower cost than REST API.
answers.C: API Gateway WebSocket API to maintain persistent connections with clients, routing messages by $connect/$disconnect/custom route keys, and enabling server-to-server push via the @connections API.
answers.D: API Gateway REST API with a Lambda authorizer and a Kinesis Data Streams integration to buffer incoming requests and process them asynchronously.
answers.E: API Gateway Private API (VPC Endpoint) to expose the chat API to internal VPC clients only via PrivateLink, without internet exposure.

explanation: REST API (option A) is the only API Gateway type that supports all three required features: request validators (body schema and parameter validation), usage plans with API key-based throttling, and WAF Web ACL association. HTTP API is cheaper and lower-latency but lacks usage plans, request validation, and WAF support (as of current feature parity). WebSocket API (option C) maintains persistent bidirectional connections — the browser connects once and sends/receives messages without polling. Route keys ($connect, $disconnect, custom) handle connection lifecycle and message routing. The @connections management API allows the backend to push messages to specific connected clients. Option B incorrectly claims HTTP API supports WAF and usage plans. Option D describes a valid async pattern but doesn't address the chat API requirement. Option E (Private API) restricts access to VPC, which is the opposite of a public chat application requirement.

stem: A company is implementing the AWS Well-Architected Sustainability pillar to reduce its carbon footprint. Match each sustainability optimization to the correct AWS approach.

answers.A: Migrate EC2 workloads to AWS Graviton processors
answers.B: Use AWS Spot Instances for non-critical batch workloads
answers.C: Implement S3 Intelligent-Tiering for infrequently accessed data
answers.D: Adopt serverless architecture (Lambda, Fargate)
answers.E: Enable EC2 Auto Scaling with aggressive scale-in policies

subquestions.prompt: Reduce the energy consumption per compute unit by 60% by switching from x86 to ARM-based processors that achieve better performance per watt for the same workload.
Increase average server utilization from 10% to 70-80% by running workloads on spare capacity in AWS data centers, indirectly improving overall data center energy efficiency.
Reduce unnecessary storage of infrequently accessed data on high-performance hardware by automatically moving objects to energy-efficient cold storage tiers based on access patterns.
Eliminate idle compute resources by running code only when invoked and sharing infrastructure across thousands of customers in a multi-tenant model, maximizing hardware utilization.
Reduce over-provisioned capacity by automatically terminating idle instances during off-peak hours (nights, weekends), ensuring compute resources exist only when they are actively processing work.

explanation: Graviton (ARM) processors deliver up to 60% better energy efficiency per compute unit vs x86 — a direct sustainability win. Spot Instances run on spare AWS capacity, improving overall data center utilization without additional hardware. Intelligent-Tiering moves cold data to lower-energy storage automatically. Serverless architectures eliminate idle resource waste by sharing infrastructure at scale and running only when invoked. Aggressive scale-in policies prevent over-provisioning, ensuring capacity matches demand and idle instances are terminated.

stem: A media company serves premium video content via CloudFront. Requirements: (1) Only CloudFront (not the public internet) should be able to access the S3 origin, and (2) individual paid subscribers must receive time-limited, user-specific URLs that cannot be shared with non-subscribers. Which TWO CloudFront security features address both requirements?

answers.A: Configure Origin Access Control (OAC) on the CloudFront distribution and update the S3 bucket policy to allow only the CloudFront service principal (cloudfront.amazonaws.com) with the specific distribution ID as a condition.
answers.B: Configure Origin Access Identity (OAI) and update the S3 bucket policy to allow only the OAI's IAM ARN. This is the original method for restricting S3 origins.
answers.C: Generate CloudFront Signed URLs with an expiration time and subscriber-specific policy statements (IP restriction, not-before time). The signing is done using a CloudFront key pair associated with a trusted signer.
answers.D: Enable CloudFront field-level encryption on the distribution to encrypt the subscriber's cookie at the edge, preventing CloudFront from reading the authentication token.
answers.E: Configure CloudFront to require HTTPS with a minimum TLS 1.2 policy and an ACM certificate, encrypting content in transit between subscribers and the CloudFront edge.

explanation: Origin Access Control (option A) is the current recommended replacement for OAI — it uses the CloudFront service principal with SigV4 authentication and supports S3 server-side encryption with SSE-KMS, including newer S3 features. The bucket policy with the distribution ARN condition ensures ONLY that CloudFront distribution can access S3. Option B (OAI) is the legacy mechanism — still functional but OAC is preferred for new deployments. CloudFront Signed URLs (option C) bind access to a specific subscriber with an expiration time and optional IP/time restrictions, cryptographically preventing URL sharing. The signer uses RSA private key pairs managed via CloudFront key groups. Option D (field-level encryption) protects specific form fields from backend systems — not relevant to origin access restriction. Option E (TLS enforcement) is a transport security baseline but doesn't address origin access control or subscriber-specific access.

stem: A DevSecOps team is implementing a secure container registry strategy using Amazon ECR. Match each security or operational requirement to the correct ECR feature.

answers.A: ECR image scanning (enhanced with Inspector)
answers.B: ECR lifecycle policies
answers.C: ECR image tag immutability
answers.D: ECR cross-region replication
answers.E: ECR pull-through cache

subquestions.prompt: Automatically scan every newly pushed container image for OS and programming language package CVEs, and generate a detailed vulnerability report with CVSS scores linked to the NVD database.
Automatically delete untagged images older than 14 days and retain only the last 5 tagged versions of each image in the repository to control storage costs.
Prevent image tags (e.g., 'production', 'v1.2.3') from being overwritten by a subsequent push. Once an image is pushed with a tag, that tag must always resolve to the same image digest.
Ensure that container images are available in us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1 so that ECS deployments in each region can pull images locally without cross-region latency or egress costs.
Cache public container images from Docker Hub in ECR to reduce Docker Hub rate limit errors during CI/CD builds and avoid egress costs for frequently pulled base images.

explanation: ECR Enhanced Scanning uses Amazon Inspector for continuous CVE scanning with NVD integration and CVSS scoring. Lifecycle policies automate cleanup of old/untagged images using count-based and age-based rules. Tag immutability prevents image tag reassignment — critical for reproducible deployments and supply chain security. Cross-region replication (private registry setting) replicates repositories to multiple regions. Pull-through cache mirrors public registries (Docker Hub, Quay, GitHub Container Registry) within ECR, providing rate limit relief and reduced egress.

stem: A data governance team manages a data lake in S3 with a Glue Data Catalog. An analytics team should be able to query a customer table in Athena but must not see the email_address column or any rows where account_status = 'DELETED'. Which TWO Lake Formation features implement this column-level and row-level security?

answers.A: Grant Lake Formation column-level permissions to the analytics team's IAM role, explicitly omitting the email_address column from the granted columns in the table permission.
answers.B: Create a Glue Data Catalog view that SELECTs only the non-sensitive columns, and grant the analytics team access to the view instead of the underlying table.
answers.C: Configure a Lake Formation data filter with a row filter expression 'account_status != "DELETED"' and a column filter excluding email_address, then grant this filter to the analytics team's IAM role.
answers.D: Create an S3 bucket policy that denies the analytics team's IAM role from reading objects in the 'deleted_accounts' S3 prefix.
answers.E: Enable Lake Formation tag-based access control (LF-Tags) with a sensitivity=HIGH tag on the email_address column, and deny the analytics team's role access to HIGH sensitivity columns.

explanation: Lake Formation column-level permissions (option A) allow granting access to specific columns in a table, effectively hiding sensitive columns like email_address from the grantee. When the analytics team queries the table in Athena, they only see the permitted columns — the query engine enforces this. Lake Formation data filters (option C) combine both column and row filtering in a single policy: the row filter expression 'account_status != DELETED' excludes deleted rows, and the column filter excludes email_address. Data filters are the native Lake Formation mechanism for fine-grained access control at both dimensions simultaneously. Option B (Glue view) is a valid alternative but is a table-level solution, not a Lake Formation permission, and requires maintaining the view. Option D (S3 bucket policy) operates at the object level — it cannot filter rows or columns within a file. Option E (LF-Tags) provides coarser attribute-based control but requires tag maintenance on every column and table.

stem: A developer team is choosing the right deployment tool for different serverless and infrastructure deployment scenarios. Match each scenario to the most appropriate AWS deployment tool.

answers.A: AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM)
answers.B: AWS Serverless Application Repository (SAR)
answers.C: AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK)
answers.D: AWS CloudFormation
answers.E: AWS Elastic Beanstalk

subquestions.prompt: Define a Lambda function, API Gateway, and DynamoDB table as a serverless application using a simplified YAML syntax with shorthand transforms (AWS::Serverless::Function, AWS::Serverless::Api), with local testing support.
Publish an internal reusable serverless component (a Lambda-powered S3 thumbnail generator) to a private repository, allowing other teams in the organization to discover and deploy it with one click.

Define VPCs, EKS clusters, and RDS databases using Python classes with IDE autocomplete, type checking, and the ability to create reusable constructs that enforce organizational patterns (e.g., always enable encryption).
Manage a legacy 500-resource stack using declarative JSON/YAML templates that have been maintained for 5 years. The team wants to continue using existing templates without migrating to a new tool.

Deploy a Node.js web application without managing infrastructure. The team provides the application code and a Procfile; the service handles load balancing, auto-scaling, and platform patching automatically.

explanation: SAM extends CloudFormation with serverless-specific resource types and the 'sam local' CLI for local Lambda testing. SAR is the managed repository for sharing and discovering serverless applications — supports private organizational sharing and public publishing. CDK generates CloudFormation from familiar programming languages (TypeScript, Python, Java) with reusable constructs and type safety. CloudFormation is the foundational IaC service for maintaining existing declarative templates. Elastic Beanstalk is the PaaS for web applications where developers deploy code and the platform manages infrastructure.

stem: A compliance team requires that sensitive data in S3 must be encrypted using a key that the company exclusively controls, and the key usage must be auditable. The company also requires that the encryption key for RDS never be exposed to AWS (the keys must be managed outside AWS). Which TWO encryption configurations meet these mutually exclusive requirements?

answers.A: Use SSE-KMS with a customer-managed KMS key (CMK) for the S3 bucket. The CMK key policy prevents AWS employees from accessing plaintext data, and all key usage is logged to CloudTrail.
answers.B: Use SSE-S3 (AWS managed key, AES-256) for the S3 bucket. AWS manages the key and rotation automatically with no additional cost.
answers.C: Use SSE-C (customer-provided key) for S3 objects, providing the encryption key in each API request. AWS uses the key for the operation but does not store it.
answers.D: Enable RDS encryption using a CloudHSM-backed external key store (XKS) in AWS KMS, where the actual cryptographic operations occur in the company's CloudHSM cluster outside AWS, and the key material never leaves the HSM.
answers.E: Enable RDS transparent data encryption (TDE) with Oracle TDE key management, storing the master key in AWS Secrets Manager.

explanation: SSE-KMS with CMK (option A) gives the company exclusive control via key policy — the CMK policy specifies exactly which principals can use the key, and CloudTrail logs every kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey operation, providing the required auditability. AWS cannot access the key without policy permission. External Key Store (XKS) in KMS (option D) allows KMS to proxy cryptographic operations to an external key manager (CloudHSM, on-premises HSM) — the key material never leaves the HSM and AWS cannot perform operations without calling the external key store. This satisfies 'key never exposed to AWS' for RDS. Option B (SSE-S3) uses an AWS-managed key — the company does not exclusively control it. Option C (SSE-C) is for S3 only — each API call must include the key, which is impractical for RDS and doesn't provide audit logging. Option E (TDE with Secrets Manager) stores key metadata in Secrets Manager, not the key material in an external HSM.

stem: A solutions architect is explaining EC2 instance lifecycle behaviors to a development team. Match each lifecycle scenario to the correct EC2 behavior or feature.

answers.A: EC2 Hibernation
answers.B: EC2 Stop-Start (EBS-backed)
answers.C: EC2 Terminate
answers.D: EC2 Spot Instance interruption (2-minute notice)
answers.E: EC2 Instance Store (ephemeral storage)

subquestions.prompt: A data science workload loads a 50 GB dataset into RAM. The researcher finishes for the day and wants to save the in-memory state so they can resume tomorrow without reloading the data. The instance must retain all in-flight computations.
An EC2 instance is stopped overnight to save costs. When started the next morning, it gets a new public IP address but retains the same private IP and all data on its EBS volumes.
When this action is taken on an EBS-backed instance, the root EBS volume is deleted by default (if DeleteOnTermination=true) and the instance ID can no longer be started.

AWS needs to reclaim capacity and sends this notification to an instance, giving the application 2 minutes to checkpoint state, complete in-flight requests, or gracefully shut down before forced termination.
An instance uses fast NVMe SSD storage for temporary files. All data on this storage type is lost when the instance is stopped, hibernated, or terminated — it only persists across reboots.

explanation: EC2 Hibernation saves RAM contents to the EBS root volume and stops the instance — on restart, RAM is restored and processes resume from where they left off. Stop-Start preserves EBS data and private IP but changes the public IP (unless Elastic IP). Terminate deletes the instance permanently; root EBS volumes are deleted by default. Spot interruption notice gives 2 minutes for graceful shutdown, accessible via instance metadata (action=terminate or action=stop). Instance Store is ephemeral SSD/HDD that doesn't survive stops or termination — suitable for scratch space, caches, or buffers.

stem: A startup runs a SaaS application with Aurora MySQL. The application experiences unpredictable traffic spikes (10x normal load during viral events) and the database must scale from near-zero during off-hours to handle peak load within seconds. The team also uses read replicas for analytics. Which TWO Aurora Serverless v2 behaviors must the architect understand to correctly design the cluster?

answers.A: Aurora Serverless v2 scales capacity in fine-grained increments (0.5 ACU steps) within seconds, based on load, between a configured minimum and maximum ACU range — no instance class selection required.
answers.B: Aurora Serverless v2 requires the entire cluster (writer and all readers) to use Serverless v2 capacity; you cannot mix Serverless v2 writer with provisioned reader instances in the same cluster.
answers.C: Aurora Serverless v2 reader instances can be added to a Serverless v2 writer cluster and will also scale independently based on their own load, providing independent read scaling.
answers.D: Aurora Serverless v2 pauses completely to 0 ACUs after a configurable idle period, providing zero-cost idle periods — this pause behavior is the same as Serverless v1.
answers.E: Aurora Serverless v2 can be used as a Global Database secondary, providing serverless read scaling in a secondary region for globally distributed reads.

explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 (option A) scales in 0.5 ACU increments in response to load changes within seconds — much finer-grained and faster than v1's coarser, slower scaling. The minimum can be set to 0.5 ACU (near zero cost when idle, but NOT fully paused). Option C is correct — you CAN mix Serverless v2 writers with Serverless v2 or provisioned readers in the same cluster. Each reader scales independently. Option B is false — mixed clusters are supported. Option D is false — Serverless v2 does NOT pause to 0 ACUs (minimum is 0.5 ACU). Serverless v1 supported pausing to 0; v2 maintains warm capacity. Option E is true but not one of the key design considerations — it's a bonus feature.

stem: A security engineer is explaining AWS network control differences to junior engineers. Match each network control behavior to the correct AWS feature.

answers.A: Network ACL rule evaluation
answers.B: Security Group rule evaluation
answers.C: Security Group rule aggregation
answers.D: Network ACL stateless behavior
answers.E: Security Group stateful behavior

subquestions.prompt: Rules are processed in ascending numeric order. The first rule that matches the traffic is applied and evaluation stops. A DENY rule with rule number 100 will block traffic that would match an ALLOW rule at 200.

If no rule in the attached security groups explicitly allows traffic, the traffic is implicitly denied. There is no explicit deny rule — only allow rules. All traffic is denied unless a rule permits it.
When multiple security groups are attached to an ENI, the effective rules are the union of all rules from all attached groups. If any security group allows traffic, the traffic is permitted.
Allowing inbound port 443 does NOT automatically allow the outbound response traffic. A corresponding outbound rule (typically allowing ephemeral ports 1024-65535) must be explicitly added.
Allowing inbound port 443 automatically tracks the connection state and allows the outbound response traffic back to the client, without needing an explicit outbound rule.

explanation: NACLs process rules in numeric order — the first match wins, enabling explicit DENY overrides. Security groups use implicit deny — only ALLOW rules exist, any traffic not matching is dropped. Multiple security groups on an ENI use union evaluation. NACLs are stateless — return traffic requires its own explicit rule (typically ephemeral port range). Security groups are stateful — established connection return traffic is automatically allowed, regardless of outbound rules.

stem: A company stores 90 days of application logs in CloudWatch Logs at a cost of $8,000/month. They only query logs from the last 7 days for troubleshooting but must retain all logs for 2 years for compliance. Which TWO approaches reduce costs while meeting retention requirements?

answers.A: Set the CloudWatch Logs log group retention period to 7 days to automatically expire old log events and reduce storage costs.
answers.B: Configure a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to stream log data in real-time to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, which delivers logs to S3 with Intelligent-Tiering storage class for long-term retention.
answers.C: Use CloudWatch Logs Export to S3 to export logs older than 7 days to S3 Standard-IA or Glacier, then set a log group retention of 7 days to delete them from CloudWatch Logs.
answers.D: Enable CloudWatch Logs Insights to compress log data in place, reducing storage costs by 60-80% without changing the retention policy.
answers.E: Move the application to emit logs directly to Kinesis Data Firehose instead of CloudWatch Logs, storing them in S3 from the start and using Athena for ad-hoc log analysis.

explanation: Option B (subscription filter to Kinesis Firehose to S3) continuously streams logs to S3 as they are ingested. Combined with setting log group retention to 7 days, this retains logs in CloudWatch for troubleshooting while archiving to much cheaper S3 storage (Intelligent-Tiering archives to Glacier tier at $0.004/GB vs CloudWatch Logs at ~$0.03/GB). Option C (export to S3 + 7-day retention) is the batch equivalent — use CreateExportTask to export old logs to S3 before they expire in CloudWatch. Both approaches move logs to S3 where long-term storage costs are 90%+ cheaper. Option A alone violates the 2-year compliance requirement by deleting logs after 7 days. Option D is false — CloudWatch Logs Insights is a query tool; it cannot compress stored log data. Option E is a valid architectural change but requires application code changes and is a bigger scope than an optimization.

stem: A DevOps team is building a golden AMI pipeline. Match each AMI management requirement to the correct EC2 Image Builder or AMI feature.

answers.A: EC2 Image Builder pipeline with automated testing
answers.B: AMI copy across regions
answers.C: AMI sharing with AWS Organizations
answers.D: EC2 Image Builder STIG hardening component
answers.E: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager with patch baselines

subquestions.prompt: Automate the weekly build of a hardened Amazon Linux 2 AMI: install agents, apply OS patches, run CIS benchmark tests, and automatically distribute the approved AMI to all AWS accounts in the organization.
Make a golden AMI available in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 for disaster recovery deployments, preserving the AMI's encryption and tags from the source us-east-1 AMI.
Allow all accounts in a specific OU within AWS Organizations to launch instances from a hardened AMI without sharing the AMI ID individually with each of the 40 accounts.

Apply Department of Defense Security Technical Implementation Guide configurations to an AMI, automatically remediating hundreds of security control requirements (password policies, audit settings, services).
Apply OS security patches to running EC2 instances on a scheduled basis, using maintenance windows and patch compliance baselines, without rebuilding the AMI for each patch cycle.

explanation: Image Builder pipelines automate AMI creation with build/test/distribute phases — tests run in the image builder environment before distribution. AMI copy replicates AMIs to other regions preserving encryption. AMI sharing with Organizations uses a launch permission that applies to entire OUs. Image Builder STIG components are pre-built automation for applying DoD STIG hardening. SSM Patch Manager applies patches to running instances using maintenance windows and patch baselines — complementary to golden AMIs for ongoing patching.

stem: A real-time analytics platform uses Kinesis Data Streams with 10 shards. A single consumer application is struggling to keep up with the 80 MB/s ingest rate (10 shards × 8 MB/s per shard ingest capacity). A second analytics application also needs to read the same stream simultaneously without impacting the first consumer's throughput. Which TWO changes address both the consumer throughput and multi-consumer isolation requirements?

answers.A: Register the second consumer as an Enhanced Fan-Out consumer using RegisterStreamConsumer. Each registered consumer receives its own dedicated 2 MB/s per shard read throughput, independent of other consumers.
answers.B: Increase the number of shards to 20 using UpdateShardCount to double read throughput, allowing both consumers to share the increased capacity.
answers.C: Configure the first consumer to use Standard GetRecords with polling, and use LATEST as the shard iterator type so it only processes new records and doesn't compete with the second consumer for shard capacity.
answers.D: Also register the first consumer as an Enhanced Fan-Out consumer. With both registered, each gets 2 MB/s per shard (20 MB/s total for 10 shards) independently, allowing simultaneous consumption without throttling.
answers.E: Split each shard into two using SplitShard operations, doubling total shard count to 20 and providing each consumer with dedicated shards by partitioning by consumer ID.

explanation: Standard GetRecords has a shared 2 MB/s per shard read limit across ALL consumers on a shard. With two consumers sharing standard reads, each gets at most 1 MB/s per shard — insufficient for 8 MB/s ingest. Enhanced Fan-Out (option A) gives each registered consumer a dedicated 2 MB/s per shard push-based subscription via HTTP/2, completely isolated from other consumers. Registering BOTH consumers as Enhanced Fan-Out consumers (option D) provides each with 2 MB/s per shard × 10 shards = 20 MB/s per consumer — adequate to keep up with 8 MB/s ingest plus margin. Option B (resharding) increases ingest capacity but doesn't address the multi-consumer read isolation problem — both consumers would still share standard read limits. Option C (LATEST iterator) affects where reading starts, not throughput. Option E (SplitShard for dedicated shards) is an anti-pattern — it doubles costs without solving multi-consumer isolation.

RI Recommendations analyzes On-Demand usage patterns for specific instance types and recommends RI purchases with break-even analysis. stem: A global e-commerce platform requires an active-active multi-region architecture where users in both us-east-1 and eu-west-1 can read AND write, with data synchronized between regions. The RTO must be near-zero (no manual failover). Which TWO database services natively support active-active multi-region write capabilities?

answers.A: Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables, which provides fully managed multi-master replication across up to 10 regions with sub-second replication and last-writer-wins conflict resolution.
answers.B: Amazon Aurora Global Database with write forwarding enabled, which allows secondary regions to process writes that are forwarded to the primary region — but this is NOT active-active (one writer).
answers.C: Amazon RDS Multi-AZ with cross-region read replicas promoted to primary in case of failure — suitable for active-active with manual promotion.
answers.D: Amazon ElastiCache Global Datastore (Redis) with two-region replication, where both clusters can accept writes and synchronize changes bidirectionally.
answers.E: Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) multi-region replication, which supports writes to any region with eventual consistency replication between regions.

explanation: DynamoDB Global Tables (option A) is the canonical AWS multi-master database — all replica tables in all regions accept writes simultaneously. Conflicts are resolved by last-writer-wins (based on timestamps). Replication lag is typically sub-second. Option E (Keyspaces multi-region) also supports writes to any region with eventual consistency — it uses Cassandra's multi-master replication model. Option B is incorrect about Aurora Global Database: write forwarding allows secondary regions to process writes, but they are forwarded to the single primary — this is NOT active-active. The primary is still the sole writer; the secondary forwards writes to the primary via the PrivateLink network. Option C (RDS read replicas) requires manual promotion — not near-zero RTO. Option D is incorrect: ElastiCache Global Datastore has a primary cluster and secondary read-only clusters — writes go to primary only.

stem: A SaaS platform fronts its application with Amazon CloudFront and an Application Load Balancer. The company must terminate TLS at CloudFront for internet clients and also encrypt traffic from CloudFront to the ALB, with automatic certificate renewal and no manual private-key handling. Which TWO actions should the solutions architect take? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Request an ACM public certificate in us-east-1 and attach it to the CloudFront distribution.
answers.B: Request an ACM public certificate in the ALB's Region and attach it to the ALB HTTPS listener.
answers.C: Export the CloudFront certificate private key from ACM and install the same certificate manually on the ALB.
answers.D: Use a self-signed certificate on the ALB because CloudFront does not validate the origin certificate chain when HTTPS is selected.
answers.E: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer because ACM certificates cannot be used with ALB listeners.

explanation: CloudFront requires ACM certificates to be requested or imported in us-east-1, so an ACM public certificate in that Region is the correct choice for internet-facing TLS termination. The ALB needs its own certificate in the ALB's Region so CloudFront can use HTTPS to the origin with a trusted certificate chain. ACM public certificates cannot have their private keys exported, self-signed origin certificates complicate trust and validation, and ALBs fully support ACM-managed TLS listeners.

stem: A research company needs at least 2.5 Gbps of encrypted connectivity from its on-premises network to AWS within days, not months. Using the public internet is acceptable temporarily, but a single VPN tunnel is not sufficient. The company also wants automatic path load sharing across tunnels. Which TWO design choices BEST meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answers.A: Terminate the VPNs on an AWS Transit Gateway and enable Equal-Cost Multi-Path (ECMP) routing.
answers.B: Use a Virtual Private Gateway because it automatically load-balances all tunnels from all customer gateways equally.
answers.C: Establish multiple AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections from separate customer gateway devices or appliances.
answers.D: Use a single AWS Client VPN endpoint because client sessions can aggregate throughput for data center traffic.
answers.E: Order a 1 Gbps hosted AWS Direct Connect connection as the only path and expect it to be provisioned immediately.

explanation: When internet-based connectivity must exceed the practical throughput of a single tunnel, the AWS pattern is to use multiple Site-to-Site VPN connections from separate customer gateways and terminate them on a Transit Gateway. Transit Gateway supports ECMP so traffic can be load-shared across equal-cost BGP paths. Client VPN is for individual remote users, a single hosted Direct Connect does not meet the immediate timeline or bandwidth target by itself, and Virtual Private Gateway is not the preferred design for ECMP-based aggregation across multiple connections in this scenario.
tags: Selecting the appropriate bandwidth allocation for a network device (for example, a single VPN compared with multiple VPNs, Direct Connect speed)
